I have now told you my own and Tom’s adventures, together with some valuable collateral particulars; and having acquitted myself of my engagement, I wish you a very good night, and pleasant dreams.

===Chinese===
那女佣又道——

"我这就下到巷子里，叫乔·加维（Joe Gavvey）上来，把剩下的茶具家伙收拾了，一并搬到你们新寓所去。"

我们便一同出门而去，我想我们每一个人，在最后一道跨过那不祥的门槛之时，都呼吸得舒坦了些。

末了，依照小说界那个自古相传、不仅把英雄送过种种历险、还要把他顺顺当当送出人世的惯例，我不妨再补上几句。你必已看出，对于惯于编撰小说的人来说，那血肉之躯的英雄是何物，那么这所砖、木、灰泥所造的老宅，对于我这位忠实的实录者，亦是何物。是以我责无旁贷，要把它最终的结局一并记下——事情不过是这样：我这段故事之后约莫两年，这宅子被一位自称杜尔斯托夫男爵（Baron Duhlstoerf）的江湖医生租下，他在客厅窗里摆满了一瓶瓶浸在白兰地里的、难以形容的骇人物件，又在报上登满了照例那一套夸大其词、欺世盗名的广告。这位先生在他的诸般美德之中，并不把"节制"算入，一夜，他酒喝得太多，竟点着了床帷，烧坏了自己，也把这宅子烧了个精光。其后它被重建了一回，曾有一时，一个承办殡丧的人在此处开了业。

我如今已把我与汤姆两人的奇遇、连同几则可贵的旁证细节，都讲与你听了；我既已践约，便祝你晚安，并做好梦。

## An Authentic Narrative of a Haunted House / 一幢凶宅的真实记述

===Original===
[The Editor of the *University Magazine* submits the following very remarkable statement, with every detail of which he has been for some years acquainted, upon the ground that it affords the most authentic and ample relation of a series of marvellous phenomena, in nowise connected with what is technically termed "spiritualism," which he has anywhere met with. All the persons—and there are many of them living—upon whose separate evidence some parts, and upon whose united testimony others, of this most singular recital depend, are, in their several walks of life, respectable, and such as would in any matter of judicial investigation be deemed wholly unexceptionable witnesses. There is not an incident here recorded which would not have been distinctly deposed to on oath had any necessity existed, by the persons who severally, and some of them in great fear, related their own distinct experiences. The Editor begs most pointedly to meet *in limine* the suspicion, that he is elaborating a trick, or vouching for another ghost of Mrs. Veal. As a mere story the narrative is valueless: its sole claim to attention is its absolute truth. For the good faith of its relator he pledges his own and the character of this Magazine. With the Editor's concurrence, the name of the watering place, and some special circumstances in no essential way bearing upon the peculiar character of the story, but which might have indicated the locality, and possibly annoyed persons interested in house property there, have been suppressed by the narrator. Not the slightest liberty has been taken with the narrative, which is presented precisely in the terms in which the writer of it, who employs throughout the first person, would, if need were, fix it in the form of an affidavit.]

===Chinese===
［《大学杂志》（University Magazine）主编谨呈下文这一份极为非凡的陈述，其每一细节他已熟知数年，所以公之于众，乃因它所记录的一系列惊人现象，与他平生所见任何材料相比，最为翔实充分，且与世人技术上所谓的"通灵术"（spiritualism）毫无瓜葛。这份至为离奇的记述，有些部分有赖于各位证人的分别举证，另一些则赖其众口一词；这些人——其中不少如今仍健在——在各自行当里皆为体面之人，若置于任何司法调查之中，皆会被视为毫无可指摘之处的人证。此处所载每一桩事件，假若当年确有必要，那些各自讲述——其中数人且是在极度恐惧之中讲述——亲身经历之人，皆会毫不模糊地宣誓作证。主编恳请于篇首即正面回应一种疑虑：他绝非在精心编排一场戏法，亦非在为又一个"韦尔夫人之鬼"（ghost of Mrs. Veal）背书。单就故事而言，此记毫无价值；它唯一值得一读之处，在于其绝对的纪实性。至于讲述者的诚信，他以本人的人格与本刊的声誉一并担保。经主编首肯，讲述者隐去了那处海滨胜地的地名，以及若干对故事本身的特质并无实质影响、却可能暴露地点所在、并给当地房产主添扰的特殊情节。全文未对原叙作丝毫改动，其措辞一如执笔者——他始终以第一人称行文——若有必要，本可一字不改地据以立为宣誓书的原貌呈现。］

===Original===
Within the last eight years—the precise date I purposely omit—I I was ordered by my physician, my health being in an unsatisfactory state, to change my residence to one upon the seacoast; and accordingly, I took a house for a year in a fashionable watering-place, at a moderate distance from the city in which I had previously resided, and connected with it by a railway.

Winter was setting in when my removal thither was decided upon; but there was nothing whatever dismal or depressing in the change. The house I had taken was to all appearance, and in point of convenience, too, quite a modern one. It formed one in a cheerful row, with small gardens in front, facing the sea, and commanding sea air and sea views in perfection. In the rear it had coach-house and stable, and between them and the house a considerable grass-plot, with some flowerbeds, interposed.

Our family consisted of my wife and myself, with three children, the eldest about nine years old, she and the next in age being girls; and the youngest, between six and seven, a boy. To these were added six servants, whom, although for certain reasons I decline giving their real names, I shall indicate, for the sake of clearness, by arbitrary ones. There was a nurse, Mrs. Southerland; a nursery-maid, Ellen Page; the cook, Mrs. Greenwood; and the housemaid, Ellen Faith; a butler, whom I shall call Smith, and his son, James, about two-and-twenty.

We came out to take possession at about seven o'clock in the evening; everything was comfortable and cheery; good fires lighted, the rooms neat and airy, and a general air of preparation and comfort, highly conducive to good spirits and pleasant anticipations.

===Chinese===
过去八年之内——确切年份我刻意略去——因身体欠佳，遵医嘱我须迁居海滨；于是我在一处时髦的海水浴场租下一宅，租期一年，此地距我原先所居之城路程适中，且有铁路相通。

决定迁居之时正值入冬，但此番搬迁并无半点萧瑟压抑之感。我所租下的宅子，无论外观还是起居便利，都十足是一座新式宅邸。它与一排明快的房屋相连，屋前各有小花园，面朝大海，尽得海风海景之美。屋后另设有车房马厩，二者与正屋之间隔着一片颇大的草坪，间以几方花圃。

家中人丁计有我与妻子、并三名子女：长女约九岁，其次也是个女孩，最小的男孩在六七岁之间。此外尚有仆人六名，虽因种种缘由我不便写出他们的真名，但为求清晰，姑且以假名指代。计有：保姆萨瑟兰夫人（Mrs. Southerland）；育婴女仆埃伦·佩奇（Ellen Page）；厨娘格林伍德夫人（Mrs. Greenwood）；女仆埃伦·费思（Ellen Faith）；一名男管家，姑名之为史密斯（Smith）；以及他的儿子，年约二十二岁的詹姆斯（James）。

我们傍晚七时许前来接管入住；屋中一切妥帖明快；炉火已旺，各房整洁通风，处处见悉心备办、舒适安居的气象，颇能令人心绪舒畅，对日后生出美好的指望。

===Original===
The sitting-rooms were large and cheerful, and they and the bedrooms more than ordinarily lofty, the kitchen and servants' rooms, on the same level, were well and comfortably furnished, and had, like the rest of the house, an air of recent painting and fitting up, and a completely modern character, which imparted a very cheerful air of cleanliness and convenience.

There had been just enough of the fuss of settling agreeably to occupy us, and to give a pleasant turn to our thoughts after we had retired to our rooms. Being an invalid, I had a small bed to myself—resigning the four-poster to my wife. The candle was extinguished, but a night-light was burning. I was coming upstairs, and she, already in bed, had just dismissed her maid, when we were both startled by a wild scream from her room; I found her in a state of the extremest agitation and terror. She insisted that she had seen an unnaturally tall figure come beside her bed and stand there. The light was too faint to enable her to define anything respecting this apparition, beyond the fact of her having most distinctly seen such a shape, colourless from the insufficiency of the light to disclose more than its dark outline.

We both endeavoured to reassure her. The room once more looked so cheerful in the candlelight, that we were quite uninfluenced by the contagion of her terrors. The movements and voices of the servants downstairs still getting things into their places and completing our comfortable arrangements, had also their effect in steeling us against any such influence, and we set the whole thing down as a dream, or an imperfectly-seen outline of the bed-curtains. When, however, we were alone, my wife reiterated, still in great agitation, her clear assertion that she had most positively seen, being at the time as completely awake as ever she was, precisely what she had described to us. And in this conviction she continued perfectly firm.

===Chinese===
起居室宽敞明快，与卧室一样，天花板都格外高敞；厨房与仆役房与之同层，陈设齐备而舒适，与全屋别处一样，带着新近油漆、新近修缮的气派，十足一副现代做派，自有一种令人愉悦的洁净便利之感。

初来安顿的种种忙碌恰如其分地占住了我们，待回到各自房中歇下，倒也令人心生舒畅。我因是病体，独自睡一张小床——把那张四柱大床让给了妻子。蜡烛已经吹熄，点着一盏夜灯。我正要上楼，她已就寝，刚刚打发走了贴身女仆，这时她房中忽然传出一声凄厉的尖叫，把我们两人都吓了一跳；我赶到时，见她惊恐万状、不能自已。她一口咬定，亲眼看见一个高得出奇的人影来到她床边，立在那里。灯光太暗，她无法看清这鬼影的任何细节，所能确证的只是：她分明看见了那样一个轮廓，由于光线不足，只见一团漆黑的形影，辨不出颜色。

我和旁人都尽力宽慰她。烛光之下，屋子重又显得那样明亮，我们丝毫未被她的恐惧传染。楼下仆人们还在搬挪归置、料理善后，他们走动的脚步声、说话的声响，也叫我们益发不受影响；我们于是把这事全然归结为一场梦，或是床帷在昏暗中看走了眼的轮廓。然而待到只剩我们两人时，妻子仍惊魂未定，反复坚称：她当时清醒无比，绝无半点迷糊，所见正是她方才所述，分毫不差。这一信念，她始终不曾动摇。

===Original===
A day or two after this, it came out that our servants were under an apprehension that, somehow or other, thieves had established a secret mode of access to the lower part of the house. The butler, Smith, had seen an ill-looking woman in his room on the first night of our arrival; and he and other servants constantly saw, for many days subsequently, glimpses of a retreating figure, which corresponded with that so seen by him, passing through a passage which led to a back area in which were some coal-vaults.

This figure was seen always in the act of retreating, its back turned, generally getting round the corner of the passage into the area, in a stealthy and hurried way, and, when closely followed, imperfectly seen again entering one of the coal-vaults, and when pursued into it, nowhere to be found.

The idea of anything supernatural in the matter had, strange to say, not yet entered the mind of any one of the servants. They had heard some stories of smugglers having secret passages into houses, and using their means of access for purposes of pillage, or with a view to frighten superstitious people out of houses which they needed for their own objects, and a suspicion of similar practices here, caused them extreme uneasiness. The apparent anxiety also manifested by this retreating figure to escape observation, and her always appearing to make her egress at the same point, favoured this romantic hypothesis. The men, however, made a most careful examination of the back area, and of the coal-vaults, with a view to discover some mode of egress, but entirely without success. On the contrary, the result was, so far as it went, subversive of the theory; solid masonry met them on every hand.

===Chinese===
此事过后一两日，仆人们中间便传出一种忧虑：不知怎的，窃贼似乎已经开辟了一条潜入房屋下层的暗道。管家史密斯在我们到达头一晚，就在自己房里见到过一个面相不善的女人；其后数日，他与其余仆人屡屡瞥见一个退避离去的人影，与他所见那番模样恰相吻合，那人影穿过一条通往后方场院的过道，场院里设有几间煤窖。

这身影每次出现，总是正在退避之中，背对着人，多半是悄然匆忙地绕过过道的拐角没入场院；若紧紧跟上，又会隐约看见它钻进其中一间煤窖，一旦追入其中，却再也寻不着踪影。

说来奇怪，事情涉超自然一节，那时竟从未掠过任何一名仆人的脑海。他们曾听过一些走私客凿暗道入宅的故事，说走私客借这种暗道行劫掠之事，或存心把迷信之人吓出宅子，以便他们另有所图；此地疑有同类勾当，令他们极为不安。那退避的身影显然急于躲开众人的目光，又总在同一处脱身，也助长了这种异想天开的揣测。然而男仆们对后院和煤窖作了极其仔细的勘查，意图找出某种出口，却一无所获。情形恰恰相反，勘查所得反而颠覆了此说——四下里所遇，尽是结结实实的砖石。

===Original===
I called the man, Smith, up, to hear from his own lips the particulars of what he had seen; and certainly his report was very curious. I give it as literally as my memory enables me:—

His son slept in the same room, and was sound asleep; but he lay awake, as men sometimes will on a change of bed, and having many things on his mind. He was lying with his face towards the wall, but observing a light and some little stir in the room, he turned round in his bed, and saw the figure of a woman, squalid, and ragged in dress; her figure rather low and broad; as well as I recollect, she had something—either a cloak or shawl—on, and wore a bonnet. Her back was turned, and she appeared to be searching or rummaging for something on the floor, and, without appearing to observe him, she turned in doing so towards him. The light, which was more like the intense glow of a coal, as he described it, being of a deep red colour, proceeded from the hollow of her hand, which she held beside her head, and he saw her perfectly distinctly. She appeared middle-aged, was deeply pitted with the smallpox, and blind of one eye. His phrase in describing her general appearance was, that she was "a miserable, poor-looking creature."

He was under the impression that she must be the woman who had been left by the proprietor in charge of the house, and who had that evening, after having given up the keys, remained for some little time with the female servants. He coughed, therefore, to apprise her of his presence, and turned again towards the wall. When he again looked round she and the light were gone; and odd as was her method of lighting herself in her search, the circumstances excited neither uneasiness nor curiosity in his mind, until he discovered next morning that the woman in question had left the house long before he had gone to his bed.

===Chinese===
我把史密斯叫到楼上，亲口听他讲述所见的原委；他的报告委实离奇得很。我凭记忆所及，尽量照原话引述如下：——

他那夜与儿子同住一室，儿子睡得正熟；他却醒着——人换了床有时便会如此，何况他心事重重。他本来面墙侧卧，忽见房中有一线光、一阵轻微的响动，便在床上翻过身来，只见一个女人的身影，衣着褴褛肮脏；身形低矮壮阔；我若没记错，她身上披着什么——是斗篷还是披巾——头戴一顶软帽。她背对着他，似在地上翻找、搜摸什么东西，翻找之间，身子不觉朝他这边转过来，却像不曾察觉他。那光，据他形容，更像是煤块炽燃时那种浓烈的赤红辉光，发自她手掌弯成的凹窝，她举到鬓边，于是他把她看得清清楚楚。她看去是中年模样，脸上密布天花痘瘢，瞎了一只眼。他形容其人总貌的原话是："一个可怜兮兮、穷酸相的东西。"

他当时满以为，她必是房主留下看守此宅的那个妇人——当晚交出钥匙之后，她还在女仆们那里盘桓了一阵。于是他咳了一声，好让她知道房中有人，便又转身朝墙睡了。待他再回头看时，那女人和那光都不见了；她那照明寻物之法虽怪，他却既未生不安，也未起疑窦，直至次日清晨才发觉：那位妇人早在他上床就寝之前许久，便已离开了这宅子。

===Original===
I examined the man very closely as to the appearance of the person who had visited him, and the result was what I have described. It struck me as an odd thing, that even then, considering how prone to superstition persons in his rank of life usually are, he did not seem to suspect anything supernatural in the occurrence; and, on the contrary, was thoroughly persuaded that his visitant was a living person, who had got into the house by some hidden entrance.

On Sunday, on his return from his place of worship, he told me that, when the service was ended, and the congregation making their way slowly out, he saw the very woman in the crowd, and kept his eye upon her for several minutes, but such was the crush, that all his efforts to reach her were unavailing, and when he got into the open street she was gone. He was quite positive as to his having distinctly seen her, however, for several minutes, and scouted the possibility of any mistake as to identity; and fully impressed with the substantial and living reality of his visitant, he was very much provoked at her having escaped him. He made inquiries also in the neighbourhood, but could procure no information, nor hear of any other persons having seen any woman corresponding with his visitant.

===Chinese===
我把这仆人细细盘问了一番，专问那来访之人的模样，所得正是上文所述。有一桩事令我颇觉古怪：即便到了那时，考虑到他这等身份的人向来极易迷信，他却似乎丝毫未疑此事有超自然之处；恰恰相反，他坚信那位来客是个活人，是从某处暗道潜入此宅的。

礼拜那天，他从教堂回来告诉我：礼拜完毕、会众正缓缓散场之际，他在人群里瞥见了那个女人，盯着她看了足有好几分钟，无奈人太挤，他怎么也挤不到她跟前，待他挤到外面街上，她已不见踪影。不过他十分笃定，自己分明盯着她看了好几分钟，对认错人一说嗤之以鼻；他既深信那来客是有血有肉的活人，对她竟从眼皮底下溜走，十分恼火。他也在左近四下打听，却一无所得，也听不到有旁人见过与此相符的妇人。

===Original===
The cook and the housemaid occupied a bedroom on the kitchen floor. It had whitewashed walls, and they were actually terrified by the appearance of the shadow of a woman passing and repassing across the side wall opposite to their beds. They suspected that this had been going on much longer than they were aware, for its presence was discovered by a sort of accident, its movements happening to take a direction in distinct contrariety to theirs.

This shadow always moved upon one particular wall, returning after short intervals, and causing them extreme terror. They placed the candle, as the most obvious specific, so close to the infested wall, that the flame all but touched it; and believed for some time that they had effectually got rid of this annoyance; but one night, notwithstanding this arrangement of the light, the shadow returned, passing and repassing, as heretofore, upon the same wall, although their only candle was burning within an inch of it, and it was obvious that no substance capable of casting such a shadow could have interposed; and, indeed, as they described it, the shadow seemed to have no sort of relation to the position of the light, and appeared, as I have said, in manifest defiance of the laws of optics.

I ought to mention that the housemaid was a particularly fearless sort of person, as well as a very honest one; and her companion, the cook, a scrupulously religious woman, and both agreed in every particular in their relation of what occurred.

===Chinese===
厨娘和女仆住在厨房那一层的一间卧室里。屋里四壁粉刷雪白，她俩竟被一个女人影子骇得魂不附体——那影子就在她俩床铺对面的侧墙上来回游移。她俩疑心这事由来已久，只是自己一向不曾发觉；原来这影子之被发现，纯属偶然：它的移动方向恰好与她俩的动作截然相左。

这影子总在同一面墙上移动，隔不多久又折回来，把她俩吓得不轻。她俩把蜡烛——这是最现成的破解法子——挪到紧贴那闹鬼的墙面，烛火几乎要舔着墙皮；有一阵子她俩当真以为已把这祸祟彻底驱除了。可有一夜，尽管烛火这般布置，那影子竟又回来了，依旧在那面墙上往返游移，而屋里仅有的一支蜡烛就在距墙不到一寸之处燃着；显而易见，绝无任何足以投下这般阴影的物体横亘其间；况且据她俩描述，这影子与光源的位置了无干系，一如我前文所言，是公然无视光学定律的。

我应当说明：那女仆本是个天不怕地不怕的人，为人又极诚实；她的同伴厨娘则是个虔诚恪守宗教的妇人；她俩所述种种，事无巨细，全然吻合。

===Original===
Meanwhile, the nursery was not without its annoyances, though as yet of a comparatively trivial kind. Sometimes, at night, the handle of the door was turned hurriedly as if by a person trying to come in, and at others a knocking was made at it. These sounds occurred after the children had settled to sleep, and while the nurse still remained awake. Whenever she called to know "who is there," the sounds ceased; but several times, and particularly at first, she was under the impression that they were caused by her mistress, who had come to see the children, and thus impressed she had got up and opened the door, expecting to see her, but discovering only darkness, and receiving no answer to her inquiries.

With respect to this nurse, I must mention that I believe no more perfectly trustworthy servant was ever employed in her capacity; and, in addition to her integrity, she was remarkably gifted with sound common sense.

===Chinese===
与此同时，育儿室也并非全无烦恼，只是起初尚属细枝末节。夜间，有时门把手被人急急拧动，像有人要闯进来；有时又响起一阵敲门声。这些声响都发生在孩子们已经睡熟、保姆尚还醒着的时候。每逢她出声相问"是谁"，那声响便戛然而止；但有几次，尤其是起初，她总以为是女主人前来看视孩子，这样想着便起身开门，满心以为会见到女主人，却只见一片漆黑，任她怎么发问，也无人应答。

关于这位保姆，我必须说一句：我相信，在她这一行当里，再也找不出比她更可靠的人了；她不仅为人忠厚，而且天分甚高，颇具难得的见识。

===Original===
One morning, I think about three or four weeks after our arrival, I was sitting at the parlour window which looked to the front, when I saw the little iron door which admitted into the small garden that lay between the window where I was sitting and the public road, pushed open by a woman who so exactly answered the description given by Smith of the woman who had visited his room on the night of his arrival as instantaneously to impress me with the conviction that she must be the identical person. She was a square, short woman, dressed in soiled and tattered clothes, scarred and pitted with smallpox, and blind of an eye. She stepped hurriedly into the little enclosure, and peered from a distance of a few yards into the room where I was sitting. I felt that now was the moment to clear the matter up; but there was something stealthy in the manner and look of the woman which convinced me that I must not appear to notice her until her retreat was fairly cut off. Unfortunately, I was suffering from a lame foot, and could not reach the bell as quickly as I wished. I made all the haste I could, and rang violently to bring up the servant Smith. In the short interval that intervened, I observed the woman from the window, who having in a leisurely way, and with a kind of scrutiny, looked along the front windows of the house, passed quickly out again, closing the gate after her, and followed a lady who was walking along the footpath at a quick pace, as if with the intention of begging from her. The moment the man entered I told him—"the blind woman you described to me has this instant followed a lady in that direction, try to overtake her." He was, if possible, more eager than I in the chase, but returned in a short time after a vain pursuit, very hot, and utterly disappointed. And, thereafter, we saw her face no more.

===Chinese===
某日清晨——我想约莫是我们到达之后三四周——我坐在朝前的起居室窗前，忽见那扇通往小花园的铁制小门被一个女人推开。那小花园正夹在我所坐的窗下与公路之间。这女人与史密斯所描述他到达之夜闯进他房中的那妇人，吻合得分毫不差，我登时便断定：必是同一个人无疑。她身形矮壮方正，衣衫又脏又破，满脸天花瘢痕，瞎着一只眼。她急匆匆踏入那方小围地，隔着几码远朝我所坐的屋里张望。我感到清算此事的时机已到；可这女人的神情举止里透着一股鬼祟，使我相信，非得等她的退路被彻底切断，才能让她察觉我已注意到她。不巧我那时正犯着脚疾，行动不便，没能如我所愿那般快够着拉铃绳。我竭尽全力，猛力拉铃，要叫史密斯上来。就在这短短一瞬之间，我从窗口望见那女人，竟又不慌不忙、似在审视地沿屋前各窗打量了一番，随即快步走了出去，随手带上小门，尾随一位正快步走在人行道上的女士，一副要上前乞讨的模样。仆人一进门我便吩咐他："你描述给我听的那个瞎眼女人，方才就朝那个方向尾随一位女士去了，快去追。"他追起来若非比我还急，至少也不相上下，可追了一阵空手而归，气喘吁吁，大失所望。自那以后，我们再也没见过她的面。

===Original===
All this time, and up to the period of our leaving the house, which was not for two or three months later, there occurred at intervals the only phenomenon in the entire series having any resemblance to what we hear described of "Spiritualism." This was a knocking, like a soft hammering with a wooden mallet, as it seemed in the timbers between the bedroom ceilings and the roof. It had this special peculiarity, that it was always rythmical, and, I think, invariably, the emphasis upon the last stroke. It would sound rapidly "one, two, three, *four*—one, two, three, *four*;" or "one, two, *three*—one, two, *three*," and sometimes "one, *two*—one, *two*," etc., and this, with intervals and resumptions, monotonously for hours at a time.

At first this caused my wife, who was a good deal confined to her bed, much annoyance; and we sent to our neighbours to inquire if any hammering or carpentering was going on in their houses but were informed that nothing of the sort was taking place. I have myself heard it frequently, always in the same inaccessible part of the house, and with the same monotonous emphasis. One odd thing about it was, that on my wife's calling out, as she used to do when it became more than usually troublesome, "stop that noise," it was invariably arrested for a longer or shorter time.

===Chinese===
在这整段时间里，直到我们两三个月后搬离此宅为止，始终有一种现象不时出现——它是全部怪事之中，唯一与我们平日所闻"通灵术"（Spiritualism）略略相似的一桩。那是一阵敲击声，像用木槌轻柔地捶打，听来出自卧室天花板与屋顶之间的木料之中。它有一个特别的怪处：永远是有节奏的，而且——我想——重音总是落在最后一下。它会急促地响起"一、二、三、*四*——一、二、三、*四*"；或是"一、二、*三*——一、二、*三*"；有时则是"一、*二*——一、*二*"，如此等等，断断续续、复又响起，单调地一敲便是几个钟头。

起初这声音叫我妻子很是心烦——她多半时候卧病在床；我们派人去向四邻打听，是否他们家中正有锤击木工之类活计，得到的回话却是：并无此事。我自己也曾屡屡听见，总是在屋中那一处无法企及的所在，带着同样单调的重音。其中有一桩怪事：每逢我妻子不堪其扰而出声呵斥——她惯常如此——喊一声"别吵了！"那敲击声便总会停息，或长或短地静上一阵。

===Original===
Of course none of these occurrences were ever mentioned in hearing of the children. They would have been, no doubt, like most children, greatly terrified had they heard anything of the matter, and known that their elders were unable to account for what was passing; and their fears would have made them wretched and troublesome.

They used to play for some hours every day in the back garden—the house forming one end of this oblong enclosure, the stable and coach-house the other, and two parallel walls of considerable height the sides. Here, as it afforded a perfectly safe playground, they were frequently left quite to themselves; and in talking over their days' adventures, as children will, they happened to mention a woman, or rather the woman, for they had long grown familiar with her appearance, whom they used to see in the garden while they were at play. They assumed that she came in and went out at the stable door, but they never actually saw her enter or depart. They merely saw a figure—that of a very poor woman, soiled and ragged—near the stable wall, stooping over the ground, and apparently grubbing in the loose clay in search of something. She did not disturb, or appear to observe them; and they left her in undisturbed possession of her nook of ground. When seen it was always in the same spot, and similarly occupied; and the description they gave of her general appearance—for they never saw her face—corresponded with that of the one-eyed woman whom Smith, and subsequently as it seemed, I had seen.

===Chinese===
当然，这些事从未在孩子们听得到的地方提起过。孩子们大抵都一样，倘若他们听了什么风声，又知道长辈对这些怪事也说不清所以然，必定会吓得不轻；而一旦害怕起来，便既可怜又难缠。

孩子们每天都要在后花园里玩耍几个钟头——这处长方形围地的两端，一端是正屋，另一端是马厩和车房，两侧则是两堵相当高的平行院墙。这里是个十足安全的玩耍之地，他们常被独自留在那里；孩子们嘛，总会把白日的见闻絮絮叨叨讲出来，说着说着，便提到了一个女人——或者不如说"那个"女人，因为他们对她那副模样早已见惯不惊了——他们玩耍时常在花园里见到她。他们想当然地以为她从马厩那扇门进出，却从未真正看见她进门或离去。他们所见的只是一个身影——一个极穷酸的女人，衣衫肮脏褴褛——挨着马厩的墙根，俯身在地下，像是在松土里刨挖、翻找什么东西。她不打扰他们，也似不曾留意他们；孩子们也由她安宁地占据着那一角地皮。她每次被瞧见，总在同一处地点，干同样的营生；孩子们对她总体模样所作的描述——因为他们始终没见过她的脸——恰与史密斯所见、其后似乎又为我所见的那个独眼妇人相吻合。

===Original===
The other man, James, who looked after a mare which I had purchased for the purpose of riding exercise, had, like everyone else in the house, his little trouble to report, though it was not much. The stall in which, as the most comfortable, it was decided to place her, she peremptorily declined to enter. Though a very docile and gentle little animal, there was no getting her into it. She would snort and rear, and, in fact, do or suffer anything rather than set her hoof in it. He was fain, therefore, to place her in another. And on several occasions he found her there, exhibiting all the equine symptoms of extreme fear. Like the rest of us, however, this man was not troubled in the particular case with any superstitious qualms. The mare had evidently been frightened; and he was puzzled to find out how, or by whom, for the stable was well-secured, and had, I am nearly certain, a lockup yard outside.

One morning I was greeted with the intelligence that robbers had certainly got into the house in the night; and that one of them had actually been seen in the nursery. The witness, I found, was my eldest child, then, as I have said, about nine years of age. Having awoke in the night, and lain awake for some time in her bed, she heard the handle of the door turn, and a person whom she distinctly saw—for it was a light night, and the window-shutters unclosed—but whom she had never seen before, stepped in on tiptoe, and with an appearance of great caution. He was a rather small man, with a very red face; he wore an oddly cut frock coat, the collar of which stood up, and trousers, rough and wide, like those of a sailor, turned up at the ankles, and either short boots or clumsy shoes, covered with mud. This man listened beside the nurse's bed, which stood next the door, as if to satisfy himself that she was sleeping soundly; and having done so for some seconds, he began to move cautiously in a diagonal line, across the room to the chimneypiece, where he stood for a while, and so resumed his tiptoe walk, skirting the wall, until he reached a chest of drawers, some of which were open, and into which he looked, and began to rummage in a hurried way, as the child supposed, making search for something worth taking away. He then passed on to the window, where was a dressing-table, at which he also stopped, turning over the things upon it, and standing for some time at the window as if looking out, and then resuming his walk by the side wall opposite to that by which he had moved up to the window, he returned in the same way toward the nurse's bed, so as to reach it at the foot. With its side to the end wall, in which was the door, was placed the little bed in which lay my eldest child, who watched his proceedings with the extremest terror. As he drew near she instinctively moved herself in the bed, with her head and shoulders to the wall, drawing up her feet; but he passed by without appearing to observe, or, at least, to care for her presence. Immediately after the nurse turned in her bed as if about to waken; and when the child, who had drawn the clothes about her head, again ventured to peep out, the man was gone.

===Chinese===
另一个男仆詹姆斯，照管着我为骑行锻炼而买的一匹母马；他与屋里每一个人一样，也有自己的一桩小烦恼要禀报，虽然事情不大。本来打算把母马关进最舒适的那间马厩，她却断然不肯进去。这小牲口虽极驯良温顺，却怎么也弄不进那间厩。她又是喷鼻又是扬蹄，宁可受任何罪、遭任何苦，也不肯把蹄子踏进去半步。他无可奈何，只好把她安置到另一间。有几次他发现她待在那间厩里，浑身上下尽是一匹马惊恐至极的种种模样。不过此人也和我们其余人一样，在这事上并未受什么迷信疑虑的搅扰。母马分明受了惊；至于怎么受的惊、被谁所惊，他百思不得其解，因为马厩防护周全，而且——我几乎可以肯定——外面还有一道能上锁的院落。

一天清晨，便有人来报：夜里窃贼定然钻进了屋子；其中一个竟被人亲眼在育儿室里撞见。我细问之下，得知目击者是我的长女，即前文所说，那时约莫九岁。她夜里醒来，在床上醒着躺了一阵，听见门把手一转，便有一个人踮着脚、神色极尽小心地走了进来——那夜月色明亮，窗板未合，她看得一清二楚——可这人她从未见过。此人身材偏矮，脸膛极红；身穿一件剪裁古怪的长礼服，领子立着；下身一条粗而宽的裤子，形如水手所穿，裤脚卷起至踝；脚上蹬着短靴或笨重的鞋，沾满泥污。这人贴着保姆的床——那张床就靠着门——侧耳倾听了一阵，似要确认保姆睡得正熟；如此听了数秒，便开始小心翼翼地斜穿过房间，走到壁炉架前，在那儿站了一会儿，又踮起脚沿墙而行，直到一只五斗橱前——橱中有几格敞着——他朝里张望，便急急忙忙地翻找起来，孩子心想，他是在搜寻什么值得带走的东西。接着他走到窗前，那里有一张梳妆台，他也停了下来，把台上的物件翻来翻去，又在窗前站了好一阵，像是在朝外张望；然后他沿着与方才相反的那面侧墙重新走动起来，照原路折回保姆的床边，走到床脚处。靠门那端的山墙边，侧放着一张小床，我的长女便躺在其中，怀着极度的恐惧注视着他的一举一动。待他走近，她本能地在床上挪动，把头和肩膀贴向墙壁，蜷起双脚；可他从旁走过，似不曾察觉、至少是不曾理会她的存在。紧接着保姆在床上翻了个身，像是要醒；待孩子——她已把被褥蒙在头上——再大着胆子探头偷看时，那人已经不见了。

===Original===
The child had no idea of her having seen anything more formidable than a thief. With the prowling, cautious, and noiseless manner of proceeding common to such marauders, the air and movements of the man whom she had seen entirely corresponded. And on hearing her perfectly distinct and consistent account, I could myself arrive at no other conclusion than that a stranger had actually got into the house. I had, therefore, in the first instance, a most careful examination made to discover any traces of an entrance having been made by any window into the house. The doors had been found barred and locked as usual; but no sign of anything of the sort was discernible. I then had the various articles—plate, wearing apparel, books, etc., counted; and after having conned over and reckoned up everything, it became quite clear that nothing whatever had been removed from the house, nor was there the slightest indication of anything having been so much as disturbed there. I must here state that this child was remarkably clear, intelligent, and observant; and that her description of the man, and of all that had occurred, was most exact, and as detailed as the want of perfect light rendered possible.

I felt assured that an entry had actually been effected into the house, though for what purpose was not easily to be conjectured. The man, Smith, was equally confident upon this point; and his theory was that the object was simply to frighten us out of the house by making us believe it haunted; and he was more than ever anxious and on the alert to discover the conspirators. It often since appeared to me odd. Every year, indeed, more odd, as this cumulative case of the marvellous becomes to my mind more and more inexplicable—that underlying my sense of mystery and puzzle, was all along the quiet assumption that all these occurrences were one way or another referable to natural causes. I could not account for them, indeed, myself; but during the whole period I inhabited that house, I never once felt, though much alone, and often up very late at night, any of those tremors and thrills which everyone has at times experienced when situation and the hour are favourable. Except the cook and housemaid, who were plagued with the shadow I mentioned crossing and recrossing upon the bedroom wall, we all, without exception, experienced the same strange sense of security, and regarded these phenomena rather with a perplexed sort of interest and curiosity, than with any more unpleasant sensations.

===Chinese===
孩子做梦也没想过自己见到的会是什么比窃贼更可怕的东西。她所见那人的做派举止，与这类梁上君子潜行、谨慎、无声无息的惯伎，全然相符。听了她条理分明、前后一致的说法，我自己也得不出别的结论，只能断定：确有外人潜入了此宅。于是我首先命人作了一番极其仔细的勘查，要查出是否有哪扇窗子留下了被人闯入的痕迹。各处门户都如常闩好锁好；却丝毫看不出此类迹象。我又命人把各样物件——银器、衣物、书籍等等——逐一清点；逐件过目、逐一核算之后，已十分清楚：屋里没有一件东西被带走，甚至连被翻动过的蛛丝马迹也寻不到。在此我须说明：这孩子心智异常清晰伶俐，观察入微；她对人、对所发生之事的描述，极其精确，在光线不足的情形下已详尽到了无以复加的地步。

我确信确有人闯入了此宅，只是其目的殊难揣测。仆人史密斯在这一桩上与我同样笃定；他的揣测是：对方的目的不过是装神弄鬼，使我们相信此宅有鬼，从而把我们吓走；他愈发焦急、愈发警惕地想要揪出这伙同谋。此后我常常觉得此事古怪。事实上，一年比一年更觉古怪——这桩离奇之事愈积愈多、在我心中愈发不可解——在我那种种神秘难解的感觉之下，始终潜藏着一个安然的假定：这一切，总可以归之于自然的原因。我固然自己也说不清究竟；可是在我居住此宅的全部时日里，尽管常常独处、又常常深夜不眠，我却从未有过那种人人偶尔会有的颤栗寒噤——每逢境遇与时辰相宜，那种感觉便会袭来。除了厨娘和女仆——她们被我所言那道在卧室墙上来回游移的影子搅扰不已——我们众人无一例外，都怀着同样一种奇异的安然之感；与其说怀着什么不快的情绪，倒不如说带着几分困惑的好奇与兴味在打量这些异象。

===Original===
The knockings which I have mentioned at the nursery door, preceded generally by the sound of a step on the lobby, meanwhile continued. At that time (for my wife, like myself, was an invalid) two eminent physicians, who came out occasionally by rail, were attending us. These gentlemen were at first only amused, but ultimately interested, and very much puzzled by the occurrences which we described. One of them, at last, recommended that a candle should be kept burning upon the lobby. It was in fact a recurrence to an old woman's recipe against ghosts—of course it might be serviceable, too, against impostors; at all events, seeming, as I have said, very much interested and puzzled, he advised it, and it was tried. We fancied that it was successful; for there was an interval of quiet for, I think, three or four nights. But after that, the noises—the footsteps on the lobby—the knocking at the door, and the turning of the handle recommenced in full force, notwithstanding the light upon the table outside; and these particular phenomena became only more perplexing than ever.

The alarm of robbers and smugglers gradually subsided after a week or two; but we were again to hear news from the nursery. Our second little girl, then between seven and eight years of age, saw in the night time—she alone being awake—a young woman, with black, or very dark hair, which hung loose, and with a black cloak on, standing near the middle of the floor, opposite the hearthstone, and fronting the foot of her bed. She appeared quite unobservant of the children and nurse sleeping in the room. She was very pale, and looked, the child said, both "sorry and frightened," and with something very peculiar and terrible about her eyes, which made the child conclude that she was dead. She was looking, not at, but in the direction of the child's bed, and there was a dark streak across her throat, like a scar with blood upon it. This figure was not motionless; but once or twice turned slowly, and without appearing to be conscious of the presence of the child, or the other occupants of the room, like a person in vacancy or abstraction. There was on this occasion a night-light burning in the chamber; and the child saw, or thought she saw, all these particulars with the most perfect distinctness. She got her head under the bedclothes; and although a good many years have passed since then, she cannot recall the spectacle without feelings of peculiar horror.

===Chinese===
我曾提及育儿室门外的那种敲门声，通常先有一阵脚步声在过厅响起，这时仍不绝如缕。那时（因我妻子与我一样也是病体）有两位名医时常乘火车前来为我们诊治。这两位先生起初只觉好笑，后来渐生出兴趣，终而被我们所描述的种种怪事难住了。其中一位终于建议：在过厅里点一支长明蜡烛。这其实是重拾了一条老太太驱鬼的老法子——当然，对付冒名行骗之徒或许同样管用；无论如何，他既如我所说那般大感兴趣、大惑不解，便作了此议，我们也就照办。我们一度以为奏了效：足足安静了，我记得，有三四个夜晚。可那之后，种种响动——过厅里的脚步声、敲门声、拧动门把手的声音——又照旧猖獗起来，全不顾门外桌上那点烛光；而这桩桩异象，愈发叫人摸不着头脑了。

窃贼与走私客的恐慌，过了一两周便渐渐平息；可我们很快又要从育儿室听到新的消息。我的二女儿，那时在七八岁之间，夜里——唯有她一人醒着——看见一个年轻女子，一头乌黑、或极深色的头发披散着，身披一件黑色斗篷，立在房间正中、壁炉石板对面，正对着她的床脚。她似全然不曾察觉屋里熟睡的孩子和保姆。她面色极其苍白，神情——据孩子说——"又悲又怕"，眼中更有一种说不出的特别而可怖的东西，使孩子断定她已经死了。她并非在看着孩子的床，而是朝床的方向望着；她喉间横着一道暗色痕，像一道渗着血的伤疤。这身影并非纹丝不动：她曾有一两次缓缓转过身去，似乎毫未察觉屋中有孩子或其他人在，那模样，像是一个神魂出窍、心不在焉的人。这一回，屋里点着一盏夜灯；孩子看见——或自以为看见——上述种种细节，清晰至极。她把头钻进了被窝；虽则此后已过了许多年，她每每回想此景，仍觉一种异乎寻常的恐怖。

===Original===
One day, when the children were playing in the back garden, I asked them to point out to me the spot where they were accustomed to see the woman who occasionally showed herself as I have described, near the stable wall. There was no division of opinion as to this precise point, which they indicated in the most distinct and confident way. I suggested that, perhaps, something might be hidden there in the ground; and advised them digging a hole there with their little spades, to try for it. Accordingly, to work they went, and by my return in the evening they had grubbed up a piece of a jawbone, with several teeth in it. The bone was very much decayed, and ready to crumble to pieces, but the teeth were quite sound. I could not tell whether they were human grinders; but I showed the fossil to one of the physicians I have mentioned, who came out the next evening, and he pronounced them human teeth. The same conclusion was come to a day or two later by the other medical man. It appears to me now, on reviewing the whole matter, almost unaccountable that, with such evidence before me, I should not have got in a labourer, and had the spot effectually dug and searched. I can only say, that so it was. I was quite satisfied of the moral truth of every word that had been related to me, and which I have here set down with scrupulous accuracy. But I experienced an apathy, for which neither then nor afterwards did I quite know how to account. I had a vague, but immovable impression that the whole affair was referable to natural agencies. It was not until some time after we had left the house, which, by the by, we afterwards found had had the reputation of being haunted before we had come to live in it, that on reconsideration I discovered the serious difficulty of accounting satisfactorily for all that had occurred upon ordinary principles. A great deal we might arbitrarily set down to imagination. But even in so doing there was, *in limine*, the oddity, not to say improbability, of so many different persons having nearly simultaneously suffered from different spectral and other illusions during the short period for which we had occupied that house, who never before, nor so far as we learned, afterwards were troubled by any fears or fancies of the sort. There were other things, too, not to be so accounted for. The odd knockings in the roof I frequently heard myself.

===Chinese===
一日，孩子们正在后花园玩耍，我要他们指给我看，那偶尔如前文所述现身的女人，惯常在马厩墙根何处被人瞧见。这一确切地点，孩子们毫无异议，指得极其分明笃定。我提议：说不定地底下埋着什么东西；便劝他们拿小铲子在那里挖个坑，试试看。于是他们动起手来，等我傍晚归家时，他们已刨出了一块颚骨，上头还连着几颗牙齿。骨头已朽得厉害，行将碎裂，牙齿却完好无损。我辨不出这些是不是人的臼齿；但我把这块"化石"拿给前文提到的那位医生看——他次日傍晚前来——他断定是人的牙齿。一两日之后，另一位医生也得出了同样的结论。今日回顾全案，有一桩几乎不可思议之处：既有这样的证据摆在眼前，我竟没有雇个劳力，把那处地面彻底掘开搜查一番。我只能如实相告：事情就是这样。我对所闻、并在此一丝不苟记录下来的每一句话，其所述皆为真实的诚信，毫不怀疑。可我当时却生出一种冷漠懈怠之心，其缘由我彼时不懂，事后也始终不甚了了。我有一种模糊却不可动摇的印象：整件事总可归之于自然的缘由。直到我们离开此宅之后一段时间——顺带一提，我们后来才得知，此宅在我们入住之前便已有闹鬼之名——再行回想，我才发觉：欲以寻常道理圆满地解释所发生的一切，实有重重困难。其中大半，我们尽可武断地推给"想象"二字。可即便如此，篇首便有一桩奇处——莫如说是一桩不可能之事：如此众多的人，各不相同，在我们居住此宅的那短短一段时日里，竟几乎同时为种种不同的鬼影及其他幻象所扰；而他们此前从未、据我们所知此后也从未受过任何同类恐惧或妄想的纠缠。此外还有些事，也不能如此搪塞。屋顶之中那古怪的敲击声，我便曾亲耳屡屡听见。

===Original===
There were also, which I before forgot to mention, in the daytime, rappings at the doors of the sitting-rooms, which constantly deceived us; and it was not till our "come in" was unanswered, and the hall or passage outside the door was discovered to be empty, that we learned that whatever else caused them, human hands did not. All the persons who reported having seen the different persons or appearances here described by me, were just as confident of having literally and distinctly seen them, as I was of having seen the hard-featured woman with the blind eye, so remarkably corresponding with Smith's description.

About a week after the discovery of the teeth, which were found, I think, about two feet under the ground, a friend, much advanced in years, and who remembered the town in which we had now taken up our abode, for a very long time, happened to pay us a visit. He good-humouredly pooh-poohed the whole thing; but at the same time was evidently curious about it. "We might construct a sort of story," said I (I am giving, of course, the substance and purport, not the exact words, of our dialogue), "and assign to each of the three figures who appeared their respective parts in some dreadful tragedy enacted in this house. The male figure represents the murderer; the ill-looking, one-eyed woman his accomplice, who, we will suppose, buried the body where she is now so often seen grubbing in the earth, and where the human teeth and jawbone have so lately been disinterred; and the young woman with dishevelled tresses, and black cloak, and the bloody scar across her throat, their victim. A difficulty, however, which I cannot get over, exists in the cheerfulness, the great publicity, and the evident very recent date of the house." "Why, as to that," said he, "the house is *not* modern; it and those beside it formed an old government store, altered and fitted up recently as you see. I remember it well in my young days, fifty years ago, before the town had grown out in this direction, and a more entirely lonely spot, or one more fitted for the commission of a secret crime, could not have been imagined."

===Chinese===
此外还有一事，我先前忘了提及：白天，起居室的门上常常响起叩门声，屡屡将我们骗了；直到我们应了一声"进来"，却无人答话，开门一看，门外的厅堂或过道空无一人，我们这才明白：其起因不论为何，断非人手所为。所有禀报曾看见我所记述的各色人物或形影的人，都和我一样笃定：他们确确实实、清清楚楚地看见了，正如我看见那个面目刻薄、瞎了一只眼、与史密斯所述惊人吻合的妇人一样笃定。

发现牙齿之后约一周——那些牙齿，我记得是在地下约两英尺处挖出的——一位年事已高的老友前来探访，他记得我们如今安身的这座城镇，记得的时日可谓久远。他好脾气地把这事一股脑儿嗤之以鼻；但同时分明又满怀好奇。"我们大可编出一则故事来，"我说（此处所引，自是我们对话的大意与要旨，而非一字不差的原话），"给现身的这三个身影，各自分派在这宅子里上演的某出骇人悲剧中所应承担的角色。那个男影，是凶手；那个面目可憎的独眼妇人是他的同谋，我们不妨假定，是她把尸首埋在了她如今屡屡被人瞧见刨土翻寻、并新近掘出人牙与颚骨之处；而那个披发、身着黑色斗篷、喉间横着一道血痕的年轻女子，则是他俩的受害人。不过，有一层难处我无法逾越：这宅子如此明快、如此地处显要、又显然如此之新。" "嘿，说到这个，"他答道，"这宅子可并不新；它和它两旁那些房子，本是一座旧时的官家仓库，近来才如你所见这般改建装修的。我少时——五十年前——对它记忆犹新；那时这座城还未向这个方向扩展，再没有比这更偏僻冷清的地方了，再没有比这更宜于暗行凶险之事的所在了。"

===Original===
I have nothing to add, for very soon after this my physician pronounced a longer stay unnecessary for my health, and we took our departure for another place of abode. I may add, that although I have resided for considerable periods in many other houses, I never experienced any annoyances of a similar kind elsewhere; neither have I made (stupid dog! you will say), any inquiries respecting either the antecedents or subsequent history of the house in which we made so disturbed a sojourn. I was content with what I knew, and have here related as clearly as I could, and I think it a very pretty puzzle as it stands.

---

[Thus ends the statement, which we abandon to the ingenuity of our readers, having ourselves no satisfactory explanation to suggest; and simply repeating the assurance with which we prefaced it, namely, that we can vouch for the perfect good faith and the accuracy of the narrator.—Editor, Dublin University Magazine.]

===Chinese===
此外我无可补充，因为此后不久，我的医生便判定，于我身体而言，无须再久留，我们便启程迁往他处了。我还可以补一句：尽管此后我在许多别的宅子里都住过相当长的时日，却再未在别处遭遇过类似的烦扰；我也未曾（您必会说：真是一条蠢狗！）——未曾对我们那段不得安宁的栖身之所，就其过往来历或日后情形，作过任何查访。我所知者不过如此，已竭尽所能据实陈述于此；我觉得，此事之全貌，作为一桩绝妙的谜题，已然足矣。

---

［陈述至此告终。我们将其交付于读者的巧思，自己提不出任何圆满的解释；唯再郑重申明篇首所作的保证：我们可以担保，讲述者用心之至诚、记述之精准，皆无可置疑。——《都柏林大学杂志》（Dublin University Magazine）主编谨识。］

## Passage in the Secret History of an Irish Countess / 一位爱尔兰伯爵夫人的秘史轶闻

Being a Fifth Extract from the Legacy of the Late Francis Purcell, P.P. of Drumcoolagh. / 已故德鲁姆库拉（Drumcoolagh）教区神父（P.P.）弗朗西斯·珀塞尔（Francis Purcell）遗稿之第五则摘录。

===Original===
The following paper is written in a female hand, and was no doubt communicated to my much-regretted friend by the lady whose early history it serves to illustrate, the Countess D——. She is no more—she long since died, a childless and a widowed wife, and, as her letter sadly predicts, none survive to whom the publication of this narrative can prove "injurious, or even painful." Strange! two powerful and wealthy families, that in which she was born, and that into which she had married, have ceased to be—they are utterly extinct.

To those who know anything of the history of Irish families, as they were less than a century ago, the facts which immediately follow will at once suggest *the names* of the principal actors; and to others their publication would be useless—to us, possibly, if not probably, injurious. I have, therefore, altered such of the names as might, if stated, get us into difficulty; others, belonging to minor characters in the strange story, I have left untouched.

===Chinese===
下面这份文稿出自女子手笔，无疑是由它所记述的早年经历的那位女主人公——即 D——伯爵夫人（the Countess D——）——亲手交给我那位令人深切怀念的故友的。斯人已逝——她早已离世，膝下无儿无女，又做了寡妇；而正如她在信中凄然预言的那样，这桩往事的公之于世，已不会给在世的任何人带来"伤害，甚或痛苦"。说来可叹！两个煊赫而富甲一方的家族——她所生于其中的那一个，与她所嫁入的那一个——如今俱已灰飞烟灭——彻底断绝了。

凡略知不及百年前爱尔兰诸世家掌故的人，读到紧接着叙述的那桩桩事实，自能一眼猜出*主要当事人的名姓*；而对其他人，公布这些姓氏也毫无用处——对我等而言，则不无——甚且相当可能——招致祸患。因此，凡一旦写明便可能给吾辈惹来麻烦的姓名，我均已更改；至于这桩离奇故事中若干次要人物的名字，则一仍其旧，未加改动。

---

My dear friend— / 亲爱的朋友——

===Original===
You have asked me to furnish you with a detail of the strange events which marked my early history, and I have, without hesitation, applied myself to the task, knowing that, while I live, a kind consideration for my feelings will prevent your giving publicity to the statement; and conscious that, when I am no more, there will not survive one to whom the narrative can prove injurious, or even painful.

===Chinese===
你曾要我细述我早年那段离奇经历，我已毫不犹豫地着手此事；因为我知道，只要我尚在人世，你出于对我的体贴，绝不会将这番陈述公之于众；我也深知，待我辞世之后，再不会有哪个人会因为这段往事的流传而受到伤害，甚至感到痛苦。

===Original===
My mother died when I was quite an infant, and of her I have no recollection, even the faintest. By her death, my education and habits were left solely to the guidance of my surviving parent; and, as far as a stern attention to my religious instruction, and an active anxiety evinced by his procuring for me the best masters to perfect me in those accomplishments which my station and wealth might seem to require, could avail, he amply discharged the task.

My father was what is called an oddity, and his treatment of me, though uniformly kind, flowed less from affection and tenderness than from a sense of obligation and duty. Indeed, I seldom even spoke to him except at mealtimes, and then his manner was silent and abrupt; his leisure hours, which were many, were passed either in his study or in solitary walks; in short, he seemed to take no further interest in my happiness or improvement than a conscientious regard to the discharge of his own duty would seem to claim.

===Chinese===
母亲在我尚在襁褓之时便已去世，对于她，我连最模糊的记忆也没有。她一死，我的教养与习惯便全然交由我那尚在人世的父亲一手掌管了；就他那份对我宗教教诲的严正关切，以及为使我精通与我身份家财相称的种种才艺而四处延请良师的那番上心而言，这差使他算是尽得相当周全了。

父亲是世人所谓的"怪人"；他待我，虽始终不失和善，却更多出于一种义务与本分之感，而非出自亲情与疼爱。说实话，除了吃饭的时候，我几乎难得与他交谈，而即便在饭桌上，他的举止也是沉默而生硬的；他那许多闲暇光阴，不是消磨在书房里，便是在独自散步中度过；总之，对于我的快乐与长进，除了良心上对本分的考量所要求的那一点之外，他似乎再无别的兴致。

===Original===
Shortly before my birth a circumstance had occurred which had contributed much to form and to confirm my father's secluded habits—it was the fact that a suspicion of *murder* had fallen upon his younger brother, though not sufficiently definite to lead to an indictment, yet strong enough to ruin him in public opinion.

This disgraceful and dreadful doubt cast upon the family name, my father felt deeply and bitterly, and not the less so that he himself was thoroughly convinced of his brother's innocence. The sincerity and strength of this impression he shortly afterwards proved in a manner which produced the dark events which follow. Before, however, I enter upon the statement of them, I ought to relate the circumstances which had awakened the suspicion; inasmuch as they are in themselves somewhat curious, and, in their effects, most intimately connected with my after-history.

===Chinese===
在我出生前不久，发生了一桩事，对我父亲那闭门索居的性子之养成与加固，颇有推波助澜之效——那便是：一桩*谋杀*的嫌疑落在了他弟弟头上；这嫌疑虽尚不够确凿到足以提起公诉的地步，却已足以使其在众人口中身败名裂。

这一可耻而又可怕的疑云蒙在家族姓氏之上，父亲痛感切肤、苦楚难当；而尤其令他难堪的是，他自己偏偏坚信弟弟是清白的。不久之后，他便以一种方式印证了自己这份信念的真诚与坚定——而正是这一印证，引出了下文那一连串阴森可怕的事件。然而，在我着手陈述这些事件之前，理应先将那唤起嫌疑的种种情由交代一番；因为那些情由本身已颇为离奇，而其后果，又与我此后的一生有着千丝万缕的关联。

===Original===
My uncle, Sir Arthur T——n, was a gay and extravagant man, and, among other vices, was ruinously addicted to gaming; this unfortunate propensity, even after his fortune had suffered so severely as to render inevitable a reduction in his expenses by no means inconsiderable, nevertheless continued to actuate him, nearly to the exclusion of all other pursuits; he was, however, a proud, or rather a vain man, and could not bear to make the diminution of his income a matter of gratulation and triumph to those with whom he had hitherto competed, and the consequence was, that he frequented no longer the expensive haunts of dissipation, and retired from the gay world, leaving his coterie to discover his reasons as best they might.

He did not, however, forego his favourite vice, for, though he could not worship his great divinity in the costly temples where it was formerly his wont to take his stand, yet he found it very possible to bring about him a sufficient number of the votaries of chance to answer all his ends. The consequence was, that Carrickleigh, which was the name of my uncle's residence, was never without one or more of such visitors as I have described.

===Chinese===
我的叔父阿瑟·T——n 爵士（Sir Arthur T——n）是个风流浮华、挥霍无度的人，诸般恶癖之中，又以赌之一道为害最烈，几乎将他拖入倾家荡产的境地；即便他的家财早已大伤元气，以至非得将开支削减一笔不小的数目不可，这要命的癖好却仍如附骨之疽，驱之不散，几乎排除了他一切旁的营生；所幸他这人好面子——或者说得更近些，是个虚荣之人——实在不忍见自己进项的短绌，反成了那些昔日与他争豪斗富之辈额手称庆、引为快事的由头；于是他再也不踏足那些一掷千金的花柳繁华之地，就此退出了交际场，由着他那一班圈中人去自行揣测其中缘故。

然而他并未戒除那心爱的恶癖；虽说再不能在他从前惯常驻足的奢华殿堂里供奉他那位大神，可要把足够多的赌徒招到身边来以遂其愿，倒也并非难事。其结果是，卡里克利（Carrickleigh）——这便是我叔父宅邸之名——家中宾客络绎不绝，前文所述那类访客，从不曾缺过一位两位。

===Original===
It happened that upon one occasion he was visited by one Hugh Tisdall, a gentleman of loose habits, but of considerable wealth, and who had, in early youth, travelled with my uncle upon the Continent; the period of his visit was winter, and, consequently, the house was nearly deserted excepting by its regular inmates; it was therefore highly acceptable, particularly as my uncle was aware that his visitor's tastes accorded exactly with his own.

Both parties seemed determined to avail themselves of their suitability during the brief stay which Mr. Tisdall had promised; the consequence was, that they shut themselves up in Sir Arthur's private room for nearly all the day and the greater part of the night, during the space of nearly a week, at the end of which the servant having one morning, as usual, knocked at Mr. Tisdall's bedroom door repeatedly, received no answer, and, upon attempting to enter, found that it was locked; this appeared suspicious, and, the inmates of the house having been alarmed, the door was forced open, and, on proceeding to the bed, they found the body of its occupant perfectly lifeless, and hanging halfway out, the head downwards, and near the floor. One deep wound had been inflicted upon the temple, apparently with some blunt instrument which had penetrated the brain; and another blow, less effective, probably the first aimed, had grazed the head, removing some of the scalp, but leaving the skull untouched. The door had been double-locked upon the *inside*, in evidence of which the key still lay where it had been placed in the lock.

===Chinese===
话说有那么一回，一位名叫休·蒂斯德尔（Hugh Tisdall）的绅士前来造访——此人行止虽放浪，家产却颇为殷实，年少时还曾与叔父同游欧陆；他来访时正值隆冬，府中除了常住的家人仆从之外，几乎是门庭冷落；故而这桩造访颇受欢迎，何况叔父深知这位客人的口味与自己正是一拍即合。

看样子双方都打定主意，要在蒂斯德尔先生应允小住的短短几天里，将彼此这份臭味相投发挥到极致；其结果便是：一连将近一周，他们几乎整日整夜地将自己关在阿瑟爵士的私室之内。到了这一周尽头，一日清晨，仆人照例去敲蒂斯德尔先生卧室的房门，敲了又敲，无人应答；待要推门进去，却发现门已反锁；此情此景，颇为可疑，府中人闻讯都惊动起来，门被强行撞开，众人走到床边一看，只见床上那人早已气息全无，半个身子悬在床外，头朝下，几乎垂到了地板。太阳穴上有一处深创，显系被某种钝器击中所致，那钝器直透脑中；另有一击，力道稍弱，大约是最先挥出的那一击，只擦破了头皮，削去了一片头发，却未伤及头骨。房门是从*里侧*双重上锁的——钥匙仍插在锁孔原处，便是明证。

===Original===
The window, though not secured on the interior, was closed—a circumstance not a little puzzling, as it afforded the only other mode of escape from the room; it looked out, too, upon a kind of courtyard, round which the old buildings stood, formerly accessible by a narrow doorway and passage lying in the oldest side of the quadrangle, but which had since been built up, so as to preclude all ingress or egress; the room was also upon the second story, and the height of the window considerable. Near the bed were found a pair of razors belonging to the murdered man, one of them upon the ground, and both of them open. The weapon which had inflicted the mortal wound was not to be found in the room, nor were any footsteps or other traces of the murderer discoverable.

At the suggestion of Sir Arthur himself, a coroner was instantly summoned to attend, and an inquest was held; nothing, however, in any degree conclusive was elicited; the walls, ceiling, and floor of the room were carefully examined, in order to ascertain whether they contained a trapdoor or other concealed mode of entrance—but no such thing appeared.

===Chinese===
那扇窗，虽说里头并未加闩，却是关着的——这一情形着实令人费解，因为窗子乃是这间屋子除房门之外唯一的出路；窗外正对着一方天井似的庭院，老宅子的四围屋舍便环着它而立，从前原有一道窄门和一条过道与庭院相通，位于这四合院最古老的那一面，但后来早已被砖石封死，任谁也进不去、出不来；何况这间屋子又是在二楼，窗子离地甚高。床头附近发现了死者的一副剃刀，一把落在地上，两把都已打开。那件造成致命伤的凶器，在屋里却遍寻不见；至于凶手的脚印或任何别的踪迹，更是无从查考。

应阿瑟爵士本人之请，验尸官即刻被传到场，死因研讯也随之举行；然而审来审去，竟无半点确凿的结论可寻；屋子的墙壁、天花板、地板，俱经一一细勘，欲查明其中是否藏有暗门或别的什么隐秘入口——却终无所获。

===Original===
Such was the minuteness of investigation employed, that, although the grate had contained a large fire during the night, they proceeded to examine even the very chimney, in order to discover whether escape by it were possible; but this attempt, too, was fruitless, for the chimney, built in the old fashion, rose in a perfectly perpendicular line from the hearth to a height of nearly fourteen feet above the roof, affording in its interior scarcely the possibility of ascent, the flue being smoothly plastered, and sloping towards the top like an inverted funnel, promising, too, even if the summit were attained, owing to its great height, but a precarious descent upon the sharp and steep-ridged roof; the ashes, too, which lay in the grate, and the soot, as far as it could be seen, were undisturbed, a circumstance almost conclusive of the question.

Sir Arthur was of course examined; his evidence was given with clearness and unreserve, which seemed calculated to silence all suspicion. He stated that, up to the day and night immediately preceding the catastrophe, he had lost to a heavy amount, but that, at their last sitting, he had not only won back his original loss, but upwards of four thousand pounds in addition; in evidence of which he produced an acknowledgment of debt to that amount in the handwriting of the deceased, and bearing the date of the fatal night. He had mentioned the circumstance to his lady, and in presence of some of the domestics; which statement was supported by *their* respective evidence.

===Chinese===
查得之细，竟至如此地步：虽说壁炉里夜间曾烧着旺火，他们仍旧把烟囱也细细勘验了一番，要看看能否由此逃脱；然而这一番工夫也属徒劳——那烟囱是老式的，从炉床笔直地拔起，一直通出屋顶之上将近十四英尺之高，内里几乎无从攀援：烟道抹得溜光，越往上越往里收，活像一只倒置的漏斗；退一步说，纵使当真攀到了顶，凭它那般高度，要落到那棱角分明、陡峭如削的屋脊上，也不过是九死一生的勾当；况且炉栅里积着的灰烬，还有那目力所及之处的烟囱，都纹丝未动——这一节，几乎已将问题盖棺定论。

阿瑟爵士自然也受了讯问；他供述清楚坦荡，一副足以平息一切嫌疑的架势。据他陈述，直至那场惨剧发生的前一日与当夜为止，他本是输得极惨的；然而到了他们最后那一局，他不仅把先前输的全赢了回来，还倒赢了四千多镑；为作佐证，他出示了一张那一数目的欠据，正是死者的亲笔，所署日期便是那夺命之夜。他早已将此事告知夫人，且当着几个仆人的面提及；此一说，也各有*他们*的证词为凭。

===Original===
One of the jury shrewdly observed, that the circumstance of Mr. Tisdall's having sustained so heavy a loss might have suggested to some ill-minded persons accidentally hearing it, the plan of robbing him, after having murdered him in such a manner as might make it appear that he had committed suicide; a supposition which was strongly supported by the razors having been found thus displaced, and removed from their case. Two persons had probably been engaged in the attempt, one watching by the sleeping man, and ready to strike him in case of his awakening suddenly, while the other was procuring the razors and employed in inflicting the fatal gash, so as to make it appear to have been the act of the murdered man himself. It was said that while the juror was making this suggestion Sir Arthur changed colour.

Nothing, however, like legal evidence appeared against him, and the consequence was that the verdict was found against a person or persons unknown; and for some time the matter was suffered to rest, until, after about five months, my father received a letter from a person signing himself Andrew Collis, and representing himself to be the cousin of the deceased. This letter stated that Sir Arthur was likely to incur not merely suspicion, but personal risk, unless he could account for certain circumstances connected with the recent murder, and contained a copy of a letter written by the deceased, and bearing date, the day of the week, and of the month, upon the night of which the deed of blood had been perpetrated. Tisdall's note ran as follows:

===Chinese===
陪审团中有一人颇为精明，他指出：蒂斯德尔先生既输了偌大一笔款子，此事万一叫哪个心怀歹意之人偶然听去，未尝不会起意——先将他谋害，再布置成自尽模样，而后劫走他的财物；而剃刀被发现时挪了位置、又离了刀盒，正可为此一说添一力证。作案的，大约是两个人：一个在熟睡的人身旁守望，只待他猛然惊醒便即行凶；另一个则去取剃刀，下手施那致命一割，好叫一切看上去如同死者亲手所为。据说这位陪审员发表此议之时，阿瑟爵士面色骤变。

然而并无半点堪作法律证据的物事指到他头上，于是裁定的结果，便是罪责归于一不知名之人或数不知名之人；此事就此搁置了一阵。约莫五个月之后，我父亲收到一封信，署名安德鲁·科利斯（Andrew Collis），自称是死者的表亲。信中说，阿瑟爵士除非能将这桩新近命案的若干情由解释清楚，否则不仅难免嫌疑，恐还有人身的祸患；随信还附了一份死者亲笔书信的抄件，所署之年月日、星期，正与那血案发生之夜相合。蒂斯德尔的便函全文如下：

---

===Original===
> "Dear Collis,
> "I have had sharp work with Sir Arthur; he tried some of his stale tricks, but soon found that *I* was Yorkshire too: it would not do—you understand me. We went to the work like good ones, head, heart and soul; and, in fact, since I came here, I have lost no time. I am rather fagged, but I am sure to be well paid for my hardship; I never want sleep so long as I can have the music of a dice-box, and wherewithal to pay the piper. As I told you, he tried some of his queer turns, but I foiled him like a man, and, in return, gave him more than he could relish of the genuine *dead knowledge*.
> "In short, I have plucked the old baronet as never baronet was plucked before; I have scarce left him the stump of a quill; I have got promissory notes in his hand to the amount of—if you like round numbers, say, thirty thousand pounds, safely deposited in my portable strongbox, alias double-clasped pocketbook. I leave this ruinous old rat-hole early on tomorrow, for two reasons—first, I do not want to play with Sir Arthur deeper than I think his security, that is, his money, or his money's worth, would warrant; and, secondly, because I am safer a hundred miles from Sir Arthur than in the house with him. Look you, my worthy, I tell you this between ourselves—I may be wrong, but, by G——, I am as sure as that I am now living, that Sir A—— attempted to poison me last night; so much for old friendship on both sides.

===Chinese===
> "亲爱的科利斯：
> "我跟阿瑟爵士这一场厮杀，着实凶险；他使出了几招惯用的老把戏，可很快便发觉*我*也不是省油的灯：那一套行不通了——你懂我的意思。我俩如临大敌，一头扎进去，身、心、魂全豁了出去；说实在的，自打我到了这儿，分秒未曾虚掷。我颇为疲惫，可这点苦楚必定会有厚报；只要有骰盅叮当作响可供消遣，又有银钱付那奏乐之人的花销，我便不觉困倦。正如我曾告诉你的，他又试了几手怪招，却被我一一识破；我回敬他的，也尽是他消受不起的，货真价实的*夺命杀招*。
> "一句话，我把这老准男爵宰得之狠，只怕空前绝后；连一管秃笔头都几乎没给他剩下；他亲笔写下的本票，落在我手里的，总计——说个整数罢——三万镑之巨，已稳稳当当收进我这随身保险箱，又名双搭扣皮夹子之中。我明日一早便要离开这个破败的老鼠窝，原因有二：其一，我不想跟阿瑟爵士赌得太深——深到他那点担保——也即他的现钱或值钱家当——所无法支撑的地步；其二，是因为我离阿瑟爵士一百英里之远，比与他同处一室要安全得多。听好，老兄，这话只在你我之间讲讲——也许我看走了眼，可我对天起誓，就如我此刻活生生站在这儿一般确凿，昨夜阿爵士是要下毒害我的；两边的老交情，原来不过如此。

---

===Original===
> "When I won the last stake, a heavy one enough, my friend leant his forehead upon his hands, and you'll laugh when I tell you that his head literally smoked like a hot dumpling. I do not know whether his agitation was produced by the plan which he had against me, or by his having lost so heavily—though it must be allowed that he had reason to be a little funked, whichever way his thoughts went; but he pulled the bell, and ordered two bottles of champagne. While the fellow was bringing them he drew out a promissory note to the full amount, which he signed, and, as the man came in with the bottles and glasses, he desired him to be off; he filled out a glass for me, and, while he thought my eyes were off, for I was putting up his note at the time, he dropped something slyly into it, no doubt to sweeten it; but I saw it all, and, when he handed it to me, I said, with an emphasis which he might or might not understand:
> " 'There is some sediment in this; I'll not drink it.'
> " 'Is there?' said he, and at the same time snatched it from my hand and threw it into the fire. What do you think of that? have I not a tender chicken to manage? Win or lose, I will not play beyond five thousand tonight, and tomorrow sees me safe out of the reach of Sir Arthur's champagne. So, all things considered, I think you must allow that you are not the last who have found a knowing boy in
> "Yours to command,
> "Hugh Tisdall."

===Chinese===
> "我赢下最后一注时——那一注可不算小——我的这位朋友把额头抵在双手之上；说来你都要笑，他的脑袋瓜当真冒了烟，活像一只滚烫的肉馅饼。我说不准他这失态，是因为正在盘算着对付我的法子呢，还是因为输得太惨——不过平心而论，无论他心里转的是什么念头，都够他心惊肉跳一阵的了；可他拉了铃，叫了两瓶香槟。趁那仆人取酒的工夫，他抽出一张全额的本票，签了字，待那人端着瓶子和杯子进来，他便把人打发走了；他替我斟了一杯，趁他以为我视线移开的时候——那时我正收着他那张本票——悄悄往里头滴了点什么，无疑是为了给酒'添点甜头'；这一切我都看在眼里，待他把杯子递给我，我加重了语气——这语气他未必听得懂，也未必听不懂：
> " '这酒里有沉淀；我不喝。'
> " '是吗？'他说着，一把从我手中夺过杯子，扔进了火里。此一举，你以为如何？我手上这只嫩鸡，岂是寻常角色？输也好，赢也罢，今晚我再不下五千以上；明日，我便稳稳当当地脱出阿瑟爵士那香槟的射程。综上种种，我想你总该承认，你并非最后一个撞上行家的——
> "听候差遣的，
> "休·蒂斯德尔。"

===Original===
Of the authenticity of this document I never heard my father express a doubt; and I am satisfied that, owing to his strong conviction in favour of his brother, he would not have admitted it without sufficient inquiry, inasmuch as it tended to confirm the suspicions which already existed to his prejudice.

Now, the only point in this letter which made strongly against my uncle, was the mention of the "double-clasped pocketbook" as the receptacle of the papers likely to involve him, for this pocketbook was not forthcoming, nor anywhere to be found, nor had any papers referring to his gaming transactions been found upon the dead man. However, whatever might have been the original intention of this Collis, neither my uncle nor my father ever heard more of him; but he published the letter in Faulkner's newspaper, which was shortly afterwards made the vehicle of a much more mysterious attack. The passage in that periodical to which I allude, occurred about four years afterwards, and while the fatal occurrence was still fresh in public recollection. It commenced by a rambling preface, stating that "a *certain person* whom *certain* persons thought to be dead, was not so, but living, and in full possession of his memory, and moreover ready and able to make *great* delinquents tremble." It then went on to describe the murder, without, however, mentioning names; and in doing so, it entered into minute and circumstantial particulars of which none but an *eyewitness* could have been possessed, and by implications almost too unequivocal to be regarded in the light of insinuation, to involve the "titled gambler" in the guilt of the transaction.

===Chinese===
这文件的真伪，我从未听父亲有过半点疑心；而我深信，以他笃信弟弟之心，若非经过充分查证，断不会轻易认可此物——因为这信的内容，恰恰助长了对弟弟不利的那些嫌疑。

这封信里头，唯有一处对叔父极为不利，那便是信中提及一只"双搭扣皮夹子"，说是装着足以牵累他的票据；然而这只皮夹子，却始终不曾现身，哪儿也找不着，死者身上也未搜出任何与赌事相关的字据。不过，无论那位科利斯起初打的什么主意，叔父与父亲此后再未听到他的半点音讯；只是他将那封信刊在了福克纳（Faulkner）所办的报纸上，而那张报纸，不久之后又成了另一桩更为扑朔迷离的攻讦的传声筒。我所指的那一段文字，刊出在约莫四年之后，彼时那桩惨祸在众人记忆中尚属新鲜。文章开头是一段东拉西扯的引子，声称"某一位被某些人以为已不在人世的*某人*，其实并未身亡，尚且活在人间，神志清明，记忆完好，而且又有意愿、又有能耐，叫那些*大*奸大恶之徒闻之股栗。"文章随后便描摹起那桩谋杀，却不提姓名；其描摹之细、举证之周，唯有*亲历其境的目击者*方能做到；又以几乎明明白白、不容作旁的解会的种种暗指，将那位"有头衔的赌徒"织进了这桩罪案之中。

===Original===
My father at once urged Sir Arthur to proceed against the paper in an action of libel; but he would not hear of it, nor consent to my father's taking any legal steps whatever in the matter. My father, however, wrote in a threatening tone to Faulkner, demanding a surrender of the author of the obnoxious article. The answer to this application is still in my possession, and is penned in an apologetic tone: it states that the manuscript had been handed in, paid for, and inserted as an advertisement, without sufficient inquiry, or any knowledge as to whom it referred.

No step, however, was taken to clear my uncle's character in the judgment of the public; and as he immediately sold a small property, the application of the proceeds of which was known to none, he was said to have disposed of it to enable himself to buy off the threatened information. However the truth might have been, it is certain that no charges respecting the mysterious murder were afterwards publicly made against my uncle, and, as far as external disturbances were concerned, he enjoyed henceforward perfect security and quiet.

===Chinese===
父亲当即力劝阿瑟爵士以诽谤之名起诉那张报纸；可他断然不听，也不许父亲在这件事上采取任何法律步骤。父亲 nonetheless 以威胁的口吻致函福克纳，要他交出那篇恶毒文章的作者。这封信的回函，至今仍存于我手；信里措辞歉然，声称那篇文稿是有人送来、付了钱、当作广告登出去的，并未加以详查，亦不知其所指何人。

然而叔父始终未采取任何步骤，以在众人的口碑之中为自己洗刷清白；而他随即又变卖了一处小小的产业，所得之款作何用途，无人知晓，于是便有风言风语，说他之所以脱手这处产业，是为了出钱堵住那即将曝光的口风。无论真相如何，有一点是确凿的：此后再未有人公开就那桩神秘命案对叔父提出任何指控；就外间的纷扰而言，他此后倒享着太平清静，安然无恙。

===Original===
A deep and lasting impression, however, had been made upon the public mind, and Sir Arthur T——n was no longer visited or noticed by the gentry and aristocracy of the county, whose attention and courtesies he had hitherto received. He accordingly affected to despise these enjoyments which he could not procure, and shunned even that society which he might have commanded.

This is all that I need recapitulate of my uncle's history, and I now recur to my own. Although my father had never, within my recollection, visited, or been visited by, my uncle, each being of sedentary, procrastinating, and secluded habits, and their respective residences being very far apart—the one lying in the county of Galway, the other in that of Cork—he was strongly attached to his brother, and evinced his affection by an active correspondence, and by deeply and proudly resenting that neglect which had marked Sir Arthur as unfit to mix in society.

===Chinese===
然而公众心中早已留下了深刻而持久的印象；郡中的绅士贵人们，从前对阿瑟爵士礼数周全、殷勤备至，如今再不登门，也再不与之来往。他于是装出一副瞧不上这些他已无缘沾染的乐趣的模样，甚至连那些他本可颐指气使、呼之即来的应酬，也一概回避了。

关于叔父的过往，我要追述的，尽于此矣。如今再回到我自己身上来。虽说在我记忆所及的范围之内，父亲与叔父从未相互走动——一则两人都是惯于久坐、遇事拖延、闭门索居的性子，二则各自的住处相去甚远——一个在戈尔韦（Galway）郡，一个在科克（Cork）郡——可父亲对弟弟却一往情深，这份手足之爱，既见于他们之间频繁的书信往还，也见于他愤然、骄傲地反击世人那种将阿瑟爵士摈于社交圈外的冷落。

===Original===
When I was about eighteen years of age, my father, whose health had been gradually declining, died, leaving me in heart wretched and desolate, and, owing to his previous seclusion, with few acquaintances, and almost no friends.

The provisions of his will were curious, and when I had sufficiently come to myself to listen to or comprehend them, surprised me not a little: all his vast property was left to me, and to the heirs of my body, forever; and, in default of such heirs, it was to go after my death to my uncle, Sir Arthur, without any entail.

At the same time, the will appointed him my guardian, desiring that I might be received within his house, and reside with his family, and under his care, during the term of my minority; and in consideration of the increased expense consequent upon such an arrangement, a handsome annuity was allotted to him during the term of my proposed residence.

===Chinese===
我约莫十八岁那年，父亲久病缠身、日渐衰弱，终于撒手人寰，留下我心如死灰、孤苦伶仃；又因他生前深居简出，我相识的人寥寥，朋友几乎全无。

他遗嘱中的条款颇为奇特；待我神志稍定，听得明白、想得清楚之时，着实吃惊不小：他那偌大一份家业，悉数留与了我，及我身所出的继承人，世世代代，永以为业；若我无嗣而终，则我身后此项产业归叔父阿瑟爵士所有，不受任何限定继承的约束。

与此同时，遗嘱又指定叔父为我的监护人，嘱我于未成年期间住入他家，与其家人同住，受其照拂；念及此项安排所增的开销，在预定我居住的这段时日里，每年拨给他一笔可观的年金。

===Original===
The object of this last provision I at once understood: my father desired, by making it the direct, apparent interest of Sir Arthur that I should die without issue, while at the same time he placed me wholly in his power, to prove to the world how great and unshaken was his confidence in his brother's innocence and honour, and also to afford him an opportunity of showing that this mark of confidence was not unworthily bestowed.

It was a strange, perhaps an idle scheme; but as I had been always brought up in the habit of considering my uncle as a deeply-injured man, and had been taught, almost as a part of my religion, to regard him as the very soul of honour, I felt no further uneasiness respecting the arrangement than that likely to result to a timid girl, of secluded habits, from the immediate prospect of taking up her abode for the first time in her life among total strangers. Previous to leaving my home, which I felt I should do with a heavy heart, I received a most tender and affectionate letter from my uncle, calculated, if anything could do so, to remove the bitterness of parting from scenes familiar and dear from my earliest childhood, and in some degree to reconcile me to the measure.

===Chinese===
这最后一项条款的用意，我登时就明白了：父亲是要借这一手，使阿瑟爵士在我无嗣而终一事上，有着直接而显见的利益可图——与此同时，又把我整个人交付到他手心之中——以此来向天下人昭示，他对弟弟的清白与人品，怀有怎样深厚、怎样不可动摇的信赖；亦是要给弟弟一个机会，证明这份信赖并未托付非人。

此计固然离奇，甚至近于一厢情愿的迂阔；然而我自幼便习于将叔父视作一个含冤负屈之人，更几乎是在信仰的教诲之中，将他看作荣誉的化身；故而对于这一安排，我别无忧虑，所愁的，无非是一个素来深居简出的怯懦少女，平生头一遭便要住进一群素昧平生之人中间，心中难免的那份忐忑罢了。临行离家之前——这一别，我自知心头将何其沉重——我接到叔父一封情意恳切、温存备至的来信，此信若还抵用的话，正是要消解我自幼熟悉、自幼珍视的种种景物骤然离别的苦涩，多少叫我心安理得地接受这一安排。

===Original===
It was during a fine autumn that I approached the old domain of Carrickleigh. I shall not soon forget the impression of sadness and of gloom which all that I saw produced upon my mind; the sunbeams were falling with a rich and melancholy tint upon the fine old trees, which stood in lordly groups, casting their long, sweeping shadows over rock and sward. There was an air of neglect and decay about the spot, which amounted almost to desolation; the symptoms of this increased in number as we approached the building itself, near which the ground had been originally more artificially and carefully cultivated than elsewhere, and whose neglect consequently more immediately and strikingly betrayed itself.

As we proceeded, the road wound near the beds of what had been formerly two fishponds, which were now nothing more than stagnant swamps, overgrown with rank weeds, and here and there encroached upon by the straggling underwood; the avenue itself was much broken, and in many places the stones were almost concealed by grass and nettles; the loose stone walls which had here and there intersected the broad park were, in many places, broken down, so as no longer to answer their original purpose as fences; piers were now and then to be seen, but the gates were gone; and, to add to the general air of dilapidation, some huge trunks were lying scattered through the venerable old trees, either the work of the winter storms, or perhaps the victims of some extensive but desultory scheme of denudation, which the projector had not capital or perseverance to carry into full effect.

===Chinese===
我是在一个晴好的秋日，行近卡里克利那片古老庄园的。一路上所见的一切，在我心头投下的那一片凄凉阴郁的阴影，我久久不能忘怀；阳光以一种浓郁而伤感的色调，斜斜地洒在那些苍古的大树之上，它们一丛一丛、威仪俨然地矗立着，将修长、披拂的影子投在岩石与草坡之间。这地方处处透着一股荒废败落的气息，几乎到了满目萧然的地步；待我们行近宅子本身，这种败落的迹象便越发密集——原来宅子近处的地界，当初本是整治得最为人工、最为精心的所在，因此一任荒芜起来，其破败之相，自然也最为触目、最为扎眼。

我们一路前行，道路蜿蜒经过两方昔日鱼塘的塘底，如今那里不过是两汪死水烂泥，杂草丛生，四面又有东一丛西一丛的灌木逐年蚕食；那条林荫道本身也已坎坷破碎，许多地方石子几乎被荒草与荨麻遮掩净尽；那横亘在开阔园地之间的几道干砌石墙，也有许多处坍塌，再也起不得围篱的作用了；门柱尚能时时望见，门扇却已不知去向；更有甚者——将这满目凋残再添一重——几株粗大的树干横七竖八地躺在那些古树之间，也不知是冬日风暴的杰作，还是某个兴头上来又半途而废的大肆砍伐计划的牺牲品，总之那主事之人，财力或耐性之中，总归缺了一样，终未能将此事做到底。

===Original===
After the carriage had travelled a mile of this avenue, we reached the summit of rather an abrupt eminence, one of the many which added to the picturesqueness, if not to the convenience of this rude passage. From the top of this ridge the grey walls of Carrickleigh were visible, rising at a small distance in front, and darkened by the hoary wood which crowded around them. It was a quadrangular building of considerable extent, and the front which lay towards us, and in which the great entrance was placed, bore unequivocal marks of antiquity; the timeworn, solemn aspect of the old building, the ruinous and deserted appearance of the whole place, and the associations which connected it with a dark page in the history of my family, combined to depress spirits already predisposed for the reception of sombre and dejecting impressions.

When the carriage drew up in the grass-grown court yard before the hall-door, two lazy-looking men, whose appearance well accorded with that of the place which they tenanted, alarmed by the obstreperous barking of a great chained dog, ran out from some half-ruinous outhouses, and took charge of the horses; the hall-door stood open, and I entered a gloomy and imperfectly lighted apartment, and found no one within. However, I had not long to wait in this awkward predicament, for before my luggage had been deposited in the house, indeed, before I had well removed my cloak and other wraps, so as to enable me to look around, a young girl ran lightly into the hall, and kissing me heartily, and somewhat boisterously, exclaimed:

===Chinese===
马车沿着这条林荫道走了一英里光景，便登上一处颇为陡峭的高地之巅——这样的高低起伏，一路上所在多有，纵然谈不上便利，却也为这条崎岖的通路添了几分如画之趣。从这道山脊顶上望去，已能望见卡里克利灰扑扑的院墙，在前方不远处拔地而起，又因四围那一片苍郁的古木而愈显幽暗。那是一座颇具规模、四四方方的宅子，朝向我们这一面、也是大门所在的那一堵前墙，斑驳古拙，显是年代久远；这座老宅那饱经风霜、庄严肃穆的面容，整处地方那倾颓荒废的模样，再加上此地与我家族历史上一页阴森篇章之间的种种关联——三者合力，将我本就易于沾染沉郁晦暗之气的心绪，压得更低了。

马车在门前那长满荒草的院子里停住，两条形容慵懒的汉子——他们的模样倒与所居之处十分相称——被一条拴着链子的大狗那吵闹的吠声惊起，从几间半塌的杂屋里跑出来，接过了马匹；厅门洞开着，我走进一间幽暗、光线不足的门厅，里头空无一人。不过，这一阵尴尬我倒并未忍受多久，因为行李尚未搬进屋子——事实上，我连斗篷和别的裹身之物都还没来得及卸下、好四下张望——便见一个年轻姑娘轻快地奔进门厅，热切地、略带几分粗野地亲了我一口，嚷道：

===Original===
"My dear cousin, my dear Margaret—I am so delighted—so out of breath. We did not expect you till ten o'clock; my father is somewhere about the place, he must be close at hand. James—Corney—run out and tell your master—my brother is seldom at home, at least at any reasonable hour—you must be so tired—so fatigued—let me show you to your room—see that Lady Margaret's luggage is all brought up—you must lie down and rest yourself—Deborah, bring some coffee—up these stairs; we are so delighted to see you—you cannot think how lonely I have been—how steep these stairs are, are not they? I am so glad you are come—I could hardly bring myself to believe that you were really coming—how good of you, dear Lady Margaret."

There was real good-nature and delight in my cousin's greeting, and a kind of constitutional confidence of manner which placed me at once at ease, and made me feel immediately upon terms of intimacy with her. The room into which she ushered me, although partaking in the general air of decay which pervaded the mansion and all about it, had nevertheless been fitted up with evident attention to comfort, and even with some dingy attempt at luxury; but what pleased me most was that it opened, by a second door, upon a lobby which communicated with my fair cousin's apartment; a circumstance which divested the room, in my eyes, of the air of solitude and sadness which would otherwise have characterised it, to a degree almost painful to one so dejected in spirits as I was.

===Chinese===
"亲爱的表妹，亲爱的玛格丽特（Margaret）——我太高兴了——高兴得都快喘不过气了。我们本想不到十点钟你才会到呢；父亲在庄子里的哪个地方，离这儿一定不远。詹姆斯——科尼——快跑出去禀告老爷——我哥哥难得在家，至少难得在正经时辰在家——你一定累坏了——乏透了吧——我领你去你屋里——瞧着把玛格丽特小姐的行李全都搬上来——你快躺下歇歇——黛博拉，端些咖啡来——上这边楼梯；我们见到你可太高兴啦——你想不到我这一阵有多孤单——这楼梯可真够陡的，是不是？你能来我真高兴——我先前几乎都不敢相信你当真会来——你真好啊，亲爱的玛格丽特小姐。"

表姐这番相迎，里头尽是实心实意的亲热与欢喜，还有一副与生俱来的大方模样，登时叫我放松下来，仿佛顷刻之间便与她亲如一家了。她把我领进的那间屋子，虽说也免不了沾染整座宅邸及其周遭那一股萧索败落的气息，却显然是用心布置过的，务求舒服，甚至还带几分虽则黯淡却不失奢丽的尝试；然而最叫我欢喜的是，这屋子另有一扇门，开向一条过道，与我这美貌表姐的卧房相通；有此一节，这屋子在我眼里便除却了那原本会笼罩其上的孤寂与愁惨之气——那股气，对于心境如我那般消沉的人而言，原是要痛切难当的。

===Original===
After such arrangements as I found necessary were completed, we both went down to the parlour, a large wainscoted room, hung round with grim old portraits, and, as I was not sorry to see, containing in its ample grate a large and cheerful fire. Here my cousin had leisure to talk more at her ease; and from her I learned something of the manners and the habits of the two remaining members of her family, whom I had not yet seen.

On my arrival I had known nothing of the family among whom I was come to reside, except that it consisted of three individuals, my uncle, and his son and daughter, Lady T——n having been long dead. In addition to this very scanty stock of information, I shortly learned from my communicative companion that my uncle was, as I had suspected, completely retired in his habits, and besides that, having been so far back as she could well recollect, always rather strict, as reformed rakes frequently become, he had latterly been growing more gloomily and sternly religious than heretofore.

===Chinese===
该打点的打点停当，我们俩便一同下楼来到客厅——一间护墙板镶就的大屋，四壁挂着一张张神情森严的古旧画像，而且——叫我看了并不扫兴——那宽大的壁炉里燃着一炉欢快的旺火。到了这里，表姐才得从容与我闲谈；从她口中，我约略知晓了我尚未见过的那两位家人——她父兄——的脾性与起居。

初来之时，我对于将要寄居的这户人家可说是一无所知，只知它由三人组成：叔父，及其一子一女；至于 T——n 夫人，早已去世多年。除了这一点可怜的底细之外，不多时我又从这位健谈的同伴口中得知：叔父正如我所揣度的那样，性子极是深居简出；不止如此，据她记忆所及，他向来颇为严苛——一如那些改邪归正的浪子常有的那样——而近几年来，更比从前阴沉严刻地虔信起来。

===Original===
Her account of her brother was far less favourable, though she did not say anything directly to his disadvantage. From all that I could gather from her, I was led to suppose that he was a specimen of the idle, coarse-mannered, profligate, low-minded "squirearchy"—a result which might naturally have flowed from the circumstance of his being, as it were, outlawed from society, and driven for companionship to grades below his own—enjoying, too, the dangerous prerogative of spending much money.

However, you may easily suppose that I found nothing in my cousin's communication fully to bear me out in so very decided a conclusion.

I awaited the arrival of my uncle, which was every moment to be expected, with feelings half of alarm, half of curiosity—a sensation which I have often since experienced, though to a less degree, when upon the point of standing for the first time in the presence of one of whom I have long been in the habit of hearing or thinking with interest.

===Chinese===
至于她哥哥，她的描述便远没有那么好了，虽说她也未曾直言其短。从她口中种种，我只能得出这样一个印象：他大约便是那等游手好闲、举止粗鄙、放浪形骸、心地卑下的"乡绅坯子"之典型——这一结果，原也自然而然：他既被社交圈摈弃在外，又不得不与比自身低等的角色为伍，更兼有那样一样危险的特权——挥金如土。

然而你也不难想见，表姐这一番话，并不足以令我得出如此斩钉截铁的结论。

我一边等候着叔父——他随时都可能到家——一边心头半是惶恐、半是好奇；这种滋味，此后我时常再有体会，只是程度稍浅罢了：那便是头一回站到一个久已惯于耳闻、久已挂念于心的人面前的一刹那。

===Original===
It was, therefore, with some little perturbation that I heard, first a slight bustle at the outer door, then a slow step traverse the hall, and finally witnessed the door open, and my uncle enter the room. He was a striking-looking man; from peculiarities both of person and of garb, the whole effect of his appearance amounted to extreme singularity. He was tall, and when young his figure must have been strikingly elegant; as it was, however, its effect was marred by a very decided stoop. His dress was of a sober colour, and in fashion anterior to anything which I could remember. It was, however, handsome, and by no means carelessly put on; but what completed the singularity of his appearance was his uncut, white hair, which hung in long, but not at all neglected curls, even so far as his shoulders, and which combined with his regularly classic features, and fine dark eyes, to bestow upon him an air of venerable dignity and pride, which I have never seen equalled elsewhere. I rose as he entered, and met him about the middle of the room; he kissed my cheek and both my hands, saying:

"You are most welcome, dear child, as welcome as the command of this poor place and all that it contains can make you. I am most rejoiced to see you—truly rejoiced. I trust that you are not much fatigued—pray be seated again." He led me to my chair, and continued: "I am glad to perceive you have made acquaintance with Emily already; I see, in your being thus brought together, the foundation of a lasting friendship. You are both innocent, and both young. God bless you—God bless you, and make you all that I could wish."

===Chinese===
因此，当我先是听见外门那儿一阵轻微的骚动，继而听见一阵缓慢的脚步穿过门厅，终于亲眼看见房门洞开、叔父走进屋来之时，心头免不了微微一颤。他生得一副引人注目的相貌；无论形貌还是装束，都各有奇异之处，合在一处，整体效果便极是特异。他身量高大，少时想必风姿翩翩；然而如今，这风姿却被一个明显的佝偻之态大大折损了。他衣裳的颜色十分素淡，式样也比我记忆中任何一款都要古旧；不过料子倒是讲究，穿在身上也绝非潦草；然而使他这一副模样更臻于特异的，是他那一头未加修剪的白发——长长的、却丝毫不见疏懒散乱的发卷，一直垂到肩头；这白发与他端正古典的五官、一双有神的黑眼睛相得益彰，赋予他一种可敬可畏的尊严与傲岸之气——这副气度，我在旁处从未见过能与之比肩的。他一进门我便起身，在屋子中央迎上他；他吻了吻我的脸颊，又亲了我两只手，说道：

"孩子，你来了，再好不过；这寒舍之中，凡此种种，任凭你使唤，你能赏脸前来，便是再欢迎也没有了。能见着你，我着实欢喜——真正地满心欢喜。想必你路上没怎么累着——快请坐，快请坐。"他把我领回椅子跟前，又接着说道："你与埃米莉（Emily）已经认识了，我看了很是高兴；我看你俩今日得在一处，正是天长地久的情谊之始。你俩都天真无邪，又都年华正好。愿上帝赐福于你们——愿上帝赐福，叫你们长成我所愿的模样。"

===Original===
He raised his eyes, and remained for a few moments silent, as if in secret prayer. I felt that it was impossible that this man, with feelings so quick, so warm, so tender, could be the wretch that public opinion had represented him to be. I was more than ever convinced of his innocence.

His manner was, or appeared to me, most fascinating; there was a mingled kindness and courtesy in it which seemed to speak benevolence itself. It was a manner which I felt cold art could never have taught; it owed most of its charm to its appearing to emanate directly from the heart; it must be a genuine index of the owner's mind. So I thought.

My uncle having given me fully to understand that I was most welcome, and might command whatever was his own, pressed me to take some refreshment; and on my refusing, he observed that previously to bidding me good night, he had one duty further to perform, one in whose observance he was convinced I would cheerfully acquiesce.

He then proceeded to read a chapter from the Bible; after which he took his leave with the same affectionate kindness with which he had greeted me, having repeated his desire that I should consider everything in his house as altogether at my disposal. It is needless to say that I was much pleased with my uncle—it was impossible to avoid being so; and I could not help saying to myself, if such a man as this is not safe from the assaults of slander, who is? I felt much happier than I had done since my father's death, and enjoyed that night the first refreshing sleep which had visited me since that event.

===Chinese===
他抬眼望着上方，静默了片刻，像是在心里默祷。我心想，这样一个人，情思如此敏捷、如此温热、如此细腻，绝无可能是众人口中那种恶徒。我比从前任何时候都更坚信他的清白。

他的举止——至少在我看来——极是迷人；其中糅合着一种和蔼与殷勤，仿佛仁厚之心的本相。我觉着，这般举止，绝非冷冰冰的做作之术所能教会；它大半的魅力，全在于它仿佛发自肺腑；它必然是主人内心真实的写照。我那时是这样想的。

叔父既已使我充分明白：我的到来大受欢迎，凡他所有，任我支取；他便又劝我用些点心。我婉拒之后，他说道，与我道晚安之前，他还有一桩本分要尽——一桩他深信我必会欣然遵从的本分。

于是他便诵读了一章《圣经》；读罢，仍以相见时那般温存和蔼的口吻与我作别，又重申了一遍：屋里的一切，全凭我支配，不必客气。不用说，叔父这一番做派，叫我十分欢喜——这般欢喜，原是挡也挡不住的；我忍不住在心里嘀咕：这样一个人，倘若尚且不能免于流言的中伤，那天下还有谁能幸免？自父亲去世以来，我头一回感到心情轻快了许多；那一夜，也是父亲故世之后我头一回睡了一个安稳觉。

===Original===
My curiosity respecting my male cousin did not long remain unsatisfied—he appeared the next day at dinner. His manners, though not so coarse as I had expected, were exceedingly disagreeable; there was an assurance and a forwardness for which I was not prepared; there was less of the vulgarity of manner, and almost more of that of the mind, than I had anticipated.
