“Request him, with my compliments, to walk in,” said O’Connor; and in a few moments a gentleman entered the room.

===Chinese===
我于是更为仔细地追问奥康纳与菲茨杰拉德起冲突的始末。原来这争执起于一条皮克牌规则的运用——他们当时正玩着这种牌——两人都按有利于自己的方向来解读这条规则；奥康纳输得颇不少，本无心平气和地与人争论，于是便你来我往地吵了起来，所说的话相当尖刻；结果是他颇为仓促地离开了菲茨杰拉德的房间，决意以最不容置疑的口吻要求对方作出解释。为此他派人请来了麦克多诺，托他把那封信送去——幸而我的到来把这事拦了下来。

此时已过了正午，奥康纳要我答应留下与他共进正餐；于是我们三人入席，都因这一番焦虑的告终而兴致颇高。此地须得交代一句，为下文做个铺垫：奥康纳夫人——或者用一个更悦耳的称呼，康纳城堡的夫人——因身体不适，不能入席同餐，事实上她很少在四点之前离开自己的房间。饭后我们坐着呷红葡萄酒，谈着、笑着，十分快活，忽然一个仆人走进屋来，禀报主人说，有一位先生想与他说几句话。

"请他代我致意，进来吧，"奥康纳说；不多时，一位先生走了进来。

===Original===
His appearance was anything but prepossessing. He was a little above the middle size, spare, and rawboned; his face very red, his features sharp and bluish, and his age might be about sixty. His attire savoured a good deal of the **shabby-genteel**; his clothes, which had much of tarnished and faded pretension about them, did not fit him, and had not improbably fluttered in the stalls of Plunket Street. We had risen on his entrance, and O’Connor had twice requested of him to take a chair at the table, without his hearing, or at least noticing, the invitation; while with a slow pace, and with an air of mingled importance and effrontery, he advanced into the centre of the apartment, and regarding our small party with a supercilious air, he said:

“I take the liberty of introducing myself﻿—I am Captain McCreagh, formerly of the —﻿—﻿— infantry. My business here is with a Mr. O’Connor, and the sooner it is despatched the better.”

“I am the gentleman you name,” said O’Connor; “and as you appear impatient, we had better proceed to your commission without delay.”

“Then, Mr. O’Connor, you will please to read that note,” said the captain, placing a sealed paper in his hand.

O’Connor read it through, and then observed:

“This is very extraordinary indeed. This note appears to me perfectly unaccountable.”

“You are very young, Mr. O’Connor,” said the captain, with vulgar familiarity; “but, without much experience in these matters, I think you might have anticipated something like this. You know the old saying, ‘Second thoughts are best;’ and so they are like to prove, by G﻿—﻿—!”

“You will have no objection, Captain McCreagh, on the part of your friend, to my reading this note to these gentlemen; they are both confidential friends of mine, and one of them has already acted for me in this business.”

“I can have no objections,” replied the captain, “to your doing what you please with your own. I have nothing more to do with that note once I put it safe into your hand; and when that is once done, it is all one to me, if you read it to half the world﻿—that’s *your* concern, and no affair of mine.”

===Chinese===
他的外表丝毫不能引人好感。他身量略高于中等，瘦削而骨节粗大；脸色通红，五官尖削，泛着青色，年纪约莫六十上下。他的衣着颇有几分**穷酸而强充体面**的味道；那一身衣服，褪色败气、华而不实，并不合身，多半曾在普伦基特街（Plunket Street）的旧衣摊上飘荡过。他一进来，我们便都起身，奥康纳已两次请他在桌旁入座，他不是没听见，便是装作没听见；只顾迈着慢吞吞的步子，带着一身高傲与厚颜兼备的神气，走到屋子正中，以一种目空一切的架势打量着我们这个小圈子，说道：

"恕我冒昧自我引见——我是麦克克里格上尉（Captain McCreagh），原任某步兵团军官。我此来是为找一位奥康纳先生，此事越快了结越好。"

"我便是您所说的那位先生，"奥康纳说，"既然您心急，我们不如马上谈您带来的差事。"

"那么，奥康纳先生，请您过目这封信，"上尉说着，把一纸封了口的信放到他手里。

奥康纳从头到尾看了一遍，说道：

"这可实在出奇。这封信在我看来，简直莫名其妙。"

"您年纪还轻，奥康纳先生，"上尉以一种粗俗的亲昵说道，"不过，您虽在这些事上阅历不多，我想您也该料到会有这一出。您知道那句老话，'再思为上'；这话可真要应验了，凭——上帝起誓！"

"麦克克里格上尉，想必您的朋友不会反对，我把这封信读给这两位先生听；他们二位都是我的至交，其中一位已在此事中替我效过劳。"

"我没什么可反对的，"上尉答道，"您爱怎样处置您自己的东西就怎样处置。这封信一旦安然交到您手里，我便再无瓜葛；事既办妥，您便是读给半个世界听，于我也无差别——那是*您*的事，与我无关。"

===Original===
O’Connor then read the following:

> “Mr. Fitzgerald begs leave to state, that upon re-perusing Mr. O’Connor’s communication of this morning carefully, with an experienced friend, he is forced to consider himself as challenged. His friend, Captain McCreagh, has been empowered by him to make all the necessary arrangements.
> “T﻿—﻿— Inn, Thursday.”

I can hardly describe the astonishment with which I heard this note. I turned to the captain, and said:

“Surely, sir, there is some mistake in all this?”

“Not the slightest, I’ll assure you, sir,” said he, coolly; “the case is a very clear one, and I think my friend has pretty well made up his mind upon it. May I request your answer?” he continued, turning to O’Connor; “time is precious, you know.”

O’Connor expressed his willingness to comply with the suggestion, and in a few minutes had folded and directed the following rejoinder:

> “Mr. O’Connor having received a satisfactory explanation from Mr. Fitzgerald, of the language used by that gentleman, feels that there no longer exists any grounds for misunderstanding, and wishes further to state, that the note of which Mr. Fitzgerald speaks was not intended as a challenge.”

===Chinese===
奥康纳于是读了下面这封：

> "菲茨杰拉德先生谨此声明：今晨奥康纳先生之来函，经与一位有经验的朋友仔细重读之后，他不得不认为自己已受到挑战。他的朋友麦克克里格上尉，已受全权委托办理一切必要之安排。
> T——客栈，星期四。"

我听到这封信时之惊愕，难以尽述。我转向上尉，说道：

"先生，这中间总有几分误会吧？"

"一丝一毫也没有，先生，我向您保证，"他冷冷地说，"案情再清楚不过了，我想我朋友对此已下定了决心。可否请您赐复？"他转向奥康纳，又道，"时间宝贵，您是知道的。"

奥康纳表示乐于从命，不多时便折叠妥当，写就了下面这封回函：

> "奥康纳先生既已从菲茨杰拉德先生处获得令人满意的解释，关于该先生所用之言语，深感误解之由已不复存在；并特此声明，菲茨杰拉德先生所提及的那封便笺，本非挑战之意。"

===Original===
With this note the captain departed; and as we did not doubt that the message which he had delivered had been suggested by some unintentional misconstruction of O’Connor’s first billet, we felt assured that the conclusion of his last note would set the matter at rest. In this belief, however, we were mistaken; before we had left the table, and in an incredibly short time, the captain returned. He entered the room with a countenance evidently tasked to avoid expressing the satisfaction which a consciousness of the nature of his mission had conferred; but in spite of all his efforts to look gravely unconcerned, there was a twinkle in the small grey eye, and an almost imperceptible motion in the corner of the mouth, which sufficiently betrayed his internal glee, as he placed a note in the hand of O’Connor. As the young man cast his eye over it, he coloured deeply, and turning to McDonough, he said:

“You will have the goodness to make all the necessary arrangements for a meeting. Something has occurred to render one between me and Mr. Fitzgerald inevitable. Understand me literally, when I say that it is now totally impossible that this affair should be amicably arranged. You will have the goodness, McDonough, to let me know as soon as all the particulars are arranged. Purcell,” he continued, “will you have the kindness to accompany me?” and having bowed to McCreagh, we left the room.

As I closed the door after me, I heard the captain laugh, and thought I could distinguish the words﻿—“By —﻿—﻿— I knew Fitzgerald would bring him to his way of thinking before he stopped.”

===Chinese===
上尉带着这封信走了；我们料想，他所传达的信息，无非是出自对奥康纳第一封便笺的某种无意误解，因而相信他这封回函的结语，定能令此事归于平静。然而这一信念，这一次我们却错了；我们尚未离席，上尉竟以难以置信的速度折了回来。他走进屋来，脸上分明是刻意克制、不让自己流露出那份满足的神色——他此行的差事性质本已叫他得意；然而尽管他竭力装出一副凝重淡然的模样，那只灰色的小眼睛里却有一丝闪烁，嘴角也几乎难以察觉地动了一动，足以把他心头的窃喜泄露无遗——他把一封信放到奥康纳手里。那年轻人眼光一扫，登时满脸涨红，转向麦克多诺，说道：

"劳驾你安排决斗的一切事宜。出了些变故，使我与菲茨杰拉德先生之间的一场较量已成势所不免。请你逐字地理解我：现在要说这事还能友善了结，已是断无可能。麦克多诺，一切细节安排妥当之后，请尽快告知我。珀塞尔，"他又道，"你可愿陪我一同前往？"向麦克克里格鞠了一躬之后，我们便出了房间。

我随手带上门时，听见上尉笑了一声，恍惚还能分辨出这样几个字——"凭——起誓，我就知道菲茨杰拉德定能叫他回心转意。"

===Original===
I followed O’Connor into his study, and on entering, the door being closed, he showed me the communication which had determined him upon hostilities. Its language was grossly impertinent, and it concluded by actually threatening to “*post*” him, in case he further attempted “to be *off*.” I cannot describe the agony of indignation in which O’Connor writhed under this insult. He said repeatedly that “he was a degraded and dishohoured man,” that “he was dragged into the field,” that “there was ignominy in the very thought that such a letter should have been directed to him.” It was in vain that I reasoned against this impression; the conviction that he had been disgraced had taken possession of his mind. He said again and again that nothing but his *death* could remove the stain which his indecision had cast upon the name of his family. I hurried to the hall, on hearing McDonough and the captain passing, and reached the door just in time to hear the latter say, as he mounted his horse:

“All the rest can be arranged on the spot; and so farewell, Mr. McDonough﻿—we’ll meet at Philippi, you know;” and with this classical allusion, which was accompanied with a grin and a bow, and probably served many such occasions, the captain took his departure.

===Chinese===
我跟着奥康纳走进他的书房，一进去，门一关上，他便把那封促使他下定决心开战的书函给我看。信中措辞粗暴无礼至极，结尾竟公然威胁说，若他再企图"脱身"，便要"张榜揭发"。奥康纳在这般侮辱之下痛苦万状，那份屈辱的煎熬，我实在无从描摹。他一再说自己"是个堕落而蒙羞的人了"，说自己"是被硬拖到决斗场上去的"，又说"这样一封信竟会写给我，单是这念头本身便是奇耻大辱"。我极力说理，想打消他这念头，却全属徒劳；他已认定自己受了奇耻大辱，这一执念占据了他的全部心智。他一再说，唯有他自己的死，方能洗去他那犹豫不决给家族姓氏所抹上的污点。我听见麦克多诺与上尉走过，便急忙赶到门厅，刚到门口，便听见后者一边上马一边说道：

"其余的一切，届时当场再定便是；那么再会了，麦克多诺先生——咱们腓力比（Philippi）再见吧，您是知道的；"伴随着这句古典典故——同时咧嘴一笑、鞠了一躬，想必这句话还伺候过许多类似的场合——上尉便告辞而去。

===Original===
McDonough briefly stated the few particulars which had been arranged. The parties were to meet at the stand-house, in the race-ground, which lay at about an equal distance between Castle Connor and the town of T﻿—﻿—. The hour appointed was half-past five on the next morning, at which time the twilight would be sufficiently advanced to afford a distinct view; and the weapons to be employed were *pistols*﻿—McCreagh having claimed, on the part of his friend, all the advantages of the *challenged* party, and having, consequently, insisted upon the choice of “tools,” as he expressed himself; and it was further stipulated that the utmost secrecy should be observed, as Fitzgerald would incur great risk from the violence of the peasantry, in case the affair took wind. These conditions were, of course, agreed upon by O’Connor, and McDonough left the castle, having appointed four o’clock upon the next morning as the hour of his return, by which time it would be his business to provide everything necessary for the meeting. On his departure, O’Connor requested me to remain with him upon that evening, saying that “he could not bear to be alone with his mother.” It was to me a most painful request, but at the same time one which I could not think of refusing. I felt, however, that the difficulty at least of the task which I had to perform would be in some measure mitigated by the arrival of two relations of O’Connor upon that evening.

“It is very fortunate,” said O’Connor, whose thoughts had been running upon the same subject, “that the O’Gradys will be with us tonight; their gaiety and good-humour will relieve us from a heavy task. I trust that nothing may occur to prevent their coming.” Fervently concurring in the same wish, I accompanied O’Connor into the parlour, there to await the arrival of his mother.

===Chinese===
麦克多诺简述了已商定的几项细节。双方约定在赛马场上的看台屋子碰头，那地点与康纳城堡、T——镇的距离大致相等。约定时辰是次晨五点半，那时晨光已足够明亮，视野无碍；所用的武器是*手枪*——麦克克里格代表他的朋友，主张作为*被挑战方*所应有的一切便利，因而坚持由其挑选"家伙"，他是这么说的；此外还议定，此事须绝对保密，因为一旦走漏风声，菲茨杰拉德恐遭乡民的暴力之害，风险极大。这些条件，奥康纳自然一一应允；麦克多诺辞别城堡，约定次晨四点再来，届时由他备齐决斗所需的一切。临去之际，奥康纳请我那晚留下陪他，说"他受不了单独与他母亲相处"。这请求于我最为难堪，却又是我不忍拒绝的。然而我感到，我所要承担的这桩差事，至少其艰难之处，当可因奥康纳的两位亲戚当晚的到来，而稍得减轻。

"真是万幸，"奥康纳说道——他心里也正想着同一件事——"今晚奥格雷迪家（the O'Gradys）要来咱们这儿；他们的热闹与好性情，会替我们分担一桩重负。但愿别出什么事，耽搁了他们前来。"我衷心附和这一心愿，便陪着奥康纳走进客厅，在那里等候他母亲到来。

===Original===
God grant that I may never spend such another evening! The O’Gradys *did* come, but their high and noisy spirits, so far from relieving me, did but give additional gloom to the despondency, I might say the despair, which filled my heart with misery﻿—the terrible forebodings which I could not for an instant silence, turned their laughter into discord, and seemed to mock the smiles and jests of the unconscious party. When I turned my eyes upon the mother, I thought I never had seen her look so proudly and so lovingly upon her son before﻿—it cut me to the heart﻿—oh, how cruelly I was deceiving her! I was a hundred times on the very point of starting up, and, at all hazards, declaring to her how matters were; but other feelings subdued my better emotions. Oh, what monsters are we made of by the fashions of the world! how are our kindlier and nobler feelings warped or destroyed by their baleful influences! I felt that it would not be *honourable*, that it would not be *etiquette*, to betray O’Connor’s secret. I sacrificed a higher and a nobler duty than I have since been called upon to perform, to the dastardly fear of bearing the unmerited censure of a world from which I was about to retire. O Fashion! thou gaudy idol, whose feet are red with the blood of human sacrifice, would I had always felt towards thee as I now do!

===Chinese===
但愿上帝容我此生再不要过这样一个夜晚！奥格雷迪家果真来了，可他们那份高声喧闹的兴头，非但未能替我分担分毫，反倒给我那满心的颓丧——我可以说，是绝望——更添了几分阴郁；那些我片刻也压不下去的可怕预感，把他们的笑声化作了刺耳的杂音，仿佛是在嘲弄那一桌浑然不觉的人的笑脸与戏谑。每当我把目光投向那位母亲，我总觉得从未见过她如此既骄傲、又疼爱地望着她的儿子——这景象叫我心如刀绞——啊，我是在何等残忍地欺瞒着她！我上百次几乎要跳起身来，不顾一切地把真相告诉她；然而另一些念头压倒了我这份较好的情感。啊，世间的礼俗把咱们塑造成了何等怪物！我们天性中较为善良、高尚的情感，竟被这些恶毒的影响扭曲、乃至毁灭！我觉得，若是泄露奥康纳的秘密，便是不守*信用*，便是坏了*规矩*。于是，我出于一种怯懦——怕承担那不白之冤，来自一个我即将告退的世界——竟牺牲了一桩比我此后所尽的任何职守都更高尚、更神圣的本分。啊，时尚！你这金碧辉煌的偶像，你脚下染满了人所献祭的鲜血，但愿我过去对你，一向如今日这般！

===Original===
O’Connor was not dejected; on the contrary, he joined with loud and lively alacrity in the hilarity of the little party; but I could see in the flush of his cheek, and in the unusual brightness of his eye, all the excitement of fever﻿—he was making an effort almost beyond his strength, but he succeeded﻿—and when his mother rose to leave the room, it was with the impression that her son was the gayest and most lighthearted of the company. Twice or thrice she had risen with the intention of retiring, but O’Connor, with an eagerness which I alone could understand, had persuaded her to remain until the usual hour of her departure had long passed; and when at length she arose, declaring that she could not possibly stay longer, I alone could comprehend the desolate change which passed over his manner; and when I saw them part, it was with the sickening conviction that those two beings, so dear to one another, so loved, so cherished, should meet no more.

===Chinese===
奥康纳并不消沉；相反，他高声快活地、兴致勃勃地加入了这一小圈子的热闹；然而我从他脸颊上不寻常的潮红、从他那双异样明亮的眼睛里，看得出全是发烧一般的亢奋——他正在勉力支撑，那力气几乎已超出他的所能，可他撑住了——当他母亲起身离席时，留下的印象是，她的儿子是满座最为欢快、最为无忧无虑的人。她有两三回想起身告退，都被奥康纳以我一人才能理解的殷切挽留住了，直留到她平日离席的时辰早已过去；待她终于起身，声称实在不能再留时，也只有我一人能体会他神情间那一片苍凉的变故；而当我看着他们母子分别，心中所充满的，是那种令人作呕的确信——这两个彼此如此相爱、如此珍重、如此宝贝的人，将再无相见之日。

===Original===
O’Connor briefly informed his cousins of the position in which he was placed, requesting them at the same time to accompany him to the field, and this having been settled, we separated, each to his own apartment. I had wished to sit up with O’Connor, who had matters to arrange sufficient to employ him until the hour appointed for McDonough’s visit; but he would not hear of it, and I was forced, though sorely against my will, to leave him without a companion. I went to my room, and, in a state of excitement which I cannot describe, I paced for hours up and down its narrow precincts. I could not﻿—who could?﻿—analyse the strange, contradictory, torturing feelings which, while I recoiled in shrinking horror from the scene which the morning was to bring, yet forced me to wish the intervening time annihilated; each hour that the clock told seemed to vibrate and tinkle through every nerve; my agitation was dreadful; fancy conjured up the forms of those who filled my thoughts with more than the vividness of reality; things seemed to glide through the dusky shadows of the room. I saw the dreaded form of Fitzgerald﻿—I heard the hated laugh of the captain﻿—and again the features of O’Connor would appear before me, with ghastly distinctness, pale and writhed in death, the gouts of gore clotted in the mouth, and the eyeballs glared and staring. Scared with the visions which seemed to throng with unceasing rapidity and vividness, I threw open the window and looked out upon the quiet scene around. I turned my eyes in the direction of the town; a heavy cloud was lowering darkly about it, and I, in impious frenzy, prayed to God that it might burst in avenging fires upon the murderous wretch who lay beneath. At length, sick and giddy with excess of excitement, I threw myself upon the bed without removing my clothes, and endeavoured to compose myself so far as to remain quiet until the hour for our assembling should arrive.

===Chinese===
奥康纳简短地把他的处境告知了两位表亲，同时请他们陪他一同赴场；此事既已说定，我们便各自回房。我本想陪奥康纳熬夜——他待办的事足可忙到麦克多诺约定来访的时辰——可他执意不肯，我只得违背本心，撇下他独自一人。我回到自己房里，处在一种无从言说的亢奋之中，在那狭窄的四方之内来回踱步，一踱便是几个钟头。我无法——谁又能呢？——去解析那种种奇异、矛盾、煎熬的感觉：我一边怀着退缩的恐惧，战栗于清晨将要带来的那一场面，一边却又被一种力量逼着，巴不得这中间的时光立刻化为乌有；时钟报出的每一个钟头，仿佛都震动着、叮当地穿过我每一根神经；我的激动实在可怕；幻想把那些盘踞在我心头的人影，以超乎现实的真切召到我眼前；各种东西仿佛在屋里的昏暗阴影中悄然滑过。我看见了令我畏惧的菲茨杰拉德的身影——我听见了令我憎恶的上尉的笑声——转眼间，奥康纳的脸又浮现在我眼前，苍白可怖地清晰，死状扭曲，口中凝着一团团血污，眼珠怒突、直瞪着前方。这些幻象纷至沓来，接连不断、历历在目，我惊惧不已，猛地推开窗子，望向窗外那一片宁静的景色。我把目光投向小镇那个方向；一团浓云正黑沉沉地压在它上头，我竟以一种亵渎神明的癫狂，祈求上帝让那团云化作复仇的烈火，倾泻在那个藏身其下的杀人恶棍头上。到末了，我因过度的激动而作呕、眩晕，便和衣倒在床上，竭力让自己定下心来，至少能安静地等到我们集合的时刻到来。

===Original===
A few minutes before four o’clock I stole noiselessly downstairs, and made my way to the small study already mentioned. A candle was burning within; and, when I opened the door, O’Connor was reading a book, which, on seeing me, he hastily closed, colouring slightly as he did so. We exchanged a cordial but mournful greeting; and after a slight pause he said, laying his hand upon the volume which he had shut a moment before:

“Purcell, I feel perfectly calm, though I cannot say that I have much hope as to the issue of this morning’s rencounter. I shall avoid half the danger. If I must fall, I am determined I shall not go down to the grave with his blood upon my hands. I have resolved not to fire at Fitzgerald﻿—that is, to fire in such a direction as to assure myself against hitting him. Do not say a word of this to the O’Gradys. Your doing so would only produce fruitless altercation; they could not understand my motives. I feel convinced that I shall not leave the field alive. If I must die today, I shall avoid an awful aggravation of wretchedness. Purcell,” he continued, after a little space, “I was so weak as to feel almost ashamed of the manner in which I was occupied as you entered the room. Yes, *I*﻿—*I* who will be, before this evening, a cold and lifeless clod, was ashamed to have spent my last moment of reflection in prayer. God pardon me! God pardon me!” he repeated.

===Chinese===
差几分钟到四点，我轻手轻脚地下了楼，摸到先前说过的那间小书房。里面点着一支蜡烛；我推门进去时，奥康纳正在读一本书，见我进来，便匆匆合上，微微红了脸。我们彼此致意，热络而哀戚；略略一停，他把手放在方才合上的那本书上，说道：

"珀塞尔，我心情十分平静，虽说今晨这场较量的结局如何，我不能说自己怀有多少指望。我会避开一半的危险。倘若我必死无疑，我决意不带着他的血下到坟里去。我已打定主意，绝不向菲茨杰拉德开枪——也就是说，我要朝一个确保不会击中他的方向开枪。此事切勿对奥格雷迪家提起半个字。你说了，也不过是徒生一场无谓的争执；他们是不会明白我的用心的。我深信自己今日走不下决斗场了。如果我今日必死，我便可以免去一种可怕的、雪上加霜的苦楚。珀塞尔，"他顿了一顿，又道，"我方才竟软弱到几乎以此为耻——你进来时我正忙着的那件事。是的，*我*——*我*，这个不到今夜便要化作一块冰冷、没有生气之土块的人，竟以把最后一点沉思的光阴用在祷告上为耻。上帝宽恕我！上帝宽恕我！"他又道。

===Original===
I took his hand and pressed it, but I could not speak. I sought for words of comfort, but they would not come. To have uttered one cheering sentence I must have contradicted every impression of my own mind. I felt too much awed to attempt it. Shortly afterwards, McDonough arrived. No wretched patient ever underwent a more thrilling revulsion at the first sight of the case of surgical instruments under which he had to suffer, than did I upon beholding a certain oblong flat mahogany box, bound with brass, and of about two feet in length, laid upon the table in the hall. O’Connor, thanking him for his punctuality, requested him to come into his study for a moment, when, with a melancholy collectedness, he proceeded to make arrangements for our witnessing his will. The document was a brief one, and the whole matter was just arranged, when the two O’Gradys crept softly into the room.

“So! last will and testament,” said the elder. “Why, you have a very *blue* notion of these matters. I tell you, you need not be uneasy. I remember very well, when young Ryan of Ballykealey met McNeil the duellist, bets ran twenty to one against him. I stole away from school, and had a peep at the fun as well as the best of them. They fired together. Ryan received the ball through the collar of his coat, and McNeil in the temple; he spun like a top: it was a most unexpected thing, and disappointed his friends damnably. It was admitted, however, to have been very pretty shooting upon both sides. To be sure,” he continued, pointing to the will, “you are in the right to keep upon the safe side of fortune; but then, there is no occasion to be altogether so devilish down in the mouth as you appear to be.”

===Chinese===
我握住他的手，紧紧地握，却说不出话来。我想找几句安慰的话，却一句也找不到。若要说一句鼓舞人心的话，我便得违拗自己心中的一切判断。我太过敬畏，不敢轻易尝试。不多时，麦克多诺到了。世间哪一个倒霉的病人，初次瞧见自己将要受其苦的那一匣外科器械时，其所感到的那阵触电般的惊悸，只怕也比不上我看见门厅桌上放着的那只扁长、约莫两英尺长、以黄铜镶边的红木匣子时，心中所感到的惊悸之烈。奥康纳谢他准时，请他到书房里稍坐片刻，随即以一种沉郁的镇定，着手安排我们见证他的遗嘱。文件不长，整件事刚刚安排妥当，奥格雷迪家两兄弟便轻手轻脚地走了进来。

"哟！遗嘱和临终交代，"年长的那位说道，"哎呀，你对这些事的看法未免太*悲观*了些。我告诉你，你大可不必这么犯愁。我记得清清楚楚，当年巴利基利（Ballykealey）的小瑞安（Ryan）与决斗家麦克尼尔（McNeil）对阵时，赌注是一赔二十地押他输。我从学校里溜了出来，也跟大伙儿一样凑过去瞧了这场热闹。两人同时开枪。瑞安那一发从他衣领边上穿过去，麦克尼尔那发却打进了太阳穴；他像只陀螺似的转了一圈：这可是谁也没料到的事，叫他那帮朋友大失所望。不过大家都承认，这一场双方都打得很漂亮。话说回来，"他指着那遗嘱继续说道，"你图个万全，立下这东西，倒也无可厚非；可是，你也犯不着像现在这样，一副丧到家了的模样啊。"

===Original===
“You will allow,” said O’Connor, “that the chances are heavily against me.”

“Why, let me see,” he replied, “not so hollow a thing, either. Let me see, we’ll say about four to one against you; you may chance to throw doublets like him I told you of, and then what becomes of the odds I’d like to know? But let things go as they will, I’ll give and take four to one, in pounds and tens of pounds. There, McDonough, there’s a *get* for you; b﻿—﻿—﻿t me, if it is not. Poh! the fellow is stolen away,” he continued, observing that the object of his proposal had left the room; “but d﻿—﻿— it, Purcell, you are fond of a *soft thing*, too, in a quiet way﻿—I’m sure you are﻿—so curse me if I do not make you the same offer﻿—is it a go?”

I was too much disgusted to make any reply, but I believe my looks expressed my feelings sufficiently, for in a moment he said:

“Well, I see there is nothing to be done, so we may as well be stirring. McDonough, myself, and my brother will saddle the horses in a jiffy, while you and Purcell settle anything which remains to be arranged.”

So saying, he left the room with as much alacrity as if it were to prepare for a foxhunt. Selfish, heartless fool! I have often since heard him spoken of as “a cursed good-natured dog” and a “d﻿—﻿— good fellow”; but such eulogies as these are not calculated to mitigate the abhorrence with which his conduct upon that morning inspired me.

===Chinese===
"你总得承认，"奥康纳说，"胜算对我是大大不利的。"

"呃，让我想想，"他答道，"倒也不至于那么悬。让我想想，就算一赔四押你输吧；你也许会像我所讲的那位一样，掷出个对子来，那时候这些赔率还算得什么，我倒要请教？管它怎么着，一赔四，英镑也罢、十英镑也罢，我都接。喏，麦克多诺，这可是送上手的便宜；要不是，你就骂我。呸！这家伙溜了，"他发现他要邀赌的对象已离开屋子，便接着说，"不过，见鬼，珀塞尔，你也是喜欢稳赚不赔的便宜的人，只是闷声不响罢了——我看得出来——那么我就把同一桩买卖也下给你——怎么样，接不接？"

我实在厌恶之极，懒得作答；不过我想我的脸色已把我的心情表露无遗，因为不一会儿他便说：

"好吧，看来这儿没我什么事了，那咱们也该动起来了。麦克多诺、我、我兄弟，我们马上把马备好鞍，你和珀塞尔把余下要安排的事料理一下。"

说罢便出了房门，那股利落劲儿，仿佛是去为一场猎狐做准备的。自私、无情的蠢货！我后来常听人说他"是个脾气顶呱呱的好人"、"是个该死的好伙计"；可这一类颂词，并不能消减他那天早晨的行径所激起的、我心中的厌恶。

===Original===
The chill mists of night were still hovering on the landscape as our party left the castle. It was a raw, comfortless morning﻿—a kind of drizzling fog hung heavily over the scene, dimming the light of the sun, which had now risen, into a pale and even a grey glimmer. As the appointed hour was fast approaching, it was proposed that we should enter the race-ground at a point close to the stand-house﻿—a measure which would save us a ride of nearly two miles, over a broken road; at which distance there was an open entrance into the race-ground. Here, accordingly, we dismounted, and leaving our horses in the care of a country fellow who happened to be stirring at that early hour, we proceeded up a narrow lane, over a side wall of which we were to climb into the open ground where stood the now deserted building, under which the meeting was to take place. Our progress was intercepted by the unexpected appearance of an old woman, who, in the scarlet cloak which is the picturesque characteristic of the female peasantry of the south, was moving slowly down the avenue to meet us, uttering that peculiarly wild and piteous lamentation well known by the name of “the Irish cry,” accompanied throughout by all the customary gesticulation of passionate grief. This rencounter was more awkward than we had at first anticipated; for, upon a nearer approach, the person proved to be no other than an old attached dependent of the family, and who had herself nursed O’Connor. She quickened her pace as we advanced almost to a run; and, throwing her arms round O’Connor’s neck, she poured forth such a torrent of lamentation, reproach, and endearment, as showed that she was aware of the nature of our purpose, whence and by what means I knew not. It was in vain that he sought to satisfy her by evasion, and gently to extricate himself from her embrace. She knelt upon the ground, and clasped her arms round his legs, uttering all the while such touching supplications, such cutting and passionate expressions of woe, as went to my very heart.

===Chinese===
我们一行离开城堡时，夜里那一片寒雾犹在田野上徘徊。那是一个阴冷、凄凉的早晨——一种濛濛的雾气沉甸甸地笼罩着四下，把已经升起的太阳光，化成了一抹苍白、甚至灰蒙蒙的微光。因约定的时辰将至，有人提议我们从一个紧靠看台屋子的地方进入赛马场——这样可以省下近两英里的骑行，免走一段崎岖的路；而离此处两英里开外，才是赛马场的正式入口。于是我们便在此处下了马，把马交给一个恰好这么早就起身走动的乡下汉子照看，便沿着一条窄巷子往前走，预备翻过巷子一边的一道矮墙，进入那片开阔地——如今已废弃的那座屋子便立在那里，决斗便要在那底下进行。我们的去路却被一个意想不到的人影截住了——一个老妇人，披着南部乡下妇人特有的那种鲜红色斗篷——这斗篷是她们最有画意的一件装束——正缓缓顺着林荫道迎着我们走来，嘴里发出那种被称作"爱尔兰式号哭"的、独特的凄厉哀号，自始至终伴着极度悲伤时所有的那一应手势。这一撞见，比我们起初所想的更为棘手；因为走近一看，这人不是别人，正是这家的一个老仆、一个死心塌地跟着这家人的仆妇，她当年还亲自奶过奥康纳。我们越往前走，她便越加快了脚步，几乎是跑着迎上来；她一把搂住奥康纳的脖子，倾泻出那样一通哀号、嗔怪、亲昵交织的洪流——显然，她已经知道我们此行的性质，从何处、以何种方式得知，我便不得而知了。他竭力想用些敷衍的话安抚她，又想轻轻从她怀中挣出来，却是徒然。她跪倒在地，两臂紧紧抱住他的双腿，口中不停地发出那样动人心魄的恳求，那样锥心刺骨、情真意切的悲号——字字句句，都直钻到我心里去。

===Original===
At length, with much difficulty, we passed this most painful interruption; and, crossing the boundary wall, were placed beyond her reach. The O’Gradys damned her for a troublesome hag, and passed on with O’Connor, but I remained behind for a moment. The poor woman looked hopelessly at the high wall which separated her from him she had loved from infancy, and to be with whom at that minute she would have given worlds, she took her seat upon a solitary stone under the opposite wall, and there, in a low, subdued key, she continued to utter her sorrow in words so desolate, yet expressing such a tenderness of devotion as wrung my heart.

“My poor woman,” I said, laying my hand gently upon her shoulder, “you will make yourself ill; the morning is very cold, and your cloak is but a thin defence against the damp and chill. Pray return home and take this; it may be useful to you.”

So saying, I dropped a purse, with what money I had about me, into her lap, but it lay there unheeded; she did not hear me.

“Oh! my child, my child, my darlin’,” she sobbed, “are you gone from me? are you gone from me? Ah, mavourneen, mavourneen, you’ll never come back alive to me again. The crathur that slept on my bosom﻿—the lovin’ crathur that I was so proud of﻿—they’ll kill him, they’ll kill him. Oh, voh! voh!”

The affecting tone, the feeling, the abandonment with which all this was uttered, none can conceive who have not heard the lamentations of the Irish peasantry. It brought tears to my eyes. I saw that no consolation of mine could soothe her grief, so I turned and departed; but as I rapidly traversed the level sward which separated me from my companions, now considerably in advance, I could still hear the wailings of the solitary mourner.

===Chinese===
费了好大的劲，我们终于越过了这一道最为痛心的梗阻；翻过那道界墙，便到了她够不着的地方。奥格雷迪家两位把她骂作一个碍事的老虔婆，便跟着奥康纳径直往前去了，我却落后了一步。那可怜的妇人绝望地望着那道把她与所爱之人隔开的高墙——这个人，她从襁褓之中便爱起；这一刻若能与他在一起，她愿拿整个世界来换——她在对面墙根下的一块孤零零的石头上坐下，低低的、压住嗓门地，继续诉说着她的悲伤，言辞是那样苍凉，却又流露着那样一种献身般的柔情，直拧我的心。

"可怜的大娘，"我说着，轻轻把手搭在她肩上，"您要把自己弄出病来的；早晨这么冷，您这件斗篷又单薄，挡不住这潮气寒气。求您还是回家去吧，把这个收下；也许对您有用。"

说着，我把一个钱袋——里头装着我随身所有的钱——丢到她膝上，可那钱袋就那么搁着，无人理睬；她没有听见我说话。

"啊！我的孩子，我的孩子，我的心肝啊，"她哽咽道，"你就这么离开我了吗？你就这么离开我了吗？啊，我的心肝宝贝，我的心肝宝贝，你再也别想活着回到我身边来了。那个在我怀里睡过的小可怜——那个我是多么引以为傲的、亲爱的小可怜——他们要杀了他，他们要杀了他。啊，呜！呜！"

这番话的动人口吻、那份真情、那种全然忘我的倾泻，未曾亲耳听过爱尔兰乡民哀号之人，是谁也想象不出的。它把眼泪逼到了我的眼眶。我看我这点安慰再也抚不平她的悲伤，便转身走了；可当我快步穿过那片把我与我那已远远在前的同伴们隔开的平整草地时，我仍能听见那孤单哀哭之人一声声的悲号。

===Original===
As we approached the stand-house, it was evident that our antagonists had already arrived. Our path lay by the side of a high fence constructed of loose stones, and on turning a sharp angle at its extremity, we found ourselves close to the appointed spot, and within a few yards of a crowd of persons, some mounted and some on foot, evidently awaiting our arrival. The affair had unaccountably taken wind, as the number of the expectants clearly showed; but for this there was now no remedy.

As our little party advanced we were met and saluted by several acquaintances, whom curiosity, if no deeper feeling, had brought to the place. Fitzgerald and the Captain had arrived, and having dismounted, were standing upon the sod. The former, as we approached, bowed slightly and sullenly﻿—while the latter, evidently in high good humour, made his most courteous obeisance. No time was to be lost; and the two seconds immediately withdrew to a slight distance, for the purpose of completing the last minute arrangements. It was a brief but horrible interval﻿—each returned to his principal to communicate the result, which was soon caught up and repeated from mouth to mouth throughout the crowd. I felt a strange and insurmountable reluctance to hear the sickening particulars detailed; and as I stood irresolute at some distance from the principal parties, a top-booted squireen, with a hunting whip in his hand, bustling up to a companion of his, exclaimed:

“Not fire together!﻿—did you ever hear the like? If Fitzgerald gets the first shot all is over. McDonough sold the pass, by —﻿—﻿—, and that is the long and the short of it.”

===Chinese===
我们走近看台屋子时，显然对方已经到了。我们的路沿着一道用乱石垒成的高篱笆走，走到篱笆尽头一个尖锐的拐角处一转弯，便发觉自己已到了约定地点的近旁，与一群人——有的骑在马上、有的步行——相距不过几码之遥，显然是在等我们到来。这事不知怎的已走漏了风声，看那群等着瞧热闹的人数便一清二楚；事已至此，也无可挽回了。

我们这一小队人走上前去，迎面便遇见好几位熟人，向我们致意——把他们引到这儿来的，即便是没有更深的情感，至少也是好奇。菲茨杰拉德和上尉已经到了，下了马，站在草皮上。我们走近时，前者略略点了点头，神色阴沉——后者呢，分明心情极佳，行了一个最为殷勤的礼。事不宜迟；两位副手立刻退到稍远处，去敲定最后那些细节。这是一段短暂却可怖的间隙——两人各自回到自家委托人身边，传达商定的结果，不多时便被众人拾起，在人群中口口相传。我心里有一种奇异而不可克服的抗拒，不愿去听那些令人作呕的细节；正当我犹豫地站在离当事人稍远的地方时，一个脚蹬高统马靴、手持猎鞭的小乡绅，急匆匆地凑到一个同伴跟前，嚷道：

"不同时开枪！——你几时听过这种事？要是菲茨杰拉德先开枪，那就全完了。麦克多诺把关口卖了，凭——起誓，事情的来龙去脉，便是如此。"

===Original===
The parties now moved down a little to a small level space, suited to the purpose; and the captain, addressing McDonough, said:

“Mr. McDonough, you’ll now have the goodness to toss for choice of ground; as the light comes from the east the line must of course run north and south. Will you be so obliging as to toss up a crown-piece, while I call?”

A coin was instantly chucked into the air. The captain cried, “Harp.” The *head* was uppermost, and McDonough immediately made choice of the southern point at which to place his friend﻿—a position which it will be easily seen had the advantage of turning his back upon the light﻿—no trifling superiority of location. The captain turned with a kind of laugh, and said:

“By —﻿—﻿—, sir, you are as cunning as a dead pig; but you forgot one thing. My friend is a left-handed gunner, though never a bit the worse for that; so you see there is no odds as far as the choice of light goes.”

He then proceeded to measure nine paces in a direction running north and south, and the principals took their ground.

“I must be troublesome to you once again, Mr. McDonough. One toss more, and everything is complete. We must settle who is to have the *first slap*.”

A piece of money was again thrown into the air; again the captain lost the toss and McDonough proceeded to load the pistols. I happened to stand near Fitzgerald, and I overheard the captain, with a chuckle, say something to him in which the word “cravat” was repeated. It instantly occurred to me that the captain’s attention was directed to a bright-coloured muffler which O’Connor wore round his neck, and which would afford his antagonist a distinct and favourable mark. I instantly urged him to remove it, and at length, with difficulty, succeeded. He seemed perfectly careless as to any precaution. Everything was now ready; the pistol was placed in O’Connor’s hand, and he only awaited the word from the captain.

===Chinese===
双方随即稍稍向下移到一小片平整之处，正合用；上尉对麦克多诺说道：

"麦克多诺先生，劳驾您现在抛硬币决定场地之选；因光从东方来，这条线自然得是南北向。可否劳您抛一枚克朗币上来，由我来喊？"

一枚硬币立刻被抛上半空。上尉喊了一声："竖琴。"朝上的是*人头*那一面，麦克多诺便立即选了南端那一点，安排他的朋友就位——这个位置，不难看出，占了一个便宜：背对着光源——这可不是微不足道的一点地利。上尉转过身来，带着几分笑，说道：

"凭——起誓，先生，您可真像头死猪一般精明；可您忘了一件事。我这朋友是个左撇子枪手，虽说一点不比旁人差；您瞧，论光线的选择，这就扯平了。"

于是他量出九步，方向正南北，两位当事人便各就各位。

"还得再烦您一次，麦克多诺先生。再抛一次，一切便妥。我们得定下谁先*开第一枪*。"

一枚钱币再次抛上半空；上尉又输了这一次抛硬币，麦克多诺便着手给手枪装填弹药。我恰巧站在菲茨杰拉德附近，听见上尉得意地嘿嘿一笑，对他说了一句什么，其中"领巾"一词重复了两遍。我顿时想到，上尉的注意力是指向奥康纳脖子上那条颜色鲜亮的围巾——这条围巾会给他对手一个清晰、有利的目标。我立刻劝他取下来，费了好大劲才劝成。他对任何防范都仿佛满不在乎。一切此时俱已齐备；手枪放到了奥康纳手中，他只等上尉一声令下。

===Original===
McCreagh then said:

“Mr. McDonough, is your principal ready?”

McDonough replied in the affirmative; and, after a slight pause, the captain, as had been arranged, uttered the words:

“Ready﻿—fire.”

O’Connor fired, but so wide of the mark that someone in the crowd exclaimed:

“Fired in the air.”

“Who says he fired in the air?” thundered Fitzgerald. “By —﻿—﻿— he lies, whoever he is.” There was a silence. “But even if he was fool enough to fire in the air, it is not in *his* power to put an end to the quarrel by *that*. D﻿—﻿— my soul, if I am come here to be played with like a child, and by the Almighty —﻿—﻿— you shall hear more of this, each and every one of you, before I’m satisfied.”

A kind of low murmur, or rather groan, was now raised, and a slight motion was observable in the crowd, as if to intercept Fitzgerald’s passage to his horse. McCreagh, drawing the horse close to the spot where Fitzgerald stood, threatened, with the most awful imprecations, “to blow the brains out of the first man who should dare to press on them.”

===Chinese===
麦克克里格于是说道：

"麦克多诺先生，您这边准备好了吗？"

麦克多诺答说已准备停当；略略一顿，上尉便按事先所约，喊出了那两个字：

"准备——开枪。"

奥康纳开了枪，却偏离目标太远，人群中有人喊了一声：

"朝天开枪了。"

"谁说他朝天开枪？"菲茨杰拉德怒喝道。"凭——起誓，他是撒谎，不管他是谁。"四下一片沉寂。"可就算他蠢得朝天开枪，他也休想以此了结这场过节。我的灵魂啊，我若真是像个孩子似的被人耍着玩，凭着全能的——起誓，在心满意足之前，你们每一个人，每一个人，都还要听我的下文。"

人群中此刻发出一阵低低的嗡嗡声，不如说是一阵呻吟，并且可见一阵轻微的骚动，仿佛是想拦住菲茨杰拉德去取他的马。麦克克里格把马牵到菲茨杰拉德所站之处近旁，以最骇人的咒骂威胁说，"谁敢挤过来，就先把谁的脑浆轰出来。"

===Original===
O’Connor now interfered, requesting the crowd to forbear, and some degree of order was restored. He then said, “that in firing as he did, he had no intention whatever of waiving his right of firing upon Fitzgerald, and of depriving that gentleman of his right of prosecuting the affair to the utmost﻿—that if any person present imagined that he intended to fire in the air, he begged to set him right; since, so far from seeking to exort an unwilling reconciliation, he was determined that no power on earth should induce him to concede one inch of ground to Mr. Fitzgerald.”

This announcement was received with a shout by the crowd, who now resumed their places at either side of the plot of ground which had been measured. The principals took their places once more, and McCreagh proceeded, with the nicest and most anxious care, to load the pistols; and this task being accomplished, Fitzgerald whispered something in the Captain’s ear, who instantly drew his friend’s horse so as to place him within a step of his rider, and then tightened the girths. This accomplished, Fitzgerald proceeded deliberately to remove his coat, which he threw across his horse in front of the saddle; and then, with the assistance of McCreagh, he rolled the shirt sleeve up to the shoulder, so as to leave the whole of his muscular arm perfectly naked. A cry of “Coward, coward! butcher, butcher!” arose from the crowd. Fitzgerald paused.

“Do you object, Mr. McDonough? and upon what grounds, if you please?” said he.

“Certainly he does not,” replied O’Connor; and, turning to McDonough, he added, “pray let there be no unnecessary delay.”

“There is no objection, then,” said Fitzgerald.

“*I* object,” said the younger of the O’Gradys, “if nobody else will.”

“And who the devil are you, that *dares* to object?” shouted Fitzgerald; “and what d﻿—﻿—﻿d presumption prompts you to *dare* to wag your tongue here?”

“I am Mr. O’Grady, of Castle Blake,” replied the young man, now much enraged; “and by —﻿—﻿—, you shall answer for your language to me.”

===Chinese===
此时奥康纳出面干预，请众人克制，秩序总算恢复了几分。他随即说道，"他方才那样开枪，绝无放弃向菲茨杰拉德开枪之权利的意思，也绝无剥夺这位先生把此事进行到底之权利的意思——在场诸位若有谁以为他有意朝天开枪，他恳请予以纠正；因为，他非但无意强求对方违心和好，而且已下定决心，世间任何力量，都不能叫他向菲茨杰拉德先生退让一寸。"

这一番话赢得人群的一阵喝彩，众人于是各自回到所量出的那块场地两边就位。两位当事人再次就位，麦克克里格便以最为精细、最为审慎的态度，给手枪装填弹药；这一道工序完毕，菲茨杰拉德对上尉耳语了几句什么，上尉立刻把朋友的马牵到离骑手仅一步之遥的地方，又紧了紧马肚带。此事一毕，菲茨杰拉德便不慌不忙地脱下外衣，把它搭在马鞍前面的马身上；然后，在麦克克里格的帮衬之下，把衬衫袖子一直卷到肩头，把整条肌肉虬结的胳膊袒露得精光。人群中响起一阵怒吼："懦夫，懦夫！屠夫，屠夫！"菲茨杰拉德顿了一顿。

"您反对吗，麦克多诺先生？若反对，所据何由，烦请见告？"他说。

"他当然不反对，"奥康纳答道；又转向麦克多诺，补了一句，"请不要作无谓的耽搁。"

"那么，无人反对，"菲茨杰拉德说。

"*我*反对，"奥格雷迪家那位弟弟说道，"若是再没人肯反对的话。"

"你算什么东西，竟*敢*反对？"菲茨杰拉德怒喝道，"又是哪门子该死的胆大妄为，让你*敢*在这里多嘴多舌？"

"我是布莱克城堡（Castle Blake）的奥格雷迪先生（Mr. O'Grady），"那年轻人此时已怒不可遏，答道，"凭着——起誓，你这番话，我要你对我有个交代。"

===Original===
“Shall I, by —﻿—﻿—? Shall I?” cried he, with a laugh of brutal scorn; “the more the merrier, d﻿—﻿—﻿n the doubt of it﻿—so now hold your tongue, for I promise you you shall have business enough of your own to think about, and that before long.”

There was an appalling ferocity in his tone and manner which no words could convey. He seemed transformed; he was actually like a man possessed. Was it possible, I thought, that I beheld the courteous gentleman, the gay, good-humoured retailer of amusing anecdote with whom, scarce two days ago, I had laughed and chatted, in the blasphemous and murderous ruffian who glared and stormed before me!

O’Connor interposed, and requested that time should not be unnecessarily lost.

“You have not got a second coat on?” inquired the Captain. “I beg pardon, but my duty to my friend requires that I should ascertain the point.”

O’Connor replied in the negative. The Captain expressed himself as satisfied, adding, in what he meant to be a complimentary strain, “that he knew Mr. O’Connor would scorn to employ padding or any unfair mode of protection.”

===Chinese===
"我要交代？凭——起誓？我要交代？"他嚷道，发出一阵粗鄙而轻蔑的笑；"人越多越热闹，该死，越多越好——所以你这会儿还是闭嘴吧，我向你保证，用不了多久，你自有够多的麻烦要操心。"

他言语举止间那种骇人的凶蛮，绝非笔墨所能形容。他仿佛变了一个人；活像一个着了魔的人。我心中暗想：难道眼前这个满口亵渎之辞、杀气腾腾的恶棍，竟是我所见到的那一位——那位彬彬有礼的绅士，那位风趣诙谐、妙语如珠的同伴，不过两天之前，我还与他谈笑风生？

奥康纳出面斡旋，请众人不要无故耽搁。

"您没有穿第二件外衣吧？"上尉问道，"失礼了，只是我对我朋友所负的职责，要求我把这一点弄清楚。"

奥康纳答说没有。上尉表示满意，又以一种他自以为是恭维的口吻补充道，"他深知奥康纳先生是不屑于用棉絮之类的不光彩手段护身的。"

===Original===
There was now a breathless silence. O’Connor stood perfectly motionless; and, excepting the deathlike paleness of his features, he exhibited no sign of agitation. His eye was steady﻿—his lip did not tremble﻿—his attitude was calm. The Captain, having reexamined the priming of the pistols, placed one of them in the hand of Fitzgerald.﻿—McDonough inquired whether the parties were prepared, and having been answered in the affirmative, he proceeded to give the word, “Ready.” Fitzgerald raised his hand, but almost instantly lowered it again. The crowd had pressed too much forward as it appeared, and his eye had been unsteadied by the flapping of the skirt of a frieze riding-coat worn by one of the spectators.

“In the name of my principal,” said the Captain, “I must and do insist upon these gentlemen moving back a little. We ask but little; fair play, and no favour.”

The crowd moved as requested. McDonough repeated his former question, and was answered as before. There was a breathless silence. Fitzgerald fixed his eye upon O’Connor. The appointed signal, “Ready, fire!” was given. There was a pause while one might slowly reckon three﻿—Fitzgerald fired﻿—and O’Connor fell helplessly upon the ground.

“There is no time to be lost,” said McCreagh; “for, by —﻿—﻿—, you have done for him.”

So saying, he threw himself upon his horse, and was instantly followed at a hard gallop by Fitzgerald.

“Cold-blooded murder, if ever murder was committed,” said O’Grady. “He shall hang for it; d﻿—﻿—﻿n me, but he shall.”

A hopeless attempt was made to overtake the fugitives; but they were better mounted than any of their pursuers, and escaped with ease. Curses and actual yells of execration followed their course; and as, in crossing the brow of a neighbouring hill, they turned round in the saddle to observe if they were pursued, every gesture which could express fury and defiance was exhausted by the enraged and defeated multitude.

===Chinese===
此时四下里一片屏息的静寂。奥康纳一动不动地站着；除了脸上死人一般的苍白之外，他看不出丝毫激动的痕迹。他的目光沉稳——他的嘴唇不曾颤动——他的姿态是从容的。上尉重新检查过手枪的火药池，把其中一支放到菲茨杰拉德手里。——麦克多诺问双方是否准备妥当，得到肯定的答复之后，他便发出口令："准备。"菲茨杰拉德抬起了手，却又几乎立刻放了下来。原来人群挤得太靠前了，他看不大稳——一位看客所穿粗呢骑装的下摆飘动，晃了他的眼。

"以我委托人的名义，"上尉说道，"我必须、也坚决要求这几位先生稍稍后退。我们所求无多；但求公道，不求偏袒。"

人群依言后退。麦克多诺重复了方才的问题，得到的答复一如其前。四下里一片屏息的静寂。菲茨杰拉德把目光钉在奥康纳身上。约定的信号"准备，开枪！"传了出来。一阵停顿，足够一个人缓缓数到三——菲茨杰拉德开了枪——奥康纳无力地栽倒在地。

"事不宜迟，"麦克克里格说道，"因为，凭——起誓，您是把他了结了。"

说着，他翻身上了马，菲茨杰拉德立刻策马疾驰，紧随其后。

"这是冷血的谋杀，倘若世上真有谋杀这回事的话，"奥格雷迪说，"他得为此上绞架；该死，他一定得为此上绞架。"

众人徒然地试图追赶逃犯；可他们胯下的马，比任何一位追兵所骑的都好，轻而易举便脱了身。咒骂，乃至真正的诅咒号叫，一路追着他们的去路；当他们策马翻过近旁一座山岗的山脊、在马鞍上回过头来观望是否有人追赶时，那群怒不可遏却又吃了败仗的人群，把一切能表达狂怒与挑衅的姿态都使尽了。

===Original===
“Clear the way, boys,” said young O’Grady, who with me was kneeling beside O’Connor, while we supported him in our arms; “do not press so close, and be d﻿—﻿—﻿d; can’t you let the fresh air to him; don’t you see he’s dying?”

On opening his waistcoat we easily detected the wound: it was a little below the chest﻿—a small blue mark, from which oozed a single heavy drop of blood.

“He is bleeding but little﻿—that is a comfort at all events,” said one of the gentlemen who surrounded the wounded man.

Another suggested the expediency of his being removed homeward with as little delay as possible, and recommended, for this purpose, that a door should be removed from its hinges, and the patient, laid upon this, should be conveyed from the field. Upon this rude bier my poor friend was carried from that fatal ground towards Castle Connor. I walked close by his side, and observed every motion of his. He seldom opened his eyes, and was perfectly still, excepting a nervous *working* of the fingers, and a slight, almost imperceptible twitching of the features, which took place, however, only at intervals. The first word he uttered was spoken as we approached the entrance of the castle itself, when he said, repeatedly, “The back way, the back way.” He feared lest his mother should meet him abruptly and without preparation; but although this fear was groundless, since she never left her room until late in the day, yet it was thought advisable, and, indeed, necessary, to caution all the servants most strongly against breathing a hint to their mistress of the events which had befallen.

===Chinese===
"让开，伙计们，"小奥格雷迪说道——他与我都跪在奥康纳身旁，把他搀在臂间；"别挤这么近，该死的；你们就不能让他透口新鲜空气？你们没瞧见他快不行了吗？"

解开他的马甲，我们轻易便找到了伤口：在胸膛下方一点——一个青色的小印，渗出一滴沉甸甸的血珠。

"他出血不多——无论如何，这总算是个安慰，"围在伤者身边的一位绅士说道。

另一位则建议，务须尽快把他送回家去，为此，他提议把一扇门从合页上卸下来，让伤者躺在上面，从场地上抬走。我那可怜的朋友，便在这副简陋的担架上，被抬出了那片要命的地方，朝康纳城堡抬去。我紧紧走在担架旁，留意着他每一个动作。他很少睁开眼睛，除此之外纹丝不动，只是手指有一种神经质的*抽动*，脸上也微微地、几乎难以察觉地抽搐着——不过这都只是断断续续地发作。他说的第一句话，是在我们快到城堡门口时——他反复地说："走后门，走后门。"他怕他母亲毫无准备地、突然撞见他；不过这一层担心其实是多余的，因为她那天要到很晚才会离开自己的房间；即便如此，大家仍认为有必要——实属必要——严厉叮嘱所有的仆人，绝不可向夫人透半点口风，提及所发生的这一切。

===Original===
Two or three gentlemen had ridden from the field one after another, promising that they should overtake our party before it reached the castle, bringing with them medical aid from one quarter or another; and we determined that Mrs. O’Connor should not know anything of the occurrence until the opinion of some professional man should have determined the extent of the injury which her son had sustained﻿—a course of conduct which would at least have the effect of relieving her from the horrors of suspense. When O’Connor found himself in his own room, and laid upon his own bed, he appeared much revived﻿—so much so, that I could not help admitting a strong hope that all might yet be well.

“After all, Purcell,” said he, with a melancholy smile, and speaking with evident difficulty, “I believe I have got off with a trifling wound. I am sure it cannot be fatal I feel so little pain﻿—almost none.”

I cautioned him against fatiguing himself by endeavouring to speak; and he remained quiet for a little time. At length he said:

“Purcell, I trust this lesson shall not have been given in vain. God has been very merciful to me; I feel﻿—I have an internal confidence that I am not wounded mortally. Had I been fatally wounded﻿—had I been killed upon the spot, only think on it”﻿—and he closed his eyes as if the very thought made him dizzy﻿—“struck down into the grave, unprepared as I am, in the very blossom of my sins, without a moment of repentance or of reflection; I must have been lost﻿—lost forever and ever.”

I prevailed upon him, with some difficulty, to abstain from such agitating reflections, and at length induced him to court such repose as his condition admitted of, by remaining perfectly silent, and as much as possible without motion.

===Chinese===
有两三位绅士，一个接一个地骑马离了场，承诺说会在我们一行到达城堡之前追上我们，从这一方或那一方带来医生；我们议定，在某某一位内行判定她儿子所受创伤之轻重之前，绝不可让奥康纳夫人知道这件事——这一处置，至少可使她免受那种悬而未决的恐怖煎熬。待奥康纳回到自己的房间、躺到自己的床上，他似乎精神大振——振得我竟忍不住生出一丝强烈的希望：也许一切还来得及。

"说到底，珀塞尔，"他说，露出一个忧郁的微笑，说话明显十分吃力，"我想我这不过是挨了一道轻伤。我肯定它要不了命——我几乎感觉不到痛——几乎没有。"

我叮嘱他切莫因费力说话而劳累了自己；他便安静了一阵。末了他说道：

"珀塞尔，我相信这一课不会白白地受过。上帝对我实在是慈悲；我觉得——我有一种内心的把握，我伤得并不致命。倘若我伤得致命——倘若我当场便被打死，你只想想看——"他说着便闭上了眼睛，仿佛光是这个念头就叫人头晕——"就被这样打进了坟里，毫无准备，正深陷在罪孽之中，连一刻忏悔、一刻反省的工夫都没有；那我便万劫不复了——万劫不复，永永远远。"

我颇费了一番口舌，才劝住他不再作这样激动的回想，终于劝得他尽量地静养——保持完全的沉默，并尽量不动。

===Original===
O’Connor and I only were in the room; he had lain for some time in tolerable quiet, when I thought I distinguished the bustle attendant upon the arrival of someone at the castle, and went eagerly to the window, believing, or at least hoping, that the sounds might announce the approach of the medical man, whom we all longed most impatiently to see.

My conjecture was right; I had the satisfaction of seeing him dismount and prepare to enter the castle, when my observations were interrupted, and my attention was attracted by a smothered, gurgling sound proceeding from the bed in which lay the wounded man. I instantly turned round, and in doing so the spectacle which met my eyes was sufficiently shocking.

I had left O’Connor lying in the bed, supported by pillows, perfectly calm, and with his eyes closed: he was now lying nearly in the same position, his eyes open and almost starting from their sockets, with every feature pale and distorted as death, and vomiting blood in quantities that were frightful. I rushed to the door and called for assistance; the paroxysm, though violent, was brief, and O’Connor sank into a swoon so deep and deathlike, that I feared he should waken no more.

===Chinese===
房间里只有我与奥康纳两人；他相当安静地躺了一阵，我忽而觉得我听见了城堡里有人到来的那一阵动静，便急忙走到窗前，以为——至少是希望——那动静是宣告那位我们众人望眼欲穿的医生的到来。

我猜得不错；我欣慰地看见他下了马、正要进城堡——可就在这时，我的观察被打断了，我的注意被一种沉闷的、咕噜咕噜的声音吸引了过去，那声音从伤者所躺的床上传来。我立刻转过身去——这一转身，映入眼帘的那一幕，实在够叫人触目惊心。

方才我离开奥康纳时，他还倚着枕头躺在床上，十分安详，双目微阖：此刻他几乎还是那一个姿势躺着，眼睛却睁得大大的，几乎要从眼眶里暴出来，每一道五官都如死人一般苍白、扭曲，正大口大口地呕吐着鲜血，那血量之大，令人不寒而栗。我冲到门口呼唤人来帮忙；这一阵发作虽烈，却很短暂，奥康纳随即陷入了一种深而类死的昏厥，我生怕他再也醒不过来了。

===Original===
The surgeon, a little, fussy man, but I believe with some skill to justify his pretensions, now entered the room, carrying his case of instruments, and followed by servants bearing basins and water and bandages of linen. He relieved our doubts by instantly assuring us that “the patient” was still living; and at the same time professed his determination to take advantage of the muscular relaxation which the faint had induced to examine the wound﻿—adding that a patient was more easily “handled” when in a swoon than under other circumstances.

After examining the wound in front where the ball had entered, he passed his hand round beneath the shoulder, and after a little pause he shook his head, observing that he feared very much that one of the vertebrae was fatally injured, but that he could not say decidedly until his patient should revive a little. Though his language was very technical, and consequently to me nearly unintelligible, I could perceive plainly by his manner that he considered the case as almost hopeless.

O’Connor gradually gave some signs of returning animation, and at length was so far restored as to be enabled to speak. After some few general questions as to how he felt affected, etc., etc., the surgeon, placing his hand upon his leg and pressing it slightly, asked him if he felt any pressure upon the limb? O’Connor answered in the negative﻿—he pressed harder, and repeated the question; still the answer was the same, till at length, by repeated experiments, he ascertained that all that part of the body which lay behind the wound was paralysed, proving that the spine must have received some fatal injury.

===Chinese===
医生进来了——他是个矮小、忙忙叨叨的男人，但我相信他多少有些本事，足以印证他的自负——他提着那匣器械，身后跟着端着盆、水、亚麻绷带的仆人们。他立刻让我们放下心来，向我们保证"病人"还活着；同时又声称，他决意要趁着昏厥所引起的肌肉松弛来查看伤口——还说，病人在昏迷之时比在别的情形下更易于"上手"处置。

他先查看了正面子弹射入处的伤口，又把手伸到肩胛下面去摸索，顿了一顿，摇了摇头，说恐怕有一节脊椎已受了致命的损伤，但要等病人略略苏醒之后，才能断言。他这话虽满是术语，因而对我而言几乎不知所云，但从他的神色我分明可以看出，他已把这一例视作几乎没有指望。

奥康纳渐渐地显出几分回苏的迹象，终于恢复到可以开口说话了。问过几句关于他自觉如何等等的寻常话之后，医生便把手按到他腿上，轻轻一按，问他这条腿可觉得有压力？奥康纳答说没有——他按得重了些，又问了一遍；回答仍是一样；这样反复试了几回，终于查明，伤口以下、身躯后部的那一片已全然瘫痪——可见脊柱必已受了某种致命的损伤。

===Original===
“Well, doctor,” said O’Connor, after the examination of the wound was over; “well, I shall do, shan’t I?”

The physician was silent for a moment, and then, as if with an effort, he replied:

“Indeed, my dear sir, it would not be honest to flatter you with much hope.”

“Eh?” said O’Connor with more alacrity than I had seen him exhibit since the morning; “surely I did not hear you aright; I spoke of my recovery﻿—surely there is no doubt; there can be none﻿—speak frankly, doctor, for God’s sake﻿—am I dying?”

The surgeon was evidently no stoic, and his manner had extinguished in me every hope, even before he had uttered a word in reply.

“You are﻿—you are indeed dying. There is no hope; I should but deceive you if I held out any.”

As the surgeon uttered these terrible words, the hands which O’Connor had stretched towards him while awaiting his reply fell powerless by his side; his head sank forward; it seemed as if horror and despair had unstrung every nerve and sinew; he appeared to collapse and shrink together as a plant might under the influence of a withering spell.

===Chinese===
"那么，医生，"查完伤口之后，奥康纳问道，"那么，我能挺过去，对吧？"

医生沉默了片刻，似乎竭了一把力，才答道：

"实在说，我亲爱的先生，给您太多希望，便是不诚实了。"

"嗯？"奥康纳说道，其爽利是那天早晨以来我未曾见过的；"我一定是听错了；我说的是我能不能好起来——这事总该没有疑问吧；一定没有疑问——请您直说吧，医生，看在上帝份上——我是不是要死了？"

这位医生显然不是个铁石心肠的人，而他的神气，早在他说出一个字的回答之前，便已把我心中最后一线希望都掐灭了。

"您是——您确乎是要死了。毫无指望；我若给您一线希望，那便是在欺骗您。"

当医生说出这几句可怕的话时，奥康纳方才向他伸出去等候回答的那双手，无力地垂到了身侧；他的头向前垂了下去；仿佛惊恐与绝望已把他每一根神经、每一根筋腱都尽数松开了；他整个人仿佛塌了下去、缩成一团，正如一株植物在某种枯萎咒术之下所发生的那样。

===Original===
It has often been my fate, since then, to visit the chambers of death and of suffering; I have witnessed fearful agonies of body and of soul; the mysterious shudderings of the departing spirit, and the heartrending desolation of the survivors; the severing of the tenderest ties, the piteous yearnings of unavailing love﻿—of all these things the sad duties of my profession have made me a witness. But, generally speaking, I have observed in such scenes something to mitigate, if not the sorrows, at least the terrors, of death; the dying man seldom seems to feel the reality of his situation; a dull consciousness of approaching dissolution, a dim anticipation of unconsciousness and insensibility, are the feelings which most nearly border upon an appreciation of his state; the film of death seems to have overspread the mind’s eye, objects lose their distinctness, and float cloudily before it, and the apathy and apparent indifference with which men recognise the sure advances of immediate death, rob that awful hour of much of its terrors, and the deathbed of its otherwise inevitable agonies.

This is a merciful dispensation; but the rule has its exceptions﻿—its terrible exceptions. When a man is brought in an instant, by some sudden accident, to the very verge of the fathomless pit of death, with all his recollections awake, and his perceptions keenly and vividly alive, without previous illness to subdue the tone of the mind as to dull its apprehensions﻿—then, and then only, the deathbed is truly terrible.

===Chinese===
自那以后，探访死亡与苦难之所，便常是我的命数；我见过肉身与灵魂种种可怖的煎熬；临终之灵那不可解的颤栗，生者那肝肠寸断的凄凉；最亲密之情的生生割断，那徒劳之爱最为哀切的渴慕——凡此种种，我这圣职的悲苦本分，都叫我成了见证者。然而一般说来，在这种种场面之中，我总见到有几分东西，纵不能减轻死亡的悲愁，至少也能减轻死亡的恐惧；临终之人似乎很少真切的感到自身处境之实在；对将近的消亡的一种朦胧意识，对即将失去知觉、失去感受的一种隐约预感，已是他所能体会自身处境的最近的一步了；死亡的翳膜似乎已罩住了心灵之眼，万物失了它们的清晰，朦胧地在其前飘浮，而人们识得眼前必死的步步逼近时那种麻木与表面上的淡然，从那可怖的一刻夺去了大半的恐怖，也从临终之榻夺去了别种情形下所不可避免的煎熬。

这是一种仁慈的安排；然而此例也有其例外——其骇人的例外。当一个人因某桩突如其来的灾祸，转瞬之间便被推到死亡那无底深渊的边上，全部的记忆都醒着，全部的知觉都敏锐而鲜活地醒着，又没有先期的疾病来挫抑心气、钝化其预感——这时，也唯独这时，临终之榻才是真正可怖的。

===Original===
Oh, what a contrast did O’Connor afford as he lay in all the abject helplessness of undisguised terror upon his deathbed, to the proud composure with which he had taken the field that morning. I had always before thought of death as of a quiet sleep stealing gradually upon exhausted nature, made welcome by suffering, or, at least, softened by resignation; I had never before stood by the side of one upon whom the hand of death had been thus suddenly laid; I had never seen the tyrant arrayed in his terror till then. Never before or since have I seen horror so intensely depicted. It seemed actually as if O’Connor’s mind had been unsettled by the shock; the few words he uttered were marked with all the incoherence of distraction; but it was not words that marked his despair most strongly, the appalling and heart-sickening groans that came from the terror-stricken and dying man must haunt me while I live; the expression, too, of hopeless, imploring agony with which he turned his eyes from object to object, I can never forget. At length, appearing suddenly to recollect himself, he said, with startling alertness, but in a voice so altered that I scarce could recognise the tones:

“Purcell, Purcell, go and tell my poor mother; she must know all, and then, quick, quick, quick, call your uncle, bring him here; I must have a chance.” He made a violent but fruitless effort to rise, and after a slight pause continued, with deep and urgent solemnity: “Doctor, how long shall I live? Don’t flatter me. Compliments at a deathbed are out of place; doctor, for God’s sake, as you would not have my soul perish with my body, do not mock a dying man; have I an hour to live?”

“Certainly,” replied the surgeon; “if you will but endeavour to keep yourself tranquil; otherwise I cannot answer for a moment.”

“Well, doctor,” said the patient, “I will obey you; now, Purcell, my first and dearest friend, will you inform my poor mother of﻿—of what you see, and return with your uncle; I know you will.”

===Chinese===
啊，奥康纳临终之时，毫无掩饰地躺在那赤裸裸的恐怖之中，一副惨然的、无依无靠的模样——这与那天早晨他走上决斗场时所带着的那副骄傲而镇定的气度，形成了何等的对照。在此之前，我总把死亡想作是一场悄然袭向疲惫身心的安眠，因苦难而为人所乐见，或者至少为顺从之心所柔化；我从未站在一个被死亡之手如此骤然按上之人的身旁；我从未见过这位暴君以它的恐怖全副武装起来——直到那一刻。无论此前此后，我从未见过如此强烈的恐惧显在一张脸上。简直像是奥康纳的心神已被这一击所搅乱；他所说的那几句话，都带着失魂落魄的颠三倒四；然而最能标出他绝望的，并非言语，从这个被恐惧攫住的垂死之人身上发出的那种骇人的、令人心碎的呻吟，必将在我的有生之年萦绕不去；他绝望而无助、哀求似的苦痛之中，把目光从这一物移到那一物的那个神情，我也永世不能忘怀。终于，他仿佛忽然清醒过来，以一种令人一惊的机敏说道，但嗓音已变得我几乎认不出来：

"珀塞尔，珀塞尔，去告诉我那可怜的母亲；她必须知道一切，然后，快，快，快，去叫你叔父，把他带到这儿来；我必须有个机会。"他猛烈却徒劳地挣扎着想坐起来，略略一顿，又以一种深沉而迫切的庄严继续说道："医生，我还能活多久？不要奉承我。临终之榻上的客套是失当的；医生，看在上帝份上，您既不愿我的灵魂随我的肉身一同沉沦，就请莫要戏弄一个垂死之人；我还有一个钟点可活吗？"

"当然，"医生答道，"只要您能尽力保持心神镇定；不然，我连一刻也不敢担保。"

"好吧，医生，"那病人说，"我听从您；现在，珀塞尔，我最早、最亲爱的朋友，你可愿去把我那可怜的母亲——把她所见之事告知于她，然后与你叔父一同回来；我知道你愿意的。"

===Original===
I took the dear fellow’s hand and kissed it, it was the only answer I could give, and left the room. I asked the first female servant I chanced to meet, if her mistress were yet up, and was answered in the affirmative. Without giving myself time to hesitate, I requested her to lead me to her lady’s room, which she accordingly did; she entered first, I supposed to announce my name, and I followed closely; the poor mother said something, and held out her hands to welcome me; I strove for words; I could not speak, but nature found expression; I threw myself at her feet and covered her hands with kisses and tears. My manner was enough; with a quickness almost preternatural she understood it all; she simply said the words: “O’Connor is killed;” she uttered no more.

How I left the room I know not; I rode madly to my uncle’s residence, and brought him back with me﻿—all the rest is a blank. I remember standing by O’Connor’s bedside, and kissing the cold pallid forehead again and again; I remember the pale serenity of the beautiful features; I remember that I looked upon the dead face of my friend, and I remember no more.

===Chinese===
我握住这可亲可爱的朋友的手，凑到唇边吻了吻——这是我所能给的唯一回答——便出了房门。我向所遇见的第一个女仆打听，她家夫人是否已经起身，得到了肯定的答复。我不容自己犹豫，便请她领我到夫人房里去，她便依言领了我去；她先进去，我猜是去通报我的姓名，我紧随其后；那可怜的母亲说了句什么，伸出双手来欢迎我；我竭力想找句话来说；我说不出话来，但天性找到了表达；我扑到她脚前，把她的双手吻个不住，泪水洒了一手。我的神情已足够说明一切；她以一种近乎超自然的敏捷，顿时全都明白了；她只说了这么一句话："奥康纳死了；"此外再无一言。

我是怎么离开那间屋子的，我自己也不知道；我疯了一般骑马赶到叔父住处，把他带了回来——余下的一切，都是一片空白。我只记得我站在奥康纳床边，一遍又一遍地吻那张冰冷、苍白的前额；我只记得那张美丽的脸上，那一种苍白的安详；我只记得我望着我的朋友那张已死之人的脸——此外我什么都不记得了。

===Original===
For many months I lay writhing and raving in the frenzy of brain fever; a hundred times I stood tottering at the brink of death, and long after my restoration to bodily health was assured, it appeared doubtful whether I should ever be restored to reason. But God dealt very mercifully with me; His mighty hand rescued me from death and from madness when one or other appeared inevitable. As soon as I was permitted pen and ink, I wrote to the bereaved mother in a tone bordering upon frenzy. I accused myself of having made her childless; I called myself a murderer; I believed myself accursed; I could not find terms strong enough to express my abhorrence of my own conduct. But, oh! what an answer I received, so mild, so sweet, from the desolate, childless mother! its words spoke all that is beautiful in Christianity﻿—it was forgiveness﻿—it was resignation. I am convinced that to that letter, operating as it did upon a mind already predisposed, is owing my final determination to devote myself to that profession in which, for more than half a century, I have been a humble minister.

===Chinese===
一连许多个月，我辗转呓语，陷在脑热病的狂乱之中；上百次我踉跄地站在死亡的边缘；而在我身体的健康确定恢复之后很久，我是否能恢复理智，仍属可疑。然而上帝对我实在是慈悲；他那大能之手，在死亡与疯狂二者之一仿佛已无可避免之时，把我从两者之中救拔了出来。我一获允使用笔墨，便以一种近乎癫狂的口吻，写信给那位失去独子的母亲。我控诉自己害她没了孩子；我骂自己是杀人凶手；我相信自己受了诅咒；我想不出足够强烈的字眼，来表达我对自己所作所为的憎恶。然而，啊！我所收到的回信，是何等的一封回信——那样温和，那样甜美，出自那位凄凉无子的母亲之手！信中的话，道尽了基督教一切之美——那是宽恕——那是顺命。我深信，正是那封信——它在一个早已有所准备的心智之上发挥了作用——使我最终立下了献身于这一圣职的决心；半个多世纪以来，我便是在这一圣职之中，做一个微贱的仆人。

===Original===
Years roll away, and we count them not as they pass, but their influence is not the less certain that it is silent; the deepest wounds are gradually healed, the keenest griefs are mitigated, and we, in character, feelings, tastes, and pursuits, become such altered beings, that but for some few indelible marks which past events must leave behind them, which time may soften, but can never efface; our very identity would be dubious. Who has not felt all this at one time or other? Who has not mournfully felt it? This trite, but natural train of reflection filled my mind as I approached the domain of Castle Connor some ten years after the occurrence of the events above narrated. Everything looked the same as when I had left it; the old trees stood as graceful and as grand as ever; no plough had violated the soft green sward; no utilitarian hand had constrained the wanderings of the clear and sportive stream, or disturbed the lichen-covered rocks through which it gushed, or the wild coppice that overshadowed its sequestered nooks﻿—but the eye that looked upon these things was altered, and memory was busy with other days, shrouding in sadness every beauty that met my sight.

===Chinese===
岁月流转，我们并不去数它经过的脚步，然而它那无声的影响，并不因其无声便有丝毫减损；最深的伤口渐渐愈合，最烈的悲恸渐渐平复，而我们——在性情、情感、趣味与所务之上——竟化作判若两人之辈，若不是往事必会留下的一些不可磨灭的印记——时间或可使之柔和，却永不能将其抹去——则我们这身分本身都将叫人狐疑。谁不曾一度有过这样的感触？谁又不曾怀着哀愁有过这样的感触？这一串寻常却又出诸本然的思绪，充盈着我的心——那时我正走近康纳城堡的地界，距上述事件的发生，已过了约莫十年。一切都如我离去时那样；老树依旧如往日一般优雅而庄严地伫立着；没有犁铧亵渎过那一片柔软的绿茵；没有那一双功利之手，曾去约束那清澈、活泼的小溪的曲折流淌，或曾惊扰它所穿流而过的、覆着苔藓的岩石，或曾惊扰为它那幽僻的角落投下浓荫的野林——然而，望着这一切的那双眼睛，已经变了；而记忆正忙于别个年月，把每一桩映入我眼帘的美，都笼罩上了一层悲伤。

===Original===
As I approached the castle my emotions became so acutely painful that I had almost returned the way I came, without accomplishing the purpose for which I had gone thus far; and nothing but the conviction that my having been in the neighbourhood of Castle Connor without visiting its desolate mistress would render me justly liable to the severest censure, could overcome my reluctance to encountering the heavy task which was before me. I recognised the old servant who opened the door, but he did not know me. I was completely changed; suffering of body and mind had altered me in feature and in bearing, as much as in character. I asked the man whether his mistress ever saw visitors. He answered:

“But seldom; perhaps, however, if she knew that an old friend wished to see her for a few minutes, she would gratify him so far.”

At the same time I placed my card in his hand, and requested him to deliver it to his mistress. He returned in a few moments, saying that his lady would be happy to see me in the parlour, and I accordingly followed him to the door, which he opened. I entered the room, and was in a moment at the side of my early friend and benefactress. I was too much agitated to speak; I could only hold the hands which she gave me, while, spite of every effort, the tears flowed fast and bitterly.

“It was kind, very, very kind of you to come to see me,” she said, with far more composure than I could have commanded; “I see it is very painful to you.”

===Chinese===
待我走到城堡近前，心中的情感已痛切得叫人难以承受，我几乎要原路折返，连此行远来的目的也不顾了；唯有一种想法支撑着我——倘若我身在康纳城堡左近却不来探访它那凄凉的女主人，我便理所当然地该受最严厉的责难——唯有这一念头，方能克服我心头对眼前这桩沉重任务的抵触。开门的老仆我认得出来，可他已不认得我了。我已全然改了模样；身心的苦难，在我的容貌和气度上所造成的变化，一如在我的性情上那样。我问那人，他家夫人可曾见客。他答道：

"难得一见了；不过，倘若她得知有一位老友愿意见她几分钟，她大概会赏这个面子的。"

说着，我把名片放到他手里，请他转交夫人。他不多时便回来说，夫人乐意在客厅里见我；我便跟着他走到客厅门口，他把门打开。我走进屋里，转眼便到了我这位早年的朋友、这位恩主的身旁。我激动得说不出话来；只能握着她伸过来的那双手，而泪水却不管怎样克制，还是止不住地、苦涩地流下来。

"您能来看我，真是太好了，太、太好了，"她说道，那镇定远非我所能企及；"我看，这对您来说是十分痛苦的事。"

===Original===
I endeavoured to compose myself, and for a little time we remained silent; she was the first to speak:

“You will be surprised, Mr. Purcell, when you observe the calmness with which I can speak of him who was dearest to me, who is gone; but my thoughts are always with him, and the recollections of his love”—her voice faltered a little—“and the hope of meeting him hereafter enables me to bear existence.”

I said I know not what; something about resignation, I believe.

“I hope I am resigned; God made me more so,” she said. “Oh, Mr. Purcell, I have often thought I loved my lost child *too* well. It was natural﻿—he was my only child﻿—he was﻿—” She could not proceed for a few moments: “It was very natural that I should love him as I did; but it may have been sinful; I have often thought so. I doted upon him﻿—I idolised him﻿—I thought too little of other holier affections; and God may have taken him from me, only to teach me, by this severe lesson, that I owed to heaven a larger share of my heart than to anything earthly. I cannot think of him now without more solemn feelings than if he were with me. There is something holy in our thoughts of the dead; I feel it so.” After a pause, she continued﻿—“Mr. Purcell, do you remember his features well? they were very beautiful.” I assured her that I did. “Then you can tell me if you think this a faithful likeness.” She took from a drawer a case in which lay a miniature. I took it reverently from her hands; it was indeed very like﻿—touchingly like. I told her so; and she seemed gratified.

===Chinese===
我竭力定下心来，有一会儿，我们相对无言；是她先开口：

"珀塞尔先生，您见我能这样平静地谈到那个于我最亲最爱、却已离世的人，一定会觉得诧异；然而我的思念总与他同在，而一想到他对我的爱——"她的声音微微颤了一下——"一想到日后还能与他重聚，这希望便使我还能撑着活下去。"

我说了些什么，自己也不甚了然；大约是关于顺命的话吧。

"我希望我是顺命的；是上帝使我更加顺命了，"她说。"啊，珀塞尔先生，我时常想，我是太爱那个失去的孩子了。这是人之常情——他是我唯一的孩子——他是——"她好一会儿说不出话来："我那样爱他，原是极其自然的；可是，这也许是有罪的；我常常这样想。我宠他——我敬他如神明——我把别的更神圣的情感看得太轻了；上帝之所以把他从我身边带走，也许只是为了借这一番严酷的教训告诉我：我对上天所欠的那份心，本该比对世间任何事物都要多。如今我一想到他，便不能不怀着比他还在我身边时更为庄重的情怀。我们思念亡者之时，其中总带着几分神圣；我是这般感觉的。"顿了一顿，她接着说——"珀塞尔先生，您可还记得他的容貌吗？他生得是很美的。"我向她保证我记得。"那么您能告诉我，您觉得这一幅像画得像不像。"她从一只抽屉里取出一只小匣，匣中放着一幅袖珍画像。我恭而敬之地从她手中接过；那确是极像——动人地像。我如此告诉她；她似乎颇感欣慰。

===Original===
As the evening was wearing fast, and I had far to go, I hastened to terminate my visit, as I had intended, by placing in her hand a letter from her son to me, written during his sojourn upon the Continent. I requested her to keep it; it was one in which he spoke much of her, and in terms of the tenderest affection. As she read its contents the heavy tears gathered in her eyes, and fell, one by one, upon the page; she wiped them away, but they still flowed fast and silently. It was in vain that she tried to read it; her eyes were filled with tears: so she folded the letter, and placed it in her bosom. I rose to depart, and she also rose.

“I will not ask you to delay your departure,” said she; “your visit here must have been a painful one to you. I cannot find words to thank you for the letter as I would wish, or for all your kindness. It has given me a pleasure greater than I thought could have fallen to the lot of a creature so very desolate as I am; may God bless you for it!” And thus we parted; I never saw Castle Connor or its solitary inmate more.

===Chinese===
天色将晚，我又有远路要走，便如我原先所打算的那样，赶紧结束这次拜访——我把她儿子当年旅居欧陆之时写给我的一封信，放到了她的手里。我请她留下这封信；信中他多处谈到她，措辞至为温存。她读着信的内容，沉甸甸的泪珠涌上眼眶，一滴一滴地落在信纸上；她把它们拭去，可泪水仍是涌得又急又无声。她想读下去，却是徒然；她的眼里已满是泪水：于是她把信折好，揣进怀里。我起身告辞，她也站起身来。

"我就不留您了，"她说，"您这一趟来，想必是十分痛苦的了。这封信，您对我的种种好意，我找不出话来按我的心意谢您。这一番心意给了我一份快乐，远胜过我以为像我这样凄凉的一个人，还能分得到的；愿上帝为此赐福给您！"我们就这样分别了；康纳城堡，以及它那位形单影只的主人，我此后再未见过。

## “The Quare Gander” Being a Twelfth Extract from the Legacy of the Late Francis Purcell, P.P. of Drumcoolagh. / “那只古怪的老鹅”——已故德鲁姆库拉教区神父弗朗西斯·珀塞尔遗稿之第十二则摘录。

===Original===
As I rode at a slow walk, one soft autumn evening, from the once noted and noticeable town of Emly, now a squalid village, towards the no less remarkable town of Tipperary, I fell into a meditative mood.

My eye wandered over a glorious landscape; a broad sea of cornfields, that might have gladdened even a golden age, was waving before me; groups of little cabins, with their poplars, osiers, and light mountain ashes, clustered shelteringly around them, were scattered over the plain; the thin blue smoke arose floating through their boughs in the still evening air. And far away with all their broad lights and shades, softened with the haze of approaching twilight, stood the bold wild Galties.

As I gazed on this scene, whose richness was deepened by the melancholy glow of the setting sun, the tears rose to my eyes, and I said:

“Alas, my country! what a mournful beauty is thine. Dressed in loveliness and laughter, there is mortal decay at thy heart: sorrow, sin, and shame have mingled thy cup of misery. Strange rulers have bruised thee, and laughed thee to scorn, and they have made all thy sweetness bitter. Thy shames and sins are the austere fruits of thy miseries, and thy miseries have been poured out upon thee by foreign hands. Alas, my stricken country! clothed with this most pity-moving smile, with this most unutterably mournful loveliness, thou sore-grieved, thou desperately-beloved! Is there for thee, my country, a resurrection?”

===Chinese===
一个柔和的秋日黄昏，我骑马缓行，从昔日赫赫有名、引人注目的埃姆利镇——如今不过是一处破败的村落——朝着一毫不逊其声名的蒂珀雷里镇（Tipperary）而去，途中不觉陷入了一种沉思的心绪。

我的目光在一片壮丽的景色上流连；一望无际的麦田如汪洋般在我面前起伏摇荡，纵是黄金时代的人见了，怕也要满心欢喜；成群的小茅屋，伴着各自的杨树、柳树和轻盈的山梣，簇拥相护般聚拢在屋的四周，星星点点散落在平原之上；一缕缕淡蓝的炊烟在静寂的暮气里升腾，从那些枝丫间悠悠穿过。而远处，那一道道明暗相间的阔大光影，在渐近薄暮的轻霭中变得柔和，那雄浑粗犷的盖尔蒂山脉（Galties）便矗立在那里。

我凝望着眼前这幅景象——落日那一抹苍凉的余晖，将它的丰饶衬得愈发深沉——泪水不觉涌上了眼眶，我喃喃自语道：

“唉，我的祖国！你拥有的是一种何等令人哀伤的美。你披着可爱与欢笑的衣裳，心口却怀着致命的腐朽：忧愁、罪恶与羞辱，早已搅和成你那杯苦酒。异族的统治者揉躏了你，嘲弄了你，将你一切的美好都化作苦涩。你的羞辱与罪恶，不过是你的苦难所结出的冷峻之果，而你的苦难，乃是自外族之手倾泻到你身上的。唉，我那伤痕累累的祖国！披着这一袭最令人心生怜惜的微笑，带着这一身最难以言喻的凄艳之美，你这痛彻肺腑的、你这爱之欲狂的所在！我的祖国，你可有复活重生的一日么？”

===Original===
I know not how long I might have continued to rhapsodize in this strain, had not my wandering thoughts been suddenly recalled to my own immediate neighbourhood by the monotonous clatter of a horse’s hoofs upon the road, evidently moving, at that peculiar pace which is neither a walk nor a trot, and yet partakes of both, so much in vogue among the southern farmers.

In a moment my pursuer was up with me, and checking his steed into a walk he saluted me with much respect. The cavalier was a light-built fellow, with good-humoured sunburnt features, a shrewd and lively black eye, and a head covered with a crop of close curly black hair, and surmounted with a turf-coloured caubeen, in the packthread band of which was stuck a short pipe, which had evidently seen much service.

My companion was a dealer in all kinds of local lore, and soon took occasion to let me see that he was so.

After two or three short stories, in which the scandalous and the supernatural were happily blended, we happened to arrive at a narrow road or bohreen leading to a snug-looking farmhouse.

“That’s a comfortable bit iv a farm,” observed my comrade, pointing towards the dwelling with his thumb; “a shnug spot, and belongs to the Mooneys this long time. ’Tis a noted place for what happened wid the famous gandher there in former times.”

“And what was that?” inquired I.

“What was it happened wid the gandher!” ejaculated my companion in a tone of indignant surprise; “the gandher iv Ballymacrucker, the gandher! Your raverance must be a stranger in these parts. Sure every fool knows all about the gandher, and Terence Mooney, that was, rest his sowl. Begorra, ’tis surprisin’ to me how in the world you didn’t hear iv the gandher; and may be it’s funnin me ye are, your raverance.”

===Chinese===
我不知道自己满可以照这副腔调一路感慨下去多久，要不是马蹄在道上发出那单调的嘚嘚声，把我这四处游移的思绪猛然唤回了眼前——那蹄声分明是以一种古怪的步子行进：既非慢走，亦非快跑，却二者兼而有之，这等步法在南方的农户中间极为风行。

转眼间，追上来的人已与我并辔，他勒住坐骑放缓为慢步，极恭敬地向我见礼。这位骑客是个身形瘦削利落的小伙子，一副被日头晒得黝黑的面孔透着和气，一双精明灵动的黑眼睛，满头密密卷曲的黑发，头上扣着一顶草皮色的旧软帽（caubeen），帽子的 packthread 布带里插着一管短烟斗，那烟斗看去分明已用了不少年月。

我这同伴是各种乡野掌故的行家，不多时便寻了话头，有意让我瞧出他这一点。

他讲了两三个短篇故事，把那伤风败俗的与超自然的巧妙地揉在一处——讲罢，我们恰巧来到一条通向一座外观齐整农舍的窄路，或者照当地的叫法，一条小径（bohereen）跟前。

“那可是块舒坦的小田产，”我的同伴用大拇指朝那宅子一挑，说道，“一处安生之所，老早就归穆尼家（the Mooneys）所有了。这地方可出名呢，就为从前在那只大名鼎鼎的老鹅身上出过一桩事。”

“出了什么事？”我问道。

“在那只老鹅身上出了什么事！”我的同伴以一种又气又惊的口吻失声叫道；“巴利马克拉卡（Ballymacrucker）的那只老鹅，那只老鹅啊！神父大人怕是这一带的外乡人吧。哪怕是最傻的傻瓜也全知道那只老鹅，还有那已故的特伦斯·穆尼（Terence Mooney）——愿他的灵魂安息。老天作证，我真纳闷儿，您到底怎么会连那只老鹅都没听说过；莫不成神父大人是在打趣我吧。”

===Original===
I assured him to the contrary, and conjured him to narrate to me the facts, an unacquaintance with which was sufficient it appeared to stamp me as an ignoramus of the first magnitude.

It did not require much entreaty to induce my communicative friend to relate the circumstance, in nearly the following words:

“Terence Mooney was an honest boy and well to do; an’ he rinted the biggest farm on this side iv the Galties; an’ bein’ mighty cute an’ a sevare worker, it was small wonder he turned a good penny every harvest. But unluckily he was blessed with an ilegant large family iv daughters, an’ iv coorse his heart was allamost bruck, striving to make up fortunes for the whole of them. An’ there wasn’t a conthrivance iv any soart or description for makin’ money out iv the farm, but he was up to.

“Well, among the other ways he had iv gettin’ up in the world, he always kep a power iv turkeys, and all soarts iv poultrey; an’ he was out iv all rason partial to geese﻿—an’ small blame to him for that same﻿—for twice’t a year you can pluck them as bare as my hand﻿—an’ get a fine price for the feathers, an’ plenty of rale sizable eggs﻿—an’ when they are too ould to lay any more, you can kill them, an’ sell them to the gintlemen for goslings, d’ye see, let alone that a goose is the most manly bird that is out.

===Chinese===
我连忙向他否认，恳求他把事情的来龙去脉讲给我听；须知，对这桩事一无所知，看样子已足以把我打头号大草包的印记烙在脑门上了。

并不需怎样恳求，我这位健谈的朋友便把事情原委道来，所用的字眼大抵如下：

“特伦斯·穆尼是个正派后生，日子过得挺殷实；他租着盖尔蒂山这边最大的一处农庄；人又精明、干活又下力气，每逢秋收总能挣下个好数目，这也算不得什么稀奇。可不巧得很，老天赏了他一大群闺女，您想啊，他为了给这一群都置办份嫁妆，心都快要操碎了。但凡能从这农庄里榨出钱来的种种法子，他没有想不出来的。

“嗯，在他往上爬的种种门道里头，有一条：他向来养着好大一群火鸡，还有各式各样的家禽；他对鹅尤其偏爱得没有道理——这倒也怪不得他——因为一年里头鹅能拔两回毛，拔得像我手掌一样光溜溜的——鹅毛能卖个好价钱，又能下许许多多实实在在的大鹅蛋——等它们老得再也下不出蛋来，你还能把它们宰了，当成小鹅卖给那些老爷们，您瞧是不是，且不说鹅这种禽类，是飞禽走兽里头顶有男子气概的一种。

===Original===
“Well, it happened in the coorse iv time that one ould gandher tuck a wondherful likin’ to Terence, an’ divil a place he could go serenadin’ about the farm, or lookin’ afther the men, but the gandher id be at his heels, an’ rubbin’ himself agin his legs, an’ lookin’ up in his face jist like any other Christian id do; an’ begorra, the likes iv it was never seen﻿—Terence Mooney an’ the gandher wor so great.

“An’ at last the bird was so engagin’ that Terence would not allow it to be plucked any more, an’ kep it from that time out for love an’ affection﻿—just all as one like one iv his childer.

“But happiness in perfection never lasts long, an’ the neighbours begin’d to suspect the nathur an’ intentions iv the gandher, an’ some iv them said it was the divil, an’ more iv them that it was a fairy.

“Well, Terence could not but hear something of what was sayin’, an’ you may be sure he was not altogether asy in his mind about it, an’ from one day to another he was gettin’ more ancomfortable in himself, until he detarmined to sind for Jer Garvan, the fairy docthor in Garryowen, an’ it’s he was the ilegant hand at the business, an’ divil a sperit id say a crass word to him, no more nor a priest. An’ moreover he was very great wid ould Terence Mooney﻿—this man’s father that was.

“So without more about it he was sint for, an’ sure enough the divil a long he was about it, for he kem back that very evenin’ along wid the boy that was sint for him, an’ as soon as he was there, an’ tuck his supper, an’ was done talkin’ for a while, he begined of coorse to look into the gandher.

“Well, he turned it this away an’ that away, to the right an’ to the left, an’ straight-ways an’ upside-down, an’ when he was tired handlin’ it, says he to Terence Mooney:

“ ‘Terence,’ says he, ‘you must remove the bird into the next room,’ says he, ‘an’ put a petticoat,’ says he, ‘or anny other convaynience round his head,’ says he.

===Chinese===
“嗯，日子一长，有一只老公鹅对特伦斯生出了非同寻常的亲近之情，特伦斯无论去农庄的哪一处闲逛、或去监工，这只老鹅都跟在他脚后跟，拿身子蹭他的腿，仰起头来看他的脸，就跟随便哪个基督徒做出来的举动一模一样；老天作证，这等奇事前所未见——特伦斯·穆尼和这只老鹅，竟亲热成那个样子。

“到末了，这鸟儿实在讨人喜欢，特伦斯便不许人再拔它的毛了，打那以后把它当个宝贝养着——同自己的亲生孩子一般无二。

“可十全十美的幸福终究不能长久，邻人们渐渐起了疑心，疑心这只老鹅的品性和来历，有人说是魔鬼，更多的人说，是仙灵（fairy）。

“嗯，旁人议论的种种，特伦斯多少也听进了一些，您可想而知，他心里头总不太自在，一天比一天别扭，直到他下定决心，打发人去请加里奥恩（Garryowen）那位治仙灵的郎中杰尔·加文（Jer Garvan）来——要说这一行当，他可真是一把好手，再凶的鬼怪也不敢对他哼一声，跟见了神父一般。况且，他与老特伦斯·穆尼——就是这位的父亲——交情深厚得很。

“于是二话不说便派人去请，果不其然，那人手脚利落得很，当天傍晚便跟着去请他的那个小子一道回来了，一到，吃了晚饭，闲话说过一阵，自然便着手查看那只老鹅。

“他把那鹅翻来覆去，左看右看，正着看倒着看，看够了、摸够了，便对特伦斯·穆尼说道：

“‘特伦斯，’他说，‘你得把这鸟儿挪到隔壁屋里去，’他说，‘再拿条衬裙，’他说，‘或者随便什么别的家什，’他说，‘把它的头蒙起来，’他说。

===Original===
“ ‘An’ why so?’ says Terence.

“ ‘Becase,’ says Jer, says he.

“ ‘Becase what?’ says Terence.

“ ‘Becase,’ says Jer, ‘if it isn’t done you’ll never be asy again,’ says he, ‘or pusilanimous in your mind,’ says he; ‘so ax no more questions, but do my biddin’,’ says he.

“ ‘Well,’ says Terence, ‘have your own way,’ says he.

An’ wid that he tuck the ould gandher, an’ giv’ it to one iv the gossoons.

“ ‘An’ take care,’ says he, ‘don’t smother the crathur,’ says he.

Well, as soon as the bird was gone, says Jer Garvan says he:

“ ‘Do you know what that ould gandher *is*, Terence Mooney?’

“ ‘Divil a taste,’ says Terence.

“ ‘Well then,’ says Jer, ‘the gandher is your own father,’ says he.

“ ‘It’s jokin’ you are,’ says Terence, turnin’ mighty pale; ‘how can an ould gandher be my father?’ says he.

“ ‘I’m not funnin’ you at all,’ says Jer; ‘it’s thrue what I tell you, it’s your father’s wandhrin’ sowl,’ says he, ‘that’s naturally tuck pissession iv the ould gandher’s body,’ says he. ‘I know him many ways, and I wondher,’ says he, ‘you do not know the cock iv his eye yourself,’ says he.

“ ‘Oh blur an’ ages!’ says Terence, ‘what the divil will I ever do at all at all,’ says he; ‘it’s all over wid me, for I plucked him twelve times at the laste,’ says he.

===Chinese===
“‘这是干什么？’特伦斯问。

“‘因为，’杰尔说。

“‘因为什么？’特伦斯问。

“‘因为，’杰尔说，‘这事不做，你这辈子别想再安生，’他说，‘心里头也不能踏实，’他说；‘所以别再问了，照我吩咐的做便是，’他说。

“‘好吧，’特伦斯说，‘随你的便，’他说。

说着他便抱起那只老鹅，交给一个小厮。

“‘还有，小心着点儿，’他说，‘别把这可怜东西闷死了，’他说。

那鸟儿一弄走，杰尔·加文便开口道：

“‘特伦斯·穆尼，你可知道那只老公鹅*是*什么？’

“‘我哪里知道，’特伦斯说。

“‘那我就告诉你，’杰尔说，‘这只老鹅，就是你的父亲，’他说。

“‘你是在说笑吧，’特伦斯说着，脸都白了；‘一只老公鹅怎么会是我父亲？’他说。

“‘我一点都不跟你打趣，’杰尔说，‘我告诉你的句句是实话，那是你父亲的游魂，’他说，‘自然而然地附在了这只老公鹅的身上，’他说。‘我从好些地方都能认出他来，倒奇怪，’他说，‘连你自己怎么都没瞧出他那只眼睛的神气，’他说。

“‘哎哟，老天爷呀！’特伦斯叫道，‘我到底可怎么办才好啊，’他说；‘这下全完了，我至少拔过他十二回毛，’他说。

===Original===
“ ‘That can’t be helped now,’ says Jer; ‘it was a sevare act surely,’ says he, ‘but it’s too late to lamint for it now,’ says he; ‘the only way to prevint what’s past,’ says he, ‘is to put a stop to it before it happens,’ says he.

“ ‘Thrue for you,’ says Terence, ‘but how the divil did you come to the knowledge iv my father’s sowl,’ says he, ‘bein’ in the owld gandher,’ says he.

“ ‘If I tould you,’ says Jer, ‘you would not undherstand me,’ says he, ‘without book-larnin’ an’ gasthronomy,’ says he; ‘so ax me no questions,’ says he, ‘an’ I’ll tell you no lies. But blieve me in this much,’ says he, ‘it’s your father that’s in it,’ says he; ‘an’ if I don’t make him spake tomorrow mornin’,’ says he, ‘I’ll give you lave to call me a fool,’ says he.

“ ‘Say no more,’ says Terence, ‘that settles the business,’ says he; ‘an’ oh! blur and ages is it not a quare thing,’ says he, ‘for a dacent respictable man,’ says he, ‘to be walkin’ about the counthry in the shape iv an ould gandher,’ says he; ‘and oh, murdher, murdher! is not it often I plucked him,’ says he, ‘an’ tundher and ouns might not I have ate him,’ says he; and wid that he fell into a could parspiration, savin’ your prisince, an was on the pint iv faintin’ wid the bare notions iv it.

“Well, whin he was come to himself agin, says Jerry to him quite an’ asy:

“ ‘Terence,’ says he, ‘don’t be aggravatin’ yourself,’ says he; ‘for I have a plan composed that ’ill make him spake out,’ says he, ‘an’ tell what it is in the world he’s wantin’,’ says he; ‘an’ mind an’ don’t be comin’ in wid your gosther, an’ to say agin anything I tell you,’ says he, ‘but jist purtind, as soon as the bird is brought back,’ says he, ‘how that we’re goin’ to sind him tomorrow mornin’ to market,’ says he. ‘An’ if he don’t spake tonight,’ says he, ‘or gother himself out iv the place,’ says he, ‘put him into the hamper airly, and sind him in the cart,’ says he, ‘straight to Tipperary, to be sould for ating,’ says he, ‘along wid the two gossoons,’ says he, ‘an’ my name isn’t Jer Garvan,’ says he, ‘if he doesn’t spake out before he’s halfway,’ says he. ‘An’ mind,’ says he, ‘as soon as iver he says the first word,’ says he, ‘that very minute bring him aff to Father Crotty,’ says he; ‘an’ if his raverince doesn’t make him ratire,’ says he, ‘like the rest iv his parishioners, glory be to God,’ says he, ‘into the siclusion iv the flames iv purgathory,’ says he, ‘there’s no vartue in my charums,’ says he.

===Chinese===
“‘那也无可挽回了，’杰尔说，‘这事确实做得狠了，’他说，‘可如今懊悔也迟了，’他说；‘要防已经发生过的事，’他说，‘唯一的法子，便是趁它还没发生就先制止住，’他说。

“‘你这话在理，’特伦斯说，‘可你到底是怎么知道我父亲的灵魂，’他说，‘在这老公鹅里头的？’他说。

“‘我要告诉了你，’杰尔说，‘你也听不明白，’他说，‘少了书本学问，再加一门通灵术（gasthronomy），’他说；‘所以别再问我，’他说，‘我也不会拿谎话搪塞你。但这一点你只管信我，’他说，‘里头那个，就是你父亲，’他说；‘要是我不能叫他在明天早上开口说话，’他说，‘你尽可以叫我一声傻瓜，’他说。

“‘别说了，’特伦斯说，‘事情就这么定了，’他说；‘哎哟！老天爷呀，这岂不是一桩怪事，’他说，‘一个体面的、受人敬重的汉子，’他说，‘竟化作一只老公鹅的模样，’他说，‘在这乡间四处溜达；’他说；‘哦，要命，要命！我以前可没少拔他的毛，’他说，‘老天爷保佑，我说不定还吃过他呢，’他说；说着，他便出了一身冷汗——恕我冒昧——光是想一想这事，已几乎要昏过去了。

“嗯，等他回过神来，杰里便不慌不忙地对他说道：

“‘特伦斯，’他说，‘别再自己折磨自己了，’他说；‘我已经想好一条计策，保管叫他开口，’他说，‘把他在世上到底想要什么说出来，’他说；‘还有，记住，’他说，‘别等会儿又来插嘴，’他说，‘我吩咐你什么，你都别说半个不字，’他说，‘等那鸟儿一弄回来，’他说，‘你就装作，’他说，‘咱们打算明儿一早把它送到集市上去卖，’他说。‘要是它今夜还不开口，’他说，‘或者自己不识趣地溜走，’他说，‘就趁早把它塞进柳条筐里，’他说，‘装上大车，’他说，‘直送到蒂珀雷里去，’他说，‘当成肉鹅卖掉，’他说，‘再叫上那两个小子跟着，’他说，‘要是我叫杰尔·加文，’他说，‘它走不到半路就得开口，’他说。‘还有，记住，’他说，‘等它说出第一个字，’他说，‘就立刻把它送到克罗蒂神父（Father Crotty）那里去，’他说；‘要是神父大人不能叫他退避，’他说，‘像他教区里其余的信众那样——感谢天主——叫他退避到炼狱之火的幽闭里头去，’他说，‘那我这套法术便算不得灵验，’他说。

===Original===
“Well, wid that the ould gandher was let into the room agin, an’ they all bigined to talk iv sindin’ him the nixt mornin’ to be sould for roastin’ in Tipperary, jist as if it was a thing andoubtingly settled.
