With patient scrutiny I endeavoured to ascertain the nature of the fastenings which secured the door.

The planks, fortunately, having been nailed together fresh, had shrunk considerably, so as to leave wide chinks between each and its neighbour.

By means of these apertures I saw that my dungeon was secured, not by a lock, as I had feared, but by a strong wooden bar, running horizontally across the door, about midway upon the outside.

===Chinese===
我所立这间——说是屋子，不如说是囚室——约莫八英尺见方，其高度却与其他尺寸颇不相称：从地板到屋顶，少说也有十二至十四英尺。墙上高处一道狭缝，透进一线微光，却也足以叫我确信：这囚室之内空无一物，可以使住客的栖身不至比我最坏的仇敌所盼望的，更舒坦一分半毫。

我的头一个念头，自然是去看那门牢不牢——我所说那道射箭孔又高又窄，绝无逃出的指望。我凝神细听，要看明门外是否布了岗。

四下里一点声息也无。我便以肩抵门，拼尽浑身力气与分量，要把它撞开。然而它纹丝不动；我这一番诉诸蛮力的努力既告落空，又疲又馁，便颓然瘫在地上。

然而我这性子，原非长久甘于绝望之麻木的；不过几分钟，我又站了起来。

我耐心地细细察看，要弄清那门的门闩是何光景。

所幸那些木板是湿时钉就的，干后大大收缩，板与板之间便留下一道道宽缝。

借着这些缝隙，我看明白：我这囚室的门，并不像我所惧的那样用锁锁着，而是用一根粗木横闩，从外面横过门板、约在中段处别住。

===Original===
"Now," thought I, "if I can but slip my fingers through the opening of the planks, I can easily remove the bar, and then—"

My attempts, however, were all frustrated by the manner in which my hands were fastened together, each embarrassing the other, and rendering my efforts so hopelessly clumsy, that I was obliged to give them over in despair.

I turned with a sigh from my last hope, and began to pace my narrow prison floor, when my eye suddenly encountered an old rusty nail or holdfast sticking in the wall.

All the gold of Plutus would not have been so welcome as that rusty piece of iron.

I instantly wrung it from the wall, and inserting the point between the planks of the door into the bolt, and working it backwards and forwards, I had at length the unspeakable satisfaction to perceive that the beam was actually yielding to my efforts, and gradually sliding into its berth in the wall.

I have often been engaged in struggles where great bodily strength was required, and every thew and sinew in the system taxed to the uttermost; but, strange as it may appear, I never was so completely exhausted and overcome by any labour as by this comparatively trifling task.

Again and again was I obliged to desist, until my cramped finger-joints recovered their power; but at length my perseverance was rewarded, for, little by little, I succeeded in removing the bolt so far as to allow the door to open sufficiently to permit me to pass.

With some squeezing I succeeded in forcing my way into a small passage, upon which my prison-door opened.

This led into a chamber somewhat more spacious than my cell, but still containing no furniture, and affording no means of escape to one so crippled with bonds as I was.

===Chinese===
"好，"我心想，"只要我把手指头从板缝里伸出去，便能轻易把那横闩抽开，那时——"

然而我这一番尝试，全被两只手被绑在一处的窘境所挫：这一只碍着那一只，两手相互掣肘，叫我的努力笨拙得毫无指望，我只好绝望地作罢。

我叹了口气，从这最后一线希望上转过脸，开始在我那狭窄囚室的地板上踱步；忽然，我眼睛撞见墙上一根生了锈的旧钉子——也可以说是一只搭扣。

即便普路托斯（Plutus）所有的黄金，也不见得比那一截锈铁更叫我欣喜。

我立时把它从墙上拧下来，把尖端插入门板的缝里、伸到横闩处，前后拨动；终于，我有了一种难以言喻的快慰——我察觉那横木竟当真在我手下松动，一寸一寸地滑回它在墙里的槽里。

我多次身历需用极大体力的搏斗，浑身每一根筋、每一条腱都绷到极处；然而说来奇怪：我从未像干这件相比之下微不足道的小事这般，疲乏到这般田地、力竭到这般田地。

我一遍又一遍地不得不歇手，直歇到抽筋的指节恢复气力；然而我的恒心终有回报——一点一点地，我终于把横闩抽到那般地步：门可以开得够大，容我钻过去了。

我又挤又钻地钻进了一条小过道——我这囚室的门便通到这条过道。

过道通向一间比我的囚室稍宽敞些的屋子，却仍无一件家具；对一个如我这般被绳索束得行动不便的人而言，也无半分可逃之路。

===Original===
At the far extremity of this room was a door which stood ajar, and, stealthily passing through it, I found myself in a room containing nothing but a few raw hides, which rendered the atmosphere nearly intolerable.

Here I checked myself, for I heard voices in busy conversation in the next room.

I stole softly to the door which separated the chamber in which I stood from that from which the voices proceeded.

A moment served to convince me that any attempt upon it would be worse than fruitless, for it was secured upon the outside by a strong lock, besides two bars, all which I was enabled to ascertain by means of the same defect in the joining of the planks which I have mentioned as belonging to the inner door.

I had approached this door very softly, so that, my proximity being wholly unsuspected by the speakers within, the conversation continued without interruption.

Planting myself close to the door, I applied my eye to one of the chinks which separated the boards, and thus obtained a full view of the chamber and its occupants.

It was the very apartment into which I had been first conducted. The outer door, which faced the one at which I stood, was closed, and at a small table were seated the only tenants of the room—two officers, one of whom was Captain Oliver. The latter was reading a paper, which I made no doubt was the document with which I had been entrusted.

===Chinese===
这间屋子的最里头有一道门，半开半掩；我悄无声息地穿过去，发觉自己置身于一间屋里——屋里别无他物，只有几张生皮子，把空气熏得几乎令人作呕。

我到此便收住了脚，因为隔壁屋里有人正谈得起劲。

我蹑手蹑脚地走到那道门前——这道门隔开了我所立之屋与那传声之屋。

我片刻便明白，对此门打任何主意，都比徒劳更糟：它从外头被一把结实的大锁锁着，再加两道横闩——这一切，我都是借我所说过、内门那种板缝拼合不严的破绽，一一探看明白。

我方才是极轻地走近这道门的，故而屋里的说话人对我近在咫尺一无所觉，那谈兴也便不曾间断。

我把身子贴近门板，把眼睛凑到板缝处，由此把那屋子里头的光景、连屋里的人，看了个一清二楚。

那正是我被最初领进去的那间屋子。与我相对的外门紧闭着；一张小桌旁坐着这屋里仅有的两个人——两位军官，其中之一便是奥利弗上尉。他正在读一份文书——我毫不怀疑，那便是我所奉命护送的那一份。

===Original===
"The fellow deserves it, no doubt," said the junior officer. "But, methinks, considering our orders from headquarters, you deal somewhat too hastily."

"Nephew, nephew," said Captain Oliver, "you mistake the tenor of our orders. We were directed to conciliate the peasantry by fair and gentle treatment, but not to suffer spies and traitors to escape. This packet is of some value, though not, in all its parts, intelligible to me. The bearer has made his way hither under a disguise, which, along with the other circumstances of his appearance here, is sufficient to convict him as a spy."

There was a pause here, and after a few minutes the younger officer said:

"Spy is a hard term, no doubt, uncle; but it is possible—nay, likely, that this poor devil sought merely to carry the parcel with which he was charged in safety to its destination. Pshaw! he is sufficiently punished if you duck him, for ten minutes or so, between the bridge and the milldam."

"Young man," said Oliver, somewhat sternly, "do not obtrude your advice where it is not called for; this man, for whom you plead, murdered your own father!"

I could not see how this announcement affected the person to whom it was addressed, for his back was towards me; but I conjectured, easily, that my last poor chance was gone, for a long silence ensued. Captain Oliver at length resumed:

"I know the villain well. I know him capable of any crime; but, by ———, his last card is played, and the game is up. He shall not see the moon rise tonight."

===Chinese===
"这家伙罪有应得，自是无疑，"那年轻些的军官说，"然而在我看来，念及司令部的命令，您的处置未免过于草率。"

"侄儿，侄儿，"奥利弗上尉道，"你误解了那命令的要旨。命我等以公道宽厚之礼安抚乡民，却不许奸细叛贼逍遥法外。这一封包颇有几分要紧，虽则其内有些去处，我也看不大明白。这送件人乔装潜行到此，这副乔装、连同他现身此间的种种光景，已足以坐实他奸细之名。"

此处一停；过了几分钟，那年长的——不，那年少的军官说道：

"奸细二字，未免太重，伯父；然而也有可能——不，多半如此——这可怜虫不过是想把所托之物安然送到地头罢了。啐！您把他吊起来、在桥和磨坊坝之间浸上十来分钟，也就罚得够了。"

"年轻人，"奥利弗厉声说道，"不必你插嘴处，休要多言；你为之求情的这个人，便是害死你亲生父亲的人！"

我看不见这番话对那位受语之人有何影响——他背对着我；然而我轻易便揣度出，我那一线可怜的指望也已落空，因为随之而来的是长久的沉默。终于，奥利弗上尉又开了口：

"这恶棍，我了如指掌。我知他无恶不作；可是，他妈的，他最后一张牌已打出，这局棋完啦。今夜月亮升起之前，他休想看见。"

===Original===
There was here another pause.

Oliver rose, and going to the outer door, called:

"Hewson! Hewson!"

A grim-looking corporal entered.

"Hewson, have your guard ready at eight o'clock, with their carbines clean, and a round of ball-cartridge each. Keep them sober; and, further, plant two upright posts at the near end of the bridge, with a cross one at top, in the manner of a gibbet. See to these matters, Hewson: I shall be with you speedily."

The corporal made his salutations, and retired.

Oliver deliberately folded up the papers with which I had been commissioned, and placing them in the pocket of his vest, he said:

"Cunning, cunning Master Hardress Fitzgerald hath made a false step; the old fox is in the toils. Hardress Fitzgerald, Hardress Fitzgerald, I will blot you out."

He repeated these words several times, at the same time rubbing his finger strongly upon the table, as if he sought to erase a stain:

"I will blot you out!"

There was a kind of glee in his manner and expression which chilled my very heart.

"You shall be first shot like a dog, and then hanged like a dog: shot tonight, and hung tomorrow; hung at the bridgehead—hung, until your bones drop asunder!"

===Chinese===
此处又是一停。

奥利弗站起身，走到外门前，唤道：

"休森！休森（Hewson）！"

一个面目狰狞的下士走了进来。

"休森，八点钟把你那一班卫兵备好，卡宾枪擦干净，每人一发实弹。叫他们清醒着；此外，在桥头近处竖两根木桩，顶上横一根，做成绞架的模样。这几件事你去办，休森：我随后就到。"

那下士行了礼，退了出去。

奥利弗慢条斯理地把我所奉命护送的那几份文书折好，放进马甲口袋里，说道：

"狡黠、狡黠的哈德勒斯·菲茨杰拉德老爷，这一回可走错了一步棋；老狐狸落网啦。哈德勒斯·菲茨杰拉德，哈德勒斯·菲茨杰拉德，我要把你抹掉。"

他把这几句话重复了好几遍，一面用力地在桌上搓着手指，仿佛要擦去什么污渍：

"我要把你抹掉！"

他的神情与言语之间有一种得意，叫我从心底发凉。

"先叫你像条狗一样被枪毙，再像条狗一样被吊起来：今夜枪毙，明日绞死；在桥头绞死——绞着，直绞到你的骨头一节一节散落下来！"

===Original===
It is impossible to describe the exultation with which he seemed to dwell upon, and to particularise the fate which he intended for me.

I observed, however, that his face was deadly pale, and felt assured that his conscience and inward convictions were struggling against his cruel resolve. Without further comment the two officers left the room, I suppose to oversee the preparations which were being made for the deed of which I was to be the victim.

A chill, sick horror crept over me as they retired, and I felt, for the moment, upon the brink of swooning. This feeling, however, speedily gave place to a sensation still more terrible. A state of excitement so intense and tremendous as to border upon literal madness, supervened; my brain reeled and throbbed as if it would burst; thoughts the wildest and the most hideous flashed through my mind with a spontaneous rapidity that scared my very soul; while, all the time, I felt a strange and frightful impulse to burst into uncontrolled laughter.

Gradually this fearful paroxysm passed away. I kneeled and prayed fervently, and felt comforted and assured; but still I could not view the slow approaches of certain death without an agitation little short of agony.

I have stood in battle many a time when the chances of escape were fearfully small. I have confronted foemen in the deadly breach. I have marched, with a constant heart, against the cannon's mouth. Again and again has the beast which I bestrode been shot under me; again and again have I seen the comrades who walked beside me in an instant laid forever in the dust; again and again have I been in the thick of battle, and of its mortal dangers, and never felt my heart shake, or a single nerve tremble: but now, helpless, manacled, imprisoned, doomed, forced to watch the approaches of an inevitable fate—to wait, silent and moveless, while death as it were crept towards me, human nature was taxed to the uttermost to bear the horrible situation.

===Chinese===
他那种絮絮地、不厌其烦地描画我所注定之下场的得意劲儿，实非笔墨所能形容。

然而我留意到，他面色惨白如死人；我深信，他的良心、他内心的信念，正在与他那残忍的决断相抗衡。两位军官未再多言，便出了屋——我料想，是去看那桩以我为祭品的勾当的预备去了。

他们一走，一种阴冷、令人作呕的恐惧爬遍我全身；那一瞬我几乎就要昏厥过去。然而这一阵感觉很快便让位于一种更为可怕的东西。一种近乎字面意义上的癫狂——那种激烈至极、排山倒海般的亢奋——随之而来；我的脑壳发晕、突突乱跳，像是要炸开；最狂乱、最狰狞的念头，以一种不由自主的迅猛在我脑中一闪一闪，惊得我灵魂出窍；而与此同时，我心里又涌起一股古怪而可怖的冲动，要放声大笑、笑个不住。

渐渐地，这一阵可怖的发作过去了。我跪下，虔诚地祷告；我得了安慰，也得了安稳；然而眼看那无可回避的死亡一步一步逼近，我仍不能不心如刀绞——只差少分毫便是。

我曾多少回立于战阵之上，那时逃生的指望小得吓人。我曾在那死地一般的缺口上与敌人对峙。我曾怀着不改的恒心，向那炮口之下进军。我座下的牲口曾一回又一回在我胯下被击毙；与我并肩而行的袍泽，曾一回又一回在一瞬之间永远卧于尘土；我曾一回又一回置身战事最密、死地最险之处，而心不曾一颤、一根神经不曾一抖：然而如今——孤弱无援、身带枷锁、囚于幽室、命在旦夕，被迫眼睁睁看着那无可回避的命数一步步逼近——被迫沉默不动地等着死亡仿佛一寸一寸爬近身来——人性已被榨到极处，方能承受这般可怖的境地。

===Original===
I returned again to the closet in which I had found myself upon recovering from the swoon.

The evening sunshine and twilight was fast melting into darkness, when I heard the outer door, that which communicated with the guardroom in which the officers had been amusing themselves, opened and locked again upon the inside.

A measured step then approached, and the door of the wretched cell in which I lay being rudely pushed open, a soldier entered, who carried something in his hand; but, owing to the obscurity of the place, I could not see what.

"Art thou awake, fellow?" said he, in a gruff voice. "Stir thyself; get upon thy legs."

His orders were enforced by no very gentle application of his military boot.

"Friend," said I, rising with difficulty, "you need not insult a dying man. You have been sent hither to conduct me to death. Lead on! My trust is in God, that He will forgive me my sins, and receive my soul, redeemed by the blood of His Son."

There here intervened a pause of some length, at the end of which the soldier said, in the same gruff voice, but in a lower key:

"Look ye, comrade, it will be your own fault if you die this night. On one condition I promise to get you out of this hobble with a whole skin; but if you go to any of your d——d gammon, by G——, before two hours are passed, you will have as many holes in your carcase as a target."

"Name your conditions," said I, "and if they consist with honour, I will never balk at the offer."

===Chinese===
我又退回到我从昏厥中醒来时那间小屋。

夕照与暮色正迅速融为一片黑暗；这时我听见外门——那道通到军官们方才取乐的卫兵室的外门——开了，又从里头重新上了锁。

接着，一阵有节奏的脚步声走近；我所卧那间凄惨囚室的门被粗暴地推开，一个兵士走了进来，手里拿着什么；可屋里太暗，我看不清是什么。

"醒了么，家伙？"他以一种粗嘎的嗓音说道，"动一动；站起来。"

他这命令，是用一只军靴不大客气地踢在我身上加以贯彻的。

"朋友，"我艰难地站起身说道，"对一个将死之人，您大可不必如此侮辱。您被派来，是要押我去就死。请带路罢！我信上帝，他必赦我罪愆，收纳我的灵魂——这灵魂已由他圣子之血所赎。"

此后是相当长的一阵沉默；末了，那兵士又开口，还是那副粗嘎嗓音，只是压低了些：

"听着，伙计，今夜你若送命，全是你自家招的。依一个条件，我保你能囫囵着从这一团糟里脱身；可你若跟我来那一套混账花腔，老天在上，不出两个钟头，你身上就要像靶子一样布满窟窿。"

"说出你的条件来，"我说，"若与体面无碍，这买卖我绝不推辞。"

===Original===
"Here they are: you are to be shot tonight, by Captain Oliver's orders. The carbines are cleaned for the job, and the cartridges served out to the men. By G——, I tell you the truth!"

Of this I needed not much persuasion, and intimated to the man my conviction that he spoke the truth.

"Well, then," he continued, "now for the means of avoiding this ugly business. Captain Oliver rides this night to headquarters, with the papers which you carried. Before he starts he will pay you a visit, to fish what he can out of you with all the fine promises he can make. Humour him a little, and when you find an opportunity, stab him in the throat above the cuirass."

"A feasible plan, surely," said I, raising my shackled hands, "for a man thus completely crippled and without a weapon."

"I will manage all that presently for you," said the soldier. "When you have thus dealt with him, take his cloak and hat, and so forth, and put them on; the papers you will find in the pocket of his vest, in a red leather case. Walk boldly out. I am appointed to ride with Captain Oliver, and you will find me holding his horse and my own by the door. Mount quickly, and I will do the same, and then we will ride for our lives across the bridge. You will find the holster-pistols loaded in case of pursuit; and, with the devil's help, we shall reach Limerick without a hair hurt. My only condition is, that when you strike Oliver, you strike home, and again and again, until he is finished; and I trust to your honour to remember me when we reach the town."

===Chinese===
"条件便是：今夜你就要被枪决——奉奥利弗上尉之命。卡宾枪已擦净待命，弹药也已分发到人。老天在上，我句句属实！"

这一层我无须多劝便信了，便向那人表示，我相信他说的句句是真。

"那么，"他接着说，"如今且说如何躲过这桩棘手事。奥利弗上尉今夜要骑马去司令部，带着你所护送的那几份文书。动身之前，他会来看你，用尽种种动听的许诺，想从你嘴里套出点什么。你不妨顺他一顺；待你寻得空档，便一刀捅进他喉咙——胸甲以上的那一截。"

"好一个可行的妙计，"我说着，举起被铐住的双手，"对一个这般被绑得动弹不得、又手无寸铁的人来说。"

"这些我此刻便替你安排，"那兵士说，"你既如此打发了他，便取他的斗篷、帽子之类戴上；那些文书，你在他马甲口袋里找得到，装在一只红色皮匣里。然后你大模大样地走出来。我奉命与奥利弗上尉同行，你会在门口看见我牵着他的马、和自家的马。你快上马，我也上；然后咱们就拼着命地过桥。枪套里的手枪是装好弹的，以防有人来追；凭魔鬼相助，咱们便能毫发无损地到利默里克。我唯一的条件是：你动手之时，要一刀捅实，再一刀、再一刀，捅到他彻底了账为止；至于到了城里，我信你这个体面人，不会忘了我。"

===Original===
I cannot say whether I resolved right or wrong, but I thought my situation, and the conduct of Captain Oliver, warranted me in acceding to the conditions propounded by my visitant, and with alacrity I told him so, and desired him to give me the power, as he had promised to do, of executing them.

With speed and promptitude he drew a small key from his pocket, and in an instant the manacles were removed from my hands.

How my heart bounded within me as my wrists were released from the iron grip of the shackles! The first step toward freedom was made—my self-reliance returned, and I felt assured of success.

"Now for the weapon," said I.

"I fear me, you will find it rather clumsy," said he; "but if well handled, it will do as well as the best Toledo. It is the only thing I could get, but I sharpened it myself; it has an edge like a skean."

He placed in my hand the steel head of a halberd. Grasping it firmly, I found that it made by no means a bad weapon in point of convenience; for it felt in the hand like a heavy dagger, the portion which formed the blade or point being crossed nearly at the lower extremity by a small bar of metal, at one side shaped into the form of an axe, and at the other into that of a hook. These two transverse appendages being muffled by the folds of my cravat, which I removed for the purpose, formed a perfect guard or hilt, and the lower extremity formed like a tube, in which the pike-handle had been inserted, afforded ample space for the grasp of my hand; the point had been made as sharp as a needle, and the metal he assured me was good.

===Chinese===
我也说不上自己这一决断是对是错；然而我以为，以我所处之境、以奥利弗上尉所行之状，我便应允这位不速之客所提的条件，乃是无可非议的。我欣然以此相告，并请他践诺，给我执行的条件。

他麻利地从兜里摸出一把小钥匙，一转眼的工夫，那手铐便从我腕上卸了下来。

当我的手腕从那铁铐的钳制中得脱之时，我的心是怎样在胸膛里蹦跳啊！通向自由的第一步已经迈出——我的自信随之一并归来，我预感到必能成功。

"如今要兵器。"我说。

"我恐怕您会觉着它不大趁手，"他说，"可只要使得好，它不逊于最好的托莱多（Toledo）名剑。这是我所能弄到的唯一一件，不过锋刃是我自家磨的；锋利得像一把短剑（skean）。"

他把一截戟的钢制戟头放进我手里。我紧握住它，发觉论趁手，倒也算不上一件坏兵器；握在手中如同一柄沉甸甸的匕首——那构成刀锋或尖端的部位，在近末端处被一小段金属横档穿过：一头做成斧形，另一头做成钩形。这两道横档，我用解下的领巾一裹，便成了一处妥帖的护手或剑锷；那末端原本插戟柄的管状部位，则给我的手掌留下了充裕的握处；尖端磨得如针一般锋利，那钢料——他向我担保——是上好的。

===Original===
Thus equipped he left me, having observed, "The captain sent me to bring you to your senses, and give you some water that he might find you proper for his visit. Here is the pitcher; I think I have revived you sufficiently for the captain's purpose."

With a low savage laugh he left me to my reflections.

Having examined and adjusted the weapon, I carefully bound the ends of the cravat, with which I had secured the cross part of the spearhead, firmly round my wrist, so that in case of a struggle it might not easily be forced from my hand; and having made these precautionary dispositions, I sat down upon the ground with my back against the wall, and my hands together under my coat, awaiting my visitor.

The time wore slowly on; the dusk became dimmer and dimmer, until it nearly bordered on total darkness.

"How's this?" said I, inwardly; "Captain Oliver, you said I should not see the moon rise tonight. Methinks you are somewhat tardy in fulfilling your prophecy."

As I made this reflection, a noise at the outer door announced the entrance of a visitant. I knew that the decisive moment was come, and letting my head sink upon my breast, and assuring myself that my hands were concealed, I waited, in the attitude of deep dejection, the approach of my foe and betrayer.

As I had expected, Captain Oliver entered the room where I lay. He was equipped for instant duty, as far as the imperfect twilight would allow me to see; the long sword clanked upon the floor as he made his way through the lobbies which led to my place of confinement; his ample military cloak hung upon his arm; his cocked hat was upon his head, and in all points he was prepared for the road.

===Chinese===
他这般把我装备齐了，便告辞而去，临行说一句："上尉派我来叫你醒醒神，给你些水喝，好叫他来时你正合适见他。水罐在这儿；我想我已把你拾掇得够精神，够上尉使的了。"

他低低狞笑一声，便把我丢给自家的思绪。

我把那兵器查验调弄停当，又把缠住戟头横档的领巾两端，牢牢地绑在腕上，以备搏斗之时，那兵器不至轻易脱手；这些防备的安排既妥，我便背靠墙壁坐在地上，两手拢在大衣底下，等候我的来客。

时光缓缓地流逝；暮色越来越淡、越来越淡，几近于一片漆黑。

"这是怎么回事？"我暗自说道，"奥利弗上尉，您说我今夜看不见月亮升起。我看您应验这一句预言，未免太慢了些吧。"

正这般想着，外门处一阵动静，宣告来客已至。我知道决定的一刻到了，便把头垂到胸前，又确认两手藏得妥帖，便以一副万念俱灰的姿态，等着我的仇敌、我的谋害者走近。

不出我所料，奥利弗上尉走进了我所卧之屋。暮色昏沉，我所能看清的范围有限，却也辨出他已是一副即刻启程的装束：那柄长剑随着他穿过通往我这囚处的几道门廊，在地板上叮当作响；他那件宽大的军大衣挂在臂弯；三角帽戴在头上；方方面面，都已为上路打点停当。

===Original===
This tallied exactly with what my strange informant had told me.

I felt my heart swell and my breath come thick as the awful moment which was to witness the death-struggle of one or other of us approached.

Captain Oliver stood within a yard or two of the place where I sat, or rather lay; and folding his arms, he remained silent for a minute or two, as if arranging in his mind how he should address me.

"Hardress Fitzgerald," he began at length, "are you awake? Stand up, if you desire to hear of matters nearly touching your life or death. Get up, I say."

I arose doggedly, and affecting the awkward movements of one whose hands were bound,

"Well," said I, "what would you of me? Is it not enough that I am thus imprisoned without a cause, and about, as I suspect, to suffer a most unjust and violent sentence, but must I also be disturbed during the few moments left me for reflection and repentance by the presence of my persecutor? What do you want of me?"

"As to your punishment, sir," said he, "your own deserts have no doubt suggested the likelihood of it to your mind; but I now am with you to let you know that whatever mitigation of your sentence you may look for, must be earned by your compliance with my orders. You must frankly and fully explain the contents of the packet which you endeavoured this day to destroy; and further, you must tell all that you know of the designs of the popish rebels."

===Chinese===
这一切，与那位古怪报信人所言，分毫不差。

那见证你我二人之一死亡搏斗的可怕时刻将至，我觉得心头膨胀、气息粗重。

奥利弗上尉在我所坐——不如说所卧——之处一两步远的地方站定；他抱起双臂，沉默了一两分钟，仿佛在心中斟酌该如何开口。

"哈德勒斯·菲茨杰拉德，"他终于开口道，"你醒了么？站起来，若你愿听几桩与你生死攸关之事。我叫你站起来。"

我怏怏地立起身，装出一副双手被绑之人才有的笨拙举动——

"那么，"我说，"你要我怎样？我无缘无故被囚于此，又——如我所料——将受一桩极不公道、极暴虐的判决，这还不够么？非得连我留给反省与忏悔的那最后几个瞬间，也要被我迫害者的人影所搅扰？你到底要我怎样？"

"至于你的刑罚，先生，"他说，"是你自家所行之状，无疑已在你心中唤起了它的可能；然而我今来此，是要让你知道：你所盼的刑罚之减免，唯有听命于我方能换取。你必须坦率而详尽地说明你今日所企图销毁的那封包的内容；此外，你必须把你所知的、那些天主教叛贼的一切图谋，和盘托出。"

===Original===
"And if I do this I am to expect a mitigation of my punishment—is it not so?"

Oliver bowed.

"And what is this mitigation to be? On the honour of a soldier, what is it to be?" inquired I.

"When you have made the disclosure required," he replied, "you shall hear. 'Tis then time to talk of indulgences."

"Methinks it would then be too late," answered I. "But a chance is a chance, and a drowning man will catch at a straw. You are an honourable man, Captain Oliver. I must depend, I suppose, on your good faith. Well, sir, before I make the desired communication I have one question more to put. What is to befall me in case that I, remembering the honour of a soldier and a gentleman, reject your infamous terms, scorn your mitigations, and defy your utmost power?"

"In that case," replied he, coolly, "before half an hour you shall be a corpse."

"Then God have mercy on your soul!" said I; and springing forward, I dashed the weapon which I held at his throat.

I missed my aim, but struck him full in the mouth with such force that most of his front teeth were dislodged, and the point of the spearhead passed out under his jaw, at the ear.

===Chinese===
"我若照办，便可指望减刑——是也不是？"

奥利弗一躬身。

"那么这减刑又是什么？凭一个军人的体面，它究竟是什么？"我追问道。

"等你作完所要求的供状，"他答道，"你自然会知晓。到那时再谈恩典，亦不为迟。"

"在我看来，到那时便太迟了，"我答道，"然而一线生机总归是生机，将溺之人便是稻草也要抓。您是一位体面人，奥利弗上尉。我想，我也只能仰仗您的信义了。好罢，先生，在我把所求之言和盘托出之前，我还有一问要问：倘若我——念及一个军人、一个君子的体面——拒绝您这可耻的条件、鄙视您的恩典、并且无畏于您的威权之极处，那我将会如何？"

"若是那样，"他冷冷地答道，"不出半个钟头，你便是一具尸体。"

"那么，愿上帝怜悯你的灵魂！"我说着，纵身一跃，把手中的兵器直朝他喉咙搠去。

我未搠中所指之处，却正正搠在他嘴上，力道之大，把他大多数门牙都撞落了；那戟尖从他颌下穿出，从耳畔透了出来。

===Original===
My onset was so sudden and unexpected that he reeled back to the wall, and did not recover his equilibrium in time to prevent my dealing a second blow, which I did with my whole force. The point unfortunately struck the cuirass, near the neck, and glancing aside it inflicted but a flesh wound, tearing the skin and tendons along the throat.

He now grappled with me, strange to say, without uttering any cry of alarm; being a very powerful man, and if anything rather heavier and more strongly built than I, he succeeded in drawing me with him to the ground. We fell together with a heavy crash, tugging and straining in what we were both conscious was a mortal struggle. At length I succeeded in getting over him, and struck him twice more in the face; still he struggled with an energy which nothing but the tremendous stake at issue could have sustained.

I succeeded again in inflicting several more wounds upon him, any one of which might have been mortal. While thus contending he clutched his hands about my throat, so firmly that I felt the blood swelling the veins of my temples and face almost to bursting. Again and again I struck the weapon deep into his face and throat, but life seemed to adhere in him with an almost insect tenacity.

My sight now nearly failed, my senses almost forsook me; I felt upon the point of suffocation when, with one desperate effort, I struck him another and a last blow in the face. The weapon which I wielded had lighted upon the eye, and the point penetrated the brain; the body quivered under me, the deadly grasp relaxed, and Oliver lay upon the ground a corpse!

===Chinese===
我这攻势来得太突、太出他意料，他踉跄着退到墙边，未及稳住身形，我便又出了一记，这一记我使尽了全力。可惜戟尖搠在颈边的胸甲上，一滑，只划开一道皮肉之伤，把他喉咙一带的皮肉与筋腱扯开了去。

此刻他与我扭作一处——说来奇怪——竟未发一声呼救；他是个极强壮之人，若论体重与体格，比我还要略胜一筹。他终于把我一同拖倒在地。我们一同重重地摔下，彼此拉扯角力，都心知肚明这是一场你死我活的相搏。终于我翻到了他身上，又在他脸上连搠两下；他仍奋力挣扎，那股劲头，若非有这场相搏背后那惊天赌注撑着，是断然撑不起的。

我又在他身上连搠数下，每一处都可能致命。正在这般相持之际，他双手紧掐住我喉咙，掐得那样死，只觉我太阳穴与脸上的血管都几乎要胀裂。我一次、再一次把那兵器深深搠进他的脸与喉，可他的性命却仿佛虫豸一般，死死黏附不走。

我的视线几乎要看不见了，神智也几乎要离我而去；我自觉就要憋死——便在这时，我使尽最后的力气，又在他脸上加了一记、也是最后一击。我手中所执的兵器，正落在眼睛上，尖端直透脑中；那身躯在我底下一抽搐，那要命的钳制松开了——奥利弗瘫在地上，成了一具尸首！

===Original===
As I arose and shook the weapon and the bloody cloth from my hand, the moon which he had foretold I should never see rise, shone bright and broad into the room, and disclosed, with ghastly distinctness, the mangled features of the dead soldier; the mouth, full of clotting blood and broken teeth, lay open; the eye, close by whose lid the fatal wound had been inflicted, was not, as might have been expected, bathed in blood, but had started forth nearly from the socket, and gave to the face, by its fearful unlikeness to the other glazing orb, a leer more hideous and unearthly than fancy ever saw. The wig, with all its rich curls, had fallen with the hat to the floor, leaving the shorn head exposed, and in many places marked by the recent struggle; the rich lace cravat was drenched in blood, and the gay uniform in many places soiled with the same.

It is hard to say, with what feelings I looked upon the unsightly and revolting mass which had so lately been a living and a comely man. I had not any time, however, to spare for reflection; the deed was done—the responsibility was upon me, and all was registered in the book of that God who judges rightly.

With eager haste I removed from the body such of the military accoutrements as were necessary for the purpose of my disguise. I buckled on the sword, drew off the military boots, and donned them myself, placed the brigadier wig and cocked hat upon my head, threw on the cloak, drew it up about my face, and proceeded, with the papers which I found as the soldier had foretold me, and the key of the outer lobby, to the door of the guardroom; this I opened, and with a firm and rapid tread walked through the officers, who rose as I entered, and passed without question or interruption to the street-door. Here I was met by the grim-looking corporal, Hewson, who, saluting me, said:

"How soon, captain, shall the file be drawn out and the prisoner despatched?"

"In half an hour," I replied, without raising my voice.

===Chinese===
我立起身来，把手上的兵器与那块血污的领巾甩开；他曾预言我无缘得见升起的那轮月亮，此刻正又明又大地照进屋里，把那死兵支离破碎的面目，照得纤毫毕现、阴森可怖：那张嘴，满满地含着凝血与断牙，张着；那只紧贴着致命伤口的眼——出人意料地——并未浸在血泊之中，而是几乎从眼眶里凸了出来，与另一只渐渐失神的眼球那种骇人的不相称，叫这张脸添了一种斜睨之态，比想象力所能企及的更狰狞、更不像阳世之物。那顶带着浓密卷发的假发，连同帽子，一齐落在地板上，露出那颗剃光的头颅——许多地方还带着方才那场相搏的痕迹；那富丽的花边领巾浸透了血，那身鲜艳的军服也多处沾上了同样的污渍。

我望着这一堆丑陋、可憎的血肉——不久之前，这还是一个活生生的、俊朗的人——所怀着的是何等心情，实难言传。然而我并无半点闲暇可以用来反省；事情已经做了——责任在我肩上，这一切都已记入那审判公允的上帝之册了。

我急切地从尸首上剥下我那乔装所必需的几件军中装束。我束上剑，扒下马靴、套在自家的脚上，把那顶带着卷发的假发与三角帽戴在头上，把军大衣一披、将脸一裹，便带着那几份文书——果如那兵士所言，我在他身上找得到——和通往外门廊的钥匙，走向卫兵室的门。我把门一开，便踏着沉稳迅捷的步子，从那几个起立相迎的军官中间穿过，一路无阻无问，径直走到临街的大门。在那儿，我迎面遇上那面目狰狞的休森下士，他朝我一礼，说道：

"上尉，那一行刑队何时拉出来、把囚犯打发掉？"

"半个钟头之内。"我答道，并未提高嗓音。

===Original===
The man again saluted, and in two steps I reached the soldier who held the two horses, as he had intimated.

"Is all right?" said he, eagerly.

"Ay," said I, "which horse am I to mount?"

He satisfied me upon this point, and I threw myself into the saddle; the soldier mounted his horse, and dashing the spurs into the flanks of the animal which I bestrode, we thundered along the narrow bridge. At the far extremity a sentinel, as we approached, called out, "Who goes there? stand, and give the word!" Heedless of the interruption, with my heart bounding with excitement, I dashed on, as did also the soldier who accompanied me.

"Stand, or I fire! give the word!" cried the sentry.

"God save the king, and to hell with the prince!" shouted I, flinging the cocked hat in his face as I galloped by.

The response was the sharp report of a carbine, accompanied by the whiz of a bullet, which passed directly between me and my comrade, now riding beside me.

"Hurrah!" I shouted; "try it again, my boy."

And away we went at a gallop, which bid fair to distance anything like pursuit.

Never was spur more needed, however, for soon the clatter of horses' hoofs, in full speed, crossing the bridge, came sharp and clear through the stillness of the night.

Away we went, with our pursuers close behind; one mile was passed, another nearly completed. The moon now shone forth, and, turning in the saddle, I looked back upon the road we had passed.

===Chinese===
那人又行了一礼；我两步便跨到那牵两匹马的兵士跟前——果如他所言。

"得手了么？"他急切地问。

"成了。"我说，"我骑哪一匹？"

他给我指点明白；我翻身上了马。那兵士也上了他的马；他把马刺往我所骑的牲口肋上一戳，我们便轰隆隆地冲过那座窄桥。到了桥的远端，一个哨兵见我们逼近，便喊道："什么人？站住，对口号！"我全然不顾这一拦阻，心头又蹦又跳，只管冲了过去，与我同行的那兵士也是一样。

"站住，不然开火了！对口号！"哨兵喊。

"上帝保佑王上，亲王见鬼去吧！"我高声喊道，疾驰而过之际，把那顶三角帽朝他脸上甩去。

回答的是卡宾枪一声清脆的枪响，伴着一颗子弹的呼啸——子弹贴着我与我那位如今并骑在旁的同伴之间穿过去了。

"好哇！"我喊道，"再来一下啊，老兄。"

我们便这般放马疾驰，那速度，足可甩脱任何追赶。

然而从来没有比此刻更用得上马刺的了：不多时，一队马蹄全速奔过桥面的嗒嗒声，便穿过夜的寂静，又急又清地传了过来。

我们一路飞驰，追赶者紧咬不放；一里过去了，又一里也快走完。这时月亮露出云来；我在鞍上一回头，望向来路。

===Original===
One trooper had headed the rest, and was within a hundred yards of us.

I saw the fellow throw himself from his horse upon the ground.

I knew his object, and said to my comrade:

"Lower your body—lie flat over the saddle; the fellow is going to fire."

I had hardly spoken when the report of a carbine startled the echoes, and the ball, striking the hind leg of my companion's horse, the poor animal fell headlong upon the road, throwing his rider head-foremost over the saddle.

My first impulse was to stop and share whatever fate might await my comrade; but my second and wiser one was to spur on, and save myself and my despatch.

I rode on at a gallop, turning to observe my comrade's fate. I saw his pursuer, having remounted, ride rapidly up to him, and, on reaching the spot where the man and horse lay, rein in and dismount.

He was hardly upon the ground, when my companion shot him dead with one of the holster-pistols which he had drawn from the pipe; and, leaping nimbly over a ditch at the side of the road, he was soon lost among the ditches and thornbushes which covered that part of the country.

Another mile being passed, I had the satisfaction to perceive that the pursuit was given over, and in an hour more I crossed Thomond Bridge, and slept that night in the fortress of Limerick, having delivered the packet, the result of whose safe arrival was the destruction of William's great train of artillery, then upon its way to the besiegers.

Years after this adventure, I met in France a young officer, who I found had served in Captain Oliver's regiment; and he explained what I had never before understood—the motives of the man who had wrought my deliverance. Strange to say, he was the foster-brother of Oliver, whom he thus devoted to death, but in revenge for the most grievous wrong which one man can inflict upon another!

===Chinese===
一个骑兵已超出其余众人，距我们不过百步之遥。

我看见那汉子翻身下马，扑倒在地。

我知他所图，便对同伴说：

"伏低些——伏在鞍上；那汉子要开火了。"

我话音未落，一声卡宾枪响惊起四下回声；那弹丸打中我同伴坐骑的后腿，那可怜的牲口一头栽倒在路上，把骑手从鞍上倒栽葱似的掀了出去。

我的头一个念头，是停下与同伴共担任何命数；可第二个、也是更明智的念头，是纵马前行，救我自己和我的文书。

我策马疾驰，回头去看同伴的下场。我看见那追赶者重又上马，飞驰到他跟前，到了人马倒卧之处，便勒马下鞍。

他那双脚还未落地，我那同伴便用从枪套里抽出来的一柄手枪，将他一枪送了命；随即灵巧地跃过路边一道沟，不多时便消失在那覆盖该处的、纵横的沟渠与荆棘丛里。

我又走过一里，便欣喜地察觉追赶已告放弃；又过了一个钟头，我越过了托蒙德桥（Thomond Bridge），那一夜便在利默里克的要塞里安睡——文书既已送到，其结果，是威廉正送往围城军中的那一支庞大炮队，被尽数摧毁。

此番奇遇之后数年，我在法国遇见一位年轻军官，得知他曾在奥利弗上尉的团里服役；他为我解了一桩我从前始终不解之事——那位救我性命者的动机。说来奇怪：那人竟是奥利弗的乳兄弟，他却这般将奥利弗送上死路——乃是为一桩一个人所能加诸另一个人的、最惨毒的冤仇报仇！

## Billy Malowney’s Taste of Love and Glory / 比利·马洛尼的爱情与荣耀之味

===Original===
Let the reader fancy a soft summer evening, the fresh dews falling on bush and flower. The sun has just gone down, and the thrilling vespers of thrushes and blackbirds ring with a wild joy through the saddened air; the west is piled with fantastic clouds, and clothed in tints of crimson and amber, melting away into a wan green, and so eastward into the deepest blue, through which soon the stars will begin to peep.
Let him fancy himself seated upon the low mossy wall of an ancient churchyard, where hundreds of grey stones rise above the sward, under the fantastic branches of two or three half-withered ash-trees, spreading their arms in everlasting love and sorrow over the dead.
The narrow road upon which I and my companion await the tax-cart that is to carry me and my basket, with its rich fruitage of speckled trout, away, lies at his feet, and far below spreads an undulating plain, rising westward again into soft hills, and traversed (every here and there visibly) by a winding stream which, even through the mists of evening, catches and returns the funereal glories of the skies.
As the eye traces its wayward wanderings, it loses them for a moment in the heaving verdure of whitethorns and ash, from among which floats from some dozen rude chimneys, mostly unseen, the transparent blue film of turf smoke. There we know, although we cannot see it, the steep old bridge of Carrickadrum spans the river; and stretching away far to the right the valley of Lisnamoe: its steeps and hollows, its straggling hedges, its fair-green, its tall scattered trees, and old grey tower, are disappearing fast among the discoloured tints and haze of evening.

===Chinese===
且请读者想象一个柔和的夏日黄昏，清新的露珠正落在灌木与花朵之上。太阳刚刚落下，鸫鸟与乌鸫那令人心颤的晚祷之歌，带着一种狂野的欢愉，回荡在那因日落而略显凄凉的空中；西方天际堆叠着奇幻的云朵，染作深红与琥珀之色，渐次融为一线黯淡的绿意，再往东，便沉入最深的湛蓝——不多时，星星便要从那蓝色中一一探出头来。
且请他想象自己坐在一座古墓园那低矮生苔的围墙之上，园中数百块灰白的石碑从草皮间拔地而起，矗立在两三棵半枯的白蜡树那奇崛的枝桠之下，那些枝桠舒展着臂膀，仿佛怀着永恒的爱与哀愁，庇护着地下的亡者。
我与我那同伴正在等候一辆轻便马车，好把我和我那只篮子——里头满满当当地盛着斑鳟鱼——一并载走；那条窄路便从他脚下穿过，再往下，是一片连绵起伏的平原铺展开来，往西又隆起一道道柔和的丘陵，一条蜿蜒的小溪穿行其间（时隐时现），即便隔着暮霭，也能撷取、并映回那苍天之上葬礼般的辉煌。
目光沿着那小溪迂回的游走一路追溯，一时竟会迷失在山楂与白蜡树那起伏的青翠之中；树丛之间，从十几根粗陋的烟囱里——大多看不见——飘出一缕缕透明的淡蓝泥炭烟。我们虽看不见，却知道就在那儿，卡里克阿德拉姆（Carrickadrum）那座陡峭的古桥正横跨河上；往右远远伸展开去的，则是利斯纳莫（Lisnamoe）的山谷：它的坡地与洼地，它那零零落落的篱笆，它的集市草坪，它那些高耸而散落的树木，还有那座灰白的老塔楼，正迅速地隐没在暮色那褪了色的光斑与薄雾之中。

===Original===
Those landmarks, as we sit listlessly expecting the arrival of our modest conveyance, suggest to our companion﻿—a bare-legged Celtic brother of the gentle craft, somewhat at the wrong side of forty, with a turf-coloured caubeen, patched frieze, a clear brown complexion, dark-grey eyes, and a right pleasant dash of roguery in his features﻿—the tale, which, if the reader pleases, he is welcome to hear along with me just as it falls from the lips of our humble comrade.
His words I can give, but your own fancy must supply the advantages of an intelligent, expressive countenance, and, what is perhaps harder still, the harmony of his glorious brogue, that, like the melodies of our own dear country, will leave a burden of mirth or of sorrow with nearly equal propriety, tickling the diaphragm as easily as it plays with the heartstrings, and is in itself a national music that, I trust, may never, never﻿—scouted and despised though it be﻿—never cease, like the lost tones of our harp, to be heard in the fields of my country, in welcome or endearment, in fun or in sorrow, stirring the hearts of Irish men and Irish women.
My friend of the caubeen and naked shanks, then, commenced, and continued his relation, as nearly as possible, in the following words:

===Chinese===
我们正百无聊赖地等着那辆寒酸的交通工具到来，这几处地标，便勾起了我们这位同伴的一段故事——他是凯尔特血统的兄弟，打鱼这门斯文行当里光着腿的一位，年纪已过了四十好几，头戴一顶泥炭色的扁圆帽（caubeen），身上披着打了补丁的粗呢外衣，一张脸是清朗的棕色，一双深灰色的眼睛，眉宇之间带着一股子颇为讨喜的促狭劲儿——读者若是愿意，不妨与我一同听听，这故事便要原原本本地从我们这位卑微伙伴的口中流淌出来。
他的话我尚能转述，但他那一张机敏而富于神采的面孔所带来的妙处，却须由诸君自行想象；而更难复现的，或许是他那动听的土腔（brogue）所成的和谐——那腔调一如我们亲爱祖国之地的旋律，无论是留下一缕欢笑，还是留下一缕哀愁，都同样恰如其分；它能轻易地逗人发笑，也能同样轻易地撩拨人的心弦；它本身就是一曲民族的乐音——我只盼它永永远远——尽管为人所嘲弄、所轻鄙——永永远远不会像我们那失去的古竖琴之音一般，从此在我国的田野之上销声匿迹，无论是在欢迎与亲昵之时，还是在戏谑与悲戚之际，都能继续激荡爱尔兰男儿与爱尔兰女儿的心。
于是，我这位头戴扁圆帽、光着小腿的朋友，便开了口，将他这段故事一段段讲下去，所用的字句，大致如下：

---

===Original===
Av coorse ye often heerd talk of Billy Malowney, that lived by the bridge of Carrickadrum. “Leum-a-rinka” was the name they put on him, he was sich a beautiful dancer. An’ faix, it’s he was the rale sportin’ boy, every way﻿—killing the hares, and gaffing the salmons, an’ fightin’ the men, an’ funnin’ the women, and coortin’ the girls; an’ be the same token, there was not a colleen inside iv his jurisdiction but was breakin’ her heart wid the fair love iv him.
Well, this was all pleasant enough, to be sure, while it lasted; but inhuman beings is born to misfortune, an’ Bill’s divarshin was not to last always. A young boy can’t be continially coortin’ and kissin’ the girls (an’ more’s the pity) without exposin’ himself to the most eminent parril; an’ so signs an’ what should happen Billy Malowney himself, but to fall in love at last wid little Molly Donovan, in Coolnamoe.
I never could ondherstand why in the world it was Bill fell in love wid *her*, above all the girls in the country. She was not within four stone weight iv being as fat as Peg Brallaghan; and as for redness in the face, she could not hould a candle to Judy Flaherty. (Poor Judy! she was my sweetheart, the darlin’, an’ coorted me constant, ever antil she married a boy of the Butlers; an’ it’s twenty years now since she was buried under the ould whitethorn in Garbally. But that’s no matther!)

===Chinese===
您当然常听人说起比利·马洛尼（Billy Malowney）啦，就住在卡里克阿德拉姆那座桥边。「跳跃舞者莱姆」（Leum-a-rinka）是人家给他起的名号，因为他跳起舞来实在漂亮极了。说真的，他可真是个道道地地的玩乐好手——样样在行——猎野兔，叉鲑鱼，跟汉子们打架，跟女人们逗趣，追起姑娘来更是没完；这不，他管界之内，没哪个姑娘不是为了他那份俊俏的爱，把心都给碎了去。
哎，这些事儿快活是快活，那是自然；只可惜人生在世，本就生来要遭厄运的，比利的快活日子自然也长不了。一个年轻小伙子，整日价追着姑娘、亲着姑娘（唉，可惜呀可惜），哪能不把自己搁到天大的险地里头呢？果不其然，比利·马洛尼自个儿就出了事——他竟爱上了库尔纳莫（Coolnamoe）的小莫莉·多诺万（Molly Donovan）。
我这辈子也闹不明白，天下那么多姑娘，比利偏偏怎么就看上了*她*。论胖，她离佩格·布拉拉根（Peg Brallaghan）还差着四英石上下呢；至于脸红嘛，她也万万比不上朱迪·弗莱厄蒂（Judy Flaherty）。（可怜的朱迪！她可是我的心上人，那宝贝儿，对我一往情深、殷勤备至，直到后来嫁给了一个巴特勒家（the Butlers）的小子；如今她葬在加巴利（Garbally）那棵老山楂树下，已是二十个年头了。不过这都不打紧！）

===Original===
Well, at any rate, Molly Donovan tuck his fancy, an’ that’s everything! She had smooth brown hair﻿—as smooth as silk﻿—an’ a pair iv soft coaxin’ eyes﻿—an’ the whitest little teeth you ever seen; an’, bedad, she was every taste as much in love wid himself as he was.
Well, now, he was raly stupid wid love: there was not a bit of fun left in him. He was good for nothin’ an airth bud sittin’ under bushes, smokin’ tobacky, and sighin’ till you’d wonder how in the world he got wind for it all.
An’, bedad, he was an illigant scholar, moreover; an’, so signs, it’s many’s the song he made about her; an’ if you’d be walkin’ in the evening, a mile away from Carrickadrum, begorra you’d hear him singing out like a bull, all across the country, in her praises.

===Chinese===
哎，话又说回来，莫莉·多诺万入了他的眼，这便是一切！她有一头光滑的棕发——滑如丝缎——一双柔和娇嗔的眼睛——还有您所见过的最白净的小牙；而且，天哪，她爱他，原也不下于他爱她，分毫不少。
哎，这一来，他可真叫被爱情冲昏了头：身上一丝乐子都没剩下。除了蹲在树底下抽着烟、唉声叹气——您都要纳闷，他哪来那么多气力叹个没完——他简直一无所用了。
再者，他还是个体面的读书人呢；这不，他为她作的歌可多了去了；倘若您傍晚时分出去走走，离卡里克阿德拉姆还有一英里远呢，便能听见他扯着嗓子、像公牛似的吼唱，穿过整片乡野，全是在夸她。

===Original===
Well, ye may be sure, ould Tim Donovan and the wife was not a bit too well plased to see Bill Malowney coortin’ their daughter Molly; for, do ye mind, she was the only child they had, and her fortune was thirty-five pounds, two cows, and five illigant pigs, three iron pots and a skillet, an’ a trifle iv poultry in hand; and no one knew how much besides, whenever the Lordid be plased to call the ould people out iv the way into glory!
So, it was not likely ould Tim Donovan id be fallin’ in love wid poor Bill Malowney as aisy as the girls did; for, barrin’ his beauty, an’ his gun, an’ his dhudheen, an’ his janius, the divil a taste of property iv any sort or description he had in the wide world!

===Chinese===
哎，您可想而知，老蒂姆·多诺万（Tim Donovan）两口子瞧见比尔·马洛尼来追他们闺女莫莉，心里头可不大痛快；要知道，她可是他们膝下唯一的孩子，她的陪嫁是三十五镑钱、两头奶牛、五头上好的猪、三口铁锅外加一只长柄小平锅，还有少许家禽在手；此外还不知有多少呢，只要天主哪天高兴，把这两位老人家接去享福便是！
所以啊，老蒂姆·多诺万要像那些姑娘一样轻轻松松地爱上可怜的比尔·马洛尼，可没那么容易；因为，除却他那副好相貌、他那杆枪、他那根短柄小烟斗（dhudheen）和他的那点天分，他在这个广阔天地里头，可真是一星半点的产业、形形色色的财物都没有啊！

===Original===
Well, as bad as that was, Billy would not give in that her father and mother had the smallest taste iv a right to intherfare, good or bad.
“An’ you’re welcome to rayfuse me,” says he, “whin I ax your lave,” says he; “an’ I’ll ax your lave,” says he, “whenever I want to coort yourselves,” says he; “but it’s your daughter I’m coortin’ at the present,” says he, “an that’s all I’ll say,” says he; “for I’d as soon take a doase of salts as be discoursin’ ye,” says he.
So it was a rale blazin’ battle betune himself and the ould people; an’, begorra, there was no soart iv blaguardin’ that did not pass betune them; an’ they put a solemn injection on Molly again seein’ him or meetin’ him for the future.

===Chinese===
哎，情形纵然如此糟糕，比利却偏不肯让步，说她的爹娘哪怕是半分干预的权利，无论好坏，都一概没有。
「您尽可以拒绝我，」他说，「等我求您准许的时候，」他说；「而等我要来追您二老的时候，」他说，「我自然会来求您准许，」他说；「可眼下我追的，是您家的闺女，」他说，「我要说的就这些，」他说；「因为跟您二位絮叨，我还不如灌一剂泻盐呢，」他说。
于是，这便成了他跟二老之间一场真正如火如荼的大战；哎呀，种种难听的恶言恶语，没有哪一样没在他们中间来回过几遭；他们还郑重其事地严禁莫莉今后再见他的面、再跟他相会。

===Original===
But it was all iv no use. You might as well be pursuadin’ the birds agin flying, or sthrivin’ to coax the stars out iv the sky into your hat, as be talking common sinse to them that’s fairly bothered and burstin’ wid love. There’s nothin’ like it. The toothache an’ cholic together id compose you betther for an argyment than itself. It leaves you fit for nothin’ bud nansinse.
It’s stronger than whisky, for one good drop iv it will make you drunk for one year, and sick, begorra, for a dozen.
It’s stronger than the say, for it’ll carry you round the world an’ never let you sink, in sunshine or storm; an’, begorra, it’s stronger than Death himself, for it is not afeard iv him, bedad, but dares him in every shape.

===Chinese===
可这统统无济于事。你去劝鸟类别飞，或者想把天上的星星哄进你的帽子里，都同跟一个被爱情搅得昏头胀脑、满心欲爆的人讲道理一样徒劳。天下再没第二样东西能与之相比。牙疼绞肠痧一块儿发作，反倒更能叫你坐下来好好听人讲理。爱情这东西，只叫你一无所能，只会胡说八道。
它比威士忌还烈，因为单单一滴上好的，就能叫你醉上一年，还能叫你，老天，苦上十二年。
它比大海还要强大，因为它能载着你走遍天涯海角，无论日晒雨淋，都绝不让你沉没；而且，老天作证，它比死亡本尊还强横，因为它压根儿不惧死亡，敢在它每一种形貌前公然挑衅。

===Original===
But lovers has quarrels sometimes, and, begorra, when they do, you’d a’most imagine they hated one another like man and wife. An’ so, signs an’, Billy Malowney and Molly Donovan fell out one evening at ould Tom Dundon’s wake; an’ whatever came betune them, she made no more about it but just draws her cloak round her, and away wid herself and the sarvant-girl home again, as if there was not a corpse, or a fiddle, or a taste of divarsion in it.
Well, Bill Malowney follied her down the boreen, to try could he deludher her back again; but, if she was bitther before, she gave it to him in airnest when she got him alone to herself, and to that degree that he wished her safe home, short and sulky enough, an’ walked back again, as mad as the devil himself, to the wake, to pay a respect to poor Tom Dundon.
Well, my dear, it was aisy seen there was something wrong avid Billy Malowney, for he paid no attintion the rest iv the evening to any soart of divarsion but the whisky alone; an’ every glass he’d drink it’s what he’d be wishing the divil had the women, an’ the worst iv bad luck to all soarts iv courting, until, at last, wid the goodness iv the sperits, an’ the badness iv his temper, an’ the constant flusthration iv cursin’, he grew all as one as you might say almost, saving your presince, bastely drunk!

===Chinese===
可恋人之间有时也免不了口角，老天，他们一旦吵起来，您简直会以为他们彼此恨之入骨，活像一对儿结发夫妻。果不其然，有一天晚上，在老汤姆·邓登（Tom Dundon）的守灵夜上，比利·马洛尼同莫莉·多诺万就闹翻了；两人之间到底起了什么纠葛，外人不得而知，只见她二话不说，一把将斗篷裹在身上，带着女仆径自回家去了，那架势，倒好像屋里既没停着尸首，也没拉着提琴，更没有半点乐子可寻。
哎，比利·马洛尼顺着那条小径一路追了下去，想看看能不能把她哄回来；可她先前若只是尖酸，待把这地方只剩他俩时，她可就当真地对他发作起来，发作得那般厉害，以至于他没好气地祝了她一声「平安到家」，便气鼓鼓、阴沉沉地掉头折回——那火气大得，简直跟魔鬼本尊一个样——回灵堂去，好歹给可怜的老汤姆·邓登尽一份礼数。
哎，我的老天，比利·马洛尼这副模样，谁瞧一眼都知道是出了岔子；因为这一晚余下的工夫，他再不搭理任何玩乐，只一味地喝那威士忌；每灌下一杯，便要咒骂一声女人都见鬼去吧，咒骂各式各样的求亲都倒大霉去吧；直到最后，仗着烈酒的劲道，加上脾气的败坏，再加那不绝于口的咒骂所带来的烦躁，他整个人，恕我直言，几乎可以说已经是烂醉如泥、不堪入目了！

===Original===
Well, who should he fall in wid, in that childish condition, as he was deploying along the road almost as straight as the letter S, an’ cursin’ the girls, an’ roarin’ for more whisky, but the recruiting-sargent iv the Welsh Confusileers.
So, cute enough, the sargent begins to convarse him, an’ it was not long until he had him sitting in Murphy’s public-house, wid an elegant dandy iv punch before him, an’ the king’s money safe an’ snug in the lowest wrinkle of his breeches-pocket.
So away wid him, and the dhrums and fifes playing, an’ a dozen more unforthunate bliggards just listed along with him, an’ he shakin’ hands wid the sargent, and swearin’ agin the women every minute, until, be the time he kem to himself, begorra, he was a good ten miles on the road to Dublin, an’ Molly and all behind him.

===Chinese===
哎，就在这副孩童似的醉态之中，他沿着大路一路「行军」，走得几乎跟字母 S 一样笔直，嘴里一边咒骂着姑娘，一边嚷着要再来点威士忌——您猜他撞见了谁？正撞上了威尔士「混成步兵团」的一位招募军士。
那军士机灵得很，便凑上前去跟他搭起话来；没多大工夫，便已把他请进墨菲（Murphy）开的酒馆里坐着了，面前摆着一杯漂漂亮亮的潘趣酒，国王陛下赏下的饷钱，也妥妥帖帖、舒舒服服地揣进了他马裤口袋最底下那条褶子里。
就这么着，他便被带走了——一路上鼓乐齐鸣，还有一打同样倒霉的穷光蛋刚刚跟他一道应了募——他一边跟军士握手，一边每时每刻都在赌咒发誓说再也不理女人了；直到他神志清醒过来时，老天，他已经走上通往都柏林的大路足足十里了，莫莉和那一切，全都抛在了身后。

===Original===
It id be no good tellin’ you iv the letters he wrote to her from the barracks there, nor how she was breaking her heart to go and see him just wanst before he’d go; but the father an’ mother would not allow iv it be no manes.
An’ so in less time than you’d be thinkin’ about it, the colonel had him polished off into a rale elegant soger, wid his gun exercise, and his bagnet exercise, and his small sword, and broad sword, and pistol and dagger, an’ all the rest, an’ then away wid him on boord a man-a-war to furrin parts, to fight for King George agin Bonyparty, that was great in them times.
Well, it was very soon in everyone’s mouth how Billy Malowney was batin’ all before him, astonishin’ the ginerals, an frightenin’ the inimy to that degree, there was not a Frinchman dare say parley voo outside of the rounds iv his camp.

===Chinese===
他从那兵营里给她写了多少封信，她又是怎样肝肠寸断地只想在他开拔之前去看他最后一面，这些事跟您说也没多大意思；反正她爹娘是无论如何都不准。
于是，您还没回过神来呢，上校便已把他操练成一个体体面面、像模像样的兵了——枪法练了，刺刀练了，短剑、阔剑、手枪、匕首，样样都练全了——接着便把他送上了一艘战船，开往异国他乡，去为乔治国王（King George）抗击波拿巴（Bonyparty）打仗——那阵子，波拿巴正是风光一时的人物。
哎，没过多久，比利·马洛尼如何所向披靡、如何惊呆了一众将军、又如何把敌人吓得不敢露头的事，便已传遍了人人口中——他这一震慑，竟没一个法国佬敢在他营盘方圆之外说一句「巴莱武」（parley voo）了。

===Original===
You may be sure Molly was proud iv that same, though she never spoke a word about it; until at last the news kem home that Billy Malowney was surrounded an’ murdered by the Frinch army, under Napoleon Bonyparty himself. The news was brought by Jack Brynn Dhas, the peddlar, that said he met the corporal iv the regiment on the quay iv Limerick, an’ how he brought him into a public-house and thrated him to a naggin, and got all the news about poor Billy Malowney out iv him while they war dhrinkin’ it; an’ a sorrowful story it was.
The way it happened, accordin’ as the corporal tould him, was jist how the Jook iv Wellington detarmined to fight a rale tarin’ battle wid the Frinch, and Bonyparty at the same time was aiqually detarmined to fight the divil’s own scrimmidge wid the British foorces.
Well, as soon as the business was pretty near ready at both sides, Bonyparty and the general next undher himself gets up behind a bush, to look at their inimies through spyglasses, and thry would they know any iv them at the distance.

===Chinese===
莫莉心里头自然是为这事骄傲的，尽管她嘴上半个字也没提过；直到最后，消息传回家来：比利·马洛尼被法国大军包围、惨遭杀害，而统兵的正是拿破仑·波拿巴（Napoleon Bonyparty）本人。这消息是杰克·布林·达斯（Jack Brynn Dhas）那个小贩带回的，他说他在利默里克（Limerick）的码头上撞见该团的一位下士，便把他请进一家酒馆，请他喝了一小杯酒，就在两人对饮之际，把可怜的比利·马洛尼的种种情由都掏了出来；那真是个叫人伤心的故事。
据那下士讲，事情的原委是这样：威灵顿公爵（the Jook iv Wellington，即 the Duke of Wellington）决意要跟法国人打一场惊天动地的大仗，与此同时，波拿巴也同等坚决地要跟英国大军干上一场鬼哭神嚎的恶战。
哎，双方差不多都准备妥当之后，波拿巴便同他麾下仅次于自己的那位将军躲到一丛灌木后头，举着望远镜朝敌人望过去，想看看那么远的距离上，能不能认出其中哪一位来。

===Original===
“Bedadad!” says the gineral, afther a divil iv a long spy, “I’d bet half a pint,” says he, “that’s Bill Malowney himself,” says he, “down there,” says he.
“Och!” says Bonypart, “do you tell me so?” says he﻿—“I’m fairly heart-scalded with that same Billy Malowney,” says he; “an’ I think if I was wanst shut iv him I’d bate the rest iv them aisy,” says he.
“I’m thinking so myself,” says the gineral, says he; “but he’s a tough bye,” says he.
“Tough!” says Bonypart, “he’s the divil,” says he.
“Begorra, I’d be better plased.” says the gineral, says he, “to take himself than the Duke iv Willinton,” says he, “an’ Sir Edward Blakeney into the bargain,” says he.
“The Duke of Wellinton and Gineral Blakeney,” says Bonypart, “is great for planning, no doubt,” says he; “but Billy Malowney’s the boy for *action*,” says he﻿—“an’ action’s everything, just now,” says he.

===Chinese===
「天哪！」那位将军望了老半天望远镜之后说道，「我敢赌上半品脱酒，」他说，「底下那个，准是比尔·马洛尼本人，」他说，「就那儿，」他说。
「哎哟！」波拿巴说，「此话当真？」他说——「这个比利·马洛尼真叫我头疼透了，」他说；「我想，只要能先把这小子打发掉，剩下的那些我都不在话下，」他说。
「我也是这么想的，」那位将军说；「不过他可是个难对付的小子，」他说。
「难对付！」波拿巴说，「他简直是魔鬼，」他说。
「老天，我宁可，」那位将军说，「拿下他本人，也不愿拿威灵顿公爵（the Duke iv Willinton），」他说，「外带爱德华·布莱克尼爵士（Sir Edward Blakeney）一并算上，」他说。
「威灵顿公爵和布莱克尼将军，」波拿巴说，「长于谋划，这是不假，」他说；「可比利·马洛尼才是*实干*的料，」他说——「而眼下，实干才是一切，」他说。

===Original===
So wid that Bonypart pushes up his cocked hat, and begins scratching his head, and thinning and considherin’ for the bare life, and at last says he to the gineral:
“Gineral Commandher iv all the Foorces,” says he, “I’ve hot it,” says he: “ordher out the forlorn hope,” says he, “an’ give them as much powdher, both glazed and blasting,” says he, “an’ as much bullets do ye mind, an’ swan-dhrops an’ chain-shot,” says he, “an’ all soorts iv waipons an’ combustables as they can carry; an’ let them surround Bill Malowney,” says he, “an’ if they can get any soart iv an advantage,” says he, “let them knock him to smithereens,” says he, “an’ then take him presner,” says he; “an’ tell all the bandmen iv the Frinch army,” says he, “to play up ‘Garryowen,’ to keep up their sperits,” says he, “all the time they’re advancin’. An’ you may promise them anything you like in my name,” says he; “for, by my sowl, I don’t think its many iv them ’ill come back to throuble us,” says he, winkin’ at him.

===Chinese===
于是波拿巴把那顶三角帽往上推了推，挠起头来，挖空心思、苦苦盘算了好一阵；末了他对那将军说：
「全军统帅将军，」他说，「我有主意了，」他说：「把敢死队（the forlorn hope）调出去，」他说，「火药管够，上光的、爆破的，都给他们，」他说，「子弹嘛，您记着，也管够，还有天鹅弹和链弹，」他说，「各式武器和燃烧品，能扛多少扛多少；让他们把比尔·马洛尼团团围住，」他说，「只要能捞着半点便宜，」他说，「就把他炸成碎片，」他说，「然后再把他活捉，」他说；「再叫法国大军里所有的乐手，」他说，「都奏起《加里奥文》（Garryowen），给他们壮壮胆，」他说，「让他们一路前进时都奏着。您尽可以拿我的名义，答应他们任何您喜欢的好处，」他说；「因为，凭我的灵魂起誓，我想这里头没几个能活着回来搅扰咱们的，」他说着，冲他眨了眨眼。

===Original===
So away with the gineral, an’ he ordhers out the forlorn hope, an’ tells the band to play, an’ everything else, just as Bonypart desired him. An’ sure enough, whin Billy Malowney heerd the music where he was standin’ taking a blast of the dhudheen to compose his mind for murdherin’ the Frinchmen as usual, being mighty partial to that tune intirely, he cocks his ear a one side, an’ down he stoops to listen to the music; but, begorra, who should be in his rare all the time but a Frinch grannideer behind a bush, and seeing him stooped in a convanient forum, bedad he let flies at him sthraight, and fired him right forward between the legs an’ the small iv the back, glory be to God! with what they call (saving your presence) a bum-shell.

===Chinese===
于是那将军便去了，把敢死队调了出去，吩咐乐队奏乐，诸事一一照办，全按波拿巴吩咐的来。果不其然，比利·马洛尼当时正站在原地抽着一斗烟，好平心静气地像往常一样去屠杀那些法国佬——他本就格外爱听这支曲子——一听见那乐声，便把耳朵侧向一边，弯下腰去细听那音乐；可是，老天，他身后的灌木丛里竟然一直藏着一个法国掷弹兵，见他弯腰弯得正是时候，便径直朝他开了火，一枪正中他两腿之间、后腰那块软处，赞美上帝！用的那种玩意儿——恕我直言——叫做「轰屁股弹」（bum-shell）。

===Original===
Well, Bill Malowney let one roar out iv him, an’ away he rowled over the field iv battle like a slitther (as Bonypart and the Duke iv Wellington, that was watching the manoeuvres from a distance, both consayved) into glory.
An’ sure enough the Frinch was overjoyed beyant all bounds, an’ small blame to them﻿—an’ the Duke of Wellington, I’m toult, was never all out the same man sinst.
At any rate, the news kem home how Billy Malowney was murdhered by the Frinch in furrin parts.

===Chinese===
哎，比利·马洛尼大吼了一声，便像个滑动的东西一般，从战场上滚了开去（据远处观战的波拿巴和威灵顿公爵两人一致的看法），一路滚进了荣耀里去。
于是法国人自然欣喜若狂、无以复加——这倒也怪不得他们——而据说威灵顿公爵呢，自那以后便再也没像从前那样意气风发过。
无论如何，比利·马洛尼在异国他乡被法国人杀害的消息，就这么传回了家乡。

===Original===
Well, all this time, you may be sure, there was no want iv boys comin’ to coort purty Molly Donovan; but one way ar another, she always kept puttin’ them off constant. An’ though her father and mother was nathurally anxious to get rid of her respickably, they did not like to marry her off in spite iv her teeth.
An’ this way, promising one while and puttin’ it off another, she conthrived to get on from one Shrove to another, until near seven years was over and gone from the time when Billy Malowney listed for furrin sarvice.
It was nigh hand a year from the time whin the news iv Leum-a-rinka bein’ killed by the Frinch came home, an’ in place iv forgettin’ him, as the saisins wint over, it’s what Molly was growin’ paler and more lonesome every day, antil the neighbours thought she was fallin’ into a decline; and this is the way it was with her whin the fair of Lisnamoe kem round.

===Chinese===
哎，这一路下来，您尽管信，前来向漂亮的莫莉·多诺万求亲的小伙子可是从未断过的；可她不是这样推托、就是那样搪塞，总能一次又一次地把他们打发掉。虽说她爹娘做父母的，自然急着想把她体面地嫁出去，却也不愿违背她的心意硬把她许配了。
就这样，她一时答应、一时又拖着，竟从这一个圣灰节（Shrove）挨到了下一个圣灰节，直挨到比利·马洛尼应募远赴海外服役之后，整整将近七年都过去了。
「跳跃舞者莱姆」被法国人打死的消息传回家乡，至今也快满一年了；非但没能忘掉他，反倒随着四季更替，莫莉的脸色一日比一日苍白、神情一日比一日孤寂，邻里们都觉着她是要痨病上身了；待到利斯纳莫的集市日又转回来时，她便是这般光景。

===Original===
It was a beautiful evenin’, just at the time iv the reapin’ iv the oats, and the sun was shinin’ through the red clouds far away over the hills iv Cahirmore.
Her father an’ mother, an’ the boys an’ girls, was all away down in the fair, and Molly Sittin’ all alone on the step of the stile, listening to the foolish little birds whistlin’ among the leaves﻿—an’ the sound of the mountain-river flowin’ through the stones an’ bushes﻿—an’ the crows flyin’ home high overhead to the woods iv Glinvarlogh﻿—an’ down in the glen, far away, she could see the fair-green iv Lisnamoe in the mist, an’ sunshine among the grey rocks and threes﻿—an’ the cows an’ the horses, an’ the blue frieze, an’ the red cloaks, an’ the tents, an’ the smoke, an’ the ould round tower﻿—all as soft an’ as sorrowful as a dhrame iv ould times.

===Chinese===
那是个美丽的黄昏，正值收割燕麦的时节，阳光透过远方卡希尔莫尔（Cahirmore）群山上空的红色云朵洒落下来。
她的爹娘，还有家里的男孩女孩，全都下山赶集去了，只莫莉一个人独坐在台阶式的栅栏豁口处，听着那些傻乎乎的小鸟在树叶间啁啾——听着山间那条小河流过石头与灌木的潺潺声——听着头顶高处的乌鸦成群飞回格林瓦洛（Glinvarlogh）那片林子——而在底下远处的幽谷里，她能望见利斯纳莫那片集市草坪，在雾气与阳光中，隐现于灰白的岩石与树木之间——那些牛啊、马啊，还有那蓝色的粗呢、红色的斗篷、帐篷、炊烟，以及那座古老的圆塔楼——一切都那么柔和，又那么凄婉，仿佛一场旧日时光的梦。

===Original===
An’ while she was looking this way, an’ thinking iv Leum-a-rinka﻿—poor Bill iv the dance, that was sleepin’ in his lonesome glory in the fields iv Spain﻿—she began to sing the song he used to like so well in the ould times﻿—

> “Shule, shule, shale aroon;”

an’ when she ended the verse, what do you think but she heard a manly voice just at the other side iv the hedge, singing the last words over again!
Well she knew it; her heart flutthered up like a little bird that id be wounded, and then dhropped still in her breast. It was himself. In a minute he was through the hedge and standing before her.
“*Leum!*” says she.
“*Mavourneen cuishla machree!*” says he; and without another word they were locked in one another’s arms.

===Chinese===
她正这般望着，心里想着「跳跃舞者莱姆」——想着那可怜的、舞步飞扬的比尔，此刻正孤寂而荣耀地长眠在西班牙的旷野之上——她便唱起了他从前最爱听的那首歌——

> 「走吧，走吧，我的心肝，走吧；」（Shule, shule, shale aroon;）

她刚把这一段唱完，您猜怎么着？她竟听见篱笆那一头有个男子的嗓音，正把最后那几个字一句句接唱下去！
那嗓音她再熟悉不过；她的心像一只受了伤的小鸟似的，猛地一扑腾，随即又在她胸中静止下来。正是他本人。不多时他便钻过篱笆，站到了她跟前。
「*莱姆*！」她说。
「*我的心肝，我的血脉，我的命啊*！（Mavourneen cuishla machree!）」他说；不及再说一句话，两人便紧紧相拥在了一起。

===Original===
Well, it id only be nansinse for me thryin’ an’ tell ye all the foolish things they said, and how they looked in one another’s faces, an’ laughed, an’ cried, an’ laughed again; and how, when they came to themselves, and she was able at last to believe it was raly Billy himself that was there, actially holdin’ her hand, and lookin’ in her eyes the same way as ever, barrin’ he was browner and boulder, an’ did not, maybe, look quite as merry in himself as he used to do in former times﻿—an’ fondher for all, an’ more lovin’ than ever﻿—how he tould her all about the wars wid the Frinchmen﻿—an’ how he was wounded, and left for dead in the field iv battle, bein’ shot through the breast, and how he was discharged, an’ got a pinsion iv a full shillin’ a day﻿—and how he was come back to liv the rest iv his days in the sweet glen iv Lisnamoe, an’ (if only *she’d* consint) to marry herself in spite iv them all.

===Chinese===
哎，他们之间说了多少傻话，彼此怎样望着对方的面孔，又是笑、又是哭、笑完又哭——等我一件件说给您听，那不过是胡言乱语罢了；再说，待他们惊魂稍定，她总算肯信眼前这人的确是比利本人，实实在在地握着她的手，眼睛也一如既往地望着她——只不过他皮肤黑了些、人也壮了些，神情也许不如从前那般无忧无虑——却比从前更温柔、更痴情了几分——他怎样一五一十地把跟法国佬打仗的种种讲给她听——讲他怎样受了伤，胸膛上挨了一枪，被丢在战场上当死人——讲他怎样得了退役令，领到足足一先令一天的抚恤金——讲他怎样回到这可爱的利斯纳莫山谷，打算在此度过余生，（只要*她*肯点头）便不顾一切地娶她为妻。

===Original===
Well, ye may aisily think they had plinty to talk about, afther seven years without once seein’ one another; and so signs on, the time flew by as swift an’ as pleasant as a bird on the wing, an’ the sun wint down, an’ the moon shone sweet an’ soft instead, an’ they two never knew a ha’porth about it, but kept talkin’ an’ whisperin’, an’ whisperin’ an’ talkin’; for it’s wondherful how often a tinder-hearted girl will bear to hear a purty boy tellin’ her the same story constant over an’ over; ontil at last, sure enough, they heerd the ould man himself comin’ up the boreen, singin’ the “Colleen Rue’﻿—a thing he never done barrin’ whin he had a dhrop in; an’ the misthress walkin’ in front iv him, an’ two illigant Kerry cows he just bought in the fair, an’ the sarvint boys dhriving them behind.
“Oh, blessed hour!” says Molly, “here’s my father.”
“I’ll spake to him this minute,” says Bill.
“Oh, not for the world,” says she; “he’s singin’ the ‘Colleen Rue,’ ” says she, “and no one dar raison with him,” says she.

===Chinese===
哎，您也容易想见，七年不曾相见，两人要说的话自然多得很；果不其然，时光如飞鸟掠翅，又快又惬意地流逝着——太阳落了下去，月亮便又柔又甜地接替上来，他俩竟半点也没察觉，只是一味地说话、低语，低语、说话；因为一个心软的姑娘，能听一个俊俏的小伙子把同一桩情话翻来覆去讲上多少遍还不厌倦，这件事着实奇妙；直到最后，果不其然，他们听见老人家自己沿着小径走了回来，嘴里正唱着《红发姑娘》（Colleen Rue）——这歌他平日是从不唱的，除非肚里灌了几两黄汤——太太走在前头，后头跟着两头刚在集市上买下的上好克里牛（Kerry cows），再后头是赶牛的小工。
「哎呀，要命的时辰！」莫莉说，「我爹回来啦。」
「我这就去跟他把话说清楚，」比尔说。
「哎，万万不可，」她说；「他正唱着《红发姑娘》呢，」她说，「这会儿谁也不敢去招惹他，」她说。

===Original===
“An’ where’ll I go, thin?” says he, “for they’re into the haggard an top iv us,” says he, “an’ they’ll see me iv I lep through the hedge,” says he.
“Thry the pigsty,” says she, “mavourneen,” says she, “in the name iv God,” says she.
“Well, darlint,” says he, “for your sake,” says he, “I’ll condescend to them animals,” says he.
An’ wid that he makes a dart to get in; bud, begorra, it was too late﻿—the pigs was all gone home, and the pigsty was as full as the Burr coach wid six inside.
“Och! blur-an’-agers,” says he, “there is not room for a suckin’-pig,” says he, “let alone a Christian,” says he.
“Well, run into the house, Billy,” says she, “this minute,” says she, “an’ hide yourself antil they’re quiet,” says she, “an’ thin you can steal out,” says she, “anknownst to them all,” says she.
“I’ll do your biddin’,” says he, “Molly asthore,” says he.
“Run in thin,” says she, “an’ I’ll go an’ meet them,” says she.

===Chinese===
「那我上哪儿去呢？」他说，「他们都进院子了、就在我跟前了，」他说，「我要是从篱笆钻出去，他们保准瞧见我，」他说。
「去猪圈试试，」她说，「我的心肝，」她说，「看在上帝份上，」她说。
「也罢，亲爱的，」他说，「瞧在你的份上，」他说，「我就屈尊迁就那些畜生一回，」他说。
说着他便一头冲了过去想钻进去；可是，老天，已经太迟了——猪都已回了窝，猪圈挤得跟那辆定员六人的「伯尔」长途马车（the Burr coach）一样满满当当。
「哎哟！活见鬼，」他说，「连只奶猪都塞不下了，」他说，「更别提一个活人了，」他说。
「那快进屋里去，比利，」她说，「就这会儿，」她说，「先躲一躲，等他们安顿下来，」她说，「你再偷偷溜出去，」她说，「神不知鬼不觉地，谁也瞧不见，」她说。
「我听你的，」他说，「我的莫莉宝贝（Molly asthore），」他说。
「那就快进去吧，」她说，「我去迎他们，」她说。

===Original===
So wid that away wid her, and in wint Billy, an’ where ’id he hide himself bud in a little closet that was off iv the room where the ould man and woman slep’. So he closed the doore, and sot down in an ould chair he found there convanient.
Well, he was not well in it when all the rest iv them comes into the kitchen, an’ ould Tim Donovan singin’ the “Colleen Rue” for the bare life, an’ the rest iv them sthrivin’ to humour him, and doin’ exactly everything he bid them, because they seen he was foolish be the manes iv the liquor.
Well, to be sure all this kep’ them long enough, you may be sure, from goin’ to bed, so that Billy could get no manner iv an advantage to get out iv the house, and so he sted sittin’ in the dark closet in state, cursin’ the “Colleen Rue,” and wondherin’ to the divil whin they’d get the ould man into his bed. An’, as if that was not delay enough, who should come in to stop for the night but Father O’Flaherty, of Cahirmore, that was buyin’ a horse at the fair! An’ av course, there was a bed to be med down for his raverence, an’ some other attintions; an’ a long discoorse himself an’ ould Mrs. Donovan had about the slaughter iv Billy Malowney, an’ how he was buried on the field iv battle; an’ his raverence hoped he got a dacent funeral, an’ all the other convaniences iv religion. An’ so you may suppose it was pretty late in the night before all iv them got to their beds.

===Chinese===
于是她便走了，比利也钻进了屋——您猜他藏哪儿去了？他躲进了老人家两口子睡的那间屋旁的一个小壁橱里头。他关上门，在里头一张顺手找到的旧椅子上坐了下来。
哎，他屁股还没坐稳呢，其余一众人便都涌进了厨房，老蒂姆·多诺万正扯着老命唱着《红发姑娘》，其余的人则千方百计地顺着他，他吩咐什么他们就一字不差地照做什么，因为他们瞧出来他是喝高了犯糊涂。
哎，这一通折腾，把他们上床的时辰可拖得够久，那是自然，比利便半点便宜也占不着、出不了这屋子，于是他只好端端地坐在那黑壁橱里头，一边咒骂着那首《红发姑娘》，一边心里纳闷这帮人到底什么时候才肯把老人家弄上床去。可好像这还不够磨蹭似的，偏又来了个要在他家借宿一宿的人——是卡希尔莫尔的奥弗莱赫蒂神父（Father O’Flaherty），他来集市上买马！这下当然又得为神父大人铺一张床，再加上别的什么恭敬款待；神父大人跟老多诺万太太之间，还就着比利·马洛尼如何惨遭杀害、又是如何被埋在战场之上的事，长篇大论地谈了好一阵；神父大人还盼望他总算得到了一场体面的葬礼，以及宗教上诸般应有的礼数。这么一来您可想而知，待这一屋子人全都上了床，夜已深得很了。

===Original===
Well, Tim Donovan could not settle to sleep at all at all, an’ so he kep’ discoorsin’ the wife about the new cows he bought, an’ the stripphers he sould, an’ so an for better than an hour, ontil from one thing to another he kem to talk about the pigs, an’ the poulthry; and at last, having nothing betther to discoorse about, he begun at his daughter Molly, an’ all the heartscald she was to him be raison iv refusin’ the men. An’ at last says he:
“I onderstand,” says he, “very well how it is,” says he. “It’s how she was in love,” says he, “wid that bliggard, Billy Malowney,” says he, “bad luck to him!” says he; for by this time he was coming to his raison.
“Ah!” says the wife, says she, “Tim darlint, don’t be cursin’ them that’s dead an’ buried,” says she.
“An’ why would not I,” says he, “if they desarve it?” says he.
“Whisht,” says she, “an’ listen to that,” says she. “In the name of the Blessed Vargin,” says she, “what *is* it?” says she.

===Chinese===
哎，蒂姆·多诺万却怎么也睡不安稳，于是便跟老婆唠起了他新买的牛、卖掉的干奶牛（stripphers），如此这般地说了一个多钟头；从一桩扯到另一桩，又说到了猪啊、家禽啊；末了实在没的说了，便数落起他闺女莫莉来，说她怎样一回回地回绝求婚的人，叫他这当爹的如何操碎了心。最后他说：
「我心里头，」他说，「明白得很，是怎么一桩事，」他说。「她就是，」他说，「还爱着，」他说，「那个无赖，比利·马洛尼，」他说，「叫他倒霉透顶！」他说；因为到这时候，他的酒劲儿已渐渐地醒了过来。
「哎呀！」他老婆说，「蒂姆亲爱的，可别咒那已经死去入了土的人啊，」她说。
「我为什么不能咒，」他说，「要是他罪有应得的话？」他说。
「嘘，」她说，「你听那个，」她说。「凭圣母玛利亚之名，」她说，「那*是什么*？」她说。

===Original===
An’ sure enough what was it but Bill Malowney that was dhroppin’ asleep in the closet, an’ snorin’ like a church organ.
“Is it a pig,” says he, “or is it a Christian?”
“Arra! listen to the tune iv it,” says she; “sure a pig never done the like is that,” says she.
“Whatever it is,” says he, “it’s in the room wid us,” says he. “The Lord be marciful to us!” says he.
“I tould you not to be cursin’,” says she; “bad luck to you,” says she, “for an ommadhaun!” for she was a very religious woman in herself.
“Sure, he’s buried in Spain,” says he; “an’ it is not for one little innocent expression,” says he, “he’d be comin’ all that a way to annoy the house,” says he.

===Chinese===
果不其然，那不是别的，正是比尔·马洛尼在那壁橱里头打了盹，鼾声大作，活像一架教堂里的管风琴。
「是一头猪呢，」他说，「还是一个活人？」
「嗳！您听听那调门儿，」她说；「一头猪哪能打出这样的鼾来，」她说。
「管它是人是猪，」他说，「反正在咱们这屋里，」他说。「主啊，发发慈悲吧！」他说。
「我早叫你别咒了，」她说；「你这个蠢驴，」她说，「活该倒霉！」因为她本是个顶顶虔诚的女人。
「他不是葬在西班牙吗，」他说；「单凭我这一句无心的小小咒骂，」他说，「他还不至于跑那么远的路来搅扰这屋子，」他说。

===Original===
Well, while they war talkin’, Bill turns in the way he was sleepin’ into an aisier imposture; and as soon as he stopped snorin’ ould Tim Donovan’s courage riz agin, and says he:
“I’ll go to the kitchen,” says he, “an’ light a rish,” says he.
An’ with that away wid him, an’ the wife kep’ workin’ the beads all the time, an’ before he kem back Bill was snorin’ as loud as ever.
“Oh! bloody wars﻿—I mane the blessed saints about us!﻿—that deadly sound,” says he; “it’s going on as lively as ever,” says he.
“I’m as wake as a rag,” says his wife, says she, “wid the fair anasiness,” says she. “It’s out iv the little closet it’s comin,” says she.
“Say your prayers,” says he, “an’ hould your tongue,” says he, “while I discoorse it,” says he. “An’ who are ye,” says he, “in the name iv of all the holy saints?” says he, givin’ the door a dab iv a crusheen that wakened Bill inside. “I ax,” says he, “who are you?” says he.

===Chinese===
哎，正当两人说着话，比尔在睡梦中翻了个身，换了个舒服点的姿势；他这一止住鼾声，老蒂姆·多诺万的胆子便又壮了起来，他说：
「我去厨房，」他说，「点一根麻秆（rish）来，」他说。
说罢他便去了，老婆则在一旁一直拨弄着念珠，等他回来之前，比尔又像方才那样响亮地打起鼾来。
「哎呀！血腥的战争啊——我是说愿众圣徒庇佑我们！——这要命的声音，」他说；「又跟方才一样欢了，」他说。
「我都吓得软成抹布了，」他老婆说，「担惊受怕的，」她说。「声音是从那个小壁橱里传出来的，」她说。
「你只管念你的祷文，」他说，「闭紧你的嘴，」他说，「让我去跟他周旋，」他说。「你到底是何方神圣，」他说，「凭天上众圣徒之名？」他说着，轻轻往门上拍了那么一下，把里头的比尔惊醒了。「我且问，」他说，「你是谁？」他说。

===Original===
Well, Bill did not rightly remember where in the world he was, but he pushed open the door, an’ says he:
“Billy Malowney’s my name,” says he, “an’ I’ll thank ye to tell me a betther,” says he.
Well, whin Tim Donovan heard that, an’ actially seen that it was Bill himself that was in it, he had not strength enough to let a bawl out iv him, but he dhropt the candle out iv his hand, an’ down wid himself on his back in the dark.
Well, the wife let a screech you’d hear at the mill iv Killraghlin, an’﻿—
“Oh,” says she, “the spirit has him, body an’ bones!” says she. “Oh, holy St. Bridget﻿—oh, Mother iv Marcy﻿—oh, Father O’Flaherty!” says she, screechin’ murdher from out iv her bed.

===Chinese===
哎，比尔这会儿也记不大清自己到底身在何处了，他把门一推开，说道：
「比利·马洛尼是我的名字，」他说，「劳您驾说个更好的给我听听，」他说。
哎，蒂姆·多诺万一听这话，又亲眼瞧见里头那人果真是比尔本人，顿时连喊一嗓子的力气都没了，手一松，蜡烛便掉了下去，他也在黑暗之中仰面朝天地栽倒在地。
他老婆则发出一声尖叫——您就是在基尔拉格林（Killraghlin）那座磨坊里头都能听见——
「哎呀，」她说，「那鬼魂把他连皮带骨都抓了去啦！」她说。「哎呀，神圣的圣布里吉德（St. Bridget）啊——哎呀，慈悲之母啊——哎呀，奥弗莱赫蒂神父啊！」她喊道，从床上发出一声杀猪般的惨叫。

===Original===
Well, Bill Malowney was not a minute remimberin’ himself, an’ so out wid him quite an’ aisy, an’ through the kitchen; bud in place iv the door iv the house, it’s what he kem to the door iv Father O’Flaherty’s little room, where he was jist wakenin’ wid the noise iv the screechin’ an’ battherin’; an’ bedad, Bill makes no more about it, but he jumps, wid one boult, clever an’ clane into his raverance’s bed.
“What do ye mane, you uncivilised bliggard?” says his raverance. “Is that a venerable way,” says he, “to approach your clargy?” says he.
“Hould your tongue,” says Bill, “an’ I’ll do ye no harum,” says he.
“Who are you, ye scoundhrel iv the world?” says his raverance.
“Whisht!” says he, “I’m Billy Malowney,” says he.
“You lie!” says his raverance for he was frightened beyont all bearin’﻿—an’ he makes but one jump out iv the bed at the wrong side, where there was only jist a little place in the wall for a press, an’ his raverance could not as much as turn in it for the wealth iv kingdoms. “You lie,” says he; “but for feared it’s the truth you’re tellin’,” says he, “here’s at ye in the name iv all the blessed saints together!” says he.

===Chinese===
哎，比利·马洛尼不过一转念便回过神来，于是他便从壁橱里头从容不迫地走了出来，穿过厨房；可他没摸到屋门，倒摸到了奥弗莱赫蒂神父那间小屋的门前——神父刚才正被那尖叫和打闹声吵醒呢；于是，老天，比尔也不多话，纵身一跃，干净利落地跳进了神父大人的床。
「你这是什么意思，你这没教养的无赖？」神父大人说。「这难道是，」他说，「对待你教中神职的恭敬之礼吗？」他说。
「闭嘴，」比尔说，「我便不伤你一根毫毛，」他说。
「你是何人，你这世上的恶棍？」神父大人说。
「嘘！」他说，「我是比利·马洛尼，」他说。
「你胡说！」神父大人说——他早已吓得魂不附体——纵身一跳，从床的另一边下了地，可那一侧墙上只有一处刚好能做个小橱柜的窄缝，神父大人挤在里面，便是拿万国之富与他换，他也转不开身。「你胡说，」他说；「不过，」他说，「万一你说的是实话，」他说，「那我就奉天上众圣徒之名，奉陪你这一遭！」他说。

===Original===
An’ wid that, my dear, he blazes away at him wid a Latin prayer iv the strongest description, an’, as he said himself afterwards, that was iv a nature that id dhrive the divil himself up the chimley like a puff iv tobacky smoke, wid his tail betune his legs.
“Arra, what are ye sthrivin’ to say,” says Bill; says he, “if ye don’t hould your tongue,” says he, “wid your parly voo;” says he, “it’s what I’ll put my thumb on your windpipe,” says he, “an’ Billy Malowney never wint back iv his word yet,” says he.
“Thundher-an-owns,” says his raverance, says he﻿—seein’ the Latin took no infect on him, at all at all an’ screechin’ that you’d think he’d rise the thatch up iv the house wid the fair fright﻿—“and thundher and blazes, boys, will none iv yes come here wid a candle, but lave your clargy to be choked by a spirit in the dark?” says he.

===Chinese===
说时迟那时快，我的老天，他便劈头盖脸地朝他念起一段最最厉害的拉丁文祷文来；据他事后自己讲，那段祷文之厉害，足以把魔鬼本人念得夹着尾巴、像一缕青烟似的从烟囱里蹿出去。
「嗳，你这念的是个什么东西，」比尔说；他说，「你要是不闭嘴，」他说，「再这么巴莱武地念下去，」他说；「我就拿大拇指掐住你的喉管，」他说，「比利·马洛尼说话，从来算数，」他说。
「雷公电母啊，」神父大人说道——他眼见那拉丁文在他身上一丁点儿效用也不起——叫得那个惨啊，您准以为他光凭那点害怕就能把这屋子的茅草顶都掀起来——「雷霆烈火啊，小子们，你们就没有一个肯拿根蜡烛过来的吗？就眼睁睁看着你们神职在黑地里叫一个鬼魂给掐死？」他说。

===Original===
Well, be this time the sarvint boys and the rest iv them wor up an’ half dressed, an’ in they all run, one on top iv another, wid pitchforks and spades, thinkin’ it was only what his raverence slep’ a dhrame iv the like, by means of the punch he was afther takin’ just before he rowl’d himself into the bed. But, begorra, whin they seen it was raly Bill Malowney himself that was in it, it was only who’d be foremost out agin, tumblin’ backways, one over another, and his raverence roarin’ an’ cursin’ them like mad for not waitin’ for him.
Well, my dear, it was betther than half an hour before Billy Malowney could explain to them all how it raly was himself, for begorra they were all iv them persuadin’ him that he was a spirit to that degree it’s a wondher he did not give in to it, if it was only to put a stop to the argiment.

===Chinese===
哎，这时小工们和其余一众人也都爬了起来，胡乱穿了半截衣裳，便一个压一个地冲了进来，手里举着干草叉和铁锹——他们只当是神父大人临睡前灌了那杯潘趣酒，做了这么一场噩梦罢了。可是，老天，等他们看清里头那人果真是比尔·马洛尼本人，那便只有谁抢着头一个再逃出去的份儿了——一个个连滚带爬、你压我我压你地往后栽了出去，神父大人则在他们身后破口大骂，骂他们竟不肯等等他一道走。
哎，我的老天，比利·马洛尼费了足足大半个钟头的工夫，才跟他们一众人解释清楚他实实在在就是个活人；因为，老天作证，他们个个都在苦口婆心地劝说他，说他是个鬼魂，劝到那份儿上，连他都险些要认了这个账——哪怕只是为了把这场口舌了结了呢。

===Original===
Well, his raverence tould the ould people then, there was no use in sthrivin’ agin the will iv Providence an’ the vagaries iv love united; an’ whin they kem to undherstand to a sartinty how Billy had a shillin’ a day for the rest iv his days, begorra they took rather a likin’ to him, and considhered at wanst how he must have riz out of all his nansinse entirely, or his gracious Majesty id never have condescinded to show him his countenance that way every day of his life, on a silver shillin’.

===Chinese===
于是，神父大人便告诉二老：天意与爱情的执拗一旦合而为一，再去违抗也是徒然；待他们弄个明白、确确实实地知道，比利往后余生每日都有一先令的进项，老天，他们便倒有点喜欢上他来了，而且当即就琢磨开了：他定是早已彻底脱胎换骨、不再胡闹了，否则仁慈的国王陛下岂会屈尊，每日每夜地、在一枚银先令上头赏他见自己的圣颜呢？

===Original===
An’ so, begorra, they never stopt till it was all settled﻿—an’ there was not sich a weddin’ as that in the counthry sinst. It’s more than forty years ago, an’ though I was no more nor a gossoon myself, I remimber it like yestherday. Molly never looked so purty before, an’ Billy Malowney was plisant beyont all hearin’, to that degree that half the girls in it was fairly taren’ mad﻿—only they would not let on﻿—they had not him to themselves in place iv her. An’ begorra I’d be afeared to tell ye, because you would not believe me, since that blessid man Father Mathew put an end to all soorts of sociality, the Lord reward him, how many gallons iv pottieen whisky was dhrank upon that most solemn and tindher occasion.
Pat Hanlon, the piper, had a faver out iv it; an’ Neddy Shawn Heigue, mountin’ his horse the wrong way, broke his collarbone, by the manes iv fallin’ over his tail while he was feelin’ for his head; an’ Payther Brian, the horse-docther, I am tould, was never quite right in the head ever afther; an’ ould Tim Donovan was singin’ the “Colleen Rue” night and day for a full week; an’ begorra the weddin’ was only the foundation iv fun, and the beginning iv divarsion, for there was not a year for ten years afther, an’ more, but brought round a christenin’ as regular as the sasins revarted.

===Chinese===
于是，老天，他们一刻不停，直把这事从头到脚都定下了——那以后，乡里头再没办过那样一场婚礼。这已是四十多年前的事了，虽说那会儿我还不过是个小毛孩，可如今想起来，仍像昨日一般。莫莉从没那日那般漂亮过，而比利·马洛尼那份快活劲儿更是闻所未闻——乐到那份儿上，乡间一半的姑娘都简直要气疯了——只是她们嘴上不肯承认罢了——恨不能取莫莉而代之、把他据为己有。再说，老天，我真不敢跟您说——说了您也不会信——自从那位有福之人马修神父（Father Mathew）禁绝了形形色色的欢聚以来，愿主奖赏他，那一场最是庄重又最是温情的喜事之上，究竟喝下了多少加仑的私酿威士忌。
吹风笛的帕特·汉隆（Pat Hanlon）因此害了一场热病；而内迪·肖恩·黑格（Neddy Shawn Heigue）上马上错了方向，摸着马头去够的时候，从马屁股那头翻了过去，摔断了锁骨；还有给马看病的佩特·布赖恩（Payther Brian），据我所知，自那以后脑子就没再全乎过；老蒂姆·多诺万则没日没夜地一连唱了整整一个礼拜的《红发姑娘》；再说，老天，那场婚礼不过是欢闹的根基、嬉乐的开端，因为此后十多年间，年复一年，准会有那么一场洗礼，一年不落，准时得如同四季轮回一般。

### Prologue / 编者前言

===Original===
Upon a paper attached to the narrative which follows, Doctor Hesselius has written a rather elaborate note, which he accompanies with a reference to his essay on the strange subject which the MS. illuminates.

===Chinese===
在附于下文这份记述之上的一纸笺记里，赫塞利乌斯医生（Doctor Hesselius）写下了一段相当详备的按语，并援引了他本人就这一手稿所阐明的离奇主题所撰的一篇论文。

===Original===
This mysterious subject, he treats, in that essay, with his usual learning and acumen, and with remarkable directness and condensation. It will form but one volume of the series of that extraordinary man's collected papers.

===Chinese===
这一神秘的主题，他在那篇论文中以他惯有的学识与敏锐加以探讨，行文之直捷凝练，颇堪瞩目。该文将来只不过是这位非凡人物全集系列中的一卷而已。

===Original===
As I publish the case, in these volumes, simply to interest the laity, I shall forestall the intelligent lady, who relates it, in nothing; and, after due consideration, I have determined, therefore, to abstain from presenting any précis of the learned Doctor's reasoning, or extract from his statement on a subject which he describes as "involving, not improbably, some of the profoundest arcana of our dual existence, and its intermediates."

===Chinese===
我在本丛书中公布这桩医案，无非是为了引起一般读者的兴趣，因此，对于那位讲述此案的聪慧女士，我无意抢先置喙任何内容；经过慎重考量，我遂决定，对这位博学医生的推论不作任何摘要，对其论述亦不作任何摘引——他所探讨的这一主题，他本人形容为"所涉者，颇有可能牵动我们二元存在及其居间层次的若干最深奥秘"。

===Original===
I was anxious, on discovering this paper, to reopen the correspondence commenced by Doctor Hesselius, so many years before, with a person so clever and careful as his informant seems to have been. Much to my regret, however, I found that she had died in the interval.

===Chinese===
发现这纸笺记之时，我本急欲重启赫塞利乌斯医生在多年以前与那位情报提供者所开始的通信——其人观其所述，显得那般聪敏而审慎。然而令我深感惋惜的是，我得知她已在此期间故去了。

===Original===
She, probably, could have added little to the narrative which she communicates in the following pages, with, so far as I can pronounce, such a conscientious particularity.

===Chinese===
推想起来，对于她在以下篇页中所传达的那份记述——以我所能判断的而言，她已怀着那般一丝不苟的周详将其备述——她恐怕也再难有所增补了。

## Dickon the Devil / 魔鬼迪肯

===Original===
About thirty years ago I was selected by two rich old maids to visit a property in that part of Lancashire which lies near the famous forest of Pendle, with which Mr. Ainsworth's *Lancashire Witches* has made us so pleasantly familiar. My business was to make partition of a small property, including a house and demesne, to which they had a long time before succeeded as co-heiresses.
The last forty miles of my journey I was obliged to post, chiefly by crossroads, little known, and less frequented, and presenting scenery often extremely interesting and pretty. The picturesqueness of the landscape was enhanced by the season, the beginning of September, at which I was travelling.
I had never been in this part of the world before; I am told it is now a great deal less wild, and, consequently, less beautiful.

===Chinese===
约莫三十年前，我受两位富有的老姑娘所托，前往兰开夏郡（Lancashire）靠近著名的彭德尔森林（Pendle）那一带查看一份产业——正是安斯沃思先生（Mr. Ainsworth）那部《兰开夏的女巫》（*Lancashire Witches*）使我们何等惬意地熟稔起来的所在。我所办的事，是将一处小小的产业——连带宅邸与田庄——加以分割；这处产业，她们作为共同继承人，早已继承了多时。
此行最后四十英里，我只得改乘驿车，走的尽是些岔路，鲜为人知，行旅更稀，沿途所见却往往景致极佳、趣味盎然。彼时正值九月初，我此番赶路，正值风景入画，更因时令而添了几分韵致。
这一带地方我从前从未到过；听说如今已大不如昔日荒凉，自然也便大不如昔日秀美了。

===Original===
At the inn where I had stopped for a relay of horses and some dinner—for it was then past five o'clock—I found the host, a hale old fellow of five-and-sixty, as he told me, a man of easy and garrulous benevolence, willing to accommodate his guests with any amount of talk, which the slightest tap sufficed to set flowing, on any subject you pleased.
I was curious to learn something about Barwyke, which was the name of the demesne and house I was going to. As there was no inn within some miles of it, I had written to the steward to put me up there, the best way he could, for a night.
The host of the "Three Nuns," which was the sign under which he entertained wayfarers, had not a great deal to tell. It was twenty years, or more, since old Squire Bowes died, and no one had lived in the Hall ever since, except the gardener and his wife.
"Tom Wyndsour will be as old a man as myself; but he's a bit taller, and not so much in flesh, quite," said the fat innkeeper.
"But there were stories about the house," I repeated, "that they said, prevented tenants from coming into it?"
"Old wives' tales; many years ago, that will be, sir; I forget 'em; I forget 'em all. Oh yes, there always will be, when a house is left so; foolish folk will always be talkin'; but I hadn't heard a word about it this twenty year."
It was vain trying to pump him; the old landlord of the "Three Nuns," for some reason, did not choose to tell tales of Barwyke Hall, if he really did, as I suspected, remember them.

===Chinese===
我在一家客栈停下换马、用些饭食——其时已过五点——只见店主人是个硬朗的老汉，自称六十五岁，性情随和，话多而热忱，乐意陪客人闲话，无论什么题目，只消轻轻一敲，那话匣子便滔滔不绝地打开。
我急于打听一些巴威克（Barwyke）的情形——那便是我所要去的田庄与宅邸的名字。因为那一带方圆数里之内并无客栈，我已写信给管事，托他尽力在那宅子里为我安顿一夜。
这位店主人——他在"三尼姑"（Three Nuns）这招牌之下招待过往行旅——却没有多少话可讲。老鲍斯乡绅（Squire Bowes）去世，至今已有二十余年；自那以后，除却园丁夫妇，再无人住过那座宅邸。
"汤姆·温德索（Tom Wyndsour）跟我一般年纪；不过他个子略高些，身上的肉倒不及我多。"胖店主如是说。
"可是听说那宅子有些传言，"我又道，"说是这些传言害得没人敢来租住？"
"老婆子们的瞎话罢啦；那都是多少年前的事了，先生；我全忘啦；统统忘啦。哦，那是自然，宅子这么空着，总免不了的；蠢人总是爱嚼舌头；可这二十年来，我一个字也没听人再提起过。"
再要从他嘴里套话，却是徒然；"三尼姑"的老店主不知出于何故，不肯讲巴威克宅邸（Barwyke Hall）的事——倘若他真如我所疑，还记得那些事的话。

===Original===
I paid my reckoning, and resumed my journey, well pleased with the good cheer of that old-world inn, but a little disappointed.
We had been driving for more than an hour, when we began to cross a wild common; and I knew that, this passed, a quarter of an hour would bring me to the door of Barwyke Hall.
The peat and furze were pretty soon left behind; we were again in the wooded scenery that I enjoyed so much, so entirely natural and pretty, and so little disturbed by traffic of any kind. I was looking from the chaise-window, and soon detected the object of which, for some time, my eye had been in search. Barwyke Hall was a large, quaint house, of that cagework fashion known as "black-and-white," in which the bars and angles of an oak framework contrast, black as ebony, with the white plaster that overspreads the masonry built into its interstices. This steep-roofed Elizabethan house stood in the midst of park-like grounds of no great extent, but rendered imposing by the noble stature of the old trees that now cast their lengthening shadows eastward over the sward, from the declining sun.
The park-wall was grey with age, and in many places laden with ivy. In deep grey shadow, that contrasted with the dim fires of evening reflected on the foliage above it, in a gentle hollow, stretched a lake that looked cold and black, and seemed, as it were, to skulk from observation with a guilty knowledge.

===Chinese===
我结了账，重新上路。那古旧客栈的饭菜酒食倒叫我受用，心里却不免有些失望。
车子又赶了一个多钟头，我们开始穿过一片荒原；我知道，过了这片荒原，再有一刻钟便到巴威克宅邸的门前了。
泥炭与荆豆很快被抛在身后；我们又驶入了那令我心旷神怡的林地景致之中，那样浑然天成、那样秀丽，几乎不沾半点人烟车马的烟火气。我从马车窗里望去，很快便瞥见了那一阵子我目光一直在搜寻的目标。巴威克宅邸是一座大而古怪的宅子，乃是那种俗称"黑白相间"的木骨墙架构造，橡木框架的横档与转角，黑如乌木，与填嵌其间、涂抹其上的白灰泥，恰成鲜明的对照。这座陡顶的伊丽莎白时代（Elizabethan）老宅，坐落在一片类乎园囿的庭地之中，庭地虽不算大，却因古木参天而显得气象肃穆；此刻夕阳西斜，那些古木正把渐长的影子向东投在草地上。
园墙因年深日久而呈灰色，许多地方爬满了常春藤。在一片低浅的洼地里，横卧着一方湖水，看去又冷又黑，仿佛怀着什么亏心事，有意躲开众人的目光；那湖水隐在深深的灰色阴影之中，与上方树冠上反映着的暮色残光，恰成对照。

===Original===
