“From this state of happy oblivion I was aroused by the pressure of a hand upon my shoulder, and the administration of two or three impatient jolts thoroughly awakened me. I started upright in the bed, and mechanically stretched my hand towards the pistols which lay beside me. The precaution was unnecessary; my visitor was a female﻿—the poor girl whose person I had recognised in the kitchen before. The candle had hardly wasted since I had closed my eyes; I could not have slept a quarter of an hour. I gazed fixedly upon the features of the servant girl; they were tense and pale as those of death: there was such mortal agitation in the face as filled my mind with awe. With an impressive and imploring gesture, several times repeated, she enjoined silence, and then leaning forward, she whispered with slow and startling emphasis﻿—

“ ‘Within a few minutes, *murderers* will come to your bedside: I wish you to escape. Draw the tapestry at this side of your bed; you will find a door behind it; a long passage leads from it to a flight of steps, and they to the kitchen. Wait at the head of the stairs with your drawn sword in your hand, and when you hear me say, God send us all better days, it shall be a signal to you that one of them is about to enter from the kitchen the passage where you stand; drive the sword through him, and run into the kitchen, where you will find another, perhaps two; I shall take care that no more are there. Be firm, and pray to God.’

“With these words she glided speedily from the room, leaving me horror-struck at the sudden and ghastly intimation. With silent rapidity I rose from the bed﻿—my preparations were speedily made. I stuck my pistols in my belt, and taking my naked sword under my arm, I soon found the door which my protectress had described. I extinguished the candle, and, entering the passage, closed the door behind me.

===Chinese===
"我就这么百无聊赖地躺着，疲倦那甜蜜的睡意悄悄袭来；我所躺的这间屋子渐渐模糊、朦胧起来；我的疲倦和焦虑 alike 都被深沉而平静的无知无觉所淹没。

"正当我沉浸在这种幸福的忘却之中，一只手按在我肩上、又使劲推搡了两三下，把我彻底弄醒了。我一惊，从床上直挺挺坐起，下意识地向身边的手枪伸出手去。这番小心是多余的；来人是位女子——就是我在厨房里认出的那个可怜丫头。蜡烛自从我合眼以来几乎没怎么短下去；我睡了怕还不到一刻钟。我盯着那丫头的脸看；那脸紧绷着，白得像死人的脸：她脸上那种致命的惊惶使我心头充满敬畏。她以一个令人难忘、恳求般的手势，连做了好几次，示意我噤声，然后探过身来，缓慢而惊人地一字一句低语道——

"'不出几分钟，*杀人凶手*便会到您床前：我要您逃命。把您床这边的帷幔拉开；您会发现后面有一扇门；一条长过道从那儿通到一段楼梯，楼梯又通到厨房。您手执出鞘的剑守在楼梯顶上，等听到我说，愿上帝赐我们好日子——那便是信号，告诉您其中一个正要从厨房走进您所立的那条过道；您一剑把他捅穿，然后冲进厨房，那里头还有一个，也许两个；我会设法不让更多的人在那里。要稳住，向上帝祷告。'

"说罢她便飞快地滑出了房间，留下我对这突如其来、毛骨悚然的告警目瞪口呆。我无声而迅速地从床上起来——一应准备很快便做停当。我把两支手枪插进腰带，腋下夹着出鞘的长剑，很快便找到了我的保护人所描述的那扇门。我吹灭了蜡烛，走进过道，把门在身后带上。

===Original===
“This passage was extremely narrow and low; the floor and ceiling were of stone; and, as I imagined, its whole width lay in the thickness of the wall. Along this strange corridor I cautiously pushed my way; and, after a progress which appeared all but interminable, I reached the first of a flight of steep stone steps, leading downwards, and here I paused. I had hardly ceased to move when I became conscious that every sound, even that of the lightest foot-tread upon the kitchen floor, was distinctly audible where I stood. I heard the shuffling of many feet to and fro, accompanied by a great deal of whispering. These sounds continuing for a long time, without being followed by any decisive result, my nerves were gradually wrought by the suspense in which I stood to such a pitch of excitement, that I could not remain still. I descended the stairs with the utmost caution. When I had reached the foot, I found a space which afforded little more than standing room. Straight before me, and within a few inches of my face, was the door which opened upon the kitchen. This was a double door, constructed, as I afterwards found, so as to resemble from without a sort of cupboard. A broad chink in the centre, where the two valves met, admitted a bright stream of light; and placing my eye at the aperture, I witnessed, unobserved, a scene which no occurrence of my after life has availed to obliterate.

===Chinese===
"这条过道极窄、极低；地板和顶棚都是石的；我想，它的整个宽度就藏在墙壁的厚度里。沿着这条古怪的廊道，我小心翼翼地摸索前行；走了一段似乎永无尽头的路之后，我到了一段陡峭石阶的头一磴，石阶往下通去，我便在此停住。我刚一动也不动地立定，便察觉到：每一个声响——哪怕是厨房地板上最轻的一下脚步——都清晰地传到我所立之处。我听见许多脚来回地拖沓，伴着大量的低语。这些声响持续了很久却没有任何决定性的下文，我那一颗悬着的心渐渐地把我神经绷到了亢奋的极点，再也立不住了。我以最大的小心走下楼梯。到了底下，我只寻得一块勉强能立身的小小空地。正对着我、离我脸不过几寸之遥的，便是那扇通向厨房的门。这是一扇对开门，后来我才得知，从外面看过去做成一个橱柜的模样。两扇门扉相合的正中处有一道宽缝，漏出一线明亮的光；我把眼睛凑到那缝上，无人察觉地目击了一幕——我此后一生中任何变故都没能把它从我心头抹去。

===Original===
“At the side of the chamber opposite to that at which I was placed, stood the bed in which lay the poor pedlar: his deep stertorous breathing sufficiently attested the soundness of the slumber in which he was locked. A blazing faggot flamed and flickered on the hearth, throwing an intense but uncertain light over the whole scene. Close by the fire stood two stout fellows, in one of whom I recognised, without difficulty, my good-humoured guide. Beside them sat a third, with his legs extended towards the cheering blaze, while with an air of sublime abstraction, he leisurely smoked a long pipe. At the same time I observed the girl to whom I owed the timely warning, whose success was yet so doubtful, employed in carrying towards the bed in which my poor comrade was sleeping, a large tub, or bucket. Beside the bed stood Giuseppe himself, a hideous incarnation of evil, glaring upon the unconscious slumberer. A boy, resting his head upon the foot of the bed, was fast asleep also. Such was the scene which my first glance through the aperture of the door revealed, under the fierce and restless light of the blazing wood fire. The baleful and ominous scowl which darkened the features of the ill-favoured innkeeper, and something like a foreboding of what was about to happen, rivetted my attention to the group about the humble bed where the poor little traveller lay. The innkeeper stooped forward, and with a sudden jerk of his hand threw the bedclothes down, so as to leave the upper part of the body of the sleeper bare, except for the coarse shirt which covered it. He next slid his arm gently under the shoulders of the unconscious man, and slowly drew his body towards the edge of the bed. At this moment the girl placed the bucket at the side of the pallet, and with an expression of strange horror turned towards the door where I stood, and passed on from my sight. Giuseppe now drew the shoulders completely over the edge of the couch, so that the head hung down towards the floor. The poor wretch continued to sleep. The innkeeper beckoned now to one of his companions, who stood at the fire. The man came over to the bed, and listlessly shoved the bucket with his foot, until he had brought it directly under the head of the sleeping man. I could endure no more. My resolution was taken. I set my shoulder against the door, and strained every muscle in my body in the desperate effort to burst it open. The effort, tre mendous though it was, was made in vain. The door was fastened without, and that so effectually, that the assault with which I had just taxed its strength had hardly availed to make the fastenings creak. Well was it for me, however, that this sound, slight though it was, occurred while the villain was shoving the bucket, as I have just told you, with his foot along the floor. Had that little sound but reached the ear of any of the wretches who occupied the chamber, I must have perished. On such threads hang the lives of men! Weak and exhausted by the fruitless effort which I had made, I resigned myself in mute horror to witness the tragedy which I had no power to prevent. Giuseppe now, in a whisper which froze the lifeblood at my heart, repeated the significant words﻿—‘*Il coltello*,’ *the knife*. His companion instantly turned to a cupboard, a few steps aside, and returned bearing in his hand the instru ment, whose broad blade, as he walked along, he wiped in his jacket sleeve. The cold sweat burst from every pore in my body. I shook like a man in an ague: a deadly sickness came over me; yet I could not move my eyes from the objects, the sight of which filled me with this agony. The man, with the knife in his grasp, now placed himself by the bed, half sitting upon its edge. Giuseppe took the head of the sleeping man between his hands, and supported it with the face turned directly towards the place where I stood. His companion now applied the edge of the knife to the skin of the throat, and moving it slightly along the surface, until it rested upon the spot which he judged most suitable to his purpose, he laid the palm of his left hand upon the back of the blade, and with his whole weight and strength forced it with a mangling gash, so far as almost to sever the head from the body. The crimson blood gushed, or rather spouted, from the chasm, and, with a gurgling sound, poured into the bucket. At the same moment the assassin, dropping the knife upon the floor, threw himself across the body, to control the convulsive strugglings of death. The pedlar had continued fast locked in sleep, until the knife had actually entered his throat. The moment, however, that the fatal stroke was given, the murdered man opened his eyes, and gazed with such an expression of imploring terror and agony, as fancy never beheld. At the same time he opened his mouth﻿—perhaps to shriek﻿—perhaps to pray; but sound was never more to come from thence. Blood bubbled forth, and streamed over his white and quivering face. Again and again he opened his mouth with ghastly strugglings. Nor did this fearful motion cease, until the eye fixed, and the mortal agony ended in death. The innkeeper then wrung the head round, while his companion, with the same knife, ploughed through the tendons and muscles, until they succeeded in actually cutting the head from the trunk. The body lay upon the bed, and the neck still hung bleeding over the tub, into which Giuseppe dropped the head. I could see no more. My brain grew dizzy. A sick faintness came upon me. I clambered, I know not how, up the stairs, and, sitting down upon the uppermost step, I clasped my damp forehead in my hands, and remained for some minutes almost unconscious of everything, absorbed in one dull, vague feeling of horror.

===Chinese===
"在我所立之处对面的那侧，摆着那张床，可怜的小贩就躺在上面：他粗重的鼾声足以证明他睡得何等之沉。炉膛里一捆柴烧得正旺，火焰跳动、明灭不定，把整个场景照得强烈却又摇曳。紧挨着炉火站着两个壮汉，其中一个我毫不费力地便认了出来——正是我那位和气的向导。他俩身旁坐着一个第三个人，两腿伸向那暖融融的火，神情超然物外，慢悠悠地抽着一杆长烟斗。与此同时，我看见那位我承她及时告警、而成败尚在未卜之间的姑娘，正把一只大木盆、或说是水桶，往我那可怜同伴所睡的床边搬。床边站着朱塞佩本人——一个丑陋的恶之化身，正虎视眈眈地盯着那毫不知情的酣睡者。一个男孩，头枕着床脚，也睡得正沉。这便是我透过门缝第一眼所窥见的场景——在熊熊柴火那凶猛不安的光之下。那副长在丑陋店主脸上的、凶险而 ominously 不祥的怒容，加上一丝仿佛预感到即将发生之事的预感，把我的注意力牢牢钉在那张寒酸的床四周——那可怜的小行商便躺在上面。店主向前一俯身，手猛地一掀，把被子掀了下去，让睡着的人上半身裸露出来，只剩一件粗布衬衫遮着。接着他轻轻地把胳膊伸到那毫无知觉之人的肩下，慢慢把他的身子往床沿拖。就在这时，姑娘把木桶放到铺边，带着一种奇异恐怖的神情，转身朝我所立的那扇门望了一眼，便从我视野中消失了。朱塞佩此时把那人的肩膀整个儿拖过了床沿，让头朝着地板垂了下去。那可怜虫还在睡。店主这时朝火边的一个同伙招了招手。那人走到床前，漫不经心地用脚把桶拨过去，直到把它正正地拨到睡着的人的头底下。我再也受不了了。我下定决心。我用肩膀顶住门，拼了全身每一块肌肉，发了疯似的要把门撞开。这一撞虽是雷霆万钧，却是徒劳。门从外面闩死了，闩得那么严实，我刚才那番猛撞也只是勉强叫门闩咯吱了一声罢了。不过我命不该绝，这一点点声响——虽则细微——恰好发生在那恶棍正用脚把桶拨过地板的时候。倘若这小小一声落进了屋里任何一个恶徒的耳朵里，我必死无疑。人的性命便系在这么一缕细丝之上！我那一番徒劳的努力弄得我虚弱不堪、筋疲力尽，我只好在无声的恐怖中认命，眼睁睁地看着这出我无力阻止的惨剧。这时朱塞佩以一种冻结我心头血的耳语，重复了那句意味深长的话——'*Il coltello*'，刀。他的同伙立刻转身走向几步之外的一个橱柜，回来时手里拿着那件家伙——他一边走，一边在夹克袖子上擦那宽宽的刀刃。冷汗从我全身每一个毛孔里涌出。我抖得像个打摆子的人：一阵致命的恶心涌上来；可我却无法把眼睛从那些令我痛苦欲绝的物事上移开。那握刀的人此时走到床边，半坐在床沿上。朱塞佩双手捧住睡着之人的头，让那张脸正对着我所立之处。他的同伙把刀刃贴在那人的喉皮上，沿皮肤轻轻滑动了一下，找到他自认为最合适的位置，便把左手掌按在刀背上，用全身的重量和力气猛地一压——这一刀切得血肉模糊，几乎把头颅从身上割了下来。殷红的血从那道豁口里喷涌而出，更准确地说是喷射而出，咕嘟咕嘟地灌进了木桶。与此同时，那凶手把刀往地上一扔，整个人扑到尸体上，压住那临死挣扎的抽搐。那小贩一直沉沉睡去，直到那把刀真的刺进了他的喉咙。然而致命的一刀下去的那一刻，被杀之人睁开了眼睛，以一种恳求的、恐怖而痛苦的眼神凝望着——这种神情是任何想象力都未曾见过的。与此同时，他张开了嘴——也许是想尖叫——也许是想祷告；可声音再也别想从那儿发出来了。血咕嘟嘟地冒出来，淌过他苍白、颤抖的脸。他一次又一次地张开嘴，做出可怖的挣扎。这可怕的抽动直到那双眼睛定了神、那致命的痛苦终结于死亡，才告停止。店主这才拧过那颗头，他的同伙则用同一把刀，切开筋腱和肌肉，直到他们当真把头从躯干上割了下来。尸体躺在床上，那截脖颈仍悬在木桶上方滴着血，朱塞佩便把那颗头扔进了桶里。我再也看不下去了。我头晕目眩。一阵令人作呕的昏晕袭来。我也不知自己是怎么爬上楼梯的，在最上面一磴坐下，双手抱住湿漉漉的额头，有好几分钟几乎对一切浑然不觉，整个儿沉浸在那一片沉重、朦胧的恐怖之中。

===Original===
“As soon as I came a little to myself, I plainly perceived, by what I could gather from the whisperings which I overheard from below, that the murderers were engaged in removing the body of their victim. Steps now slowly and unsteadily traversed the kitchen﻿—I suppose those of him who carried the horrible burden. The outer door was cautiously opened; the steps passed forth, and the door again closed.

“ ‘The gentleman sleeps like a top,’ whispered a gruff voice. ‘He has put out his candle, and lies still as a dormouse.’

“ ‘Take your stiletto,’ replied another. ‘Morning will break before you have finished.’

“ ‘Remove your boots, bungler,’ cried a female voice. ‘Your spurs make jingle enough to ring the dead from their graves.’

“ ‘Peace, gaol-bird,’ cried Giuseppe. ‘What’s that to thee.’

“ ‘Well, well,’ exclaimed the girl, with a slow distinct utterance, ‘God grant us all better days.’

“I needed not the warning, I had already placed myself in readiness. After a short delay the door, through which I had just witnessed the scene which I have attempted to describe, opened wide. A broad light flashed upon the rugged and narrow stairs, and a tall figure began to ascend. I stood in the deep shadow awaiting his advance; and as soon as he had arrived within two or three steps of the top, I sprang forward, and lunged full at his breast. This was not done so quickly that he did not catch a glimpse of me, as I started forward, in sufficient time to enable him with his arm imperfectly to parry the thrust. As it happened, however, this was all the worse for himself; for instead of turning the sword aside, he merely struck the point upwards, and it entered somewhere near the eye, and, penetrating the brain, killed him on the spot. Without a groan he tumbled headlong over the steps. Springing over his prostrate body, I rushed into the kitchen. Giuseppe and my honest guide were the only males within it. The latter stood nearest to me, and his astonishment at my entrance was such that he did not move. With a deliberate aim of two seconds, I levelled my pistol at his breast and fired, he fell﻿—I know not whether mortally hurt or not, but I never saw him move again. Without the loss of an instant I levelled the second pistol at the innkeeper﻿—but it missed fire﻿—the wretch ran directly to the door, but before his hand had reached the latch I was up with him. With a hideous yell of defiance he sprang round and grappled with me. His strength far exceeded what his figure seemed to promise; but I felt that he was still no match for me. In a moment I hurled him back upon the gory pallet, and planted my knee upon his breast. As we struggled, he caught my left thumb within his teeth, and clenched them upon it until they fairly ground upon the bone. Heedless of the pain, I clutched his throat in my right hand, and pressed with all my might and strength﻿—in vain he struggled﻿—the eyes started﻿—the face blackened. Froth covered my hands, and before two minutes he lay insensible.

===Chinese===
"等我稍稍回过神来，我从楼下偷听到的低语之中清楚地听出，那些凶手正忙着搬走被害人的尸首。这时一阵缓慢而踉跄的脚步穿过厨房——我猜是那个扛着那可怕重负之人的脚步。外边的门被小心翼翼地打开；脚步走出去；门又关上了。

"'那位绅士睡得跟个陀螺似的，'一个粗哑的嗓音低语道，'他熄了蜡烛，一动不动地躺着，跟只睡鼠一般。'

"'拿上你的匕首，'另一个答道，'等你们弄完，天都要亮了。'

"'把你的靴子脱了，笨手笨脚的东西，'一个女人的声音喊道，'你的马刺叮当作响，响得能把死人从坟里都唤起来。'

"'住嘴，你这蹲过牢的，'朱塞佩喝道，'关你什么事。'

"'好啦，好啦，'那姑娘以一种缓慢而清晰的语调喊道，'愿上帝赐我们好日子。'

"这信号我原不消她提醒，我早已严阵以待。稍过片刻，那扇我刚才透过它目击了所述场景的门，便大大地敞开了。一道宽阔的光闪照在粗陋而狭窄的楼梯上，一个高大的身影开始上楼。我立在深深的阴影里等他上前；待他上到离顶还有两三磴之时，我一跃而起，照他胸口便是一剑刺去。可这事做得还不够快——我向前一扑之时，他瞥见了我，还来得及用胳膊勉强挡了一下。然而这样一来，反倒对他更不利；因为他并未把剑拨开，只是把剑尖往上一挑，剑便从眼旁某处刺了进去，贯穿脑子，当场把他结果了。他连哼都没哼一声，便一头从楼梯上栽了下去。我从他俯卧的尸体上一跃而过，冲进了厨房。朱塞佩和我那位诚实的向导是屋里仅有的两个男人。后者离我最近，他一见我冲进来，惊得呆住了，竟一动不动。我屏息瞄准了两秒钟，把手枪对准他胸口便扣了扳机，他应声倒下——是死是伤我不知道，但我再没见他动弹过。我一刻也不耽搁，把第二支手枪对准了店主——可它哑了火——那恶棍直扑门口，可他的手还没碰到门闩，我便赶上了他。他发出一声骇人的、挑衅的嚎叫，猛地转身，与我扭作一团。他的力气远比他的身板看上去的要大得多；可我觉得他终究不是我的对手。眨眼之间，我便把他摔回到那张血淋淋的草垫上，一膝盖顶在他胸口。我们扭打之际，他一口咬住了我的左手拇指，咬得几乎磨到了骨头。我顾不得疼痛，右手死死掐住他的喉咙，用尽全身力气——他徒劳地挣扎——眼珠凸出——脸色发黑。白沫沾了我一手，不到两分钟他便瘫了下去。

===Original===
“ ‘For God’s sake, girl,’ cried I, ‘give me the pistol.’ Silently she obeyed me, and for a moment relaxing my grasp, I seized the weapon by the muzzle, and dashed the heavy butt into his skull﻿—he was dead. Yet such was the strength with which his teeth were locked upon my thumb, that I could not release it until I had beaten out nearly half his teeth, I forced the barrel of the pistol into his mouth, and employing it as a lever, I, with much exertion, unlocked the clenched teeth, and loosed the mangled joint. At this moment I heard a heavy step without, the latch was raised, and one of the fellows who had been present at the murder of the pedlar entered. I did not give him time to recover his surprise, but placing the pistol to his head, I said in a stern and determined voice﻿—‘Villain! lead me to a horse. If I am discovered or interrupted, I will blow your brains out.’

“ ‘Good Signor,’ said the fellow, evidently ill at his ease, ‘patience for heaven’s sake﻿—be not rash.’

“ ‘I give you five seconds,’ replied I, ‘to bring me to a horse: at the end of that time, the condition unfulfilled, I will shoot you through the head, as sure as God is in heaven. Look at those corpses﻿—you see I am in earnest.’

“The fellow said not one word more; but, being himself unarmed, led me quietly from the door of the inn at which we stood to that of the stable. I all the time holding him by the back of the collar, with the pistol close by his head.

“ ‘Choose a strong one, scoundrel,’ said I, as we entered the stable, in which stood several horses ready saddled. I compelled him to lead out the steed, and to mount first himself, and springing up behind him, I commanded him to ride on the shortest track leading to the high road to Rome. The moon had gone down, and the night was now so dark that I could not see many yards before me. In obedience to my directions the fellow rode at a hard trot. We had scarcely crossed the bridge, when two figures loomed suddenly in sight, and so directly in advance of us that it required a sudden and violent exertion of the bit which threw the animal back upon his haunches, to prevent our running foul of this nocturnal patrol.

“ ‘Who rides so hard?’ inquired one in no very dulcet accents. Here I pressed the muzzle of the pistol against my companion’s head, as a salutary hint.

“ ‘Who should it be,’ exclaimed my comrade, ‘but a friend﻿—do not you know me?’

“ ‘Faith, brother,’ replied the same harsh voice, it is well we did not rob thee, and thou us;’ and marvellously tickled with this pleasant conceit he laughed long and lustily. ‘Any news?’ added he﻿—‘any rabbits in the burrow? any nightingales in the cage﻿—eh?’

“ ‘Ay, two,’ replied my companion, ‘with their necks wrung. You will see more at the inn. Good night.’

“We were passing on, when again one of them exclaimed﻿—

“ ‘Hey! what the devil have you gotten behind you?’

“Again, I let my honest companion feel that the weapon rested upon his skull; and with much nonchalance, he replied﻿—

“ ‘What is behind me? why a bag of bloody carrion, if you must have it﻿—but we bandy words too long﻿—when I get rid of this, I’ll find you at old Beppo’s.’

“ ‘Well, good luck, most holy sexton,’ replied the horseman; ‘and as for your burden, *requiescat in pace*﻿—amen.’

“ ‘So saying, the two horsemen rode on, and we pursued our way, at the same hard pace, until the morning’s light began to streak the east.

“Watching my opportunity as we rode rapidly down a steep declivity, I bestowed my companion a vigorous shove, which sent him clean over the horse’s head; and before he had well done rolling I had left him four hundred yards behind me. With a courteous valediction I rode on, and without another adventure reached the glorious city of Rome, where strange things befell me, as I shall tell you. But first give me a cup of wine.”

===Chinese===
"'看在上帝份上，姑娘，'我喊道，'把手枪给我。'她默默地依言照办，我略一松手，便握住枪管，用那沉重的枪托朝他脑壳狠狠砸了下去——他死了。然而他那一口牙咬住我拇指的力道之大，竟使我抽不出来，直到我砸掉了他将近一半的牙，又把枪管塞进他嘴里，权作撬棍，费了好大的劲才撬开那紧咬的牙关，把那血肉模糊的指节解救出来。就在此时，我听见外面一阵沉重的脚步，门闩一抬，方才参与谋杀小贩的同伙之一走了进来。我没给他从惊愕中回过神来的工夫，把枪口顶住他的脑袋，厉声而决然地说道——'恶棍！给我牵一匹马来。要是被人发觉或拦阻，我便轰烂你的脑袋。'

"'好心的先生，'那人显然心慌意乱，说道，'看在上天的份上，宽限片刻——切勿鲁莽。'

"'我给你五秒钟，'我答道，'把我带到马跟前：时限一到，若没办到，我便一枪打穿你的头，正如上帝在天上一般确凿。瞧那些尸首——你瞧，我不是说着玩的。'

"那家伙再不敢多说一个字；他自己既没了家伙，便乖乖地把我从我们所立的客栈门口带到马厩门前。我一路揪住他的后领，枪口紧贴着他的脑壳。

"'挑一匹壮实的，混账，'我们走进马厩时我说道，厩里拴着好几匹已经备好鞍的马。我逼着他牵出那匹骏马，让他先骑上去，我自己一跃跨上马背坐在他身后，命他走最近的路直奔通往罗马的大道。月亮已经落下，夜黑得我面前几码之外便看不见东西。那人遵命疾步小跑。我们刚过桥，两个身影便赫然映入眼帘，正正地拦在我们前头，我猛地用力勒马，那畜生一下子被勒得后腿坐地，这才没撞上这对夜间的巡逻。

"'谁这么急地赶路？'其中一个以毫不悦耳的嗓音问道。这时我把枪口往同伴脑壳上顶了顶，权作有益的提醒。

"'还能是谁，'我这位同伴喊道，'自然是朋友——你认不得我了？'

"'凭信义说，兄弟，'那个同样的粗嗓门答道，'幸亏我没抢你，你也没抢我们；'他似乎被这一句妙语逗得乐不可支，纵声大笑起来。'有什么消息吗？'他接着问道——'洞里有兔子吗？笼里有夜莺吗——嗯？'

"'有，两只，'我同伴答道，'都拧断了脖子。你们到客栈去还能看见更多呢。晚安。'

"我们正要过去，其中一人又喊道——

"'嘿！你身后那鬼东西是什么？'

"我又让我这位诚实的同伴感受到那武器正贴着他的脑门；他大模大样地答道——

"'我身后是什么？哼，一袋血淋淋的死肉罢了，你非要问的话——可我们闲话太多啦——等我打发掉这玩意儿，再到老贝波那儿找你们。'

"'那么，祝你好运，最神圣的掘墓人，'那骑手答道，'至于你那件货嘛，*requiescat in pace*——但愿他安息——阿门。'

"'两个骑手说罢便策马而去，我们也以同样疾速的步子继续赶路，直到晨光开始染红东方。

"趁着我们飞速冲下一处陡坡之时，我瞅准时机，使劲给了我的同伴一推，把他整个儿从马头上掀了出去；还没等他滚停当，我已把他甩在四百码开外了。我客客气气地与他道了别，策马前行，再无别的惊险，便抵达了那座辉煌的罗马城——在那里，种种怪事降临到我头上，我自会一一讲给您听。不过先给我一杯酒再说。"

### The Village Bully / 村庄恶霸

===Original===
About thirty years ago there lived in the town of Chapelizod an ill-conditioned fellow of herculean strength, well known throughout the neighbourhood by the title of Bully Larkin. In addition to his remarkable physical superiority, this fellow had acquired a degree of skill as a pugilist which alone would have made him formidable. As it was, he was the autocrat of the village, and carried not the sceptre in vain. Conscious of his superiority, and perfectly secure of impunity, he lorded it over his fellows in a spirit of cowardly and brutal insolence, which made him hated even more profoundly than he was feared.

Upon more than one occasion he had deliberately forced quarrels upon men whom he had singled out for the exhibition of his savage prowess; and in every encounter his over-matched antagonist had received an amount of "punishment" which edified and appalled the spectators, and in some instances left ineffaceable scars and lasting injuries after it.

Bully Larkin's pluck had never been fairly tried. For, owing to his prodigious superiority in weight, strength, and skill, his victories had always been certain and easy; and in proportion to the facility with which he uniformly smashed an antagonist, his pugnacity and insolence were inflamed. He thus became an odious nuisance in the neighbourhood, and the terror of every mother who had a son, and of every wife who had a husband who possessed a spirit to resent insult, or the smallest confidence in his own pugilistic capabilities.

===Chinese===
约莫三十年前，查佩利佐德（Chapelizod）镇上住着一个性情恶劣的汉子，力大如天神，四乡八里的人都唤他"恶霸拉金"（Bully Larkin）。此人力气惊人自不待言，还练得一手好拳脚，光是这一身武艺，便足以令人畏惧。于是他便成了这村子里的独裁者，手中的权杖可不是虚摆设。他自知技压群雄，又料定没人奈何得了他，便以一种怯懦而暴戾的蛮横气焰凌驾于众人之上一一这副做派，叫人恨他之深，更甚于怕他之甚。

他不止一次存心寻衅，专挑那些人作对手，好在他们身上显摆自己那野蛮的本事；每一回交锋，力量悬殊的对手所挨的那顿"痛惩"，既叫围观者大开眼界，又叫他们胆战心惊；有几次，那一架下来，竟给对方留下了一辈子也消不掉的疤痕和终生难愈的残损。

恶霸拉金的胆气，从来不曾真正受过考验。因为他凭着自己那惊人的体重、力气和拳技，每一场胜利都来得笃定而轻松；而越是轻而易举地碾碎对手，他那好斗与蛮横便越发膨胀。他于是成了四邻之间一个可憎的祸害，成了每一个有儿子的母亲、每一个丈夫身上尚有一点血性、或对自己拳脚稍有自信的妻子的心腹之患。

===Original===
Now it happened that there was a young fellow named Ned Moran—better known by the sobriquet of "Long Ned," from his slender, lathy proportions—at that time living in the town. He was, in truth, a mere lad, nineteen years of age, and fully twelve years younger than the stalwart bully. This, however, as the reader will see, secured for him no exemption from the dastardly provocations of the ill-conditioned pugilist. Long Ned, in an evil hour, had thrown eyes of affection upon a certain buxom damsel, who, notwithstanding Bully Larkin's amorous rivalry, inclined to reciprocate them.

I need not say how easily the spark of jealousy, once kindled, is blown into a flame, and how naturally, in a coarse and ungoverned nature, it explodes in acts of violence and outrage.

"The bully" watched his opportunity, and contrived to provoke Ned Moran, while drinking in a public-house with a party of friends, into an altercation, in the course of which he failed not to put such insults upon his rival as manhood could not tolerate. Long Ned, though a simple, good-natured sort of fellow, was by no means deficient in spirit, and retorted in a tone of defiance which edified the more timid, and gave his opponent the opportunity he secretly coveted.

===Chinese===
恰巧那时镇上住着一个青年，名唤内德·莫兰（Ned Moran），因其身形瘦长如竹竿，更以"高个子内德"（Long Ned）这一诨名见知于人。他其实不过是个孩子，年方十九，比那壮硕的恶霸足足小了十二岁。然而，正如读者将见，这并未能使他幸免于这个劣性拳棍的卑劣挑衅。高个子内德在一桩晦气的时辰里，对一位体态丰腴的姑娘动了情；那姑娘呢，尽管恶霸拉金也对她百般觊觎争夺，心中却颇有意于回报他的情意。

妒忌的火星一旦点着，何其轻易便被吹成烈焰；而在一个粗鄙无节制的心性之中，它又何其自然地化作暴行与欺凌而爆发出来——此中道理，无须我在此赘述。

"那恶霸"窥准了时机，趁内德·莫兰正与一伙朋友在酒馆里喝酒，设法激他口角起来；口角之间，他自是不会放过把那些男子汉所不能忍受的羞辱，一一加到对手头上。高个子内德虽是个心地质朴、脾气随和的小伙子，骨气却半点不缺，便以一股不屈服的腔口回敬了几句——这话叫那些胆小怕事的人听着大为提气，也正给了对手一个他暗暗求之不得的把柄。

===Original===
Bully Larkin challenged the heroic youth, whose pretty face he had privately consigned to the mangling and bloody discipline he was himself so capable of administering. The quarrel, which he had himself contrived to get up, to a certain degree covered the ill blood and malignant premeditation which inspired his proceedings, and Long Ned, being full of generous ire and whiskey punch, accepted the gage of battle on the instant. The whole party, accompanied by a mob of idle men and boys, and in short by all who could snatch a moment from the calls of business, proceeded in slow procession through the old gate into the Phoenix Park, and mounting the hill overlooking the town, selected near its summit a level spot on which to decide the quarrel.

The combatants stripped, and a child might have seen in the contrast presented by the slight, lank form and limbs of the lad, and the muscular and massive build of his veteran antagonist, how desperate was the chance of poor Ned Moran.

"Seconds" and "bottle-holders"—selected of course for their love of the game—were appointed, and "the fight" commenced.

===Chinese===
恶霸拉金向这位血气方刚的青年下了战书——那张俊秀的脸，他私底下早已预定要施以自己最擅长的那番血肉模糊的整治。这场他一手挑起的口角，在某种程度上替他掩饰了那驱使他行事的恶毒用心与蓄谋，而高个子内德呢，一腔热血上涌，又灌下了几杯威士忌潘趣酒，当场便接下了战书。一行人浩浩荡荡，后面还跟着一大群无所事事的闲汉与孩童，总之凡是能从营生里抽出片刻工夫的人，皆都随行；众人缓缓穿过老城门，进了凤凰公园（Phoenix Park），登上俯瞰小镇的山丘，在山顶附近寻了一块平地，便要在那里一决此番恩怨。

双方脱去了上衣，连小孩子也能一眼看出：那少年瘦削羸弱的身形与四肢，与对手那老江湖的壮硕筋肉一比，可怜的内德·莫兰胜算何其渺茫。

"副手"与"持瓶人"一一当然是出于对这门营生的热爱而挑选出来的——都安排停当，"这一战"便开了场。

===Original===
I will not shock my readers with a description of the cool-blooded butchery that followed. The result of the combat was what anybody might have predicted. At the eleventh round, poor Ned refused to "give in"; the brawny pugilist, unhurt, in good wind, and pale with concentrated and as yet unslaked revenge, had the gratification of seeing his opponent seated upon his second's knee, unable to hold up his head, his left arm disabled; his face a bloody, swollen, and shapeless mass; his breast scarred and bloody, and his whole body panting and quivering with rage and exhaustion.

"Give in, Ned, my boy," cried more than one of the bystanders.

"Never, never," shrieked he, with a voice hoarse and choking.

===Chinese===
此后那一场冷血的屠戮，我且不细加描摹，以免惊扰了诸位看官。这场恶战的结局，原是人人都猜得到的。到了第十一回合，可怜的内德仍不肯"认输"；那壮硕的拳手毫发无损、气息悠长，因那蓄积已久、尚未餍足的复仇之心而面色发白，他心满意足地看着对手瘫坐在副手膝上，再也抬不起头来——左臂已然废了，那张脸肿成了一团血肉模糊、辨不出人形的烂泥，胸口伤痕累累、血迹斑斑，整个身躯上气不接下气地喘息着，因愤怒与虚脱而不住颤抖。

"认输吧，内德，我的孩子。"旁观的人里不止一个这样喊道。

"绝不，绝不。"他嗓音嘶哑哽咽地尖叫道。

===Original===
Time being "up," his second placed him on his feet again. Blinded with his own blood, panting and staggering, he presented but a helpless mark for the blows of his stalwart opponent. It was plain that a touch would have been sufficient to throw him to the earth. But Larkin had no notion of letting him off so easily. He closed with him without striking a blow (the effect of which, prematurely dealt, would have been to bring him at once to the ground, and so put an end to the combat), and getting his battered and almost senseless head under his arm, fast in that peculiar "fix" known to the fancy pleasantly by the name of "chancery," he held him firmly, while with monotonous and brutal strokes he beat his fist, as it seemed, almost into his face. A cry of "shame" broke from the crowd, for it was plain that the beaten man was now insensible, and supported only by the herculean arm of the bully. The round and the fight ended by his hurling him upon the ground, falling upon him at the same time with his knee upon his chest.

The bully rose, wiping the perspiration from his white face with his bloodstained hands, but Ned lay stretched and motionless upon the grass. It was impossible to get him upon his legs for another round. So he was carried down, just as he was, to the pond which then lay close to the old Park gate, and his head and body were washed beside it. Contrary to the belief of all he was not dead. He was carried home, and after some months to a certain extent recovered. But he never held up his head again, and before the year was over he had died of consumption. Nobody could doubt how the disease had been induced, but there was no actual proof to connect the cause and effect, and the ruffian Larkin escaped the vengeance of the law. A strange retribution, however, awaited him.

===Chinese===
时限已"到"，副手又把他扶着站了起来。他被自己的鲜血糊住了眼，气喘吁吁，踉踉跄跄，在那壮硕对手的拳头之下，不过是一个毫无还手之力的活靶子。明眼人一看便知，只需轻轻一推，便足以叫他扑倒在地。可拉金哪肯这么轻易放过他。他并不出拳一击——那样一拳若贸然打下去，势必叫对方登时倒地，这场架也就此收场了——他一把将这被打得血肉模糊、神志已近昏沉的人揪住，把他的头按在自己腋下，死死扣住；行家中间把这一手"妙招"笑称为"大法官席"（chancery）。他便这般将对方牢牢钳制着，以单调而凶残的节奏，一拳一拳地把拳头——瞧那情形——直直捶进对方脸上。人群里爆出一阵"可耻"的叫喊，因为谁都看得出来，那挨打的人早已不省人事，全靠恶霸那双天神般的大力臂膀撑着，才不曾瘫倒在地。这一回合、这一场架的结局，是他把对手狠狠掼倒在地，自己同时一头压上去，一膝盖顶在对方胸口上。

恶霸爬起来，用那双血迹斑斑的手抹去惨白脸上的汗珠；内德却直挺挺地躺在草地上，纹丝不动。再没法把他架起来打下一回合了。于是众人便把他原模原样地抬下了山，抬到那时还紧挨着公园老门口的那方池塘边，在塘畔为他洗抹头脸身躯。出乎众人所料，他并未断气。他被抬回家去，过了几个月，伤势总算好了几分。然而他自此再没能抬起头来，未及一年，便死于痨病。这病根从何而起，无人不晓；可要把前因后果钉成实据，却又拿不出半点真凭实据，那恶棍拉金便这样逃过了法律的惩处。然而，一桩奇异的报应，正等着他呢。

===Original===
After the death of Long Ned, he became less quarrelsome than before, but more sullen and reserved. Some said "he took it to heart," and others, that his conscience was not at ease about it. Be this as it may, however, his health did not suffer by reason of his presumed agitations, nor was his worldly prosperity marred by the blasting curses with which poor Moran's enraged mother pursued him; on the contrary he had rather risen in the world, and obtained regular and well-remunerated employment from the Chief Secretary's gardener, at the other side of the Park. He still lived in Chapelizod, whither, on the close of his day's work, he used to return across the Fifteen Acres.

It was about three years after the catastrophe we have mentioned, and late in the autumn, when, one night, contrary to his habit, he did not appear at the house where he lodged, neither had he been seen anywhere, during the evening, in the village. His hours of return had been so very regular, that his absence excited considerable surprise, though, of course, no actual alarm; and, at the usual hour, the house was closed for the night, and the absent lodger consigned to the mercy of the elements, and the care of his presiding star. Early in the morning, however, he was found lying in a state of utter helplessness upon the slope immediately overlooking the Chapelizod gate. He had been smitten with a paralytic stroke: his right side was dead; and it was many weeks before he had recovered his speech sufficiently to make himself at all understood.

===Chinese===
高个子内德死后，他反倒比从前少了些寻衅的兴致，却愈发阴沉孤僻了。有人说他"心里过意不去"，也有人说他良心上不得安宁。但无论如何，这些据说搅扰着他的心事，并未损及他的身子；可怜的莫兰那位悲愤欲绝的母亲，以种种毒咒苦苦追讨，也未能折损他世俗的兴旺——情形恰恰相反，他在这世上反倒越发得意了，竟在公园那头谋得了首席秘书官家花园里的差事，差使稳定，工钱丰厚。他仍住在查佩利佐德，每日收了工，便穿过"十五英亩地"（Fifteen Acres）回到镇上。

约莫就在我们所言那场惨剧之后三年，深秋时节，某夜，他竟一反常态，没有在他寄宿的屋子里露面；那一晚，村中也不曾有人在哪里见过他。他归家的时辰向来极有定准，他这一缺席，颇叫人诧异了一阵——当然，倒也还说不上真正的惊慌。到了惯常的时刻，屋子便照旧关门闭户，安置过夜；那位未归的房客，便被交给了风雨寒暑去发落，由他的本命星去照看。然而第二天清早，有人发现他瘫倒在紧挨查佩利佐德城门的那面斜坡上，浑身动弹不得。他已中了一记中风之症：右半边身子全无知觉；过了好几个礼拜，他才勉强恢复了一些说话的能力，能叫人稍稍听懂他的意思。

===Original===
He then made the following relation:—He had been detained, it appeared, later than usual, and darkness had closed before he commenced his homeward walk across the Park. It was a moonlit night, but masses of ragged clouds were slowly drifting across the heavens. He had not encountered a human figure, and no sounds but the softened rush of the wind sweeping through bushes and hollows met his ear. These wild and monotonous sounds, and the utter solitude which surrounded him, did not, however, excite any of those uneasy sensations which are ascribed to superstition, although he said he did feel depressed, or, in his own phraseology, "lonesome." Just as he crossed the brow of the hill which shelters the town of Chapelizod, the moon shone out for some moments with unclouded lustre, and his eye, which happened to wander by the shadowy enclosures which lay at the foot of the slope, was arrested by the sight of a human figure climbing, with all the haste of one pursued, over the churchyard wall, and running up the steep ascent directly towards him. Stories of "resurrectionists" crossed his recollection, as he observed this suspicious-looking figure. But he began, momentarily, to be aware with a sort of fearful instinct which he could not explain, that the running figure was directing his steps, with a sinister purpose, towards himself.

The form was that of a man with a loose coat about him, which, as he ran, he disengaged, and as well as Larkin could see, for the moon was again wading in clouds, threw from him. The figure thus advanced until within some two score yards of him, it arrested its speed, and approached with a loose, swaggering gait. The moon again shone out bright and clear, and, gracious God! what was the spectacle before him? He saw as distinctly as if he had been presented there in the flesh, Ned Moran, himself, stripped naked from the waist upward, as if for pugilistic combat, and drawing towards him in silence. Larkin would have shouted, prayed, cursed, fled across the Park, but he was absolutely powerless; the apparition stopped within a few steps, and leered on him with a ghastly mimicry of the defiant stare with which pugilists strive to cow one another before combat. For a time, which he could not so much as conjecture, he was held in the fascination of that unearthly gaze, and at last the thing, whatever it was, on a sudden swaggered close up to him with extended palms. With an impulse of horror, Larkin put out his hand to keep the figure off, and their palms touched—at least, so he believed—for a thrill of unspeakable agony, running through his arm, pervaded his entire frame, and he fell senseless to the earth.

===Chinese===
于是他作了下面这番陈述：——那天他似乎被耽搁到了比平日更晚，天色已黑透了，他才动身穿过公园往家走。那夜有月，但天上有一团团破碎的云，正缓缓地在苍穹里漂移。他一路未遇一个人影，耳畔所闻，唯有风穿过灌木丛与低洼处时那阵低柔的呼啸。这荒凉单调的声响、以及那彻头彻尾的孤寂，原是迷信之人最爱疑神疑鬼的境况，却并未在他心里搅起半点惴惴不安——虽说他也承认自己心情沉重，用他自己的话讲，"怪冷清的"。正当他翻过那座为查佩利佐德小镇挡风的小山山脊时，月亮一时清辉毕露，亮了几分；他的目光恰在那山脚下一片阴影沉沉的围地之间游移，忽被一幕景象攫住了：一个人影，带着那股子被人追捕时才有的拼命劲儿，翻过教堂墓地的围墙，正沿着陡坡直直地朝他奔上来。他瞧着这形迹可疑的人影，脑海里掠过种种"盗尸人"（resurrectionists）的传闻。可他渐渐生出一种自己也说不清道不明的恐惧直觉：那奔来的人影，竟怀着一种不祥的用意，径直朝他这边逼来。

那人影是一个男人的身形，身上披着一件宽松的外衣；他一边跑，一边把那外衣扯开——拉金只见，月亮又已钻进了云堆里——一甩手把它扔了出去。那人影便这般推进到离他约莫四十码开外，忽然收住了奔势，换上一副松松垮垮、大摇大摆的步子逼了过来。月亮又从云缝里清清亮亮地探出头来——老天爷啊！他眼前是怎样一幅景象？只见内德·莫兰其人，赤裸着上身，一如上场打拳时的装束，正一声不响地朝他逼近；看得之真切，仿佛那血肉之躯便活生生立在眼前。拉金想要呼喊，想要祷告，想要咒骂，想要穿过公园逃命，可他浑身使不出半点力气；那鬼影在距他不过几步之处停了下来，斜睨着他，那副神情，酷肖拳师们临阵之前彼此恫吓时那挑衅的目光——只不过，那是一种阴森可怖的模仿。他不知自己被那不属于人世间的目光摄住了多久——连多久都猜不出来——末了，那东西，无论它究竟是什么，忽然大摇大摆地贴近身来，伸出了两掌。拉金怀着一种惊悚的冲动，伸手要去挡开那身影，两人的手掌撞在了一处——至少，他自己是这般以为的——只觉一道难以言喻的剧痛窜过他的手臂，刹那间漫遍全身，他便人事不知地栽倒在地。

===Original===
Though Larkin lived for many years after, his punishment was terrible. He was incurably maimed; and being unable to work, he was forced, for existence, to beg alms of those who had once feared and flattered him. He suffered, too, increasingly, under his own horrible interpretation of the preternatural encounter which was the beginning of all his miseries. It was vain to endeavour to shake his faith in the reality of the apparition, and equally vain, as some compassionately did, to try to persuade him that the greeting with which his vision closed was intended, while inflicting a temporary trial, to signify a compensating reconciliation.

"No, no," he used to say, "all won't do. I know the meaning of it well enough; it is a challenge to meet him in the other world—in Hell, where I am going—that's what it means, and nothing else."

And so, miserable and refusing comfort, he lived on for some years, and then died, and was buried in the same narrow churchyard which contains the remains of his victim.

===Chinese===
拉金此后虽又活了许多年，他所受的惩处却惨烈无比。他落下了不治之残废；既已无力做工，便为糊口计，只得向那些从前怕他、奉承他的人乞求施舍。而那场超自然的奇遇，乃是他一切苦难的开端，他对这一场遭遇所作的那套骇人自解，更使他越陷越深、日甚一日。要动摇他对那鬼影确有其事的深信不疑，自是徒劳；正如有些人发了善心，劝他说：那幻象临了所给的"礼遇"，纵是暂且叫他受了番试炼，其本意或许正是预示一场将来补偿性的和解——这套话，同样也是白说。

"不，不，"他常说，"说什么都没用。那意思我再清楚不过了；那是要约我到另一个世界去——到地狱里去，我就要往那儿去了——就是这个意思，再没别的了。"

他便是这般，凄凄惨惨，拒人慰藉于千里之外，又苟活了几年，这才死去，葬在了同一片逼仄的教堂墓地里，与他的受害人共眠一处。

===Original===
I need hardly say, how absolute was the faith of the honest inhabitants, at the time when I heard the story, in the reality of the preternatural summons which, through the portals of terror, sickness, and misery, had summoned Bully Larkin to his long, last home, and that, too, upon the very ground on which he had signalised the guiltiest triumph of his violent and vindictive career.

I recollect another story of the preternatural sort, which made no small sensation, some five-and-thirty years ago, among the good gossips of the town; and, with your leave, courteous reader, I shall relate it.

===Chinese===
当我听到这个故事之时，那班诚实的镇民，对这桩超自然召唤的真确性，信得何其坚定不移——毋庸我再赘述。他们说，正是这一道召唤，经由恐惧、疾病与苦难三重门户，将恶霸拉金押到了他那漫长的、最后的归宿；而且，押他的那片地，恰恰就是他当年以暴力与报复为业的一生中，最最罪孽深深的那场"凯旋"所得以成就之处。

我还记得另一桩超自然的故事，约莫三十五年前，曾在镇上那班爱嚼舌根的好好先生中间，引起了不小的轰动；若蒙看官允可，我便也讲来一听。

## Prologue Martin Hesselius, the German Physician / 序言：马丁·赫塞利乌斯，德国医生

===Original===
Though carefully educated in medicine and surgery, I have never practised either. The study of each continues, nevertheless, to interest me profoundly. Neither idleness nor caprice caused my secession from the honourable calling which I had just entered. The cause was a very trifling scratch inflicted by a dissecting knife. This trifle cost me the loss of two fingers, amputated promptly, and the more painful loss of my health, for I have never been quite well since, and have seldom been twelve months together in the same place.

In my wanderings I became acquainted with Dr. Martin Hesselius, a wanderer like myself, like me a physician, and like me an enthusiast in his profession. Unlike me in this, that his wanderings were voluntary, and he a man, if not of fortune, as we estimate fortune in England, at least in what our forefathers used to term "easy circumstances." He was an old man when I first saw him; nearly five-and-thirty years my senior.

===Chinese===
我在内科与外科两方面虽皆受过严格的训练，却从未真正行过医。然而这两门学问的研究，至今仍令我深为着迷。我之退出初涉的这一体面行当，既非出于怠惰，亦非出于任性。其缘由，不过是解剖刀所造成的一道极轻的划伤。这桩微末之事，令我付出了一只手上两根手指的代价——旋即截去；更叫我痛苦的是，从此失去了健康。自那以后，我身子便不曾大好过，也难得在同一处地方连续住满十二个月。

在漂泊之中，我结识了马丁·赫塞利乌斯医生（Dr. Martin Hesselius）——他亦如我一般是个漂泊者，如我一般是个医者，又如我一般对这一行当满怀热忱。所不同者，他的漂泊乃出于自愿；论及身家，纵算不上英国人所谓的富豪，至少也如我们先辈所言，处于"宽裕之境"。我初见他时，他已是个老人；年长我近三十五岁。

===Original===
In Dr. Martin Hesselius, I found my master. His knowledge was immense, his grasp of a case was an intuition. He was the very man to inspire a young enthusiast, like me, with awe and delight. My admiration has stood the test of time and survived the separation of death. I am sure it was well-founded.

For nearly twenty years I acted as his medical secretary. His immense collection of papers he has left in my care, to be arranged, indexed and bound. His treatment of some of these cases is curious. He writes in two distinct characters. He describes what he saw and heard as an intelligent layman might, and when in this style of narrative he had seen the patient either through his own hall-door, to the light of day, or through the gates of darkness to the caverns of the dead, he returns upon the narrative, and in the terms of his art, and with all the force and originality of genius, proceeds to the work of analysis, diagnosis and illustration.

Here and there a case strikes me as of a kind to amuse or horrify a lay reader with an interest quite different from the peculiar one which it may possess for an expert. With slight modifications, chiefly of language, and of course a change of names, I copy the following. The narrator is Dr. Martin Hesselius. I find it among the voluminous notes of cases which he made during a tour in England about sixty-four years ago.

===Chinese===
在马丁·赫塞利乌斯医生身上，我寻见了我之师。其学识之渊博，可谓浩瀚无涯；其把握一桩病案，则近乎一种直觉。他正是那样一个人——足以唤起如我这般年轻热忱者心中的敬畏与欣喜。我的这份仰慕，经得起岁月的考验，也熬得过死别的阻隔。我深信它是有坚实根基的。

近二十年间，我充任他的医学秘书。他所积攒的浩繁文稿，悉数托付于我，由我整理、编目、装订成帙。他对其中若干病案的处理，甚为独特。他以两种截然不同的笔法写作：先以一种通晓事理的门外汉口吻，平实地记述其亲眼所见、亲耳所闻；待这一路叙事写至病人或是被他送出自家厅门、重见天日，或是穿过黑暗之门、长眠于亡者之穴——他便回转笔锋，重以本行的术语、凭其天分的全部气魄与独创，进而着手分析、诊断与阐发。

这些病例之中，偶有一桩令我觉着：它对一般读者所能引起的兴趣——或以为趣、或以为悚然——与其在专家眼中那种特有的兴味，截然不同。我兹将下文迻录于此，仅在文字上略作增删，并依例改换姓名。讲述者是马丁·赫塞利乌斯医生。此篇乃我在他那卷帙浩繁的病案札记中检得，为他约六十四年前游历英格兰时所手录。

===Original===
It is related in a series of letters to his friend Professor Van Loo of Leyden. The professor was not a physician, but a chemist, and a man who read history and metaphysics and medicine, and had, in his day, written a play.

The narrative is therefore, if somewhat less valuable as a medical record, necessarily written in a manner more likely to interest an unlearned reader.

These letters, from a memorandum attached, appear to have been returned on the death of the professor, in 1819, to Dr. Hesselius. They are written, some in English, some in French, but the greater part in German. I am a faithful, though I am conscious, by no means a graceful translator, and although here and there I omit some passages, and shorten others and disguise names, I have interpolated nothing.

===Chinese===
此案以一束书信的形式记述，收信者是他的友人——莱顿（Leyden）的范卢教授（Professor Van Loo）。这位教授并非医者，而是一位化学家；他博览史学、形而上学与医学，早年还曾写过一出剧本。

故此，这篇记述纵使作为医学文献稍减其价，却必然以更为浅近的笔法写就，更易唤起一位未谙此道的读者的兴味。

据附于卷末的一则备忘所记，这些书信于 1819 年教授辞世之后，已归还赫塞利乌斯医生。诸信有用英文写的，有用法文写的，但大半以德文写就。我是个忠实的——虽则自知绝非优美的——译者；其间虽偶有删节，若干处予以压缩，姓名亦加掩饰，但我绝不曾添入一文一字。

## Hyacinth O'Toole / 海厄辛斯·奥图尔

===Original===
In the course of my life I have met with more accidents and assaults than twenty other men, and they never cost me any trouble to speak of—cuts, prods, and gunshot, all came quite natural, and healed like enchantment. It was a murdering pity I was not a general. I could have stood any amount of hacking, and slashing, and riddling, and been never the worse man, nor a week on the sick-list. A shoemaker mistook me one day for a county Cork man that was paying attentions to his wife, and gave me a slice with his half-moon knife—bad luck to that ugly instrument—as I was walking down Petticoat Lane, no more thinking of his wife, I give you my solemn honour, than Saint Joseph of Arimathea was of Potiphar's. The next thing was, Baron Dromdouski—a Polish refugee of distinction, and a perfect gentleman, I will say, and played the guitar like an angel, though liable occasionally to be carried away by his feelings—stuck me with an oyster-knife, while we were differing on politics, in the "Good Samaritan" in Exchange Street. I could count up fifty such unlucky catastrophes; but I think the worst was, what happened to me as I was whistling in the hall of my lodgings, where I was waiting to take Miss Doolan out for a walk.

===Chinese===
我这辈子遭的意外、挨的殴伤，比二十个旁人加起来还多，可它们从来没给我添过什么值得一提的麻烦——刀伤、刺伤、枪伤，于我都稀松平常，好得也快，简直像中了魔法。我不曾当上一位将军，真是暴殄天物。任凭怎样的砍、剁、凿，我都挺得住，人也丝毫不减精神，病假清单上从不会超过一个礼拜。一日，我沿着衬裙巷（Petticoat Lane）走着，一位鞋匠把我错认作了科克郡（county Cork）某个对他太太献殷勤的家伙，顺手用他那把半月刀给了我一下——这把丑家伙真是见鬼去吧——我敢以名誉起誓，我当时脑子里对他的太太，绝不比亚利马太的约瑟（Saint Joseph of Arimathea）对波提乏（Potiphar）的太太想得更多。下一桩，则是德罗姆多夫斯基男爵（Baron Dromdouski）——一位有头有脸的波兰流亡客，我得说句公道话，是个地道的君子，吉他弹得天使一般，只是偶尔容易感情用事——在交易所街（Exchange Street）的"好撒玛利亚人"酒馆里，因政见相左，用一把开蚝刀捅了我一下。这类倒霉的大祸，我能一口气数上五十桩；不过最糟的，我想还得数那一回——当时我正站在寓所的门厅里吹着口哨，等着陪杜兰小姐（Miss Doolan）出去散步。

===Original===
I must tell you there's nothing on earth I hate equal to a cat, and it is the only thing that walks on feet I was ever thoroughly affeard to look in the face. It's a dread that was born with me, and it will never leave me; and I'd run into Nebuchadnezzar's fiery furnace away from one, and I think I'd have jumped after Quintus Curtius into the bottomless abyss if there was a cat behind me.

===Chinese===
我得告诉您，这世上我痛恨之物，再没有能和猫相提并论的；凡是用脚走路的东西，唯有这一样，我是不敢正眼去看它的脸的。这份惧怕是与生俱来的，至死也甩不脱；为了躲它，我情愿一头钻进尼布甲尼撒（Nebuchadnezzar）那座烈火的窑；我想，要是有一只猫追在我屁股后面，便是昆图斯·库尔提乌斯（Quintus Curtius）跳过的那种无底深渊，我也敢跟着一头栽下去。

===Original===
Well the cause of this accident I'm going to mention, was our cook, poor thing, that was flighty and out of her mind for love of a private grenadier in the Buffs, and she drove a three-pronged iron toasting-fork, between the kitchen banisters, up to the hilt in the calf of my leg. I thought it was the cat that I saw there, looking like mischief, only a minute before, and I gave a screech and a jump, and I went flying into the hall with the toasting-fork stuck in my leg. "La! Mr. Toole, what's that stuck in your leg?" cries Miss Doolan, who was that minute coming down the stairs.

===Chinese===
哎，我接下来要讲的这场祸事的起因，是我们家的厨娘——可怜的人儿——她为了巴夫斯团（the Buffs）里一个二等兵掷弹兵，神魂颠倒、闹得有些疯癫，竟隔着厨房的栏杆，把一把三齿铁烤叉，齐柄戳进了我小腿肚里。我只当那是方才瞥见的猫——一脸不怀好气的模样——便一声惨叫、纵身一跳，带着插在腿上的烤叉冲进了门厅。"哎呀！奥图尔先生（Mr. Toole），您腿上插的是什么呀？"杜兰小姐恰在这当口从楼梯上下来，惊呼道。

===Original===
"It's the cat," I roared, almost out of my senses, and away with me out of the hall-door, that chanced to be open, and down the street I pegged like a madman, knocking my hat off on an old gentleman's face, that was looking out of his study-window, and never waiting to pick it up. I thought the beast would never let go, and my hair was standing up on my head, and I wish you saw the capers I cut, trying to shake it off.

"For the Lord's sake," I implored, dancing mad in the middle of the street, "will some of you pull it off my leg? I'll give you a shilling, whoever does."

===Chinese===
"是猫！"我吼道，几乎失了心智，夺路冲出正巧敞着的门厅大门，沿着街疯也似的飞奔，一头把帽子撞落在一位正从书房窗户探头张望的老绅士脸上，也顾不得停下捡。我以为那畜生一辈子也不会松口了，头发根根倒竖，那一路我手舞足蹈作的怪相，真盼您能瞧见。

"看在上帝的份上，"我在街心疯跳着哀求，"你们哪位行行好，把它从我腿上拽下来吧？谁拽下来，我给他一先令（shilling）。"

===Original===
"I'll take it off," says a good-natured scavenger, that thought I was mad—and bedad I wasn't far from it—and he strove to catch hold of the handle of the fork; and I was so wild with fright I made a cut at the animal with my stick behind, and struck the scavenger right across the knuckles, and on I ran feeling the cat's teeth and claws, as I thought, fast in me still.

"Bad luck to you, ye Turk!" says the scavenger, shying a stone at me, as big as a lemon, and knocking a carman out of his dicky with it, pipe, whip, caubeen, and all.

"Look what's stuck in his leg, boys!" called out the blackguard little children, running after me. "See there, look, look, look what's stuck in his leg!"

===Chinese===
"我来替您弄掉，"一位好心的清道夫说——他还当我发了疯，说真的，离疯也确是不远——便伸手去抓那叉柄；我吓昏了头，回身用手杖朝那"畜生"一棍劈下，正劈在清道夫的指节上，我继续狂奔，只觉那猫的牙和爪，仍如我所想，紧紧钉在我身上。

"该死的，你这土耳其佬！"清道夫骂道，朝我扔来一块柠檬大的石头，倒把一个赶大车的车夫从车夫座上砸了下来——烟斗、马鞭、破帽子，一股脑儿全飞了。

"快看他腿上插的什么呀，伙伴们！"那群无赖小鬼追在我后头叫嚷，"瞧那儿，看哪，看哪，看哪他腿上插的什么呀！"

===Original===
"Will some of you hit it, lick it, wallop it? It's *mad*!" I holloaed.

By this time I was running up Grafton Street, and everyone looking after me, some wondering, some laughing, and some frightened.

"It's fastened in my leg!" I roared. "Will none of you pull it off?"

"*I* will," says one.

"Shoot it," says I.

"*I* will," says another.

"It's *mad*," said I.

"Stop your capers, man, and *I'll* pull it out," says another.

"Give it a lick," said I, "break its back, stick a knife in it."

"Arra! Bother ye. How much ironmongery do you want?" says another. "Stop aisy, and I'll coax it out in a jiffy."

"Do," said I, "coax it; its name's Mufti."

It was a little thief that snatched it out at last, as it trailed along the ground, and a devil of a hard pluck it took, and ran away with it and pawned it for a penny.

===Chinese===
"你们哪位揍揍它、舔舔它、狠抽它一顿？它*发疯了*！"我高喊。

这时我已经沿着格拉夫顿街（Grafton Street）一路狂奔上去，人人都回头瞧我，有的诧异，有的笑，有的吓得不轻。

"它死死钉在我腿上啦！"我吼道，"你们就没一个肯替我拽下来？"

"我来，"一个说。

"开枪打死它，"我说。

"我来，"另一个说。

"它*疯了*，"我说。

"先生你别乱蹦了，*我*来替你拔，"又一个说。

"给它一棍，"我说，"打断它的脊梁，拿刀子捅了它。"

"哎哟！去你的吧。你这铁器还想要几件？"又一个说，"安安稳稳站着，我三两下就把它哄出来。"

"好，"我说，"就哄哄它吧；它的名字叫'穆夫提'（Mufti）。"

末了是一个小贼，趁那叉子拖在地上，一把将它拔了去——拔得那叫一个狠——抱着它一溜烟跑了，当掉换了一便士。

===Original===
Well, I need go no further; I mentioned these, and might mention fifty other wounds, to show you that they were no trifles, and I can take my davy there was not one of the series that took a week to heal.

I'm happy to tell you that I was quite sufficiently well to avail myself of Mrs. Molloy's invitation to drink tea, go to the play, and return to supper with her agreeable party. I need not tell you that if I had had as many holes in my body as a colander, and was bleeding at every pore, I would have contrived, cost what it might, to drag myself to the side of the beautiful Theodora, although it was only to expire at her feet.

===Chinese===
好，我也不必再多绕舌了；我举出这几桩，原还可以再举五十桩别处的伤，只是要让您晓得，这些都绝非小事一桩，而且我可以发誓作保，这一长串伤里，没有一处耗过一个礼拜才愈合的。

我高兴地告诉您，我已痊愈到了相当程度，足可赴莫洛伊太太（Mrs. Molloy）之邀——去喝喝茶、看看戏，再回去同她那热闹的一伙人共进晚餐。我不说您也明白：便是我这副身板被戳得像只漏勺，浑身上下每个毛孔都淌着血，我也无论如何要拖着身子，爬到美丽的西奥多拉（Theodora）身边去——哪怕只是死在她脚边，也心甘情愿。

===Original===
The hour named for assembling at the hospitable lodgings of the Molloys was half-past five. I dressed myself with uncommon care. We sported wonderful high and voluminous white cravats in those days, which had a good deal the effect of modern poultices. We wore besides under-waistcoats of coloured satin, pantaloons and pumps, and blue coats with brass buttons gilt.

I was glad as I looked at myself in the glass, and brushed up my hair above my forehead into a "topping," as Mr. Bassegio called that conical triumph of the decorative art, to think that I looked a little pale.

===Chinese===
莫洛伊一家那殷勤的寓所里，约定聚齐的时辰是五点半。我穿衣打扮得格外用心。那年代我们时兴极高极蓬的白色领巾，缠在脖子上颇有几分今日膏药的风采。除此之外，还内穿彩缎马甲，脚蹬长裤与浅口舞鞋，外面罩一件饰着鎏金铜扣的蓝色礼服。

我对镜自照，把前额上方的头发拢起来，拢成一记"高耸发髻"——巴塞吉奥先生（Mr. Bassegio）把那锥形的装饰艺术杰作如此称呼——见自己面色略带几分苍白，心中倒颇为得意。

===Original===
Mundy had called on me the day after this extraction, not knowing a word of the matter, and wondering why I did not look in at the billiard-rooms. I made a rather painful effort, for I was lying on my face, to get into a more natural position, which I did with a slight groan.

"Wounded!" says he.

"Slightly," said I, "that is, they say it won't be dangerous."

"Oh! oh!" says he, smiling faintly down at me as I lay on my bed, with a look at once stern and knowing. "Gunshot, eh?"

===Chinese===
这叉子拔掉的次日，蒙迪（Mundy）来拜访我，他对这事一无所知，只纳闷我怎不去台球房露面。我原是伏身躺着的，颇费了点劲——还伴着一声轻哼——才换回一个稍微自然些的姿势。

"挂彩啦！"他说。

"轻伤，"我说，"也就是说，他们说没有性命之忧。"

"哦！哦！"他说，俯视着躺在床上的我，淡淡一笑，神色既严峻又了然，"枪伤，嗯？"

===Original===
I had told him on purpose, for I knew that he was intimately acquainted with the Molloys, and I wished Theodora to hear that I was wounded; for a man hurt in an affair of honour (and what but that could she suppose?) is the most interesting patient that can come under the steel of the faculty or the cognisance of the fair.

"Gunshot," I acquiesced; for a carbine's as good a "gun" as a pistol any day; and about the "shot," at any rate, there could be no mistake.

"Shivering an' a daisy, as you say?" he inquired. "Looking into a barrel? Ten paces, eh?"

"I'll not deny the distance was about that," said I. "We were both slightly wounded, and—that's all. I won't talk about it; we are under terms not to tell on one another; and ask me no questions and I'll tell you no lies. Are *you* asked to the Molloys' tea-party to go to the playhouse on ——— next, and back again to supper?

===Chinese===
我是有意告诉他的，因为我知道他与莫洛伊一家过从甚密，我巴望西奥多拉听见我负了伤；一个男人因荣誉之事（她能作何他想呢？）而受伤，落在外科大夫的刀下、入得小姐们的眼底，乃是最饶风致的病号。

"枪伤，"我附和道；卡宾枪无论如何也算得一把"枪"，跟手枪毫无二致；至于那"弹"字，更是断断不会弄错的。

"打得骨头都碎了，是这意思吧？"他追问，"对着枪管？十步开外，嗯？"

"距离确实差不多，我不否认，"我说。"双方都是轻伤，就——就是这样。我不想多谈；我们有约在先，不得互相告发；您也别问我，我也不对您撒谎。下回——日去莫洛伊家的茶会、再去看戏、回头吃夜宵，*您*也接到邀请了么？"

===Original===
"Yes," says Mundy, "and I mean to go; that's as fine a black-eyed, piquey-checked, bouncing grenadier of a—"

"*Stop!*" said I, making a bounce to sit up, for my blood was boiling; but I was not equal to that change of posture yet. "If you mean Miss Theodora Molloy—" I began.

"Oh! oh! So it is there the wind sits," says he, and he laughed, "I meant old Mother Molloy, of course; don't be uneasy, my dear fellow."

We parted, notwithstanding, very good friends, and I was glad to hear that he was just going to pay them a visit in their apartments on Ormond Quay, and I knew he could not keep my little secret long from that agreeable family.

===Chinese===
"是的，"蒙迪说，"我打算去；那可真是个标致极了、黑眼睛、尖下颏、活蹦乱跳的掷弹兵一般的——"

"*住嘴！*"我喝道，气得血都沸腾了，猛地要坐起来；可这姿势我还换不动。"你要是指的是西奥多拉·莫洛伊小姐——"我开口道。

"哦！哦！原来风是从那个方向吹来的，"他说罢便笑了，"我当然是指老莫洛伊太太啦；放心吧，老兄。"

尽管如此，我们分手时仍是极好的朋友；听他说正要去奥蒙德码头（Ormond Quay）他们的寓所登门拜访，我心中暗喜——这点小秘密，我知道他瞒不了那和气一家多久。

===Original===
The better part of the week had passed, as you are aware, since this visit of Mundy's, and I was now on the point of setting out to enjoy the delightful evening I had been dreaming of for so long.

When my toilet was completed, I practised sitting down and standing up, which I did, perhaps, a little stiffly; still the movement was quite feasible, and I trusted to the inspiration of Theodora's presence to make it graceful.

When all was ready I took my opera-hat and got into the hackney-coach, with a great coat-of-arms, as big as a signboard, emblazoned on each door. Some judge or Lord Mayor, or other magnifico, seemed to have owned every one of them, fifty years before, and turned them adrift to batter about the town ever since. I sat down alone in my glory. It was a roomy place. Three could easily sit at a side. I wish you felt the jolting, and bobbing, and bumping. I was in no condition to enjoy it just then, and on second thought, I readjusted my pose. I kneeled down; such, for sufficient reasons, was the attitude I preferred, with my elbows on the cushion. There was room enough for changes of the sort: it was as big as a pew, a very uneasy one, you may suppose: the noise of it was enough to deafen a cannoneer for an hour after. If all the old iron and broken glass in Dublin was being tossed by madmen in frying-pans like pancakes, it could not exceed the ring and clatter and batter of that musical enclosure. They were all alike; there was no use in fretting; I wanted to be at Ormond Quay to the minute, not to lose one moment of Theodora's company, possibly to arrive first of the lot and have her all to myself before anyone else should come in to bother us.

===Chinese===
您也晓得，自打蒙迪那次拜访之后，一个星期的大半已经过去了，我此刻正要动身出门，去享受我朝思暮想了许久的那令人销魂的夜晚。

梳妆既毕，我演习了一番坐下、起身的动作，做得或许略显僵硬；但到底做得来，我便把动作能否优雅，寄托在西奥多拉现身时给我的那份灵感上。

一切就绪，我戴上歌剧帽，钻进一辆雇佣马车——两扇车门上各绘着一块招牌般硕大的纹章。这种马车，每辆似乎都是五十年前某位法官、市长之类的达官贵人所有，此后便被弃之不顾，任它在城里一路咣当至今。我独自端坐于其间，八面威风。车内倒也宽敞。一边坐三个人也不费事。那一路的颠、簸、撞，真盼您也尝一尝。我那副身板当时可消受不起，转念一想，便重摆了个姿势：我跪了下来——理由充足得很——双肘撑在软垫上。这么换姿势地方是绰绰有余的：车厢大得像个教堂座席——您可想见，是极不舒服的那种；它的噪声足以叫一个炮兵一个小时之内听不见别的。都柏林全城所有的旧铁、碎玻璃，纵是叫疯子拿煎锅像摊煎饼似的颠来颠去，那叮当哐啷之声，也及不上这座"音乐厢"里头的喧腾。这种车全是一个模子；急也没用；我只想分秒不差地赶到奥蒙德码头，半刻也不愿错过与西奥多拉相伴的光景，说不定还能赶在众人之先到达，趁旁人还没来搅扰，把她独占片刻。

===Original===
Unfortunately, my coachman was something the worse for liquor, and delayed me considerably by tumbling out of the box, which he did three times: once on his back, once on his face, and last on his knees and elbows. He had to be helped up on to the box every time, and his hat, whip, and other appurtenances collected and restored by some charitable blackguards of his acquaintance, while I, compelled to change my attitude of devotion, was stamping in my pumps and silk stockings, in my roomy prison, and swearing till I almost burst my cravat, with my "topping," my expressive face, and my fist out of the window. At length, after many hair-breadth escapes and a long and heartrending oscillation between the house ten doors above and the house ten doors below, the particular door I wanted to stop at, I was actually liberated, and ascended the narrow stairs, preceded by the maid, with my heart thumping, I verily believe, audibly. I heard people talking, and the voice of Theodora quite distinguishable from the rest. The woman did not announce my name, and I soon discovered that she was not aware that I had followed her upstairs, for she said:

"There's a little hop-o'-my-thumb of a man in the hall, if ye plase, ma'am, that says you asked him to tay; but I think it's what he's a bit of a shop-boy that's come with a bill, and, if you like, I'll put him out by the lug."

===Chinese===
不幸的是，我的车夫喝得醉醺醺的，一连三回从御者座上栽下来，把我耽搁得不轻：一回仰面，一回俯面，最后一回是膝盖和胳膊肘齐上。每一回都得有人帮他把车夫座扶上去，他的帽子、马鞭及其他零碎，则由几个素识的、发善心的无赖替他一一捡起送回；而我呢，不得不从那种虔诚的姿势里改换出来，穿着浅口舞鞋和丝袜，在那宽敞的囚笼里直跺脚，跺得领巾几欲崩裂，探出窗外挥拳咒骂，头顶那记"高耸发髻"、那张表情丰富的脸，一齐跟着受罪。终于，经过无数千钧一发的险情，又经过在目标门前那户以上十家和以下十家之间一阵摧心折肠的来回摇摆，我才真正获释，由女仆引路，登上那道狭窄的楼梯——我相信我心跳的咚咚声简直听得见。我听见人们在谈话，西奥多拉的嗓子在里头格外分明。那女仆并没有通报我的姓名，我随即发觉，她并未察觉我跟在她身后上了楼，只听她说道：

"太太，要是您乐意，门厅里有个大拇指汤姆似的小个子男人，说是您请他来喝茶的；可我看哪，他八成是个送货铺子里的小伙计，来送账单的，您要是愿意，我就揪着他耳朵把他扔出去。"

===Original===
I was so confused and embarrassed, and above all so anxious to put an end to the discussion, before anything past all endurance should be said, that I bolted into the room, putting on the best smile I could and stretching out my hand to Mrs. Molloy, who was next me. But the maid at the door, with arms as thick as Donnelly's, the boxer, caught me by the collar at the nape of my neck with such a sudden jerk that I fell sitting on the floor, smack, as if I was shot, and she never let go her grip, but held me half-choked, sitting bolt upright, with my legs out, pumps and pantaloons, like a pair of compasses.

"How dare ye!" says the powerful maid, giving me a shake that made my teeth chatter. "How dare ye, dare ye, dare ye!"

===Chinese===
我又窘又慌，更要紧的是——生怕再说出什么忍无可忍的话来——急着要把这场议论了结，便一头冲进屋里，竭力堆出最体面的笑，向身边最近的莫洛伊太太伸出手去。谁知门口那女仆——胳膊有拳击手唐纳利（Donnelly）那般粗——一把揪住我后颈的领子，猝然一拽，我"啪"地一屁股坐到地上，活像挨了一枪；她抓着不放，把我半掐半拽，让我直挺挺地坐着，两条腿——浅口舞鞋加长裤——笔直伸着，活像一副圆规。

"你好大的胆子！"那大力女仆吼道，把我一搡，搡得我牙齿咯咯作响，"你好大的胆子，胆子，胆子！"

===Original===
I think she'd have pulled me down the stairs backwards, sitting as I was, only that Mrs. Molloy recovered her speech, and with a stamp on the floor that made the teaspoons jump in their saucers, she bawls out, "My curse on you, Juggy Hanlon, what are you doing to Mr. Dooley, my most sinsare friend? Up with ye, Mr. Dooley, and I hope you're nothing the worse, and down with you, Juggy Hanlon, and my curse go along wid ye, to the kitchen. Take a chair and an air of the fire, Mr. Dooley, the evening's a trifle could, I think; and settle your cravat at the glass there between the windows, and we won't look at ye—bad luck to her impudence. Here's my daughter Theodora, waiting to shake hands wid ye; but she won't look at ye no more than myself till ye settle your waistcoat and cravat; it's a wonder of the world she didn't make smithereens of your watch. She's *cruel* strong, that same Juggy Hanlon!"

===Chinese===
我寻思，她真能就那么拽着我倒退着下楼梯，要不是莫洛伊太太这时回过神、开了口——她一踏地板，震得茶匙在茶碟里直跳，扯着嗓子吼道："我这诅咒落到你头上，贾吉·汉隆（Juggy Hanlon），你对杜利先生（Mr. Dooley）——我最真心实意的朋友——在做什么手脚？快起来吧，杜利先生，但愿您没伤着什么；滚下去，贾吉·汉隆，带着我的诅咒给我回厨房去。杜利先生，拉把椅子，烤烤火，今晚天儿略有点寒，我想；您就着两窗之间那面镜子把领巾整一整，我们决不瞧您——这不要脸的死丫头。这是小女西奥多拉，正等着和您握手呢；可她跟我一样，在您把马甲和领巾理好之前，是不会瞧您的；真得谢天谢地，她没把您的怀表砸成齑粉。那个贾吉·汉隆手劲儿*毒*着呢！"

===Original===
I did as I was bid; I was so confounded I could hardly see my own reflection in the dingy little pier-glass. I saw in the background the images of other people indistinctly, and I heard a sound of voices, but I could not say at the time whether they were laughing at me or what they were doing.

In another minute I was shaking hands with everyone that would shake hands with me, and with some of them, I dare say, twice over at least. I was beginning to feel more like myself. It was not a very large party: Mundy was there, and Lieutenant Kramm-Sidebotham was on duty, but expected to get off in time to come to supper—there was an impudent little Galway chap, no bigger than myself, with a smirk on his red face, and a pair of calves, I give you my honour, as round as a hat, paying attentions, if you please, to Miss Theodora Molloy. I don't think he was a day under forty! With half an eye I saw what he was at. If you caught a stranger driving your only horse and new gig to the Howth races, or walking down Dame Street in your best hat, with your umbrella in his hand, you might conceive, in a small way, the feelings with which I witnessed the usurpation in question. I had no idea until that moment how entirely I had come to regard Theodora as my own. I think I could have cut his ugly little head off his shoulders, and kicked it through the window into the Liffey.

===Chinese===
我依言而行；我那时五雷轰顶，连自己在那面昏暗的小壁炉镜里的影子都几乎看不清。我影影绰绰看见背景里旁人的形影，也听见一片人声嘈杂，可当时实在说不上他们是在笑我，还是在干什么。

不到一分钟，我已和所有肯同我握手的人握过手——有几位，我敢说，至少握了两遍。我渐渐找回了点自己。这场聚会人并不多：蒙迪在座，克拉姆-赛德博瑟姆中尉（Lieutenant Kramm-Sidebotham）值班去了，但说好来得及赶回来吃夜宵——另有一位高尔韦（Galway）来的放肆小个子，个头儿不比我高，红脸上挂着得意的一笑，两条小腿肚，我以名誉担保，圆得像帽檐，居然——您瞧瞧——正在向西奥多拉·莫洛伊小姐大献殷勤。我看他少说也有四十岁！我一眼便看穿了他打的什么主意。设若有陌生人驾着您唯一的马、您崭新的双轮马车去赶豪斯（Howth）赛马会，或是戴着您最好的礼帽、夹着您的雨伞，招摇过市走在戴姆街（Dame Street）上，您大致便能体会几分我目睹这桩"僭越"时的心情。直到那一刻我才明白，自己早已把西奥多拉视为禁脔。我想我真能一刀把他那颗丑陋的小脑袋削下来，一脚踢出窗外、踢进利菲河（Liffey）里去。

===Original===
"I must introjuice you to my sinsare friend—"

"The O'Kelly of Ballynamuck," whispered the gentleman from Galway, who knew his weakness.

"Mr. Dooley—"

"*Toole*," I whispered.

"Well, ain't it all one? Mr. Toole, I beg leave to introjuice you both. Mr. Toole, this is The O'Kelly of Ballynamuck. The O'Kelly of Ballynamuck, this is Mr. Toole."

"Proud to make your acquaintance," said The O'Kelly, with a fierce sort of curtsey, that made me think that he, also, instinctively smelt a rat.

"Your most obedient, sir," said I, making him an awful low bow, and, raising my head higher than usual, I treated him at the end of it to a short, fierce stare, with another short bow at the end of that again.

===Chinese===
"我得给您二位引见一下，这位是我的真心朋友——"

"巴利纳穆克的奥凯利（The O'Kelly of Ballynamuck），"那位高尔韦来的绅士悄声补了一句，他这点虚荣心自己是晓得的。

"这位是杜利先生——"

"*奥图尔（Toole）*，"我小声更正。

"哎，这有什么两样？奥图尔先生，我这就给二位引见。奥图尔先生，这位是巴利纳穆克的奥凯利。巴利纳穆克的奥凯利，这位是奥图尔先生。"

"幸会幸会，"奥凯利说道，行了一个带几分凶相的屈膝礼，倒叫我暗想：他大概也凭着本能嗅出了味儿不对。

"卑职愿效犬马，先生，"我说着，回了他一个低得吓人的躬，又比平素更高地昂起头，在收势时送了他一记短促而凶狠的盯视，紧接着又是一个短躬。

===Original===
"Fine weather, sir! uncommon fine, Mr. Toole. Everything promises amazin'; though, of course, it don't agree with everything alike. If this weather houlds a little longer I wouldn't wonder if we had piteeties at three-halfpence!"

"*Indeed*, sir!" said I, expressing more wonder than I altogether felt, for I wasn't quite sure whether the sum he named was wonderfully high or wonderfully low. "Do you play billiards, sir?"

"No, sir; cards and cock-fightin' serves my turn. But what is cards and what is cock-fightin' compared with the delightful societee of neeture's noblest work, the objeck of our aspirations, our homage, and our life's devotion—the fair sex?"

And with this he made a flourish with his hat, and a bow to Miss Theodora, the like of which I could hardly hope to execute in half a life, with such a smile of conceit and assurance, and, I may say, of defiance, as almost drove me out of my senses, and down he went, with a whisk, into the chair next hers, and began to talk love and nonsense into her ear, under my very nose! Every now and then, I could see from the corners of his eye he gave me a look as much as to say, "I have her, and I mean to keep her; and don't you wish you may get her?"

"That fellow's disposed to put a quarrel on me," said I to myself; "*let* him; if he don't, maybe *I'll* put one upon *him*."

===Chinese===
"好天气啊，先生！好得出奇，奥图尔先生。万事都大吉大利；当然咯，天下之物，未必样样都喜欢这天气一视同仁。这天气若再持续上几日，土豆卖到三个半便士一担，我也不会吃惊！"

"*原来如此*，先生！"我说，流露出的惊异过于我真实所感，因为我实在拿不准他报的这个价到底是奇高还是奇低，"先生您打台球么？"

"不打，先生；打牌、斗鸡足矣。然而打牌也好、斗鸡也罢，怎比得上造化这最高杰作之令人销魂的交游——我们魂牵梦萦、顶礼膜拜、终生献身之对象——那秀外慧中之性别？"

说罢他帽一挥、身一躬，朝西奥多拉小姐行了一礼，那身段我苦练半生怕也难及；他脸上那一丝自负、笃定，乃至——恕我直言——挑衅的笑意，几乎把我气得失了心智，旋即一闪身坐进她身旁的椅子，就在我眼皮底下，对着她耳朵喁喁地谈起情话、扯起淡来！从他的眼角我看得见，他不时瞟我一眼，那意思分明是："她归了我，我打算一直占着；你眼馋也白搭。"

"这家伙存心要寻我的事，"我暗想，"*随*他去；他若不寻，说不定*我*倒要寻*他*一寻。"

===Original===
I dare say I looked a little bit surly, for Mrs. Molloy plucked me by the coat, and said: "Sit down at the table, here, beside me, and take a hot cup o' tay, and a cut o' that pittaytee-cake; and may I never! but ye look as if ye saw your tailor's ghost with a bill in his fingers. Sit down now, I tell you," and the imperious old lady pulled me down on the chair with a souse. "And here's for you; that's stingo; drink it, my child; and cream in it that will make you as fat as a pig."

I think in her youth Mrs. Molloy must have been very nearly as strong as Juggy Hanlon: I felt perfectly helpless in the hands of either. In deep dudgeon I swallowed lumps of potato-cake and gulped down tea, talking rather vaguely with old Mrs. Molloy, and watching Theodora and The O'Kelly of Ballynamuck with the corner of my eye.

===Chinese===
我敢说我脸上必有点愠色，因为莫洛伊太太拽了拽我的衣摆，说道："坐到桌边来，在我这儿，喝一杯热茶，再切一块那土豆饼吃；圣母保佑！您这张脸，倒像瞧见您那裁缝拿了账单显了灵。我说您就坐下吧，"这位专横的老太太一把将我按进椅子，按得我沉甸甸一沉。"这杯给您；这是烈酒；喝了吧，我的乖乖；里头有奶油，喝了管您肥得像头猪。"

我想莫洛伊太太年轻时，力气大概也不下于贾吉·汉隆：在她们两位手里，我都毫无招架之力。我满腹愤懑，吞下一块块土豆饼、灌下一口口茶，有一搭没一搭地同老莫洛伊太太搭着话，眼角的余光却时刻盯着西奥多拉和巴利纳穆克的奥凯利。

===Original===
"I see how it is, my poor little fellow," says Mrs. Molloy, with a kind wink at me, "but don't bother you head about him. Mickey Kelly there," and she winked at me again, and jogged her elbow in the direction of The O'Kelly, "can't come to the playhouse tonight; he's going to Killcock to sell a mare, and he's the boy that can do it. So Theodora'll have no one to look after her but yourself and them officers, and I leave her among you, and I think I know who'll be foremost. We leave that dear girl, me and Molloy there, just to do whatever she likes best herself. What time of day is it, Molloy?"

Old Molloy obediently grasped the seals of his huge silver watch, and hauled it, with several tugs, from the recesses of his fob.

"Why then, it's time the coaches was at the door," says Mrs. Molloy, in a tone of brisk alarm, having heard his report. "Ring the bell, some o' yez, like darlin's. Where's that Juggy Hanlon? Don't be affeard, Mr. Dooley," she interpolated to me, with a momentary playfulness, "she shan't lay a finger on you. Call two coaches, Juggy, and don't be while ye'd be lookin' about ye—mind. Run in and get ready, Theo, my child." And she added more vehemently to her helpmate, "Shake them crumbs off your small-clothes, Mr. Molloy, and, for dacency's sake, will ye wipe that butter off your chin."

===Chinese===
"我看明白啦，我可怜的小家伙，"莫洛伊太太说着，朝我使了个善意眼色，"您就别为他伤神啦。那边那个米基·凯利（Mickey Kelly），"她又朝我使了个眼色，把胳膊肘朝奥凯利那个方向顶了顶，"今儿晚上看不成戏喽；他要去基尔科克（Killcock）卖一匹母马，他可是干这行的好手。这么着，西奥多拉除开您和那几位军官，就没人照应了，我把她托付给你们这一伙，我看谁会抢在最前头，我心里是有数的。这么个可人疼的闺女，我跟这儿的莫洛伊，由着她爱怎么着就怎么着。莫洛伊，几点钟啦？"

老莫洛伊乖乖地抓住他那块大银表的表坠，连拽好几把，才把它从表袋深处拖了出来。

"哎呀，马车早该到门口啦，"莫洛伊太太听了报时，用一种急惊风似的口气说道，"你们哪个去摇铃呀，好孩子们。那个贾吉·汉隆又跑哪儿去了？别怕，杜利先生，"她忽然俏皮地对我插了一句，"她绝碰不到您一根指头。叫两辆马车来，贾吉，别磨磨蹭蹭东张西望的——听见没。进去换衣裳去，西奥，乖闺女。"她又冲她那位老帮厨更激烈地喝道，"把你裤衩上的面包渣掸掸，莫洛伊先生，看在体面的份上，把下巴上的黄油揩一揩。"

===Original===
So issuing her orders in hot haste, Mrs. Molloy fussed, and wheezed, and bustled about. Mundy was arranging his curls, and smiling blandly at his handsome features in the looking-glass; and Lieutenant Kramm was entertaining old Molloy with terrific anecdotes of his sporting and military life; and The O'Kelly was taking his leave with all the fascination and gallantry that belonged to his courtly manners. From the window I saw him get into a battered gig, and drive off at a hideous pace, pretty much at the mercy of a mad-looking horse, in a westerly direction. That red-faced thief made me very uneasy; and you may be sure it wasn't altogether about his neck I was anxious.

Well, he was gone; that was one comfort. I shook myself up, and strutted from one window to another, and Mrs. Molloy's words and looks of encouragement came back, and I began to think if a little beast like that chooses to pin himself to a girl's apron-string, what is she to do? I dare say she hated the old whisky-faced rascal as much as I did; and didn't she give me a smile over her shoulder as she left the room!

My spirits rose. I was glad to observe that Mundy, who was six feet high and wore a red coat—decisive odds—was not in the running; and Kramm was directing his attentions chiefly to the old people. The opportunity would, after all, prove as fortunate as my wildest hopes had painted it.

===Chinese===
就这样风风火火地下着一连串号令，莫洛伊太太喘着粗气，里里外外地忙碌打点。蒙迪正对镜整理鬈发，顾影自盼那张英俊面孔上温和地笑着；克拉姆中尉（Lieutenant Kramm）正用他打猎与军旅生涯的惊险轶闻，哄得老莫洛伊乐不可支；而奥凯利正以他那宫廷仪态所特有的魅力与风度，行礼告辞。我从窗里望见他登上一辆破旧的双轮马车，朝西狂奔而去，那速度快得骇人，几乎任凭一匹看着像发了疯的马摆布。那个红脸贼叫我好生不安；您大可放心，我惦记的，决不仅仅是他的脖颈。

哎，他总算走了；这是一桩安慰。我抖擞精神，从这扇窗踱到那扇窗，莫洛伊太太方才那番鼓励的言辞与神色又涌上心头，我便想：若是这等小畜生偏要死死缠上一个姑娘的围裙带，姑娘又该如何是好？我敢说她厌弃那威士忌脸的老流氓，决不亚于我；何况——她临出房门时，可不是回过头来冲我嫣然一笑么！

我的精神为之一振。我欣喜地发现，蒙迪——身长六尺、身披红军装——这本是压倒性的优势——竟无意角逐；而克拉姆则把殷勤主要献给了两位老人。看来这一晚的良机，终究会如我最狂妄的企盼所描绘的那般称心如意。

===Original===
In a few minutes more we were rolling and rattling away to the theatre. Mrs. Molloy distinguished Kramm and Mundy by placing herself under their escort, and starting first, with a tipsy coachman and a horse that had a morbid jerk in one of its legs, and seemed at every fifth step to be on the point of pitching, with a curtsey, on its head. Away they went in full fig, merrily, in this conveyance; Mrs. Molloy, as proud as a peacock to take her seat in the box next his Excellency, the Lord Lift'nant! I, old Molloy, and the lovely Theodora, whom I keep to the last, as children do their best bit, followed in our jingling, thundering, rolling coach, and in a few minutes down slammed the steps in front of the box-entrance, and I had the happiness of giving my arm to the beautiful girl I had never ceased thinking of since I saw her for the first time, in the barouche, outside the pickle-shop on Stephen's Green. Can I ever forget it!

===Chinese===
不多几时，我们便一路颠簸、辚辚地向戏院进发。莫洛伊太太为示优待，把自己托付给克拉姆和蒙迪护送，先行一步，配的是一个醉醺醺的车夫和一匹一条腿有点儿病态抽筋的马——每走五步便像要行个屈膝礼、一头栽到地上去似的。他们这辆车的气派可足了，一路欢声出发；莫洛伊太太骄傲得像只孔雀，只因能在紧挨着阁下——总督大人（Lord Lieutenant）——的包厢里落座！我、老莫洛伊，还有可爱的西奥多拉——我把她留到最后说，正如小孩子把最好的一口留到最后——坐着我们那辆叮当乱响、如雷轰鸣、一路滚动的马车随后；几分钟光景，包厢入口前的踏板"砰"地放下，我便有幸挽起那位美貌姑娘的胳膊——自从我头一回在斯蒂芬绿地（Stephen's Green）腌菜店门外那辆四轮敞篷马车里瞥见她，我便一刻也未曾忘怀过她。我怎会忘得了！

===Original===
Here we are now, all in our glory, under the blaze of the lamps. Mrs. Molloy's turban, or, as she persisted in calling that sort of coiffure, to her dying day, her "turbot," was the finest thing in green, yellow, and pink that night in the playhouse, with a big pin—I suppose they were precious stones—stuck in the front of it; her dress was of corresponding magnificence. At that time ladies wore next to no waists at all, and their clothes were made almost as tight as bolster-cases, if you just suppose a bit of string all round tied tight, and as close under the armpits as anatomy would permit. Whatever advantages this style of dress had, I think it was rather trying to persons of Mrs. Molloy's figure, and was calculated, with uncommon candour, to display every pound of flesh she boasted. She had three necklaces on, and a roll of fat for every one, and a pair of Roman-pearl pendants, that were as big as duck-eggs, and kept swinging and knocking on her inflamed shoulders whenever she turned her head. I will say this for Mrs. Molloy, that for her time of life she was as showy and plentiful a figure, and as roomy a woman as you could wish to fill a window with on a Lord Mayor's Day; and this night, in the front row of the box, next his Excellency, she was looking her very best, and, I dare say, a more striking figure than the Lord Lieutenant himself.

===Chinese===
此刻我们齐齐到场，满身荣光地置身于灯烛辉煌之中。莫洛伊太太的头巾——她至死都执拗地把那种发饰称为她的"大菱鲆"（turbot）——乃是当晚戏院里绿、黄、粉三色交辉的头一等等货，前面还别着一枚大饰针——我想那上头必是宝石；她的衣裳亦同样奢华。那个年代，太太小姐们几乎不带腰身，衣裳做得紧得近乎装羽毛褥子的套子，您只消设想周身一根绳紧紧勒住，勒到解剖学所允许、紧贴腋下的地步即可。这种式样不论有何等好处，对莫洛伊太太这副身材而言，我以为未免有些苛刻，它公道得毫不留情，把她自夸的每一磅肉都昭示出来。她颈间戴着三串项链，每一串下面都配一圈肉卷；耳垂上挂着一副罗马珍珠耳坠，足有鸭蛋那么大，她一转头，便在那双红肿的肩膀上摇来摆去、砰砰作响。我须得替莫洛伊太太说句公道话：以她这把年纪，她已是您所能指望的、最鲜亮丰腴的身段，最能撑满一扇窗户的阔绰妇人——市长节（Lord Mayor's Day）那日填满一扇窗正合适；而今晚，在紧挨着阁下的那间包厢前排座位上，她正是她最出色的模样，我敢说，比之总督大人本人，她倒更是个引人注目的人物。

===Original===
Mrs. Molloy was so anxious to get next the Lord Lieutenant, and her daughter to get as far as possible from Mrs. Molloy that Mundy and I were put side by side in the middle, Miss Theodora on my right, and the old lady on Mundy's left next the viceregal box. I remember the arrangement well, because we were hardly in our places, and I saying something engaging to Miss Theodora Molloy, sitting as I was side by side with my friend the lieutenant, when a fellow in the gallery calls out, "Three cheers for *Mundy* and his man *Friday*," and three cheers followed that made the lustres tremble.

This you may be sure made me feel rather fidgetty, more especially as who should I see but that blackguard young Figges, and all his malevolent family, grinning and sniggering away in a front row, only a box or two off. He was watching me, and laughing, you'd say, for a wager, and bursting with spite.

===Chinese===
莫洛伊太太一心要紧挨着总督大人，而她女儿则一心要离莫洛伊太太越远越好，于是蒙迪和我被并排安插在中间，西奥多拉小姐坐在我的右边，老太太则坐在蒙迪的左边，紧挨着那间副王包厢（viceregal box）。这格局我记得清清楚楚，因为我们刚一落座、我正对西奥多拉·莫洛伊小姐说着什么讨巧的话——我与我那位中尉朋友并肩坐着——顶层楼座便有个家伙高声喊道："为*蒙迪*和他那个*星期五*（man Friday）伙计，三呼万岁！"紧跟着果真三声欢呼，震得枝形吊灯直打颤。

您可想见，这叫我颇为坐立不安，更要命的是——我一眼便瞧见那个无赖小子菲格斯（Figges），还有他那满门心怀恶意的家眷，正挤在只隔一两个包厢的前排，嬉皮笑脸、窃窃私语地坏笑。他盯着我瞧，那样子，您会说，准是拿定了主意要笑个痛快，憋着一肚子坏水快要爆炸了。

===Original===
I was as sure as could be, of a thing I did not actually see, that the sneaking rascal had sent a lot of his shop-boys into the upper gallery to make fun of me before the people. Of course he saw my name down and who I was with when he went to take his places.

It was a terrible unlucky thing. It was putting me out. I could not hear half she said; and two or three times I was very near talking nonsense.

In a minute more another chap calls out from the gallery: "A cheer for the big soger with the little *hyacinth* in his buttonhole," and off goes another cheer.

Well, this blew over like the last, leaving me feeling rather small and blushing all over. But I did not pretend to think they meant me, and went on talking all the same, thinking the overture would never begin, and the curtain go up to put me out of pain.

Then there comes a thundering cheer for Mr. Toole, in the box next his Excellency, and I saw the Figgenses tittering.

No matter, I was determined to keep never-minding, and to talk on to that beautiful girl as if nothing in the world was going the least bit wrong.

===Chinese===
我虽未亲眼看见，却十拿九稳地断定：这鬼鬼祟祟的流氓，定是塞了一大群他铺子里的伙计到顶层楼座上去，好在人前拿我开涮。当然，他定座之时必已瞧见我的大名，又瞧见我与谁同座。

这真是倒霉透顶。它搅得我心神大乱。她说的话我有一半听不真切；有两三回，我险些说出一派胡言。

不过一分钟，顶层楼座又有小子喊道："为那个扣眼儿里别着小*海厄辛斯*的大兵，欢呼一声！"紧跟着又是一阵欢呼。

哎，这一阵也像方才那阵一样过去了，留下我自觉十分渺小，满脸通红。但我佯作不知他们指的是我，依旧谈笑自若，只盼序曲快些奏起、幕布快些升起，好让我从这煎熬里解脱。

紧接着又起了一阵惊天动地的欢呼——"为紧挨阁下包厢里的奥图尔先生！"——我又瞧见菲格斯一家在窃笑。

也罢，我打定主意充耳不闻，照旧同那位美貌姑娘谈笑，仿佛这世上没有任何一丁点儿不顺心的事。

===Original===
"May I make bold," says I, "to ask you, Miss Molloy, how long it is since you and Mr. O'Kelly were first acquainted?"

"And why should you care a brass farthing, Mr. Toole, to know?" says she, looking as innocent and startled-like as a little frightened bird. "Sure there's no harm in poor little Micky O'Kelly!"

"No harm, I dare say, and not much good," said I; "but whatever he is I envy him, Miss Molloy, and lament all the precious time I have lost."

I said this, you may be sure, as tenderly as I could.

"Mr. Toole, I hope you're gettin' on with her," calls out a fellow affectionately from the gallery.

"Never mind," says another, "he's the boy that'll *melt* her soon."

I felt my very cheeks tingling with shame. There was another cheer, and those accursed Figgenses grinning. Well, it could not last forever, I thought. "Will those beastly fiddlers never begin?" I thought. "Is there no one else in the house to make fun of but me? Will I ever be out o' this, dead or alive?"

===Chinese===
"我可否冒昧问一句，"我说，"莫洛伊小姐，您和奥凯利先生相识有多久啦？"

"奥图尔先生，您又何苦在乎一个铜子儿呢？"她说，神情天真而吃惊，活像一只受了惊的小鸟，"可怜的小米基·奥凯利（Micky O'Kelly）又没什么坏处呀！"

"坏处嘛，我瞧是没有，好处大概也不多，"我说，"可不论他是什么样的人，我都嫉妒他，莫洛伊小姐，我更为自己白白错过了这许多宝贵光阴而痛惜。"

您放心，这番话我说得尽可能温柔。

"奥图尔先生，但愿您跟她谈得顺手啊，"顶层楼座有个家伙一脸殷勤地冲下喊。

"别理他，"另一个说，"他小子才是个一上来就能把她*化*掉的主儿。"

我只觉双颊火辣辣地羞得发烫。又是一阵欢呼，那该死的菲格斯一家还在窃笑。哎，这总不能持续一辈子罢，我想。"这群该死的提琴手怎么还不动手？"我又想，"这屋里除了我，就没别人可供取笑了吗？我这一辈子，还能不能从这儿出去——是死是活都行？"

===Original===
The house was now filling fast; the box-doors were opening and clapping; a human flood was oozing and tumbling into the pit from every entrance. The gallery was becoming more noisy every minute; the orchestra were assembling, were chatting together, turning over music, and tuning violins, double-basses, and all sorts of instruments. There was a cheer for "Nosey," which was the nickname of the "leader" of those days. There was the usual "groan for the man in the white hat," and call for "music," and two or three fruits, small and hard, of that popular kind which were displayed by the vendors at the corner of Carlisle Bridge, in old japanned snuffer-dishes, and offered from 11 o'clock, a.m., to sun-setting, with inviting monotony, in the words, "Fourteen scarlet *craftons* for a halfpenny," hit a hat or two in the pit, and one sounded the big drum with a spirit that made the accomplished drummer start, and drew upon him a glance of indignation from "Nosey," now upon his throne. These "fine scarlet *craftons*," as I knew from experience, were as cheap and convenient an ammunition as a man could take with him to the upper gallery, when he wished to take half-an-hour's innocent diversion with bald heads in the pit. Only two or three came down now; but they were "like the first of a thundershower," as Lord Byron says, and I knew they were signs of the coming storm.

===Chinese===
此时戏院里很快便座无虚席；包厢门此开彼合，砰砰作响；一股人流从各个入口汩汩涌入、跌跌撞撞地挤进池座。顶层楼座每过一分钟便喧哗几分；乐队正陆续到齐，相互寒暄，翻着乐谱，给小提琴、低音提琴及各色乐器调着音。先是一阵为"大鼻子"（Nosey）——这是那个年代乐队"指挥"的绰号——的欢呼。接着是照例"给那个戴白帽子的男人一通嘘"，以及"奏乐"的叫嚷；还有两三个小而硬的果子——正是卡莱尔桥（Carlisle Bridge）桥头那些小贩摆在旧漆面烛剪盘里、从上午十一点到日落以诱人又单调的腔调叫卖的那种流行果子："半便士十四个红克拉夫顿果（craftons）"——飞下来砸中了池座里一两顶帽子，还有一颗精神抖擞地敲响了大鼓，惊得那位技艺娴熟的鼓手一愣，惹来此刻已登宝座的"大鼻子"一记怒视。这些"上好的红克拉夫顿果"，凭我的经验可知，乃是您想上顶层楼座、拿池座里的秃脑袋作半小时无伤大雅之消遣时，所能携带的最廉价又便利的弹药。眼下只落下两三颗；然而正如拜伦勋爵所言，它们"恰似雷阵雨的头一阵"，我深知这是暴风雨将至之兆。

===Original===
And now, on a sudden, everyone in the house stood up, the orchestra struck up "God Save the King." The Lord Lieutenant was taking his place in state, in the box next ours, and such a storm of clapping, cheering, hooting, groaning, hissing, whacking of sticks on the front of the gallery, whistling, catcalls, and other sounds rose all at once, as made the music totally inaudible, and deafened the entire audience for a time. During the whole of this period, while we could see by the elbows and fiddlesticks of the orchestra that the national anthem was still being played, much to my chagrin, I saw Mrs. Molloy, in whom I felt an interest, reflected from her lovely daughter, and a responsibility though not quite so near as Mundy's, behaving herself in a manner that, I confess, scandalised me a good deal; for, with her side and shoulder on the cushion of our box, she contrived to get her face round the partition of his Excellency's, and indeed, I may say, pretty well into it. One of her objects had been to get a good look at that dignified personage. I could soon perceive that she was engaged in a violent altercation with someone in the viceregal box, in which her face was, I may say, established.

I thought I could distinguish in her powerful voice an allusion to the well-known privilege that cats enjoy, of looking at kings; but, except the constant and vehement nodding of her turban, I could see nothing of what was going on in the state box.

===Chinese===
忽然之间，全场观众齐刷刷起立，乐队奏起《天佑吾王》。总督大人正庄严地在紧邻我们的那间包厢里就座——一时间，掌声、欢呼声、倒彩声、嘘叹声、嘶叫声、手杖敲击顶层楼座围栏的啪啪声、口哨声、猫叫般的倒好声，种种声响齐作，把乐声彻底淹没，把全场听众都震得一时耳聋。在这整段时间里——我们凭乐队手肘和琴弓的动作，可知国歌仍在演奏——令我大为懊恼的是，我瞧见莫洛伊太太（我对她本有几分关切，那是从她可爱女儿身上映照出来的关切；这份照应之责，虽不及蒙迪离她那么近），正以一种我得承认令我相当骇异的举止行事：她把半边身子和肩膀枕在我们包厢的软垫上，硬是把脸挤过了阁下那间包厢的隔板，老实说，几乎是把脸伸了进去。她此行目的之一，原就是要好好瞧瞧那位威严的大人物。不久我便察觉，她正在副王包厢里——她的脸我敢说已经安了进去——同什么人激烈地争执起来。

我仿佛能从她洪亮的嗓音里听出一句暗喻，提的是猫儿们也享有的那种众所周知的特权——可以直视国王；但除了她的头巾一刻不停、起劲地点动之外，那间副王包厢里究竟发生着什么，我一概瞧不见。

===Original===
