Tom Barnacle was in the pit, a little way out, and told me next day all he saw; and from that and Mrs. Molloy's narrative, I can relate that when her face presented itself considerable surprise and even consternation appeared in the countenances of those members of the household that were stationed in the rear of "his Excellency," who looked straight before him, as if unconscious of the appearance of the disk that had risen so unexpectedly on his horizon.

Mrs. Molloy nodded repeatedly to "his Excellency," and smiled affably, assuring him that she was proud to see him there, and that Molloy himself and her daughter being in the next box she did not think it would be manners if someone of the family did not wish his Excellency health, wealth, long life, and prosperity, which she did with a *cead mille failthe* from the heart of a Connaught woman, and the boosom of Ireland.

===Chinese===
汤姆·巴纳克尔（Tom Barnacle）那晚在池座里，坐得稍靠外，第二天把他所见的统统告诉了我；综合他所言和莫洛伊太太自述，我可以转述如下：当她的脸探过去时，"阁下"身后随侍的那些 household 成员，脸上都露出相当的惊讶，甚至惊慌；而"阁下"本人则直视前方，仿佛全然不觉他那片天际线上竟如此意外地升起了一轮圆盘。

莫洛伊太太连连朝"阁下"点头，和蔼地笑着，向他保证说，能在此见到阁下真是三生有幸；既然莫洛伊本人和她闺女就在隔壁包厢，她以为家里若没一个人前来祝愿阁下健康、富有、长寿、发达，未免有失礼数——她这便做了，带着一个康诺特（Connaught）女人发自肺腑、出自爱尔兰胸怀的一句"十万分欢迎"（céad míle fáilte）。

===Original===
His Excellency, she complained afterwards, did not appear to hear what she was saying—"them ignorant blackguards were making such a noise"—but as the speech exhibited no symptoms of drawing towards its close, one of the gentlemen, in Castle uniform, stepped forward, and said with very marked distinctness: "Unless you withdraw your face, a constable shall take you from the next box, and convey you to the watch-house."

It was upon this that Mrs. Molloy, who had a "sperit" befitting her ancient lineage, had retorted in high and scornful terms upon the "gentleman-at-large," who looked as if he would have liked to take by the throat that turbaned Turk; and it was not until she saw him, as she thought, make a sign to someone, in the rear of the box, that her prudence overcame her indignation, and, with a face of flame and many a sniff and snort, she resumed her original pose, and stared fiercely across at the side-scene opposite, and her gills palpitated for half an hour afterwards.

The frightful discord with which the representative of majesty was received, foreboded the political storm that was brewing.

===Chinese===
事后她抱怨说，阁下似乎并未听见她说些什么——"那些无知的下流坯子吵得那叫一个凶"——可这番演说却毫无收尾的迹象，于是一位身穿城堡制服的绅士走上前来，咬字极清地说道："您若不把脸收回去，就派一名警察从隔壁包厢把您带走，押进拘留所。"

便是这话激得莫洛伊太太——她那"气性"配得上她的古老门第——以高傲而轻蔑的措辞回敬了那位"逍遥绅士"；那绅士看样子恨不得掐住这位头缠巾的"土耳其女人"的喉咙；直待她瞧见——她自以为瞧见——他朝包厢后排的某人做了个手势，她这才让谨慎压过了愤懑，一张脸涨得通红，又是吸鼻子又是喷气，重新坐回原姿势，凶狠地瞪着对面的侧幕，腮帮子在之后半个钟头里还在一鼓一鼓。

王权代表所遭受的这般骇人的嘘声与倒彩，正预示着一场酝酿中的政治风暴。

===Original===
*Macbeth* was the play, and my troubles, to return from great things to small, were not over yet, for when the witches came on, and the cauldron appeared, a chap calls out from the gallery: "The boiling-pot, Mr. Toole."

I felt it the more that there was a dead silence in the house at the moment. And when the smoke began to come up, and the witches said:

> "Double, double, toil and trouble;

> Fire, burn; and, cauldron, bubble."

"Melting-day, Toole," says another. And when Macbeth said:

> "Out, out, brief candle."

There was a roar of "Short sixes."

I give you my sacred honour, I felt as if I was melting myself. I'd have liked to stand up that minute and tell the whole world I was a chandler. There's nothing on earth so torturing as a mystery, with a lot of fellows, that know all about it, poking it under your nose every minute in the presence of a great assembly.

===Chinese===
当晚演的是《麦克白》（Macbeth），撇开大事回到小事——我的麻烦尚未到头；因为女巫上场、魔釜现出之时，顶层楼座便有小子高声道："煮油锅，奥图尔先生。"

我之所以格外难堪，是因为此时全场鸦雀无声。待到烟雾升起，女巫们念道：

> "加倍，加倍，辛劳与祸殃；

> 烈火啊，烧吧；魔釜啊，沸腾吧。"

"化油日到了，奥图尔，"另一个说。麦克白念到：

> "熄灭吧，熄灭吧，短促的烛光。"

底下便是一片哄吼："短烛！六号装！"

我以神圣的荣誉起誓，我觉得自己都要被熔化了。我恨不得当场站起，向全世界宣告我是个烛匠。这世上再没有比一桩谜团更折磨人的事了——一群对内情了如指掌的家伙，在大庭广众之下，每过一分钟便把它怼到你鼻子底下戳弄一番。

===Original===
Between the acts, it was one succession of groans, and hisses, and political sentiments, and it was plain that the Lord Lieutenant and the government bigwigs were in ill odour with the gallery. It was just when Macbeth was on the point of murdering King Duncan, a chap among the gods called out, by way of a joke: "God Save the King," and with that another calls for "Patrick's Day," and then the whole gallery round set up one roar for "Patrick's Day," and nothing could you hear but "Patrick's Day—Patrick's Day," in one thunder; you'd think the ceiling would come down. And out comes the manager, and stood bowing in front of the footlights, turning up his eyes to the gods, and Nosey waiting for a signal from him to strike up the tune they wanted. He made no sign; the clamour rose awfully; he smiled, he shrugged, he bowed very low, he expanded his white gloves imploringly, as he slowly looked from one side to the other of the gallery. All would not do; they would not give him a hearing. The manager went off, bowing and smiling regretfully, and he sent on Lady Macbeth to proceed, if she could; but the storm was rising steadily, and even that royal virago was forced to submit: Lady Macbeth curtseyed low, and in turn withdrew. Again the manager came forward. He gesticulated before the gentlemen in the gallery, conveying as well as he could that their demands were complied with; he stepped forward to the footlights, signed to Nosey, who rapped on his desk with his fiddlestick, and waved that wand of power over his musical familiars, and it was to be supposed the tune, so tumultuously demanded, was at last being executed by the full strength of Nosey's band; but, of course, not a note could anyone hear in the house. The magic of "Patrick's Day" was powerless to abate the storm. That quarrel was but a pretext: there was something deeper in it. The manager bowed very low, and a sucked orange hit him on the head. At the same moment a whisky-bottle, from the upper gallery, hit the front of the Lord Lieutenant's box, and a shower of glass splinters flew in all directions. Now there were gentlemen standing up in the boxes, and gesticulating fiercely at the gallery; box-doors were opened and peaceable people were drawing back and some getting out on the corridors; the same agitation was visible in the pit. Smash goes another bottle on the side of the viceregal box.

===Chinese===
幕间休息时，嘘声、倒彩、政治性的口号此起彼伏，一连串不断；很明显，总督大人和政府的大员们，在顶层楼座里已是名声狼藉。正当麦克白要下手谋害邓肯王之际，顶层楼座那些"天神"里有位小子打趣地喊了一声："天佑吾王！"紧跟着另一位便叫起要听《圣帕特里克节》（Patrick's Day），于是整圈楼座齐声哄起《圣帕特里克节》——除开《圣帕特里克节——圣帕特里克节》之外，您什么也听不见了，一片雷鸣；您准以为天花板都要塌下来。经理走了出来，站在脚灯前连连鞠躬，翻着眼睛望向那些"天神"，"大鼻子"则等着他示意，好奏起他们要的那支曲子。他却不发信号；喧声愈发骇人地高涨；他微笑，他耸肩，他深深鞠躬，他把戴白手套的双手恳求般地摊开，缓缓地、从楼座这头望到那头。这一切都无济于事；他们不肯听他说一句话。经理苦笑着、鞠着躬退下场去，又派麦克白夫人出来，能演就接着演；可风暴仍在稳步升级，连那位王家的母老虎也只得屈服：麦克白夫人深深一行屈膝礼，也跟着退了场。经理又一次走上前来。他对着楼座里的诸位先生连连比画，竭力传达他们的要求已被允诺之意；他走到脚灯前，朝"大鼻子"做了个手势，"大鼻子"便以琴弓敲了敲谱架，挥动那根权杖般指挥棒，调度他那群通灵的乐手；按理说，那支被闹着要了半天的曲子，此刻总算由"大鼻子"全班人马演奏起来了；可全场当然连一个音符也听不见。《圣帕特里克节》的魔力，镇压不住这场风暴。那场争闹不过是借口：底下藏着更深的文章。经理把腰深深弯下，一只啃过的橙子正中他脑门。与此同时，一只威士忌酒瓶从顶层楼座飞来，砸在总督包厢的正面，一片碎玻璃四下飞溅。此时包厢里已有先生们站起身，朝楼座方向狠狠比画；包厢门此开彼合，安分守己的人纷纷退避，有的退到走廊上；池座里也可见同样的骚动。又一只酒瓶"哐啷"砸在副王包厢的侧面。

===Original===
The Viceroy, being a plucky man, continued to sit serenely with his eyes on the stage. Old Molloy popped his bald head out to see what was going on, and instantly, not a scarlet "crafton," but one of those big, yellow apples that were called cannonballs—never did they better deserve their name—burst with a thump on his shining bald head, a bit of it, as big as a walnut, hit me in the eye, exactly as I was saying, with a look of unutterable love in the unfortunate eye that I had fixed on her: "Dear Miss Theodora, fear nothing; am not I beside you?" Some pulp marked the spot where it had hit her papa, and a "noggin" of cider was streaming over his massive forehead and intelligent eyes, and I dare say old Molloy thought, for a minute, he was back again on the fair green of Ballynawhop.

If we had known that the Lord Lieutenant's box was likely to become the mark for all this artillery, I doubt if Mrs. Molloy would have been in such a hurry to secure the place of honour.

===Chinese===
副王是个有胆的人，依旧神色安详地端坐着，眼睛盯着舞台。老莫洛伊探出他那个秃脑袋想瞧瞧出了什么事，一刹那间——飞来的不是什么红的"克拉夫顿果"，而是那种被唤作"炮弹"的大黄苹果——它们从未如此名实相副过——"砰"地一声砸在他那闪闪发亮的秃脑袋上，炸开一片；其中一块核桃大的，正巧在我把那只倒霉的眼睛脉脉含情地望着她、说出"亲爱的西奥多拉小姐，别怕；有我在您身边呢？"这句话的当口，击中了我的眼睛。它击中她爸爸的那块地方，留下了一些果肉做记号；一小木杯（noggin）苹果酒正顺着他宽阔的前额、聪慧的双眼汩汩流下；我敢说，老莫洛伊有一瞬间以为自己又回到了巴利纳沃普（Ballynawhop）那片赶集的草坪上。

当初我们要是知道总督的包厢会成为这一通炮火的靶子，莫洛伊太太是否还会那么急吼吼地去抢这上座的荣光，我可就说不准了。

===Original===
"Papa dear, are ye hurted?" Miss Theodora exclaimed with much trepidation; and "Oh, la! There's mamma!" And sure enough a cat had at that moment alighted with great directness on the head of Mrs. Molloy, whirling her tasteful turban and wig over her left cheek, and displaying instead a head as bald as her husband's. A live cat, bedad! If it had dropped into the box among us, Saint Peter would not have kept *me* in it an instant! Luckily it tumbled off Mrs. Molloy's turban, head over heels among the groundlings in the pit. Grasping her wig and turban with both hands she rose exclaiming, "Take me out of this hell upon earth some of ye."

At the same instant the Lord Lieutenant, having made up his mind to retire, rose with much dignity, and received a large lemon on his back; and I myself saw a mutton kidney in the eye of the Attorney-General, in the box opposite to ours.

===Chinese===
"爹爹，您伤着没？"西奥多拉小姐慌作一团地惊呼；"哎呀，我的妈！妈在那儿！"果不其然，就在那一刹那，一只猫以极精准的轨迹，落到了莫洛伊太太的头上，把她那雅致的头巾和假发掀得卷过她的左脸颊，露出底下跟她丈夫一样光秃秃的脑壳。一只活猫，老天作证！它要真是掉进我们包厢里，圣彼得（Saint Peter）也休想把我再多留一瞬！幸亏它从莫洛伊太太的头巾上一路翻着跟头，栽进池座那些"站票看客"（groundlings）堆里。莫洛伊太太双手紧抓着假发和头巾，站起身来嚷道："你们哪位快把我从这人间地狱里弄出去吧。"

同一刹那，总督大人已下定决心退场，极有威仪地站起身来，背上挨了一只大柠檬；而我则亲眼看见，我们对面包厢里检察总长（Attorney-General）的眼睛上，糊着一只羊腰子。

===Original===
It was indeed high time for all who had ladies to look after to beat a retreat, and we were soon in the corridor, and making our way down the stairs. Theodora was on my arm. I was afraid she might faint before we got her into the coach.

"Are you ill?" I whispered, squeezing her arm gently to the lapel of my coat with my elbow. "I hope you were not very much frightened?"

Upon this the charming girl treated me to a dazzling stare of her fine black eyes, and burst out laughing.

"Ah! Then, is it what you're jokin' me, you are, Mr. Toole?" says she. "Affeard, indeed! I wish you saw the stones and claealpins hoppin' on and off the boys' polls at the Fair of Killbattery. Ha, ha! Papa's nothing the worse, ye see; and, indeed, the smack of it took a start out of me, for I only saw it with the corner of my eye, and I could not tell but it was a paving-stone was in it, and the pulp flying out alarmed me for a moment for the dear man's brains. And mamma got it, too; that was a cat, or my name's not Theodora. Mamma! Who's she with? Oh, Mundy, I see. Mamma, dear, how's your head?"

"Bad enough, joole," rejoined Mrs. Molloy. "My beautiful turbot's rooned and smathered on my head!"

===Chinese===
凡是身边带着女眷要照应的人，此时撤退确是再及时不过；不多时我们已挤进走廊，一路摸索着下楼。西奥多拉挽着我的胳膊。我怕她挨不到上马车便要晕过去。

"您身子不舒服么？"我悄声问道，用胳膊肘把她那条胳膊轻轻夹向我的衣襟，"但愿您没受太大的惊吓？"

闻言，这位迷人的姑娘送了我一记漂亮黑眼睛的炫目凝视，随即放声大笑起来。

"哈！那么说，您是在拿我开心哪，奥图尔先生？"她说，"害怕，我才不呢！您真该瞧瞧基尔巴特里（Killbattery）集市上，石头和土坷垃在小伙子们的脑袋上蹦进蹦出的光景。哈哈！爹爹一点没事儿，您瞧；说真的，那一砸倒把我吓了一跳，因为我只用眼角一扫，瞧不真切，还当扔的是一块铺路石呢，那飞溅出的果肉教我为这位好人的脑浆捏了一瞬的心。妈妈也挨了一下；那可是一只猫，要不我不叫西奥多拉。妈妈！她跟谁在一块儿？哦，是蒙迪。妈妈，您的头怎么样啦？"

"糟透了，心肝，"莫洛伊太太答道，"我那顶漂亮的大菱鲆全毁了，稀烂地糊在我头上！"

===Original===
The people who looked round to see who the speaker was who had suffered in so unusual a way, beheld Mrs. Molloy with old Molloy's red and yellow silk pocket-handkerchief tied under her chin, holding her wig and turban down in their place, and looking, certainly, not unlike that class of ladies who used to carry flatfish on their heads, and certainly I did feel a little bashful about her, for one side of her wig was dangling from under Molloy's handkerchief between her shoulders, and the Figgesses, who were coming down the stairs behind us, were laughing like hyenas. I don't think there was an unlucky thing happened to us that night but the eyes of that same beastly family were upon us.

I was thankful when Mrs. Molloy was shut up in her hack coach, and her daughter, her husband, and myself in ours.

===Chinese===
那些回头张望、想瞧瞧是哪位发言人以这般不寻常方式遭了殃的人，看见的是这样一副光景的莫洛伊太太：她下巴底下系着老莫洛伊那条红黄相间的真丝手帕，把假发和头巾按在原处，那模样——当然——倒与旧日那种头顶扁鱼叫卖的妇人颇有几分神似。我得承认，我替她确实有些难为情：她那假发有一边，正从莫洛伊的手帕底下坠下来，搭拉在她两肩之间，而跟在我们身后下楼的菲格斯一家，正笑得像一群鬣狗。我寻思，那晚我们没遭一桩倒霉事，是这一家下流胚子的眼睛没盯在我们身上的。

待到莫洛伊太太被关进她的雇佣马车，她女儿、她丈夫和我上了我们那辆，我才松了一口气。

===Original===
We had all recovered our spirits by the time we had reached our destination on Ormond Quay. Up the stairs we stumbled, talking all together, and into the front drawing-room, where Juggy Hanlon had already lighted candles. Mrs. Molloy slipped quietly upstairs to restore her distracted head to order, while we talked on in the room where we had first mustered, and we could hear the servants tramping up and down the back drawing-room, clinking plates, and jingling spoons and knives and forks, and squabbling in loud and voluble accents over the arrangement of the supper.

"Mr. Lieutenant Kramm has just been telling me, Miss Theodora, that your music is all that I should have anticipated," said I, "would it be asking too great a favour from a nightingale to sing us a song from the perch of that music-stool, and to accompany itself with a few harmonious touches of that forte-piano?"

I give you this pretty speech in full, to show you how much pains I was taking to gain the beautiful creature's heart.

"Lieutenant Kramm says more than his prayers, I'm afraid," says she, sitting down carelessly before the instrument. "Not that I sing like a nightingale, for I know very well that I don't."

But she looked all the time as if she thought that she did.

"You don't sing like the nightingale in this one respect," said I, "that you excel it beyond all calculation."

===Chinese===
待我们抵达奥蒙德码头的目的地，众人都已恢复了兴致。我们一路七嘴八舌、跌跌撞撞地上楼，进了前客厅，贾吉·汉隆已把蜡烛点上了。莫洛伊太太悄悄溜到楼上，把她那颗纷乱的脑袋收拾整齐；我们在最初集合的那间屋子里接着谈天，听见后客厅里仆人们来来回回地走动，盘子叮当、汤匙刀叉铮铮作响，嘴里还高声而流利地拌着嘴，争论着夜宵的摆布。

"西奥多拉小姐，方才克拉姆中尉正告诉我，您的音乐造诣一切都不出我所料，"我说，"敢问夜莺小姐，可否赏脸，从那琴凳的栖木上为我们唱一支歌，再以那架钢琴（forte-piano）数下和谐的触键，自弹自伴？"

我把这番漂亮话原原本本奉上，是要让您瞧瞧，我为赢取这位美人芳心，下了多大的功夫。

"克拉姆中尉夸得比他念的经还多，怕是，"她说着，漫不经心地在琴前坐下，"我可没那么像夜莺，这一点我心里有数。"

可她整个神情，却仿佛自认确是像的。

"有一点上，您确实与夜莺不同，"我说，"便是您远胜于它，难以计量。"

===Original===
"I don't mind a word you're saying, Mr. Toole; I think it's what you want to make a fool of me," said the young lady.

"Miss Molloy does not sing like the nightingale for *all* listeners," says Kramm, "only for her particular friends."

"That's it, I *hope*," said I, "and I devoutly entreat that I may be included among the number."

"Sing that glorious thing you astonished me with the other morning," said Mundy, joining the chorus of supplication. "If you don't, I'll beg of Mr. Molloy to use his influence as a father."

"Well, then, I suppose I may as well," says she. "I'll sing you one of Tommy Moore's melodies."

And, by the powers, so she did! She struck up on the piano, and I was delighted and, I do assure you, half-frightened by the power of her voice. Since I heard old "Whisky Tay" in the black-hole I had never listened to anything in the way of music half so loud! She had a way of throwing her voice into the words and swelling them out, that I never heard equalled; and when she came to the part:

> "The mo-hoon hid her li-hight,

> In the heavens that ni-hi-hight,

> And wept behind a clou-houd,

> O'er the maiden's shee-aim."

I was perfectly ravished.

===Chinese===
"您说的我半个字也不信，奥图尔先生；我看您是想拿我寻开心，"那位年轻小姐说。

"莫洛伊小姐并不对*所有*听众都唱得像夜莺，"克拉姆说，"只为她特殊的朋友才那样唱。"

"正是如此，我*正盼着*，"我说，"我虔诚地祈求，自己能被算在那群人之列。"

"唱那支前儿个早上把我镇住了的了不起的曲子吧，"蒙迪也加入了恳求的合唱，"您要是不唱，我就求莫洛伊先生行使他做父亲的权威了。"

"好吧，那我就唱罢，"她说，"我给你们唱一支汤米·穆尔（Tommy Moore）的旋律。"

老天作证，她当真唱了！她在钢琴上起了一个调，那嗓音的力道，令我既欣喜，又——我向您担保——半带惊惧。自打我在军营黑牢里听过老"威士忌·泰"（Whisky Tay）的演奏以来，我再没听过那样响亮的音乐！她有一种把嗓音灌进字句、又把它们撑得饱胀的唱法，我平生未见其匹；待她唱到那一段：

> "月‑‑哦‑‑亮藏起了它的光‑‑哎‑‑，

> 在那‑‑啊‑‑夜的苍穹‑‑呜‑‑里，

> 在一朵云‑‑嗯‑‑背后啜泣‑‑呀‑‑，

> 为‑‑啊‑‑那少女的‑‑羞‑‑耻。"

我已是如痴如醉。

===Original===
"More power! My blessing! May I never, but that *was* singing!" said I, in a state of extraordinary enthusiasm; and I do assure you I hardly knew whether I was on my head or my heels. "Thank you! *thank you!!* **thank you!!!**" I cried with growing fervour. "God bless you, my darling Miss Theodora, that was astonishing!"

Mundy was laughing all this time with a "Ha! ha! ha!" and no more disguise than he would at a clown in a circus.

"What are you laughing at, Mundy?" said I, turning on him as if I'd eat him up, with a stamp on the floor, for which I afterwards apologised to Miss Molloy, for it raised such a dust between me and Mundy I could scarcely see him, and I heard the young lady blowing and phewing, and slapping her hair with her pocket-handkerchief; and old Molloy was taken with a fit of coughing.

"*Laughing!*" says Mundy. "Ha! ha! ha! phew! I say, where's the good of smothering us? Ha! ha! ha! why, man, I tell you it is—ha! ha! ha!—hys-sis-sis-sisterical—ha! ha! ha! I can't help it, I tell you, I—ha! ha! ha!—have a sort of trembling inside whenever I'm very much moved. Miss Molloy knows all about it. Don't be a fool; I told her long ago. I've had it on parade, and at funerals, and at divine service, by Jove, and I'll not be cross-questioned, nor bamboozled, nor made more nervous by any man living. You believe me, Miss Molloy, and that's all I care about."

===Chinese===
"好气力！我给您祝福！圣母作证，这*才叫*唱歌！"我说，兴奋得异乎寻常；我向您保证，我几乎不知自己是头朝上还是脚朝上。"谢谢您！*谢谢！！***多谢！！！***"我越喊越热烈，"上帝保佑您，我心爱的西奥多拉小姐，这真叫人惊叹！"

蒙迪这会儿却一直"哈！哈！哈！"地大笑，毫不掩饰，犹如瞧马戏里的小丑一般。

"你笑什么，蒙迪？"我转过去对他，恨不得一口吞了他，一脚踏在地板上——这一下我事后向西奥多拉小姐赔了不是，因为它在我与蒙迪之间扬起老大一股灰，我几乎瞧不见他；我又听得那位小姐又是吹气又是啐声，拿手帕直拍头发；老莫洛伊则被勾起了一阵咳嗽。

"*笑！*"蒙迪说，"哈！哈！哈！啐！我说，把我们呛死有什么好处？哈！哈！哈！哎呀，老兄，我跟您说，这是——哈！哈！哈！——歇‑歇‑歇‑歇斯底里的——哈！哈！哈！我忍不住，我跟您说，我——哈！哈！哈！——每逢特别感动，里头就要这么一阵哆嗦。莫洛伊小姐全清楚的。别犯傻了；这事我老早就告诉她了。我曾在阅兵场上发作，也在葬礼上、在礼拜时发作过，老天作证，我不容许任何活人盘问我、糊弄我、把我弄得更紧张。莫洛伊小姐，您信我，我就只在乎这个。"

===Original===
"Ah! Be quiet, Toole, will ye?" It was the first time she called me by my surname, and I felt so happy I could have forgiven Mundy if he had pulled me by the nose. "It's true for him; he does really—he laughs whenever he's near cryin'. It happened to myself once, when I was getting well o' the swine-pock. Sure didn't I see the way he was over the beautiful verses my poor Uncle Barney wrote, when he was leaving Ireland in a decline, and he called the pome a 'Farewell to Allyballycarick-O-Dooley,' which was the name of his place, and there's hardly one in the world could read it without crying; and I give you my word, it was from one split of laughing with him into another! Not but what I think it would be better manners if he run his head in a pittaytie-pot, and clapped it out o' the windy, sooner than offend people by his weakness, when he felt the fit comin' on him," she concluded, with a little severity.

The discussion was ended at this point by the return of Mrs. Molloy, with her second best wig and "turbot" on her head; and just as we were going into supper in came Sidebotham. His eye was little more than sky-blue and yellow now, and a small slip of black plaister, instead of the bit of basilicon, as big as a turnpike-ticket, that was stuck across the bridge of his nose. He was not by any means so standoff with me as when I last met him, and seemed disposed to be conciliatory, and indeed he went the length of borrowing five pounds from me as we went away.

===Chinese===
"哎呀！您安静些，奥图尔，行不行？"这是她头一回唤我的姓，我心下那份欢喜，便是蒙迪来揪我的鼻子，我也能饶了他。"他说的是真的；他确是——每逢快要哭出来便要发笑。这事我自己也赶上过一回，那时我正从猪痘里将养好。您没瞧见他那副样子——我那可怜的巴尼叔叔（Uncle Barney）害着痨病要离开爱尔兰时，写了那几节美丽的诗，他把那诗题作《告别阿利巴利卡里克-奥杜利》（Farewell to Allyballycarick-O-Dooley）——那便是他那个地方的名字——那诗这世上几乎没谁能读了不哭的；可我向您发誓，我是陪他一阵接一阵地笑得直不起腰来的！话虽如此，"她略带严厉地收尾道，"我看，他在那阵子要发作时，倒不如把头扎进一只土豆锅里、再从窗户里探出去，也比用他那毛病冒犯人来得体面些。"

讨论便到此被归来的莫洛伊太太打断——她头上戴着那顶次好的假发与"大菱鲆"；我们正要入席吃夜宵时，赛德博瑟姆（Sidebotham）走了进来。他那只眼睛如今已褪成约莫天青色加黄色，鼻梁上贴着一条小小的黑膏药，取代了原先那张有收费站票据那么大的巴西利康软膏（basilicon）。他对我的态度，远不像我上回见他那般冷淡，倒像是愿意修好，果不其然，临走时他竟向我借去了五镑钱。

===Original===
I don't know how we bundled in to supper. I only know that I found myself beside Theodora. It was really an elegant supper. I remember it well, and I may as well tell you that old Molloy had a loin of roast pork before him; there was a big square of bacon, with greens, before Sidebotham—we were running, you see, a good deal on the pigs; before Mrs. Molloy, and as fat as herself, there was a grand roast goose, that came all the way from Connaught, and more fool it, considering all the good it got by the journey! And there was cow-heel and tripe, a dish that old Molloy fondly lost himself in, whenever he could get at it. There was enough cold-cannon to load a hod with; potatoes with and without the skins; there was a mountain of pancakes you might put a child to bed on; and such a good smell of stuffing, and onions, and gravy over all, that I declare to you I don't think the Prince Regent had a finer supper that night.

We were mortal hungry, and for a time conversation was a little dull; but I had the pleasure of hearing Theodora's beautiful voice every now and then, between the sounds of chumping, and munching, and gulping all round, calling on me for those little refined attentions that constitute, I may say, all the chivalry of the supper-table. Now it was:

"Mr. Toole, may I be troublesome to you for the gherkins?" And again—

"Another help o' the stuffin', ask mamma, Mr. Toole." Or—

"Show me the mustard, if you please?" Or—

"Will ye give me a dust of that pepper, Mr. Toole?"

I do assure you it was one delightful round of similar requests and attentions all through the suppertime, and as the glorious girl had a fine appetite, she worked me, in that way, to my heart's content.

===Chinese===
我们是怎么一窝蜂涌去吃夜宵的，我已记不真切。我只知道，一回头我已坐在西奥多拉身旁。那的确是极为丰盛的一席晚宴。我记得清清楚楚，不妨说与您听：老莫洛伊面前摆着一整条烤猪腰肉；赛德博瑟姆面前是一大块培根配青菜——您瞧，那一晚我们跟猪较上劲了；莫洛伊太太面前——肥美一如她本人——是一只肥大的烤鹅，一路从康诺特（Connaught）远道而来，可怜见它白跑这一趟，得了什么好处！此外还有牛蹄配牛肚，这道菜老莫洛伊一得机会便沉湎其中，乐而忘返。冷"炮弹果"多得能装满一砌匠的灰斗；带皮与去皮的土豆；一座小山似的薄煎饼，您大可把个孩子放上去安睡；再加一层 stuffing、洋葱与肉汁的浓香弥漫其上——我敢说，那晚便是摄政王（Prince Regent）亲临，也未必有更精致的夜宵。

我们饿得要命，一时间席间的谈话略见沉闷；不过我能时时听见西奥多拉那美妙的嗓音——在众人一片咀嚼、吞咽、牛饮之声的间隙里——把我召唤过去，做些小小的、文雅的伺候；这些伺候，我得说，构成了餐桌之上全部的骑士精神。这一会儿是：

"奥图尔先生，劳驾您把小酸黄瓜递给我行么？"过一会儿是——

"再给我一勺那酿馅，奥图尔先生，麻烦您问妈妈要。"或者——

"请您把芥末递一下？"或者——

"奥图尔先生，您给我撒一撮胡椒行么？"

我向您保证，整个夜宵席间，便是这一连串类此的请求与照应，绕成一圈令人愉悦的循环；这位光彩照人的姑娘胃口极好，这一路把我支使得心满意足。

===Original===
But this was only child's play compared with what followed, when the old lady called out: "Come, Molloy, where's the punch? What are you foosthering about? We're all choking with the drooth, and lookin' at ye like so many dying fishes out o' water. There's Mr. Upside—"

"Sidebotham," said the lieutenant.

"Upsidedownbotham—well, whatever it is, the young captain there, that we knew in Athlone, is makin' signs to me this half hour for drink. Come, man, stir. Juggy, good girl, bring the kittle; there's two bottle of the right sort at your elbow, and half a dozen elegant lemons. *Putt* down the bowl before him, Juggy, that's a darlint, and don't be sousing the wather in as if you were drownding so many rats. Do you know what, Mr. Upside, Mr. Downbotham, that's it; just look at that bowl—it houlds seven pints and about a wineglass; that's the very bowl Molloy was baptized in!" And she nodded impressively at Sidebotham, just as Molloy squeezed a lemon into the sacred vessel. "As sure as you sit there, Mr. Back—what your name?—no matter, I wish there was no such things as names, barrin' Christian names, of course, for the sake of religion; but what was I saying? Yes; he was baptized in that very bowl!"

===Chinese===
可这与后头来的一比，不过是小孩子过家家；老太太这时嚷了起来："喂，莫洛伊，潘趣酒呢？你磨磨蹭蹭的在干什么？我们个个渴得嗓子冒烟，眼巴巴望着你，活像一群离了水、干渴而死的鱼。这位倒立先生——"

"赛德博瑟姆（Sidebotham），"中尉纠正道。

"上下颠倒博瑟姆——也罢，随他叫什么吧，那边那位年轻的舰长，咱们在阿斯隆（Athlone）就认识的，冲我比画着想喝一口，都比画半个钟头啦。快着点儿，老爷们，动弹动弹。贾吉，好闺女，把水壶拎来；你手边有两瓶正经货，还有半打漂亮的柠檬。把酒钵*放*到他跟前，贾吉，乖闺女，别把水咕咚咕咚往里灌，倒像你在淹一窝耗子似的。您可知道，倒立先生，上下颠倒先生，就是这么个理儿；您就瞧那只钵——能装七品脱外加一杯；莫洛伊当年就是在这只钵里行的洗礼！"她对赛德博瑟姆煞有介事地点了点头，恰逢莫洛伊往那只圣器里挤了一只柠檬。"您坐着看得一清二楚，回头先生——您贵姓来着？——不打紧，我巴不得这世上没有姓名这种东西，当然啦，教名除外，那是为着宗教的缘故；可我刚说什么来着？对了；他就是在这只钵里受的洗礼！"

===Original===
"Not *ducked* in it?" says Sidebotham.

"No; but sprinkled out of it by the Reverend Father Haddock."

"He drank like a fish, I dare say, ma'am," said Sidebotham, who didn't care a fig what he said to anyone.

"I don't know, my dear, but he baptized like a Christian; and he met his death, most unfortunately, by being drownded in a bog-hole. He being a portly man, standing too near the edge, the bank gave way, and himself, and a child, and an ass and cart was all drownded together. I remember seeing him myself."

"Not in the bog-hole?" said the lieutenant.

"No, honey! It was in the high street of Athlone, when I was only a little slip of a colleen."

"We must drink to his memory, ma'am," said Sidebotham.

"With all my heart, joole," said Mrs. Molloy, who, barring a few political toasts, did not object to drink to anything.

By this time the punch, one of the few good things we unquestionably owe to England, was brewed; and infinite credit it did its "composer."

Our Philomel was the only one of the party who partook of that wonderful elixir with extreme moderation. That nightingale only touched it lightly, as it were, with her musical beak, once or twice, and, content with this little sip, listened to our agreeable conversation, our toasts, and sentiments, and to a great deal of fiery and confidential nonsense from your humble servant.

After this, I can recal nothing distinctly, except the general consciousness that I never was so happy in the course of my life; only I once or twice observed that Kramm, who sat at Theodora's other side, and did not seem to hear a word I said, kept interrupting the girl with his long-winded stories; and then I remember Sidebotham seeing me home, and talking to him a great deal about Theodora, and something very touching was said that affected me, for I remember crying while he held my hand, and I held the railings, and I lent him some money, and how I got to my bed I don't know.

---

[This amusing story, by the gifted author of *Uncle Silas* and *In a Glass Darkly*, was left at the time of the author's death unfinished as it is here, but the Editor ventures nevertheless to give it in this state to the readers of *Temple Bar*. Humour is not a product of this furiously earnest age, and we cannot afford to lose any contribution to our mirth which comes in our way.—**Editor.**]

===Chinese===
"不是*浸*进去的？"赛德博瑟姆说。

"不是浸的；是哈达克神父（Reverend Father Haddock）用钵里的水洒的。"

"我料他喝酒准像鱼一般，夫人，"赛德博瑟姆说——他这张嘴不论对谁都满不在乎。

"那我可不清楚，亲爱的，可他行洗礼是基督徒的派头；他后来结局很是不幸，淹死在一个泥炭坑里。他是个胖人，站得离坑边太近，坑沿一塌，他自己，外加一个孩子、一头驴、一辆车，一道全淹死了。他这个人，我是亲眼见过的。"

"不是在泥炭坑里见的吧？"中尉说。

"不是，心肝！是在阿斯隆的大街上，那时我还是个小丫头片子呢。"

"我们得为纪念他干一杯，夫人，"赛德博瑟姆说。

"满心乐意，心肝，"莫洛伊太太说——除开几个政治性的祝酒外，她向什么祝酒都不反对。

到这时，潘趣酒——这无可争议是我们得自英格兰的少数几桩好东西之一——已调制停当；调制它的"作曲家"理应享受无限荣光。

我们这群人里，唯有我们的菲洛梅尔（Philomel）——那位夜莺——浅尝辄止，节制得出奇。这只夜莺只用她那歌喉婉转的喙，轻轻啄了一两下便罢了，这一小口便已心满意足，转而倾听我们愉快的交谈、我们的祝酒与感兴，以及鄙人那一大堆火辣辣、推心置腹的胡言乱语。

这之后，我已记不真切，只依稀觉着这一生从未如此快活；不过我一两回留意到，坐在西奥多拉另一侧的克拉姆——他对我说的似乎一个字也听不进——却用他那冗长的故事一遍遍打断这位姑娘；再后来，我记得是赛德博瑟姆送我回家，我跟他絮絮叨叨谈了好一阵西奥多拉，他说了一句什么极为动人的话，把我触动了——因为我记得我哭了起来，他握着我的手，我抓着栏杆，我又借了点钱给他，至于我怎么上的床，那就不得而知了。

---

[这则趣闻，出自《西拉斯叔叔》（Uncle Silas）与《暗影之镜》（In a Glass Darkly）那位才华横溢的作者之手，于作者逝世之际，便如这般未及完稿而搁下，然编者仍冒昧以此种面貌，奉之于《殿厦杂志》（Temple Bar）的读者。幽默，本非这个浮躁而较真的时代所能产出的东西，凡是落到我们手上的、能博人一笑的文稿，我们都舍不得遗失。——**编者**。]

## Laura Silver Bell / 劳拉·银铃

===Original===
In the five Northumbrian counties you will scarcely find so bleak, ugly, and yet, in a savage way, so picturesque a moor as Dardale Moss. The moor itself spreads north, south, east, and west, a great undulating sea of black peat and heath.
What we may term its shores are wooded wildly with birch, hazel, and dwarf-oak. No towering mountains surround it, but here and there you have a rocky knoll rising among the trees, and many a wooded promontory of the same pretty, because utterly wild, forest, running out into its dark level.
Habitations are thinly scattered in this barren territory, and a full mile away from the meanest was the stone cottage of Mother Carke.

===Chinese===
在诺森伯兰那五个郡里，你只怕再难找到一片如此荒凉、如此丑陋，却又带着几分蛮荒的如画意味的荒野——达德尔沼（Dardale Moss）。这沼地本身向北、南、东、西四面铺展，如同一片起伏不定的茫茫黑海，尽是泥炭与石楠。
我们姑且称之为它的"岸"的地方，杂乱地长着桦树、榛树与矮橡。四周并无巍峨群山环抱，只是林木之间这里那里隆起几座石丘，又有同样的森林——因了十足的荒蛮反添了几分可爱——伸出一道道林木葱茏的岬角，探入它那阴沉的平地之上。
这一带穷乡僻壤，人烟稀疏，居所寥落；而距那最寒伧的一处茅屋也足有一英里之遥的，便是卡克老妈（Mother Carke）的石屋。

===Original===
Let not my southern reader who associates ideas of comfort with the term "cottage" mistake. This thing is built of shingle, with low walls. Its thatch is hollow; the peat-smoke curls stingily from its stunted chimney. It is worthy of its savage surroundings.
The primitive neighbours remark that no rowan-tree grows near, nor holly, nor bracken, and no horseshoe is nailed on the door.
Not far from the birches and hazels that straggle about the rude wall of the little enclosure, on the contrary, they say, you may discover the broom and the ragwort, in which witches mysteriously delight. But this is perhaps a scandal.

===Chinese===
请我那南方的读者莫要见"茅屋"二字便联想到什么舒适安逸，因而生出误会。这物件是用木瓦搭成的，墙矮矮的。屋顶的草茬塌陷下去；泥炭的青烟吝啬地从那矮小的烟囱里袅袅升起。它与它那蛮荒的周遭倒正相宜。
那些淳朴的邻里都说，近处既不长花楸，也没有冬青，没有蕨丛，门上更没有钉着马蹄铁。
倒是那小院粗陋的墙边东倒西歪的桦树与榛树近旁，他们说道，你能寻见金雀花与千里光——正是巫婆们神秘所好的那两种草。不过这或许是诋毁之辞。

===Original===
Mall Carke was for many a year the *sage femme* of this wild domain. She has renounced practice, however, for some years; and now, under the rose, she dabbles, it is thought, in the black art, in which she has always been secretly skilled, tells fortunes, practises charms, and in popular esteem is little better than a witch.
Mother Carke has been away to the town of Willarden, to sell knit stockings, and is returning to her rude dwelling by Dardale Moss. To her right, as far away as the eye can reach, the moor stretches. The narrow track she has followed here tops a gentle upland, and at her left a sort of jungle of dwarf-oak and brushwood approaches its edge. The sun is sinking bloodred in the west. His disk has touched the broad black level of the moor, and his parting beams glare athwart the gaunt figure of the old beldame, as she strides homeward stick in hand, and bring into relief the folds of her mantle, which gleam like the draperies of a bronze image in the light of a fire. For a few moments this light floods the air—tree, gorse, rock, and bracken glare; and then it is out, and gray twilight over everything.

===Chinese===
马尔·卡克（Mall Carke）多年来一直是这一片蛮荒之地的接生婆（sage femme）。不过她已歇业数年；如今私下里——人们暗中传说——摆弄起黑巫术来，这一样本事她向来精通，又替人算命、行那驱神役鬼的小术，在乡人眼里，她与一个巫婆也相差无几了。
卡克老妈进城到了威拉登（Willarden），卖了几双自织的袜子，正折返她那在达德尔沼边的粗陋住处。她的右手边，极目所及，尽是那片沼地。她一路沿来的那条窄径爬上了一道平缓的高地，她的左手边，一片矮橡与灌木交织而成的丛林逼近路边。血红的夕阳正向西沉。日轮已触到沼地那广漠漆黑的平地，它临终的余晖斜斜地照在这干瘦老妪嶙峋的身影上——她正手执木棍大步朝家走去——又勾勒出她斗篷上那一道道褶皱，那褶皱在火光般的光里熠熠生辉，宛如一尊铜像上的衣纹。这光华在片刻之间漫天漫地——树木、荆豆、岩石、蕨丛，无不灿然生光；旋即便熄灭了，灰蒙蒙的暮色笼罩了一切。

===Original===
All is still and sombre. At this hour the simple traffic of the thinly-peopled country is over, and nothing can be more solitary.
From this jungle, nevertheless, through which the mists of evening are already creeping, she sees a gigantic man approaching her.
In that poor and primitive country robbery is a crime unknown. She, therefore, has no fears for her pound of tea, and pint of gin, and sixteen shillings in silver which she is bringing home in her pocket. But there is something that would have frighted another woman about this man.

===Chinese===
四下里一片死寂，一片阴沉。这个时辰，那人烟稀疏的乡野间那点微薄的来往行人也已绝迹，再没有比这更孤寂的了。
然而就在那片丛林里——暮霭已开始在其中悄然弥漫——她望见一个身形高大的男人正朝她走来。
在这贫苦淳朴的乡间，劫掠之事闻所未闻。因此她并不为口袋里拎回家的那一磅茶叶、一品脱杜松子酒和十六先令银洋担心。可这男人身上有某种气息，足以骇倒别的女人。

===Original===
He is gaunt, sombre, bony, dirty, and dressed in a black suit which a beggar would hardly care to pick out of the dust.
This ill-looking man nodded to her as he stepped on the road.
"I don't know you," she said.
He nodded again.
"I never sid ye neyawheere," she exclaimed sternly.
"Fine evening, Mother Carke," he says, and holds his snuffbox toward her.
She widened the distance between them by a step or so, and said again sternly and pale,
"I hev nowt to say to thee, whoe'er thou beest."

===Chinese===
他形容干瘦、阴沉、嶙峋，满身污垢，穿一身黑衣裳，便是叫花子怕也懒得从尘土里捡它出来。
这面相不善的男人踏上小路时，朝她点了点头。
"我不认得你，"她说。
他又点了点头。
"我从来没在哪旮旯见过你，"她厉声道。
"晚上好啊，卡克老妈，"他说着，把他的鼻烟盒朝她递了过来。
她又往后退了一两步，拉开两人之间的距离，脸色发白地再次厉声道：
"你是何方神圣，我跟你没话可讲。"

===Original===
"You know Laura Silver Bell?"
"That's a byneyam; the lass's neyam is Laura Lew," she answered, looking straight before her.
"One name's as good as another for one that was never christened, mother."
"How know ye that?" she asked grimly; for it is a received opinion in that part of the world that the fairies have power over those who have never been baptised.
The stranger turned on her a malignant smile.
"There is a young lord in love with her," the stranger says, "and I'm that lord. Have her at your house tomorrow night at eight o'clock, and you must stick cross pins through the candle, as you have done for many a one before, to bring her lover thither by ten, and her fortune's made. And take this for your trouble."

===Chinese===
"你认得劳拉·银铃（Laura Silver Bell）吧？"
"那是个诨名；这姑娘的名字是劳拉·卢（Laura Lew），"她答道，目光直视前方。
"对于一个从未受洗的孩子来说，叫什么名字还不都一样，老妈妈。"
"你怎么知道这事的？"她阴沉地问；因为那一带的人都信，凡是没受过洗礼的人，仙灵（fairies）便能在其身上施威。
陌生人朝她露出一丝恶意的微笑。
"有位年轻的贵族爱上了她，"陌生人说，"我便是那位贵族。明晚八点，你把她带到你家里，你得拿针十字交叉地插进蜡烛里——你从前为许多人做过这事——好让她的情郎十点钟寻到她跟前，她的终身便有指望了。这点儿东西，是酬谢你的。"

===Original===
He extended his long finger and thumb toward her, with a guinea temptingly displayed.
"I have nowt to do wi' thee. I nivver sid thee afoore. Git thee awa'! I earned nea goold o' thee, and I'll tak' nane. Awa' wi' thee, or I'll find ane that will mak' thee!"
The old woman had stopped, and was quivering in every limb as she thus spoke.
He looked very angry. Sulkily he turned away at her words, and strode slowly toward the wood from which he had come; and as he approached it, he seemed to her to grow taller and taller, and stalked into it as high as a tree.

===Chinese===
他把那长长的拇指与食指伸向她，指间诱人地夹着一枚亮闪闪的几尼金币。
"我跟你没瓜葛。我从来没见过你。给我滚！你的金子我一文也没赚过，一文也不收。趁早滚开，要不我就找个人来收拾你！"
老妇人停下脚步，说话间浑身每一个关节都在打颤。
他面有怒色。听了这话，他闷闷地转身，朝他出来的那片林子大步踱去；他越走越近林子，她眼里竟觉他越走越高，待跨进林中时，已高得像一棵树一般了。

===Original===
"I conceited there would come something o't," she said to herself. "Farmer Lew must git it done nesht Sunda'. The a'ad awpy!"
Old Farmer Lew was one of that sect who insist that baptism shall be but once administered, and not until the Christian candidate had attained to adult years. The girl had indeed for some time been of an age not only, according to this theory, to be baptised, but if need be to be married.

===Chinese===
"我就料着迟早要出点事的，"她自语道，"卢老汉下个礼拜天可得把这事办了。这老糊涂！"
老汉卢农夫（Farmer Lew）属于那一派教徒，他们坚持洗礼只可行一次，且非等到信徒长大成人不可。这姑娘的年纪，按这派的说法，其实早已不只该受洗，便是嫁人也使得了。

===Original===
Her story was a sad little romance. A lady some seventeen years before had come down and paid Farmer Lew for two rooms in his house. She told him that her husband would follow her in a fortnight, and that he was in the meantime delayed by business in Liverpool.
In ten days after her arrival her baby was born, Mall Carke acting as *sage femme* on the occasion; and on the evening of that day the poor young mother died. No husband came; no wedding-ring, they said, was on her finger. About fifty pounds was found in her desk, which Farmer Lew, who was a kind old fellow and had lost his two children, put in bank for the little girl, and resolved to keep her until a rightful owner should step forward to claim her.

===Chinese===
她的身世是一段凄清的小小传奇。约莫十七年前，一位女士来到此地，向卢农夫租下他宅子里两间屋子，付了租金。她对他说，她的丈夫半个月后就到，眼下因在利物浦（Liverpool）有事务缠身，一时脱不开身。
她来到此地十日之后，便生下了孩子，马尔·卡克这回便做了接生婆；就在当天傍晚，可怜的年轻母亲便死去了。丈夫不曾来；据说她指上也没有婚戒。她的书桌里寻出约莫五十镑钱，卢农夫是个心慈的老汉，自己又夭折过两个孩子，便把这笔钱存进银行，留与这小女孩，又打定主意抚养她，直到有一天合法的亲人前来认领。

===Original===
They found half-a-dozen love-letters signed "Francis," and calling the dead woman "Laura."
So Farmer Lew called the little girl Laura; and her sobriquet of "Silver Bell" was derived from a tiny silver bell, once gilt, which was found among her poor mother's little treasures after her death, and which the child wore on a ribbon round her neck.
Thus, being very pretty and merry, she grew up as a North-country farmer's daughter; and the old man, as she needed more looking after, grew older and less able to take care of her; so she was, in fact, very nearly her own mistress, and did pretty much in all things as she liked.
Old Mall Carke, by some caprice for which no one could account, cherished an affection for the girl, who saw her often, and paid her many a small fee in exchange for the secret indications of the future.

===Chinese===
他们又寻出半打情书，落款"弗朗西斯"（Francis），称那已死的女子为"劳拉"。
于是卢农夫便唤那小女孩作劳拉；她的诨名"银铃"，则得自一枚小小的银铃铛——铃上原还镀过金——是她那可怜母亲死后，在她那一点点值钱的细软之中寻出来的，孩子用一根缎带穿着，挂在脖子上。
就这样，她出落得又俊俏又活泼，在这北方农家老汉的膝下长大；老汉一天天老去，越是需要有人照看她、却越加照看不过来；于是她几乎等于是自己做自己的主，凡事差不多都随心所欲。
老马尔·卡克，也不知出于哪一桩谁都说不清的怪脾气，竟疼爱起这姑娘来；姑娘也时常去看她，奉上些微薄的酬金，换取她对自己将来的种种隐秘指点。

===Original===
It was too late when Mother Carke reached her home to look for a visit from Laura Silver Bell that day.
About three o'clock next afternoon, Mother Carke was sitting knitting, with her glasses on, outside her door on the stone bench, when she saw the pretty girl mount lightly to the top of the stile at her left under the birch, against the silver stem of which she leaned her slender hand, and called,
"Mall, Mall! Mother Carke, are ye alane all by yersel'?"
"Ay, Laura lass, we can be clooas enoo, if ye want a word wi' me," says the old woman, rising, with a mysterious nod, and beckoning her stiffly with her long fingers.

===Chinese===
卡克老妈到家时天色已晚，那日不必再指望劳拉·银铃前来了。
次日下午三点钟光景，卡克老妈戴着老花眼镜，坐在门外石凳上织东西，只见那俊俏的姑娘轻巧地攀上她左手边那棵桦树下的踏阶顶上，把纤细的手搭在那银白的树干上，喊道：
"马尔，马尔！卡克老妈，你一个人在家吗？"
"是啊，劳拉姑娘，咱们关起门来说话不怕人听，你要有话跟我讲，"老妇人说罢，神神秘秘地点了点头，僵硬地用她那长手指招她过去。

===Original===
The girl was, assuredly, pretty enough for a "lord" to fall in love with. Only look at her. A profusion of brown rippling hair, parted low in the middle of her forehead, almost touched her eyebrows, and made the pretty oval of her face, by the breadth of that rich line, more marked. What a pretty little nose! what scarlet lips, and large, dark, long-fringed eyes!
Her face is transparently tinged with those clear Murillo tints which appear in deeper dyes on her wrists and the backs of her hands. These are the beautiful gipsy-tints with which the sun dyes young skins so richly.
The old woman eyes all this, and her pretty figure, so round and slender, and her shapely little feet, cased in the thick shoes that can't hide their comely proportions, as she stands on the top of the stile. But it is with a dark and saturnine aspect.

===Chinese===
这姑娘，说实在的，俊俏得叫一位"贵族"堕入情网也实在难怪。你且看她。一头浓密的棕色鬈发，在前额正中低低地分开，几乎垂到了眉毛，那浓密的一道发线愈发衬出她那可爱的鹅蛋脸来。多秀气的小鼻子！多鲜红的嘴唇，多乌亮、长睫翦水的大眼睛！
她的脸庞透着一层明净的色调，那是穆里略（Murillo）画中人才有的肤色，到了她的手腕和手背上便染得更深。这便是那美丽的吉卜赛式的肤色，是太阳把年轻的肌肤染得如此丰润。
老妇人把这一切——连同她那又圆润又纤细的身段、那双小巧有致的脚，虽裹在厚笨的鞋里也遮不住那秀美的轮廓——都看在眼里，这时她正立在踏阶顶上。然而老妇人看她的神情却是阴沉而冷峻的。

===Original===
"Come, lass, what stand ye for atoppa t' wall, whar folk may chance to see thee? I hev a thing to tell thee, lass."
She beckoned her again.
"An' I hev a thing to tell *thee*, Mall."
"Come hidder," said the old woman peremptorily.
"But ye munna gie me the creepin's" (make me tremble). "I winna look again into the glass o' water, mind ye."
The old woman smiled grimly, and changed her tone.
"Now, hunny, git tha down, and let ma see thy canny feyace," and she beckoned her again.
Laura Silver Bell did get down, and stepped lightly toward the door of the old woman's dwelling.

===Chinese===
"哎，姑娘，你站在墙头干啥，叫过路的人撞见可怎么好？我有桩事要告诉你，姑娘。"
她又招了招手。
"我也有桩事要告诉*你*呢，马尔。"
"过来，"老妇人不容分说道。
"可你不许叫我心里发毛（让我打哆嗦）。我再也不朝那碗水里头瞧了，你记着。"
老妇人冷冷一笑，换了语气。
"好啦，乖孩子，快下来，让我瞧瞧你那张俊脸蛋，"她又招手道。
劳拉·银铃果真下了踏阶，轻巧地朝老妇人的屋门走去。

===Original===
"Tak this," said the girl, unfolding a piece of bacon from her apron, "and I hev a silver sixpence to gie thee, when I'm gaen away heyam."
They entered the dark kitchen of the cottage, and the old woman stood by the door, lest their conference should be lighted on by surprise.
"Afoore ye begin," said Mother Carke (I soften her patois), "I mun tell ye there's ill folk watchin' ye. What's auld Farmer Lew about, he doesna get t' sir" (the clergyman) "to baptise thee? If he lets Sunda' next pass, I'm afeared ye'll never be sprinkled nor signed wi' cross, while there's a sky aboon us."

===Chinese===
"拿着，"姑娘说着，从围裙里取出一块咸肉来，"等我回家时，还有一枚六便士的银币给你。"
她俩走进那石屋黑魆魆的灶间，老妇人挨门站着，以防有人撞见她们的密谈。
"你开口之前，"卡克老妈说道（她那乡音土话我这里略加润色），"我得告诉你，有歹人正盯着你。卢老汉是怎么回事，怎么不叫那先生（指牧师）给你施洗？要是他错过下个礼拜天，我恐怕只要这天还罩在咱们头顶上，你便再也受不着那点水、画十字的恩典了。"

===Original===
"Agoy!" exclaims the girl, "who's lookin' after me?"
"A big black fella, as high as the kipples, came out o' the wood near Deadman's Grike, just after the sun gaed down yester e'en; I knew weel what he was, for his feet ne'er touched the road while he made as if he walked beside me. And he wanted to gie me snuff first, and I wouldna hev that; and then he offered me a gowden guinea, but I was no sic awpy, and to bring you here tonight, and cross the candle wi' pins, to call your lover in. And he said he's a great lord, and in luve wi' thee."

===Chinese===
"哎呀！"姑娘失声道，"谁盯着我？"
"一个黑大个儿，个头高到房梁那儿，昨儿傍晚太阳落山之后，从死人隘（Deadman's Grike）边上的林子里走了出来；我心里清楚他是个什么东西，因为他装作在我身旁走着，脚却根本没沾着地。他先要给我闻鼻烟，我没依他；后来又拿一枚金几尼给我，我可没那么傻；他要我今儿晚上把你带过来，拿针插过蜡烛，把你的情郎招来。他说他是一位大贵族，爱上了你。"

===Original===
"And you refused him?"
"Well for thee I did, lass," says Mother Carke.
"Why, it's every word true!" cries the girl vehemently, starting to her feet, for she had seated herself on the great oak chest.
"True, lass? Come, say what ye mean," demanded Mall Carke, with a dark and searching gaze.
"Last night I was coming heyam from the wake, wi' auld farmer Dykes and his wife and his daughter Nell, and when we came to the stile, I bid them good night, and we parted."

===Chinese===
"你回绝了他？"
"幸亏我回绝了，姑娘，"卡克老妈说。
"嘿，他说的字字句句都是真的！"姑娘霍地站起身来嚷道——她方才坐在那只大橡木箱上。
"真的，姑娘？来，你说清楚是怎么回事，"马尔·卡克目光阴沉、逼视着她。
"昨儿夜里我从守灵那家往家走，同路的有老戴克斯农夫（farmer Dykes）和他老伴、还有他女儿内尔（Nell），到了那踏阶跟前，我同他们道了晚安，便分了手。"

===Original===
"And ye came by the path alone in the nighttime, did ye?" exclaimed old Mall Carke sternly.
"I wasna afeared, I don't know why; the path heyam leads down by the wa'as o' auld Hawarth Castle."
"I knaa it weel, and a dowly path it is; ye'll keep indoors o' nights for a while, or ye'll rue it. What saw ye?"
"No freetin, mother; nowt I was feared on."
"Ye heard a voice callin' yer neyame?"
"I heard nowt that was dow, but the hullyhoo in the auld castle wa's," answered the pretty girl. "I heard nor sid nowt that's dow, but mickle that's conny and gladsome. I heard singin' and laughin' a long way off, I consaited; and I stopped a bit to listen. Then I walked on a step or two, and there, sure enough, in the Pie-Mag field, under the castle wa's, not twenty steps away, I sid a grand company; silks and satins, and men wi' velvet coats, wi' gowd-lace striped over them, and ladies wi' necklaces that would dazzle ye, and fans as big as griddles; and powdered footmen, like what the shirra hed behind his coach, only these was ten times as grand."

===Chinese===
"你便一个人摸黑走那条小路回家，是吗？"老马尔·卡克厉声道。
"我也不知怎的，并不害怕；回家的那条小路，是从老霍沃思城堡（Hawarth Castle）的城垣旁边经过的。"
"那路我熟悉得很，那条道阴森森的；这些日子你夜里可得乖乖待在屋里，不然要懊悔的。你看见了什么？"
"别吓唬人，老妈；没什么叫我害怕的。"
"你可听见有人唤你的名字？"
"我尽听见些不阴森的东西，除了老城垣里那阵呜呜的风声，"俊俏的姑娘答道，"我既没听见、也没看见什么阴森的东西，倒瞧见、听见不少又俊俏又热闹的。我恍惚听见远处又唱又笑，便停了一会儿听着。后来我又往前走了两步，果不其然，就在城堡墙底下那块喜鹊地（Pie-Mag field）里，不出二十步远，我瞧见了一群气派非凡的人：绫罗绸缎，男人们穿着金线滚边的天鹅绒外套，贵妇们戴着晃得人睁不开眼的项链，扇子大得像烙饼的平底锅；还有扑粉的男仆，跟在治安官马车后头的那种一样，只是这些还要气派十倍。"

===Original===
"It was full moon last night," said the old woman.
"Sa bright 'twould blind ye to look at it," said the girl.
"Never an ill sight but the deaul finds a light," quoth the old woman. "There's a rinnin brook thar—you were at this side, and they at that; did they try to mak ye cross over?"
"Agoy! didn't they? Nowt but civility and kindness, though. But ye mun let me tell it my own way. They was talkin' and laughin', and eatin', and drinkin' out o' long glasses and goud cups, seated on the grass, and music was playin'; and I keekin' behind a bush at all the grand doin's; and up they gits to dance; and says a tall fella I didna see afoore, 'Ye mun step across, and dance wi' a young lord that's faan in luv wi' thee, and that's mysel',' and sure enow I keeked at him under my lashes and a conny lad he is, to my teyaste, though he be dressed in black, wi' sword and sash, velvet twice as fine as they sells in the shop at Gouden Friars; and keekin' at me again fra the corners o' his een. And the same fella telt me he was mad in luv wi' me, and his fadder was there, and his sister, and they came all the way from Catstean Castle to see me that night; and that's t' other side o' Gouden Friars."

===Chinese===
"昨儿夜里是满月，"老妇人说。
"月亮亮得能叫人直眼瞎呢，"姑娘说。
"凡是这种祸祟之兆，魔鬼总能给照得通明，"老妇人道，"那儿有一条小溪——你在这岸，他们在那岸；他们可曾叫你过去？"
"哎呀！怎么没有？不过尽是些客气殷勤的话。可你可得容我照着自己的讲法讲。他们又说又笑，吃着喝着，从高脚杯和金盏里喝酒，坐在草地上，还有奏乐的；我躲在一丛灌木后头偷看这热闹场面；后来他们站起来跳舞；有一个我先前没瞧见的高个子说：'你得过来，跟一个爱上你的年轻贵族跳个舞，那人就是我。'可不嘛，我从睫毛底下偷偷瞧他，倒正合我的意，是个俊后生，虽说一身黑衣裳，带着剑、佩着绶带，那天鹅绒比金衣修士（Gouden Friars）铺子里卖的还要精致一倍；他也从眼角里偷瞧我。那同一个家伙对我说，他为我神魂颠倒，他爹也在，他妹妹也在，他们从猫石城堡（Catstean Castle）大老远赶来，就为那夜来看我；那地方在金衣修士的那一头。"

===Original===
"Come, lass, yer no mafflin; tell me true. What was he like? Was his feyace grimed wi' sut? a tall fella wi' wide shouthers, and lukt like an ill-thing, wi' black clothes amaist in rags?"
"His feyace was long, but weel-faured, and darker nor a gipsy; and his clothes were black and grand, and made o' velvet, and he said he was the young lord himsel'; and he lukt like it."
"That will be the same fella I sid at Deadman's Grike," said Mall Carke, with an anxious frown.
"Hoot, mudder! how cud that be?" cried the lass, with a toss of her pretty head and a smile of scorn. But the fortune teller made no answer, and the girl went on with her story.

===Chinese===
"得了，姑娘，你别胡扯；跟我说实话。他长什么样？脸上是不是抹了锅灰？是不是个宽肩膀的高个子，一副恶物的模样，黑衣裳破得快成碎布条了？"
"他脸是长脸，可长得俊，比吉卜赛人还要黑些；他衣裳是黑的，气派得很，是天鹅绒的，他说他自己就是那位年轻贵族；看他那模样倒也像。"
"那想必就是我在死人隘见到的那个家伙了，"马尔·卡克皱着眉头、忧心忡忡地说。
"啐，老妈！哪能呢？"姑娘嚷道，把她那好看的脑袋一甩，鄙夷地一笑。可这算命的女人并不答话，姑娘便继续讲她的故事。

===Original===
"When they began to dance," continued Laura Silver Bell, "he urged me again, but I wudna step o'er; 'twas partly pride, coz I wasna dressed fine enough, and partly contrairiness, or something, but gaa I wudna, not a fut. No but I more nor half wished it a' the time."
"Weel for thee thou dudstna cross the brook."
"Hoity-toity, why not?"
"Keep at heyame after nightfall, and don't ye be walking by yersel' by daylight or any light lang lonesome ways, till after ye're baptised," said Mall Carke.
"I'm like to be married first."
"Tak care *that* marriage won't hang i' the bell-ropes," said Mother Carke.

===Chinese===
"他们开始跳舞的时候，"劳拉·银铃接着说，"他又催我，可我不过去；一半是自尊心，嫌自己穿得不够体面；一半是拗劲儿，也不知是什么别的，反正我偏不过去，半步也不肯。只是我心里头大半时候巴不得过去的。"
"你没过那条溪，真是你的造化。"
"哎哟哟，为什么不能过？"
"天黑之后就乖乖待在家里，受洗之前，无论白天还是别的什么时辰，那种又长又冷清的路，你可千万别一个人走，"马尔·卡克说。
"我怕是先得嫁人呢。"
"那门亲事，可别像吊钟绳一样悬着办不成，小心着，"卡克老妈说。

===Original===
"Leave me alane for that. The young lord said he was maist daft wi' luv o' me. He wanted to gie me a conny ring wi' a beautiful stone in it. But, drat it, I was sic an awpy I wudna tak it, and he a young lord!"
"Lord, indeed! are ye daft or dreamin'? Those fine folk, what were they? I'll tell ye. Dobies and fairies; and if ye don't du as yer bid, they'll tak ye, and ye'll never git out o' their hands again while grass grows," said the old woman grimly.
"Od wite it!" replies the girl impatiently, "who's daft or dreamin' noo? I'd a bin dead wi' fear, if 'twas any such thing. It cudna be; all was sa luvesome, and bonny, and shaply."
"Weel, and what do ye want o' me, lass?" asked the old woman sharply.

===Chinese===
"这事不用你操心。那位年轻贵族说他为我差点疯了。他要给我一枚好看的戒指，上头镶着一块漂亮的宝石。可是，见鬼，我这傻丫头竟不肯收，人家可是位年轻贵族呢！"
"贵族，呸！你是疯了还是做梦？那些个阔人，他们是些什么东西？我告诉你。是妖尸和仙灵（fairies）；你要是不听话，他们就把你抓了去，只要这世上还长青草，你就再也别想从他们手里脱身，"老妇人阴沉地说。
"老天哪！"姑娘不耐烦地答道，"现在到底是谁疯了、是谁在做梦？要是真有这么回事，我早就活活吓死了。那怎么可能；一切都是那么讨人喜欢，那么漂亮，那么齐整。"
"那么，姑娘，你找我做什么？"老妇人尖刻地问。

===Original===
"I want to know—here's t' sixpence—what I sud du," said the young lass. " 'Twud be a pity to lose such a marrow, hey?"
"Say yer prayers, lass; *I* can't help ye," says the old woman darkly. "If ye gaa wi' *the* people, ye'll never come back. Ye munna talk wi' them, nor eat wi' them, nor drink wi' them, nor tak a pin's-worth by way o' gift fra them—mark weel what I say—or ye're *lost*!"
The girl looked down, plainly much vexed.
The old woman stared at her with a mysterious frown steadily, for a few seconds.
"Tell me, lass, and tell me true, are ye in luve wi' that lad?"

===Chinese===
"我想知道——这便是那六便士——我该怎么办，"少女说，"失了这样一位佳偶，岂不可惜？"
"姑娘，祷告吧；这事我帮不了你，"老妇人阴郁地说，"你要是跟了那伙人（the people），就再也回不来了。你不能跟他们搭话，不能跟他们同吃，不能跟他们同喝，不能收他们一根针的礼物——把我的话记牢——否则你就*毁了*！"
姑娘低下头，分明是十分懊恼。
老妇人眉头微蹙、神秘地盯着她，一动不动地盯了几秒钟。
"告诉我，姑娘，跟我说实话，你是不是爱上了那个小子？"

===Original===
"What for sud I?" said the girl with a careless toss of her head, and blushing up to her very temples.
"I see how it is," said the old woman, with a groan, and repeated the words, sadly thinking; and walked out of the door a step or two, and looked jealously round. "The lass is witched, the lass is witched!"
"Did ye see him since?" asked Mother Carke, returning.
The girl was still embarrassed; and now she spoke in a lower tone, and seemed subdued.
"I thought I sid him as I came here, walkin' beside me among the trees; but I consait it was only the trees themsels that lukt like rinnin' one behind another, as I walked on."

===Chinese===
"我凭什么要呢？"姑娘说，漫不经心地把头一甩，脸却一直红到了太阳穴。
"我明白了，"老妇人叹了一口气，悲哀地反复念着这话；她走出屋门一两步，疑神疑鬼地四下张望，"这姑娘中了邪了，这姑娘中了邪了！"
"打那以后你可曾再见过他？"卡克老妈折回身来问。
姑娘仍有些局促；这时她说话的声音低了些，也像被镇住了似的。
"我上这儿来的时候，恍惚看见他在树丛里走在我身旁；不过我想那只不过是那些树本身，我一路走，看上去像一棵挨一棵往后跑似的。"

===Original===
"I can tell thee nowt, lass, but what I telt ye afoore," answered the old woman peremptorily. "Get ye heyame, and don't delay on the way; and say yer prayers as ye gaa; and let none but good thoughts come nigh ye; and put nayer foot autside the door-steyan again till ye gaa to be christened; and get that done a Sunda' next."
And with this charge, given with grizzly earnestness, she saw her over the stile, and stood upon it watching her retreat, until the trees quite hid her and her path from view.
The sky grew cloudy and thunderous, and the air darkened rapidly, as the girl, a little frightened by Mall Carke's view of the case, walked homeward by the lonely path among the trees.

===Chinese===
"我没什么可告诉你了，姑娘，除了我先前说过的那些，"老妇人斩钉截铁地答道，"回家去吧，路上别耽搁；一路走一路祷告；只让好的念头近你的身；在受洗之前，再也不要把脚迈出你家门槛一步；这事下个礼拜天就得办了。"
她这般阴沉而郑重地嘱咐了一番，便送她过了踏阶，自己站在踏阶上望着她远去的背影，直到林木完全遮没了姑娘和她的去路。
天色变得阴云密布、雷声隐隐，空气迅速暗了下来；姑娘被马尔·卡克那番话吓得有些发慌，沿着林中那条孤零零的小路往家走去。

===Original===
A black cat, which had walked close by her—for these creatures sometimes take a ramble in search of their prey among the woods and thickets—crept from under the hollow of an oak, and was again with her. It seemed to her to grow bigger and bigger as the darkness deepened, and its green eyes glared as large as halfpennies in her affrighted vision as the thunder came booming along the heights from the Willarden-road.
She tried to drive it away; but it growled and hissed awfully, and set up its back as if it would spring at her, and finally it skipped up into a tree, where they grew thickest at each side of her path, and accompanied her, high over head, hopping from bough to bough as if meditating a pounce upon her shoulders. Her fancy being full of strange thoughts, she was frightened, and she fancied that it was haunting her steps, and destined to undergo some hideous transformation, the moment she ceased to guard her path with prayers.
She was frightened for a while after she got home. The dark looks of Mother Carke were always before her eyes, and a secret dread prevented her passing the threshold of her home again that night.

===Chinese===
一只黑猫——这种畜生有时也会溜到林中灌木丛里觅食——原本就紧跟在她身旁，这时从一棵老橡树的树洞底下钻了出来，又缠上了她。天色越暗，她眼里那猫竟越变越大，等到雷声顺着高地从威拉登那条路那头隆隆滚来时，它那双绿眼睛在她惊惶的目光里瞪得像两枚半便士铜板那么大。
她想把它赶走；可它发出吓人的低吼和嘶声，弓起背像是就要朝她扑过来，末了一纵身蹿上树去——路两旁的树木在这儿长得最密——便在她头顶上跟着她，从这根树枝跳到那根树枝，像是在盘算着朝她肩膀上猛扑。她满脑子古怪念头，吓得要命，便觉得这猫是一路缠着她，只等她一停了用祷告护身，便要化作某种狰狞可怖的东西。
她到家之后，那一阵子心里仍怕得很。卡克老妈那阴沉的脸色老是在她眼前晃，一种说不出的恐惧使她那一夜再也没敢迈过自家门槛半步。

===Original===
Next day it was different. She had got rid of the awe with which Mother Carke had inspired her. She could not get the tall dark-featured lord, in the black velvet dress, out of her head. He had "taken her fancy"; she was growing to love him. She could think of nothing else.
Bessie Hennock, a neighbour's daughter, came to see her that day, and proposed a walk toward the ruins of Hawarth Castle, to gather "blaebirries." So off the two girls went together.
In the thicket, along the slopes near the ivied walls of Hawarth Castle, the companions began to fill their baskets. Hours passed. The sun was sinking near the west, and Laura Silver Bell had not come home.

===Chinese===
到了第二天便不同了。卡克老妈灌进她心里的那点惧意已经烟消云散。可她再也忘不掉那个高个子、黑面庞、穿一身黑天鹅绒的贵族了。他"勾了她的魂"；她渐渐地爱上了他。她满脑子再想不出别的。
那天，邻家女儿贝西·亨诺克（Bessie Hennock）来看她，提议一同到霍沃思城堡的废墟一带去摘"越橘"。于是两个姑娘便一同出发了。
在霍沃思城堡爬满常春藤的城墙附近的山坡灌木丛里，这一对伙伴动手摘起来，把篮子一点点装满。几个钟头过去了。太阳快要在西边落下了，劳拉·银铃还没回家。

===Original===
Over the hatch of the farmhouse door the maids leant ever and anon with outstretched necks, watching for a sign of the girl's return, and wondering, as the shadows lengthened, what had become of her.
At last, just as the rosy sunset gilding began to overspread the landscape, Bessie Hennock, weeping into her apron, made her appearance without her companion.
Her account of their adventures was curious.
I will relate the substance of it more connectedly than her agitation would allow her to give it, and without the disguise of the rude Northumbrian dialect.

===Chinese===
农舍门口的半截门扉上，女仆们一次又一次伸长脖子探望，盼着姑娘回来的影子，眼看日影越拖越长，都纳闷她究竟去了哪里。
末了，就在那玫瑰色的夕照开始给大地镀上一层金的时候，贝西·亨诺克把脸埋在围裙里哭着，独自一个人回来了，身边没了她的同伴。
她讲的那一番遭遇，听来十分离奇。
她激动得上气不接下气，原话讲得颠三倒四；我便把她所说的大意，比她讲得更连贯地复述出来，也不再刻意仿效那粗鲁的诺森伯兰土话。

===Original===
The girl said, that, as they got along together among the brambles that grow beside the brook that bounds the Pie-Mag field, she on a sudden saw a very tall big-boned man, with an ill-favoured smirched face, and dressed in worn and rusty black, standing at the other side of a little stream. She was frightened; and while looking at this dirty, wicked, starved figure, Laura Silver Bell touched her, gazing at the same tall scarecrow, but with a countenance full of confusion and even rapture. She was peeping through the bush behind which she stood, and with a sigh she said:
"Is na that a conny lad? Agoy! See his bonny velvet clothes, his sword and sash; that's a lord, I can tell ye; and weel I know who he follows, who he luves, and who he'll wed."

===Chinese===
那姑娘说，她俩一道在那道围着喜鹊地的小溪旁、长满荆棘的丛莽里走着，她猛地瞧见一个骨节粗大、身形极高的男人，脸上一副抹了锅灰、面目可憎的样子，穿一身破旧发锈的黑衣，正站在一条小溪的对岸。她吓了一跳；她正端详着这个肮脏、邪恶、瘦骨嶙峋的身影时，劳拉·银铃碰了碰她，也正望着同一个高高稻草人般的身影，可脸上却是一片慌乱，甚至是狂喜的神色。她躲在她藏身的那丛灌木后头偷看，叹了一口气说：
"那不是个俊后生吗？哎呀！你瞧他那漂亮的天鹅绒衣裳，他的剑、他的绶带；我跟你说，那是一位贵族；他追的是谁、爱的是谁、要娶的是谁，我心里可清楚得很。"

===Original===
Bessie Hennock thought her companion daft.
"See how luvesome he luks!" whispered Laura.
Bessie looked again, and saw him gazing at her companion with a malignant smile, and at the same time he beckoned her to approach.
"Darrat ta! gaa not near him! he'll wring thy neck!" gasped Bessie in great fear, as she saw Laura step forward with a look of beautiful bashfulness and joy.
She took the hand he stretched across the stream, more for love of the hand than any need of help, and in a moment was across and by his side, and his long arm about her waist.

===Chinese===
贝西·亨诺克只当她疯了。
"瞧他长得多俊！"劳拉低声道。
贝西再看时，只见他正朝着她同伴露出恶意的微笑，同时又招手叫她过去。
"你这丫头！别过去！他要拧断你脖子的！"贝西见劳拉带着一种又羞怯又欣喜的美丽神情走上前去，吓得直喘。
她握住了他伸过溪来的那只手——与其说是要他扶，不如说是爱那只手——一眨眼便过了溪，到了他身边，他长长的胳膊已揽住了她的腰。

===Original===
"Fares te weel, Bessie, I'm gain my ways," she called, leaning her head to his shoulder; "and tell gud Fadder Lew I'm gain my ways to be happy, and may be, at lang last, I'll see him again."
And with a farewell wave of her hand, she went away with her dismal partner; and Laura Silver Bell was never more seen at home, or among the "coppies" and "wickwoods," the bonny fields and bosky hollows, by Dardale Moss.
Bessie Hennock followed them for a time.
She crossed the brook, and though they seemed to move slowly enough, she was obliged to run to keep them in view; and she all the time cried to her continually, "Come back, come back, bonnie Laurie!" until, getting over a bank, she was met by a white-faced old man, and so frightened was she, that she thought she fainted outright. At all events, she did not come to herself until the birds were singing their vespers in the amber light of sunset, and the day was over.
No trace of the direction of the girl's flight was ever discovered. Weeks and months passed, and more than a year.

===Chinese===
"再见吧，贝西，我走我的路啦，"她喊道，把头靠在他的肩上，"告诉卢老爹，我走我的路去享福啦，说不定，到头来，我还能再见他一面。"
她挥手作别，便跟着她那阴惨的伴侣走了；劳拉·银铃从此再没在家里出现过，也再没在达德尔沼旁的"矮林"和"老林"、那些秀美的田野和林木蓊郁的幽谷之间出现过。
贝西·亨诺克跟在后面追了一阵。
她过了溪，可他们看似走得很慢，她却不得不撒腿跑才不至于看不见他们；她一路不停地冲着她喊："回来呀，回来呀，可爱的劳丽！"直到她翻过一道土坎，迎面撞见一个脸白如纸的老头儿，她吓得当即就昏了过去——她自以为昏死了过去。无论如何，等到鸟儿在琥珀色的夕照里唱起晚祷之歌、白天已然了结之时，她才苏醒过来。
姑娘究竟朝哪个方向去了，再没寻出半点踪迹。几周几月过去了，一年有余。

===Original===
At the end of that time, one of Mall Carke's goats died, as she suspected, by the envious practices of a rival witch who lived at the far end of Dardale Moss.
All alone in her stone cabin the old woman had prepared her charm to ascertain the author of her misfortune.
The heart of the dead animal, stuck all over with pins, was burnt in the fire; the windows, doors, and every other aperture of the house being first carefully stopped. After the heart, thus prepared with suitable incantations, is consumed in the fire, the first person who comes to the door or passes by it is the offending magician.

===Chinese===
就在这当口，马尔·卡克的一只山羊死了，她心疑是达德尔沼那一头另一个与她作对的巫婆下了嫉妒的歹手。
老妇人独自在她那石头小屋里，备下了她那套法术，要查出来到底是谁害了她。
那死畜牲的心，被密密麻麻地插满了针，放在火里焚烧；事先已把屋子的窗、门以及其余一切窟窿都严严实实地堵好。如此依着相应的咒语备办的心，在火里烧化之后，头一个上门或打门口经过的人，便是那行凶的术士。

===Original===
Mother Carke completed these lonely rites at dead of night. It was a dark night, with the glimmer of the stars only, and a melancholy night-wind was soughing through the scattered woods that spread around.
After a long and dead silence, there came a heavy thump at the door, and a deep voice called her by name.
She was startled, for she expected no man's voice; and peeping from the window, she saw, in the dim light, a coach and four horses, with gold-laced footmen, and coachman in wig and cocked hat, turned out as if for a state occasion.
She unbarred the door; and a tall gentleman, dressed in black, waiting at the threshold, entreated her, as the only *sage femme* within reach, to come in the coach and attend Lady Lairdale, who was about to give birth to a baby, promising her handsome payment.

===Chinese===
卡克老妈在深更半夜独自做完了这一桩冷清的法事。那一夜天黑沉沉的，只有星星微微眨眼，一阵忧郁的夜风穿过四下稀疏的林木，呜呜地响着。
经过长久而死寂的沉默之后，门上砰地响起一记沉重的敲击，一个低沉的声音唤着她的名字。
她吓了一跳，因为她料不着会有男人的声音；她从窗缝里偷看出去，朦胧的光里只见一辆四匹马拉的马车，金线滚边的男仆，戴着假发、三角帽的车夫，那排场像是赴什么大典似的。
她抽开门闩；一个高个子、穿黑衣裳的绅士候在门槛外，恳求她——说她是附近唯一的接生婆（sage femme）——上马车去为莱尔德尔夫人（Lady Lairdale）接生，那夫人即将临盆，并许她一笔丰厚的酬金。

===Original===
Lady Lairdale! She had never heard of her.
"How far away is it?"
"Twelve miles on the old road to Golden Friars."
Her avarice is roused, and she steps into the coach. The footman claps-to the door; the glass jingles with the sound of a laugh. The tall dark-faced gentleman in black is seated opposite; they are driving at a furious pace; they have turned out of the road into a narrower one, dark with thicker and loftier forest than she was accustomed to. She grows anxious; for she knows every road and bypath in the country round, and she has never seen this one.
He encourages her. The moon has risen above the edge of the horizon, and she sees a noble old castle. Its summit of tower, watchtower and battlement, glimmers faintly in the moonlight. This is their destination.

===Chinese===
莱尔德尔夫人！她可从来没听见过这名字。
"有多远？"
"沿去金衣修士（Golden Friars）的老路十二英里。"
她的贪心被勾了起来，便上了马车。男仆啪地关上车门；车窗玻璃叮当一响，听上去像是一声冷笑。那高个子、黑面庞、穿黑衣的绅士坐在她对面；马车风驰电掣地奔着；他们已经从大路折入一条更窄的路，两旁的林木比她寻常所见更高更密，阴沉沉的。她心里不安起来；因为这周遭的大路小径她无一不熟，这条路她却从未见过。
他一路上安抚她。月亮已升上地平线，她望见一座气派非凡的古堡。堡上塔楼、瞭望塔、城堞的顶端在月色里隐隐约约地闪着微光。这便是他们的目的地。

===Original===
She feels on a sudden all but overpowered by sleep; but although she nods, she is quite conscious of the continued motion, which has become even rougher.
She makes an effort, and rouses herself. What has become of the coach, the castle, the servants? Nothing but the strange forest remains the same.
She is jolting along on a rude hurdle, seated on rushes, and a tall, big-boned man, in rags, sits in front, kicking with his heel the ill-favoured beast that pulls them along, every bone of which sticks out, and holding the halter which serves for reins. They stop at the door of a miserable building of loose stone, with a thatch so sunk and rotten, that the rooftree and couples protrude in crooked corners, like the bones of the wretched horse, with enormous head and ears, that dragged them to the door.
The long gaunt man gets down, his sinister face grimed like his hands.

===Chinese===
她忽然间一阵倦意袭来，几乎要把她压倒；然而她虽连连打着瞌睡，却清清楚楚地觉着那颠簸仍在继续，而且愈发剧烈了。
她使劲一挣，清醒过来。那马车、那古堡、那些仆人都到哪里去了？只剩这片古怪的林子还是老样子。
她正颠簸着坐在一辆粗陋的枝条拖车上，身下垫着灯心草；一个骨节粗大的高个子、衣衫褴褛的男人坐在前头，用脚后跟踢着那匹拉车的丑陋畜生——那畜生每一根骨头都支棱着——手里攥着当作缰绳用的笼头。他们在一座寒伧的乱石砌成的屋子门前停下，那屋顶的草沉陷腐烂得厉害，屋梁与椽木的接头处像犄角般歪歪扭扭地戳出来，正像把他们拉到门前的那匹惨马裸露的骨头——那马头和耳朵都大得吓人。
那又长又瘦的男人下了车，他那张阴鸷的脸跟他的手一样沾满了污垢。

===Original===
It was the same grimy giant who had accosted her on the lonely road near Deadman's Grike. But she feels that she "must go through with it" now, and she follows him into the house.
Two rushlights were burning in the large and miserable room, and on a coarse ragged bed lay a woman groaning piteously.
"That's Lady Lairdale," says the gaunt dark man, who then began to stride up and down the room rolling his head, stamping furiously, and thumping one hand on the palm of the other, and talking and laughing in the corners, where there was no one visible to hear or to answer.
Old Mall Carke recognized in the faded half-starved creature who lay on the bed, as dark now and grimy as the man, and looking as if she had never in her life washed hands or face, the once blithe and pretty Laura Lew.
The hideous being who was her mate continued in the same odd fluctuations of fury, grief, and merriment; and whenever she uttered a groan, he parodied it with another, as Mother Carke thought, in saturnine derision.
At length he strode into another room, and banged the door after him.

===Chinese===
正是那个在死人隘附近那条孤零零的路上拦住她的污垢巨人。可她觉得事到如今"非挺到底不可了"，便跟着他进了屋。
那间又大又凄惨的屋子里点着两盏灯心草烛，一张粗陋破烂的床上躺着一个女人，哀哀地呻吟着。
"那位便是莱尔德尔夫人，"那干瘦黝黑的男人说，说罢便在屋里来回踱起步来，晃着脑袋，狂躁地跺脚，一只手在另一只手掌上拍得啪啪响，又朝着墙角说话、发笑——那墙角里分明没有任何人听他、答他。
老马尔·卡克认出来了，那床上躺着的那形容枯槁、半饥半饱的活物——如今和那男人一般乌黑、一般污垢，看上去这辈子从没洗过手脸——便是当年那个快活俊俏的劳拉·卢。
与这女人做配偶的那个狰狞之物，仍在一阵阵古怪地暴怒、悲戚、欢笑之间反复无常；每逢她发出一声呻吟，他也学着来上一声，在卡克老妈看来，那是一种阴毒的嘲弄。
末了，他大步走进另一间屋子，砰地一声把门带上。

===Original===
In due time the poor woman's pains were over, and a daughter was born.
Such an imp! with long pointed ears, flat nose, and enormous restless eyes and mouth. It instantly began to yell and talk in some unknown language, at the noise of which the father looked into the room, and told the *sage femme* that she should not go unrewarded.
The sick woman seized the moment of his absence to say in the ear of Mall Carke:
"If ye had not been at ill work tonight, he could not hev fetched ye. Tak no more now than your rightful fee, or he'll keep ye here."
At this moment he returned with a bag of gold and silver coins, which he emptied on the table, and told her to help herself.

===Chinese===
到了时候，可怜那妇人的阵痛过去了，生下一个女儿。
这么个小妖精！长着又长又尖的耳朵，塌鼻梁，一双不安分的大眼睛和一张大嘴。它立刻就嚎了起来，叽里咕噜说着一种谁也听不懂的话；听见这动静，那父亲朝屋里探了探头，对接生婆说，绝不会让她白忙一场。
那病妇人趁他不在的当儿，凑到马尔·卡克的耳畔说：
"今儿夜里你若不是在干那邪门勾当，他也不能把你摄了来。你只拿你该得的酬劳，一文也不能多拿，不然他就把你留在这儿了。"
正说着，他回来了，拎着一袋金银币，哗啦一声倒在桌上，叫她自己拿。

===Original===
She took four shillings, which was her primitive fee, neither more nor less; and all his urgency could not prevail with her to take a farthing more. He looked so terrible at her refusal, that she rushed out of the house.
He ran after her.
"You'll take your money with you," he roared, snatching up the bag, still half full, and flung it after her.
It lighted on her shoulder; and partly from the blow, partly from terror, she fell to the ground; and when she came to herself, it was morning, and she was lying across her own door-stone.

===Chinese===
她拿了四先令，那是她那古老行当的酬规，不多不少；任他百般相劝，她也不肯再多拿一文。他见她推辞，那脸色变得怕人极了，吓得她冲出屋去。
他追了出来。
"你的钱，你一并带走！"他吼着，抓起那还剩半袋的钱袋，朝她背后掷了过来。
那钱袋落在她肩上；一半是被砸的，一半是吓的，她栽倒在地；待她醒过来时，已是清晨，她正横躺在自家门槛石上。

===Original===
It is said that she never more told fortune or practised spell. And though all that happened sixty years ago and more, Laura Silver Bell, wise folk think, is still living, and will so continue till the day of doom among the fairies.

===Chinese===
据说从那以后，她再没替人算过命、行过术。而这一切虽说已是六十多年前的事了，可劳拉·银铃——明白人这么想——至今仍活在世上，还将这样一直活到末日审判的那一天，活在仙灵（fairies）之中。

## Madam Crowl’s Ghost / 克萝尔老太太的鬼魂

===Original===
I’m an old woman now; and I was but thirteen, my last birthday, the night I came to Applewale House. My aunt was the housekeeper there, and a sort o’ one-horse carriage was down at Lexhoe waitin’ to take me and my box up to Applewale.

I was a bit frightened by the time I got to Lexhoe, and when I saw the carriage and horse, I wished myself back again with my mother at Hazelden. I was crying when I got into the “shay”—that’s what we used to call it—and old John Mulbery that drove it, and was a good-natured fellow, bought me a handful of apples at the Golden Lion to cheer me up a bit; and he told me that there was a currant-cake, and tea, and pork-chops, waiting for me, all hot, in my aunt’s room at the great house. It was a fine moonlight night, and I eat the apples, lookin’ out o’ the shay winda.

===Chinese===
如今我已是个老太婆了；可我过完上一个生日才十三岁，就是在那一晚，我来到了阿普尔沃尔宅（Applewale House）。我姑妈在那儿做管家，莱克斯霍（Lexhoe）那边备着一辆单匹马车，等着把我连人带箱子一同接上阿普尔沃尔。

等我赶到莱克斯霍时，心里已有些发怵；待瞧见那马和车，我恨不得回到黑兹尔登（Hazelden）母亲身边去。我钻进那“轻便马车”里时——我们都这么叫它——眼泪正簌簌地掉；赶车的老约翰·马尔伯里（John Mulbery）是个好心肠的汉子，在金狮客栈（Golden Lion）给我买了一把苹果，好叫我心里宽慰些；他还告诉我，姑妈在大宅的屋里给我备好了葡萄干蛋糕、茶，还有猪排，都热腾腾地等着我呢。那夜月色很好，我坐在马车的车窗边，一边看月亮，一边吃着苹果。

===Original===
It’s a shame for gentlemen to frighten a poor foolish child like I was. I sometimes think it might be tricks. There was two on ’em on the tap o’ the coach beside me. And they began to question me after nightfall, when the moon rose, where I was going to. Well, I told them it was to wait on Dame Arabella Crowl, of Applewale House, near by Lexhoe.

“Ho, then,” says one of them, “you’ll not be long there!”

And I looked at him as much as to say “Why not?” for I had spoken out when I told them where I was goin’, as if ’twas something clever I hed to say.

“Because,” says he, “and don’t you for your life tell no one, only watch her and see—she’s possessed by the devil, and more an half a ghost. Have you got a Bible?”

===Chinese===
让两位体面的先生来吓唬我这么个又傻又可怜的孩子，实在不大像话。我如今寻思，那没准儿是他们使的坏。车上坐我边上、同在车顶上的，正是这么两位。天黑之后，月亮升起来，他俩便盘问起我，问我上哪儿去。我便告诉他们，说是去伺候莱克斯霍附近阿普尔沃尔宅的阿拉贝拉·克萝尔老太太（Dame Arabella Crowl）。

“嗬，那敢情好，”其中一个说，“你在那儿待不长！”

我望着他，那神情分明是说“怎么就待不长？”——因为方才我说出要去的地方时，口气里带着一股子神气，倒像是我要讲的这话有多了不起似的。

“因为呀，”他说，“你千万别跟旁人提，只消留心瞧着她便知道了——她叫魔鬼附了身，多半也成了半个鬼了。你身边带着《圣经》没有？”

===Original===
“Yes, sir,” says I. For my mother put my little Bible in my box, and I knew it was there: and by the same token, though the print’s too small for my ald eyes, I have it in my press to this hour.

As I looked up at him saying “Yes, sir,” I thought I saw him winkin’ at his friend; but I could not be sure.

“Well,” says he, “be sure you put it under your bolster every night, it will keep the ald girl’s claws aff ye.”

And I got such a fright when he said that, you wouldn’t fancy! And I’d a liked to ask him a lot about the ald lady, but I was too shy, and he and his friend began talkin’ together about their own consarns, and dowly enough I got down, as I told ye, at Lexhoe. My heart sank as I drove into the dark avenue. The trees stand very thick and big, as ald as the ald house almost, and four people, with their arms out and fingertips touchin’, barely girds round some of them.

===Chinese===
“带着呢，先生，”我说。因为母亲已把我的小《圣经》塞进了我的箱子里，我知道它就在里头：顺带说一句——虽说如今那上面的字儿小得我这对老眼已瞧不大清——可那本《圣经》到这一刻还收在我的橱柜里。

我仰起脸答他一声“带着呢，先生”的时候，只觉得瞧见他冲他那位朋友挤了挤眼睛；可我又拿不准。

“那好，”他说，“你每晚务必要把它压在枕头底下，好叫那老婆子的爪子够不着你。”

他这话一出，我那一下子可吓得不轻，您怕是想都想不到！我本想多问几句那老婆子的事，可又太害臊；偏巧他和他的朋友已凑在一处聊起他们自己的私事来了，于是我就像先前说的那样，闷闷不乐地在莱克斯霍下了车。马车驶进那条黑黢黢的林荫道时，我的心直往下沉。两旁的树生得又密又大，几乎和那座老宅一般古老，有些树，要四个人伸直胳膊、指尖相搭，才勉强合抱得过来。

===Original===
Well my neck was stretched out o’ the winda, looking for the first view o’ the great house; and all at once we pulled up in front of it.

A great white-and-black house it is, wi’ great black beams across and right up it, and gables lookin’ out, as white as a sheet, to the moon, and the shadows o’ the trees, two or three up and down in front, you could count the leaves on them, and all the little diamond-shaped winda-panes, glimmering on the great hall winda, and great shutters, in the old fashion, hinged on the wall outside, boulted across all the rest o’ the windas in front, for there was but three or four servants, and the old lady in the house, and most o’ t’ rooms was locked up.

===Chinese===
我正伸长了脖子探出车窗，想头一眼瞧见那座大宅；冷不丁车就停在了它跟前。

那是座黑白相间的大宅子，一道道粗大的黑木梁横着、竖着穿插其上，山墙向着月亮探出来，白得像一张纸；前面疏疏落落立着两三棵树，树影投在地上，连叶子都数得清；大厅那扇大窗上，一块块菱形的小窗玻璃闪着微光；其余朝前的窗户，都按老式样从外面墙上装着铰链，用厚实的护窗板横着闩了起来——因为宅子里统共只有三四个仆人，外加那位老太太，大半的屋子都锁着不开了。

===Original===
My heart was in my mouth when I sid the journey was over, and this the great house afoore me, and I sa near my aunt that I never sid till noo, and Dame Crowl, that I was come to wait upon, and was afeard on already.

My aunt kissed me in the hall, and brought me to her room. She was tall and thin, wi’ a pale face and black eyes, and long thin hands wi’ black mittins on. She was past fifty, and her word was short; but her word was law. I hev no complaints to make of her; but she was a hard woman, and I think she would hev bin kinder to me if I had bin her sister’s child in place of her brother’s. But all that’s o’ no consequence noo.

===Chinese===
待我瞧见这趟路已到了头，眼前就是那座大宅，而我离那位素未谋面的姑妈已这般近，又想着那位我正是来伺候、心里却早已怕上的克萝尔老太太（Dame Crowl）——我的心一下子提到了嗓子眼。

姑妈在大厅里亲了亲我，把我领进她的屋里。她又高又瘦，脸儿苍白，一双黑眼睛，两只又长又细的手上戴着黑色的半指手套。她年过五十，话不多；可她的话便是规矩。我倒没有什么可抱怨她的；只是她是个硬心肠的女人，我想，倘若我是她姐妹的孩子，而不是她兄弟的孩子，她待我或许会亲厚几分。可这些如今都已无关紧要了。

===Original===
The squire—his name was Mr. Chevenix Crowl, he was Dame Crowl’s grandson—came down there, by way of seeing that the old lady was well treated, about twice or thrice in the year. I sid him but twice all the time I was at Applewale House.

I can’t say but she was well taken care of, notwithstanding; but that was because my aunt and Meg Wyvern, that was her maid, had a conscience, and did their duty by her.

===Chinese===
那位乡绅——他名叫切夫尼克斯·克萝尔先生（Mr. Chevenix Crowl），是克萝尔老太太的孙儿——一年里大约下来两三回，为的是瞧瞧这位老太太有没有受亏待。我在阿普尔沃尔宅的那段日子里，统共只见过他两面。

话虽如此，老太太倒也照料得不差；可这全仗着我姑妈，还有伺候她的那个女仆梅格·怀文（Meg Wyvern），两人都有良心，尽到了本分。

===Original===
Mrs. Wyvern—Meg Wyvern my aunt called her to herself, and Mrs. Wyvern to me—was a fat, jolly lass of fifty, a good height and a good breadth, always good-humoured, and walked slow. She had fine wages, but she was a bit stingy, and kept all her fine clothes under lock and key, and wore, mostly, a twilled chocolate cotton, wi’ red, and yellow, and green sprigs and balls on it, and it lasted wonderful.

She never gave me nout, not the vally o’ a brass thimble, all the time I was there; but she was good-humoured, and always laughin’, and she talked no end o’ proas over her tea; and, seeing me sa sackless and dowly, she roused me up wi’ her laughin’ and stories; and I think I liked her better than my aunt—children is so taken wi’ a bit o’ fun or a story—though my aunt was very good to me, but a hard woman about some things, and silent always.

===Chinese===
怀文太太（Mrs. Wyvern）——姑妈背地里叫她梅格·怀文，当面却教我称她怀文太太——是个五十岁的胖妇人，身量高，体格也宽，成日价乐呵呵的，走路慢吞吞。她的工钱很可观，手头却有点儿抠，那些好衣裳都锁在柜里压箱底，自家身上穿的，多半是一件巧克力色的斜纹棉布衫，上头印着红的、黄的、绿的细枝和小圆球，那衣裳竟也耐穿得出奇。

我在那儿那么久，她不曾给过我什么东西，连一只黄铜顶针的值钱都没有；可她脾气好，成天笑嘻嘻的，喝着茶能絮叨个没完；见我那样没精打采、闷闷不乐，她便用她的笑和故事来逗我精神；我想我倒是比喜欢姑妈更喜欢她——小孩子家就是这样，一点子乐子、一个故事，就把他们的心给勾去了——虽说姑妈待我也很好，只是有些事情上心硬，话又向来少。

===Original===
My aunt took me into her bedchamber, that I might rest myself a bit while she was settin’ the tea in her room. But first, she patted me on the shouther, and said I was a tall lass o’ my years, and had spired up well, and asked me if I could do plain work and stitchin’; and she looked in my face, and said I was like my father, her brother, that was dead and gone, and she hoped I was a better Christian, and wad na du a’ that lids (would not do anything of that sort).

It was a hard sayin’ the first time I set foot in her room, I thought.

===Chinese===
姑妈把我领进她的卧房，好叫我歇一歇，她好在那屋里张罗茶。可她先在我肩上拍了拍，说我这个岁数算长得高的了，抽条抽得不赖，又问我可会做些平常针线和缝缀的活计；她端详着我的脸，说我长得像我的父亲，也就是她那已过世的兄弟，又盼着我是个更守规矩的基督徒，莫要学她兄弟做那等事（原话用的是乡间土话，意思是“莫做那等勾当”）。

我头一回踏进她的屋，就听见这么一句话，我心里想，这话未免太狠了些。

===Original===
When I went into the next room, the housekeeper’s room—very comfortable, yak (oak) all round—there was a fine fire blazin’ away, wi’ coal, and peat, and wood, all in a low together, and tea on the table, and hot cake, and smokin’ meat; and there was Mrs. Wyvern, fat, jolly, and talkin’ away, more in an hour than my aunt would in a year.

While I was still at my tea my aunt went upstairs to see Madam Crowl.

===Chinese===
等我走进隔壁那间管家屋——屋里十分舒适，四面都是橡木（原文 yak，即 oak）——只见一炉好火烧得正旺，煤、泥炭和柴火混在一处烧着；桌上摆着茶，还有热腾腾的蛋糕和冒着热气的肉；怀文太太正坐在那里，胖胖的，乐呵呵的，话讲个不停，她一个钟头说的话，比姑妈一年说的还多。

我茶还没喝完，姑妈就上楼去看克萝尔老太太了。

===Original===
“She’s agone up to see that old Judith Squailes is awake,” says Mrs. Wyvern. “Judith sits with Madam Crowl when me and Mrs. Shutters”—that was my aunt’s name—“is away. She’s a troublesome old lady. Ye’ll hev to be sharp wi’ her, or she’ll be into the fire, or out o’ t’ winda. She goes on wires, she does, old though she be.”

“How old, ma’am?” says I.

“Ninety-three her last birthday, and that’s eight months gone,” says she; and she laughed. “And don’t be askin’ questions about her before your aunt—mind, I tell ye; just take her as you find her, and that’s all.”

===Chinese===
“她上楼去，是瞧着老朱迪思·斯凯尔斯（Judith Squailes）别打瞌睡，”怀文太太说。“我和沙特斯太太（Mrs. Shutters）——这是我姑妈的姓——不在的时候，就由朱迪思陪着克萝尔老太太。这位老太太可真难伺候。你得眼疾手快地看着她，一不留神她就要扑进火里，要不就从窗户里翻出去。她走起路来轻巧得很，跟踩着线儿似的，别看她上了岁数。”

“她多大年纪了，太太？”我问。

“上回过生日九十三了，那都是八个月前的事了，”她说着，笑了起来。“还有，别在你姑妈跟前问东问西的——记住，我这可是为你好；她是个什么样的人，你照着见到的样子去看待就罢了，别的别多想。”

===Original===
“And what’s to be my business about her, please, ma’am?” says I.

“About the old lady? Well,” says she, “your aunt, Mrs. Shutters, will tell you that; but I suppose you’ll hev to sit in the room with your work, and see she’s at no mischief, and let her amuse herself with her things on the table, and get her her food or drink as she calls for it, and keep her out o’ mischief, and ring the bell hard if she’s troublesome.”

“Is she deaf, ma’am?”

“No, nor blind,” says she; “as sharp as a needle, but she’s gone quite aupy, and can’t remember nout rightly; and Jack the Giant Killer, or Goody Twoshoes will please her as well as the king’s court, or the affairs of the nation.”

===Chinese===
“那太太，请问我伺候她都要做些什么呢？”我问。

“伺候这位老太太吗？这个嘛，”她说，“你姑妈沙特斯太太自会告诉你的；不过我琢磨着，你无非就是拿着针线活坐在她屋里，瞧着她别闯祸，由着她摆弄桌上那些玩意儿解闷，她要吃要喝便递给她，好歹看住她别出乱子，若是她闹得凶了，你就使劲儿拉铃。”

“她耳朵背吗，太太？”

“不背，也不瞎，”她说，“尖得跟根针似的；只是人整个儿糊涂了，什么事也记不真切；你给她讲《杀巨人杰克》（Jack the Giant Killer）也好，讲《两鞋古迪》（Goody Twoshoes）也好，在她眼里，跟国王的朝廷、国家的大事一般有趣。”

===Original===
“And what did the little girl go away for, ma’am, that went on Friday last? My aunt wrote to my mother she was to go.”

“Yes; she’s gone.”

“What for?” says I again.

“She didn’t answer Mrs. Shutters, I do suppose,” says she. “I don’t know. Don’t be talkin’; your aunt can’t abide a talkin’ child.”

“And please, ma’am, is the old lady well in health?” says I.

“It ain’t no harm to ask that,” says she. “She’s torflin’ a bit lately, but better this week past, and I dare say she’ll last out her hundred years yet. Hish! Here’s your aunt coming down the passage.”

===Chinese===
“还有，太太，上礼拜五走的那个小姑娘，是为什么走的呀？姑妈写信给我娘，说是叫她走的。”

“是啊，她是走了。”

“为什么呀？”我又问。

“我估摸着是她没回沙特斯太太的话吧，”她说，“我也不清楚。别多嘴了；你姑妈最嫌话多的孩子。”

“请问太太，老太太身子骨还硬朗吗？”我又问。

“这个问倒不妨事，”她说，“她近来身子有些不大爽利，可这过去的一周倒好些了，我敢说她活到一百岁都不成问题。嘘！你姑妈从过道那头过来了。”

===Original===
In comes my aunt, and begins talkin’ to Mrs. Wyvern, and I, beginnin’ to feel more comfortable and at home like, was walkin’ about the room lookin’ at this thing and at that. There was pretty old china things on the cupboard, and pictures again the wall; and there was a door open in the wainscot, and I sees a queer old leathern jacket, wi’ straps and buckles to it, and sleeves as long as the bedpost hangin’ up inside.

“What’s that you’re at, child?” says my aunt, sharp enough, turning about when I thought she least minded. “What’s that in your hand?”

“This, ma’am?” says I, turning about with the leathern jacket. “I don’t know what it is, ma’am.”

===Chinese===
姑妈进来了，便和怀文太太说上了话；我呢，渐觉舒坦自在起来，就在屋里走来走去，东瞧西看。碗橱上摆着几件好看的旧瓷器，墙上挂着画儿；护墙板上有一扇小门开着，我瞧见里头挂着一件古怪的旧皮坎肩，上头带着皮带和扣环，两只袖子长极了，简直跟床柱一般长。

“你这孩子，在那儿鼓捣什么？”姑妈陡地转过身来——我还道她没留心我呢——嗓门提得老高，“你手里拿的是什么？”

“这个吗，太太？”我应着，手里拎着那件皮坎肩转过身来。“我不晓得这是什么，太太。”

===Original===
Pale as she was, the red came up in her cheeks, and her eyes flashed wi’ anger, and I think only she had half a dozen steps to take, between her and me, she’d a gev me a sizzup. But she did gie me a shake by the shouther, and she plucked the thing out o’ my hand, and says she, “While ever you stay here, don’t ye meddle wi’ nout that don’t belong to ye,” and she hung it up on the pin that was there, and shut the door wi’ a bang and locked it fast.

Mrs. Wyvern was liftin’ up her hands and laughin’ all this time, quietly, in her chair, rolling herself a bit in it, as she used when she was kinkin’.

The tears was in my eyes, and she winked at my aunt, and says she, dryin’ her own eyes that was wet wi’ the laughin’, “Tut, the child meant no harm—come here to me, child. It’s only a pair o’ crutches for lame ducks, and ask us no questions mind, and we’ll tell ye no lies; and come here and sit down, and drink a mug o’ beer before ye go to your bed.”

===Chinese===
姑妈的脸原是苍白的，这会儿却腾地红了起来，眼里闪着怒光；我琢磨着，要不是她与我之间还隔着六七步远，她准得给我一巴掌。可她到底还是抓住我的肩膀摇了两下，一把将那东西从我手里夺了过去，说道：“只要你还在这个屋里待着，凡是不属于你的东西，都不许你乱碰，”说着，她把它挂回原来那根钉子上，砰的一声把门关上，牢牢地锁好。

这一阵工夫，怀文太太一直坐在椅子里，悄悄地抬手笑着，身子在椅子里来回地晃——她笑得喘不过气来的时候，就爱这么晃。

我眼里噙着泪，她冲姑妈使了个眼色，又拿手抹了抹自己笑出来的眼泪，说道：“去去，这孩子又没安坏心眼——上我这儿来，孩子。那不过是给瘸腿鸭子预备的一副拐杖罢了。你呢，别多问，我们也不会拿瞎话诓你；来，上这儿坐下，临睡前喝一大杯啤酒。”

===Original===
My room, mind ye, was upstairs, next to the old lady’s, and Mrs. Wyvern’s bed was near hers in her room, and I was to be ready at call, if need should be.

The old lady was in one of her tantrums that night and part of the day before. She used to take fits o’ the sulks. Sometimes she would not let them dress her, and at other times she would not let them take her clothes off. She was a great beauty, they said, in her day. But there was no one about Applewale that remembered her in her prime. And she was dreadful fond o’ dress, and had thick silks, and stiff satins, and velvets, and laces, and all sorts, enough to set up seven shops at the least. All her dresses was old-fashioned and queer, but worth a fortune.

===Chinese===
告诉您，我的屋子在楼上，紧挨着老太太的卧房；怀文太太的床就摆在她屋里，离她不远，若是有事，我好随叫随到。

那天夜里，还有头天大半天，老太太又犯了脾气。她动不动就要闹一阵子闷气。有时候不肯让人给她穿衣裳，有时候又不肯让人给她脱衣裳。据说她年轻的时候，是个出了名的大美人。只是阿普尔沃尔宅上下，已没一个人见过她盛年时的模样。她又极其爱打扮，厚的绸、硬的缎、天鹅绒、花边，种种衣料应有尽有，少说也够开七家铺子的。她那些衣裙件件样式古旧而怪异，可件件都值大价钱。

===Original===
Well, I went to my bed. I lay for a while awake; for a’ things was new to me; and I think the tea was in my nerves, too, for I wasn’t used to it, except now and then on a holiday, or the like. And I heard Mrs. Wyvern talkin’, and I listened with my hand to my ear; but I could not hear Mrs. Crowl, and I don’t think she said a word.

There was great care took of her. The people at Applewale knew that when she died they would every one get the sack; and their situations was well paid and easy.

===Chinese===
就这样，我上床睡下了。有一阵子我躺着睡不着；因为样样事物于我都是新的；再者，我琢磨着那茶也让我犯了精神，我平素不大喝茶，只有逢年过节偶然喝上一回。我听见怀文太太在说话，便把手贴在耳边侧耳去听；可我听不见克萝尔老太太出声，我想她是一句话也没说。

老太太是被精心照料着的。阿普尔沃尔宅上上下下的人都明白，她一旦归了西，他们每一个人都得卷铺盖走人；而他们这份差事，工钱丰厚，活计又轻省。

===Original===
