The doctor came twice a week to see the old lady, and you may be sure they all did as he bid them. One thing was the same every time; they were never to cross or frump her, any way, but to humour and please her in everything.

So she lay in her clothes all that night, and next day, not a word she said, and I was at my needlework all that day, in my own room, except when I went down to my dinner.

I would a liked to see the ald lady, and even to hear her speak. But she might as well a’ bin in Lunnon a’ the time for me.

===Chinese===
大夫一礼拜来看老太太两回，您尽可相信，上上下下都照着他吩咐的办。有一件事是回回不变的：无论如何，都不能违拗她、招惹她，事事都要顺着她、哄她高兴。

于是她就那样穿着衣裳躺了一整夜，第二天又是一天，没说过一句话；那一整天我都在自己屋里做针线活，只有下去吃午饭时才走开一会儿。

我倒很想瞧瞧那位老太太，哪怕听听她说话也好。可她那样子，倒像是整日整夜地远在伦敦（Lunnon，即 London），与我不相干了。

===Original===
When I had my dinner my aunt sent me out for a walk for an hour. I was glad when I came back, the trees was so big, and the place so dark and lonesome, and ’twas a cloudy day, and I cried a deal, thinkin’ of home, while I was walkin’ alone there. That evening, the candles bein’ alight, I was sittin’ in my room, and the door was open into Madam Crowl’s chamber, where my aunt was. It was, then, for the first time I heard what I suppose was the ald lady talking.

It was a queer noise like, I couldn’t well say which, a bird, or a beast, only it had a bleatin’ sound in it, and was very small.

I pricked my ears to hear all I could. But I could not make out one word she said. And my aunt answered:

“The evil one can’t hurt no one, ma’am, bout the Lord permits.”

===Chinese===
吃过午饭，姑妈叫我出去散一个钟头的步。等我回来时心里倒松快了——外头那些树太大，那地方又黑又僻静，又是个阴天，我独自在那儿走着，想着家，哭了老大一场。那天傍晚，蜡烛已点上，我坐在自己屋里，通向克萝尔老太太卧房的那扇门开着，姑妈就在那屋里。就在那时候，我头一回听见了——我猜那便是老太太在说话。

那声音古怪得很，像是什么在叫，我也说不大准是鸟是兽，只听出里头带着一种咩咩的哀鸣声，又细又小。

我竖起耳朵，把能听的都听进去。可她说的我一个字也听不明白。只听见姑妈答道：

“夫人，邪魔要害什么人，若非主允许，是害不成的。”

===Original===
Then the same queer voice from the bed says something more that I couldn’t make head nor tail on.

And my aunt med answer again: “Let them pull faces, ma’am, and say what they will; if the Lord be for us, who can be against us?”

I kept listenin’ with my ear turned to the door, holdin’ my breath, but not another word or sound came in from the room. In about twenty minutes, as I was sittin’ by the table, lookin’ at the pictures in the old Aesop’s Fables, I was aware o’ something moving at the door, and lookin’ up I sid my aunt’s face lookin’ in at the door, and her hand raised.

“Hish!” says she, very soft, and comes over to me on tiptoe, and she says in a whisper: “Thank God, she’s asleep at last, and don’t ye make no noise till I come back, for I’m goin’ down to take my cup o’ tea, and I’ll be back i’ noo—me and Mrs. Wyvern, and she’ll be sleepin’ in the room, and you can run down when we come up, and Judith will gie ye yaur supper in my room.”

And with that she goes.

===Chinese===
紧接着，床上那个古怪的声音又说了一些什么，我更是摸不着头脑。

姑妈又答道：“随他们做鬼脸、随他们说什么去吧，夫人；主既站在我们这边，谁能与我们作对呢？”

我侧着耳朵贴在门那边，屏住气听着，可屋里再没传出一个字、一点声响。约莫过了二十分钟，我正坐在桌边，翻看着那本旧《伊索寓言》（Aesop’s Fables）里的图画，忽觉门口有什么在动；一抬头，瞧见姑妈正从门口探进半张脸来，一只手举着示意。

“嘘！”她极轻地嘘了一声，踮着脚走到我跟前，压低嗓子悄声道：“谢天谢地，她总算睡着了。我下去喝杯茶的工夫，你千万别弄出声响；我马上就回来——我和怀文太太一道回来，今夜就由她在屋里睡；等我们上来了，你再下去，朱迪思会在我的屋里给你端上晚饭。”

说完，她就走了。

===Original===
I kep’ looking at the picture-book, as before, listenin’ every noo and then, but there was no sound, not a breath, that I could hear; an’ I began whisperin’ to the pictures and talkin’ to myself to keep my heart up, for I was growin’ feared in that big room.

And at last up I got, and began walkin’ about the room, lookin’ at this and peepin’ at that, to amuse my mind, ye’ll understand. And at last what sud I do but peeps into Madam Crowl’s bedchamber.

===Chinese===
我照旧翻着那本画书，时不时侧耳听一听，可什么声音也听不见，连一丝呼吸也听不出；我便对着画里的人低声说话，自言自语，好给自己壮壮胆——在那间大屋里，我越待越怕。

到后来，我到底坐不住了，站起身在屋里踱来踱去，东瞧瞧、西看看，您也明白，是想给自己解解闷儿。谁知到头来，我竟凑到克萝尔老太太卧房的门口，朝里头张望起来。

===Original===
A grand chamber it was, wi’ a great four-poster, wi’ flowered silk curtains as tall as the ceilin’, and foldin’ down on the floor, and drawn close all round. There was a lookin’-glass, the biggest I ever sid before, and the room was a blaze o’ light. I counted twenty-two wax candles, all alight. Such was her fancy, and no one dared say her nay.

I listened at the door, and gaped and wondered all round. When I heard there was not a breath, and did not see so much as a stir in the curtains, I took heart, and walked into the room on tiptoe, and looked round again. Then I takes a keek at myself in the big glass; and at last it came in my head, “Why couldn’t I ha’ a keek at the ald lady herself in the bed?”

===Chinese===
好一间气派的卧房！一张大四柱床，挂着绣花的绸缎帐子，那帐子一直垂到天花板那么高，下摆拖到了地上，四面合得严严实实。屋里有一面镜子，是我前所未见的大；满屋子灯火通明。我数了数，二十二支蜡烛，全都点着。这是她的脾气，没人敢说个不字。

我在门口听了听，又目瞪口呆地四下张望。听见里头没有一丝呼吸，帐子也不见半点动静，我便大着胆子踮起脚走进屋里，又四下看了一遍。接着，我往那面大镜子里瞧了瞧自己；到后来，我心里忽然冒出一个念头：“我何不就着这机会，偷偷瞧一眼床上那位老太太呢？”

===Original===
Ye’d think me a fule if ye knew half how I longed to see Dame Crowl, and I thought to myself if I didn’t peep now I might wait many a day before I got so gude a chance again.

Well, my dear, I came to the side o’ the bed, the curtains bein’ close, and my heart a’most failed me. But I took courage, and I slips my finger in between the thick curtains, and then my hand. So I waits a bit, but all was still as death. So, softly, softly I draws the curtain, and there, sure enough, I sid before me, stretched out like the painted lady on the tomb-stean in Lexhoe Church, the famous Dame Crowl, of Applewale House. There she was, dressed out. You never sid the like in they days. Satin and silk, and scarlet and green, and gold and pint lace; by Jen! ’twas a sight! A big powdered wig, half as high as herself, was atop o’ her head, and, wow!—was ever such wrinkles?—and her old baggy throat all powdered white, and her cheeks rouged, and mouse-skin eyebrows, that Mrs. Wyvern used to stick on, and there she lay proud and stark, wi’ a pair o’ clocked silk hose on, and heels to her shoon as tall as ninepins. Lawk! But her nose was crooked and thin, and half the whites o’ her eyes was open. She used to stand, dressed as she was, gigglin’ and dribblin’ before the lookin’-glass, wi’ a fan in her hand and a big nosegay in her bodice. Her wrinkled little hands was stretched down by her sides, and such long nails, all cut into points, I never sid in my days. Could it ever a bin the fashion for grit fowk to wear their fingernails so?

===Chinese===
您要是知道我那时有多么盼着能瞧克萝尔老太太一眼，怕是要笑我傻呢。我心里盘算着：这会儿要是不瞧上一眼，往后不知要等多少日子才能再撞上这么个好机会。

就这样，好姑娘，我走到床边——帐子合得紧紧的——我的心几乎要打退堂鼓了。可我还是壮起胆子，先把一根手指头伸进那厚厚的帐子缝里，接着又把整只手探了进去。我停了一会儿，四下里却如死一般寂静。于是，我一点一点地、轻轻地撩开帐子——可不是么，我眼前瞧见的，直挺挺躺在那里的，活像莱克斯霍教堂里墓石上刻的那位石像贵妇——正是阿普尔沃尔宅那位大名鼎鼎的克萝尔老太太。她就躺在那里，盛装打扮着。您在那些年头里从没见过那样的排场。绸啊缎啊，猩红配翠绿，金线、针绣花边（pint lace，即 point lace）；老天爷呀！那真叫一个气派！她头顶上戴着一顶扑了粉的大假发，足有她半个人那么高；天哪！——谁见过那样的皱纹？——她那松弛干瘪的老脖子也扑得雪白，两颊抹了胭脂，还有两道鼠皮做的眉毛——那是怀文太太往常给她粘上去的——她就那样僵直地躺着，神气活现，脚上穿着一双绣花丝袜，鞋后跟高得跟九柱戏的木柱一般。乖乖！只是她那鼻子又弯又尖，半边眼白翻露着。她往常就是这样打扮好了，拿着一把扇子，紧身胸衣上插一大束花，对着镜子又痴笑、又淌口水。她那双皱巴巴的小手直直地伸在身子两边，那副又长又尖、尖尖地削过的指甲，我这辈子都没见过那样的。莫非从前的体面人家，当真时兴把指甲留成那个样子不成？

===Original===
Well, I think ye’d a-bin frightened yourself if ye’d a sid such a sight. I couldn’t let go the curtain, nor move an inch, nor take my eyes off her; my very heart stood still. And in an instant she opens her eyes and up she sits, and spins herself round, and down wi’ her, wi’ a clack on her two tall heels on the floor, facin’ me, ogglin’ in my face wi’ her two great glassy eyes, and a wicked simper wi’ her wrinkled lips, and lang fause teeth.

Well, a corpse is a natural thing; but this was the dreadfullest sight I ever sid. She had her fingers straight out pointin’ at me, and her back was crooked, round again wi’ age. Says she:

“Ye little limb! what for did ye say I killed the boy? I’ll tickle ye till ye’re stiff!”

===Chinese===
哎，要换了是您瞧见这么一副景象，我想您自己也要害怕的。我既放不下手里的帐子，也挪不动半步，眼睛更没法从她身上移开；我的心整个儿地停住了。冷不丁地，她睁开了眼睛，一下子坐了起来，身子一旋，“啪”的一声，两只高高的鞋跟落在地板上，正对着我，那两只玻璃珠子般的大眼睛直勾勾地瞪着我的脸，皱巴巴的嘴唇撇出一脸邪恶的媚笑，露出一口又长又假的牙。

哎，死人原是件平常事；可这一幕，是我这辈子所见过的最骇人的景象。她把手指头直直地伸着，冲我指过来，背脊因年迈而佝偻，整个人弯成一个圆弧。只听她说道：

“你这小淘气鬼！你凭什么说我害死了那男孩？我要挠你，挠到你浑身僵直！”

===Original===
If I’d a thought an instant, I’d a turned about and run. But I couldn’t take my eyes off her, and I backed from her as soon as I could; and she came clatterin’ after like a thing on wires, with her fingers pointing to my throat, and she makin’ all the time a sound with her tongue like zizz-zizz-zizz.

I kept backin’ and backin’ as quick as I could, and her fingers was only a few inches away from my throat, and I felt I’d lose my wits if she touched me.

I went back this way, right into the corner, and I gev a yellock, ye’d think saul and body was partin’, and that minute my aunt, from the door, calls out wi’ a blare, and the ald lady turns round on her, and I turns about, and ran through my room, and down the stairs, as hard as my legs could carry me.

===Chinese===
我要是当时能转个念头，早就转身跑了。可我眼睛离不开她，便拼命地往后退；而她却像踩着钢丝的什么物件一般，噼里啪啦地朝我扑过来，手指头直指我的喉咙，嘴里一刻不停地发出一种舌头打颤的声音：嗞——嗞——嗞——

我一个劲儿地往后退，退得越快越好，她的手指头离我的喉咙始终不过几寸远，我只觉得她若碰我一下，我便要疯了。

我就这么退着，一直退到了墙角，发出一声尖叫——那动静，您会以为我的魂魄都要和身子分家了——就在那一刻，姑妈从门口大喊了一声，老太太转过身朝向她，我趁机一转身，穿过我的屋子，冲下楼梯，拼了命地往下跑。

===Original===
I cried hearty, I can tell you, when I got down to the housekeeper’s room. Mrs. Wyvern laughed a deal when I told her what happened. But she changed her key when she heard the ald lady’s words.

“Say them again,” says she.

So I told her.

“Ye little limb! What for did ye say I killed the boy? I’ll tickle ye till ye’re stiff.”

“And did ye say she killed a boy?” says she.

“Not I, ma’am,” says I.

Judith was always up with me, after that, when the two elder women was away from her. I would a jumped out at winda, rather than stay alone in the same room wi’ her.

===Chinese===
我到了管家屋里，那眼泪可是痛痛快快地流了一场，我跟您说。我把经过讲给怀文太太听，她起先笑了个够。可一听到老太太说的那几句话，她的口气就变了。

“你再说一遍，”她说。

我便复述了一遍。

“你这小淘气鬼！你凭什么说我害死了那男孩？我要挠你，挠到你浑身僵直。”

“你说过她害死过一个男孩吗？”她问。

“我没说过呀，太太，”我说。

打那以后，只要两位年长的妇人不在她身边，朱迪思便总是陪着我。我宁肯从窗户里跳出去，也不愿和她独处一室。

===Original===
It was about a week after, as well as I can remember, Mrs. Wyvern, one day when me and her was alone, told me a thing about Madam Crowl that I did not know before.

She being young and a great beauty, full seventy year before, had married Squire Crowl, of Applewale. But he was a widower, and had a son about nine years old.

There never was tale or tidings of this boy after one mornin’. No one could say where he went to. He was allowed too much liberty, and used to be off in the morning, one day, to the keeper’s cottage and breakfast wi’ him, and away to the warren, and not home, mayhap, till evening; and another time down to the lake, and bathe there, and spend the day fishin’ there, or paddlin’ about in the boat. Well, no one could say what was gone wi’ him; only this, that his hat was found by the lake, under a haathorn that grows thar to this day, and ’twas thought he was drowned bathin’. And the squire’s son, by his second marriage, with this Madam Crowl that lived sa dreadful lang, came in far the estates. It was his son, the ald lady’s grandson, Squire Chevenix Crowl, that owned the estates at the time I came to Applewale.

There was a deal o’ talk lang before my aunt’s time about it; and ’twas said the stepmother knew more than she was like to let out. And she managed her husband, the ald squire, wi’ her white-heft and flatteries. And as the boy was never seen more, in course of time the thing died out of fowks’ minds.

===Chinese===
据我所能记起的，大约又过了一周，有一日，只有我和怀文太太两个人在的时候，她把一桩我从不知道的、关于克萝尔老太太的事告诉了我。

说是七十多年前，她正当年轻貌美，嫁给了阿普尔沃尔的克萝尔乡绅（Squire Crowl）。可那乡绅是个鳏夫，身边已有个九岁上下的儿子。

自打某一天早上之后，这孩子就再没了音讯，也再没人见过他。谁也说不上他去了哪里。这孩子平日里放任惯了，时常一清早便溜出去——这一日，上猎场看守的小屋去找他，一道吃早饭，吃完便往养兔场跑，兴许到天黑才回家；又一日，则下到湖边去洗澡，在那儿钓上一整天的鱼，或是划着小船在水上荡来荡去。哎，谁也说不清这孩子到底出了什么事；只知这样一桩：他的帽子是在湖边一棵山楂树下找着的——那棵树至今还生在那里——众人便猜他洗澡时淹死了。而乡绅与这位克萝尔老太太——她活了长得可怕的一把年纪——第二次婚姻所生的儿子，便继承了那份家业。我在阿普尔沃尔的时候，那处家业的主人，正是这位儿子的儿子，也就是老太太的孙儿——切夫尼克斯·克萝尔乡绅。

早在姑妈到这儿来之前很久，这件事就在乡间议论纷纷了；都说那位继母心里头明白的事，远比她肯说出口的多。她是凭着白嫩的手段和满嘴的甜言蜜语，把那位老乡绅——她的丈夫——捏在手心里的。那孩子既再也没有出现过，日久天长，这事也就慢慢从人们的脑子里淡了下去。

===Original===
I’m goin’ to tell ye noo about what I sid wi’ my own een.

I was not there six months, and it was winter time, when the ald lady took her last sickness.

The doctor was afeard she might a took a fit o’ madness, as she did fifteen years befoore, and was buckled up, many a time, in a strait-waistcoat, which was the very leathern jerkin I sid in the closet, off my aunt’s room.

===Chinese===
如今我要告诉您的，是我亲眼所见的那些事。

我到那儿还没满六个月，正是冬天的时候，那位老太太染上了她最后一场病。

大夫担心她会不会又像十五年前那样，犯起疯病来——十五年前那回，她好些次被捆进一件约束衣（strait-waistcoat）里，而那件约束衣，正是我在姑妈屋里那个壁橱中所见的那件皮坎肩。

===Original===
Well, she didn’t. She pined, and windered, and went off, torflin’, torflin’, quiet enough, till a day or two before her flittin’, and then she took to rabblin’, and sometimes skirlin’ in the bed, ye’d think a robber had a knife to her throat, and she used to work out o’ the bed, and not being strong enough, then, to walk or stand, she’d fall on the flure, wi’ her ald wizened hands stretched before her face, and skirlin’ still for mercy.

Ye may guess I didn’t go into the room, and I used to be shiverin’ in my bed wi’ fear, at her skirlin’ and scrafflin’ on the flure, and blarin’ out words that id make your skin turn blue.

My aunt, and Mrs. Wyvern, and Judith Squailes, and a woman from Lexhoe, was always about her. At last she took fits, and they wore her out.

===Chinese===
哎，她倒并没有犯。她只是日渐衰弱、消瘦下去，一天不如一天，安安静静地走向了末了；直到她离世前那一两日，她才开始胡言乱语起来，有时在床上发出尖叫——那动静，您会以为是有强盗把刀子搁在了她脖子上——她还不时挣扎着要从床上爬下来，可那时她已虚弱得站也站不住、走也走不动，便一头栽倒在地上，那双干枯的老手直直地伸在脸前面，嘴里还在尖叫着求饶。

您猜也猜得到，我是断不敢进那屋去的；我躺在自己床上，听着她在地板上尖叫挣扎，吓得直打哆嗦，她嘴里喊出来的那些话，能叫人听了皮肤发紫。

姑妈、怀文太太、朱迪思·斯凯尔斯，还有从莱克斯霍叫来的一个女人，日夜轮流守着她。到末了，她发起一阵阵的抽搐，就这样被耗尽了。

===Original===
T’ sir was there, and prayed for her; but she was past praying with. I suppose it was right, but none could think there was much good in it, and sa at lang last she made her flittin’, and a’ was over, and old Dame Crowl was shrouded and coffined, and Squire Chevenix was wrote for. But he was away in France, and the delay was sa lang, that t’ sir and doctor both agreed it would not du to keep her langer out o’ her place, and no one cared but just them two, and my aunt and the rest o’ us, from Applewale, to go to the buryin’. So the old lady of Applewale was laid in the vault under Lexhoe Church; and we lived up at the great house till such time as the squire should come to tell his will about us, and pay off such as he chose to discharge.

===Chinese===
牧师也来了，为她祈祷；可她已不是能与之祷告的人了。我寻思这原是应当的，可谁也觉不出这其中有多少益处；就这样到了末了，她终于“上路”了——一切都了结了——老克萝尔太太穿好了殓衣，入了棺，又派人去请切夫尼克斯乡绅。可他人正在法国，这一耽搁就拖得老长，牧师和大夫都说不便再久停不下葬；于是除他们两位之外，再没旁人放在心上，只由姑妈和我们几个从阿普尔沃尔来的人，去送了葬。这位阿普尔沃尔的老太太便被安葬在莱克斯霍教堂底下的墓穴里；我们仍住在大宅里头，只等乡绅回来发落我们这些人，把该打发的打发了。

===Original===
I was put into another room, two doors away from what was Dame Crowl’s chamber, after her death, and this thing happened the night before Squire Chevenix came to Applewale.

The room I was in now was a large square chamber, covered wi’ yak pannels, but unfurnished except for my bed, which had no curtains to it, and a chair and a table, or so, that looked nothing at all in such a big room. And the big looking-glass, that the old lady used to keek into and admire herself from head to heel, now that there was na mair o’ that wark, was put out of the way, and stood against the wall in my room, for there was shiftin’ o’ many things in her chamber ye may suppose, when she came to be coffined.

===Chinese===
老太太去世之后，我被挪到了另一间屋子，离克萝尔老太太原先的卧房隔了两道门；而下面这件事，就发生在切夫尼克斯乡绅到阿普尔沃尔的前一夜。

我如今住的这间屋子，是一间方方正正的大屋，四面镶着橡木板壁，可屋里除却我的床——那床连帐子也没有——和一把椅子、一张桌子之类的几件零碎，便空空如也，搁在那间大屋里简直微不足道。而老太太往常对之顾影自怜、从头到脚照个不停的那面大镜子，如今既然用不着了，便被挪开，靠墙立在我的屋里——您也想象得到，她既入了殓，她那卧房里的好多物件都要挪动挪动的。

===Original===
The news had come that day that the squire was to be down next morning at Applewale; and not sorry was I, for I thought I was sure to be sent home again to my mother. And right glad was I, and I was thinkin’ of a’ at hame, and my sister Janet, and the kitten and the pymag, and Trimmer the tike, and all the rest, and I got sa fidgetty, I couldn’t sleep, and the clock struck twelve, and me wide awake, and the room as dark as pick. My back was turned to the door, and my eyes toward the wall opposite.

Well, it could na be a full quarter past twelve, when I sees a lightin’ on the wall befoore me, as if something took fire behind, and the shadas o’ the bed, and the chair, and my gown, that was hangin’ from the wall, was dancin’ up and down on the ceilin’ beams and the yak pannels; and I turns my head ower my shouther quick, thinkin’ something must a gone a’ fire.

===Chinese===
那天传来消息，说乡绅次日一早就要到阿普尔沃尔来；我心里倒乐得很，因为我想这下准能被打发回家、回到母亲身边了。我满心欢喜，满脑子想的全是家里的事——我妹妹珍妮特（Janet）、家里的小猫、南瓜（原文 pymag，即 pumpkin）、还有那条叫“修剪工”（Trimmer）的小狗，以及种种其余的人事物——我越想越坐不住，怎么也睡不着；钟敲过十二点，我仍大睁着眼，屋里漆黑一片。我背对着门，眼睛朝着对面的墙。

哎，过了十二点怕还不到一刻钟，我便瞧见面前的墙上亮了起来，像是背后有什么东西着了火，床、椅子，还有我那件挂在墙上的衣裳的影子，在天花板的横梁和橡木板壁上跳上跳下；我赶紧扭过头去瞧，只当是什么东西当真着了火。

===Original===
And what sud I see, by Jen! but the likeness o’ the ald beldame, bedizened out in her satins and velvets, on her dead body, simperin’, wi’ her eyes as wide as saucers, and her face like the fiend himself. ’Twas a red light that rose about her in a fuffin low, as if her dress round her feet was blazin’. She was drivin’ on right for me, wi’ her ald shrivelled hands crooked as if she was goin’ to claw me. I could not stir, but she passed me straight by, wi’ a blast o’ cald air, and I sid her, at the wall, in the alcove as my aunt used to call it, which was a recess where the state bed used to stand in ald times wi’ a door open wide, and her hands gropin’ in at somethin’ was there. I never sid that door befoore. And she turned round to me, like a thing on a pivot, flyerin’, and all at once the room was dark, and I standin’ at the far side o’ the bed; I don’t know how I got there, and I found my tongue at last, and if I did na blare a yellock, rennin’ down the gallery and almost pulled Mrs. Wyvern’s door off t’ hooks, and frighted her half out o’ wits.

===Chinese===
天老爷呀！我瞧见了什么——只见那老巫婆的形貌，盛装艳服地附着在她那死去的肉身上，绸缎天鹅绒一应俱全，脸上撇着媚笑，两眼瞪得像茶碟一样大，那神情活像魔鬼本人。一团红光在她周身腾起，像一团膨胀的火苗，仿佛她裙边裙角的衣裳都已着了火。她径直朝我逼过来，那双枯萎干瘪的老手弯成爪状，像是要来抓我的脸。我动弹不得，可她径直从我身旁掠过，带起一股阴冷的寒气；我瞧见她到了墙边，到了姑妈叫做“壁龛”的那个去处——那是一处凹进去的空间，从前摆过一张讲究的大床，此刻一扇门大开着，她正把手伸进门里，在里头摸索着什么。我从没见过那扇门。接着她像一个上了轴的东西似的，转过身来朝向我，狞笑着，霎时间屋里一片漆黑，我发现自己竟已站到了床的另一头；我也不知自己是怎么过去的；我终于找回了舌头，发出一声尖叫，沿着长廊一路狂奔，险些把怀文太太的门从铰链上撞下来，把她吓得半死。

===Original===
Ye may guess I did na sleep that night; and wi’ the first light, down wi’ me to my aunt, as fast as my two legs cud carry me.

Well my aunt did na frump or flite me, as I thought she would, but she held me by the hand, and looked hard in my face all the time. And she telt me not to be feared; and says she:

“Hed the appearance a key in its hand?”

“Yes,” says I, bringin’ it to mind, “a big key in a queer brass handle.”

“Stop a bit,” says she, lettin’ go ma hand, and openin’ the cupboard-door. “Was it like this?” says she, takin’ one out in her fingers, and showing it to me, with a dark look in my face.

“That was it,” says I, quick enough.

“Are ye sure?” she says, turnin’ it round.

“Sart,” says I, and I felt like I was gain’ to faint when I sid it.

“Well, that will do, child,” says she, saftly thinkin’, and she locked it up again.

===Chinese===
您猜也猜得到，那一夜我没合眼；天一亮，我便撒开两腿，拼命地奔下楼去找姑妈。

哎，姑妈倒没有像我想的那样训我骂我，她只是握住我的手，自始至终紧紧地盯着我的脸。她叫我别怕；又说道：

“那形影手里可是拿着一把钥匙？”

“是的，”我回想了一下，说道，“一把大钥匙，配着个古怪的黄铜把手。”

“等一等，”她说着，松开我的手，打开了那只橱门，“可是像这一把？”她说着，用指头拈出一把钥匙来给我看，神色阴沉地望了我一眼。

“就是它，”我赶紧答道。

“你拿得准吗？”她把钥匙转了个身，问道。

“准，”我说，瞧见那钥匙时，我觉得自己快要晕过去了。

“好吧，这就够了，孩子，”她若有所思地轻声说，又把它锁了回去。

===Original===
“The squire himself will be here today, before twelve o’clock, and ye must tell him all about it,” says she, thinkin’, “and I suppose I’ll be leavin’ soon, and so the best thing for the present is, that ye should go home this afternoon, and I’ll look out another place for you when I can.”

Fain was I, ye may guess, at that word.

My aunt packed up my things for me, and the three pounds that was due to me, to bring home, and Squire Crowl himself came down to Applewale that day, a handsome man, about thirty years ald. It was the second time I sid him. But this was the first time he spoke to me.

===Chinese===
“乡绅本人今日午时之前就要到，”她寻思着说道，“这事你得原原本本地告诉他；我估摸着自己也待不长了，眼下最要紧的是，你今天下午就回家去，待我寻到了别的去处，再替你留意。”

您也猜得到，我听了这话心里多欢喜。

姑妈替我收拾好了衣裳，连我该得的那三镑工钱，也一并打点好让我带回家去。那天，克萝尔乡绅本人也到了阿普尔沃尔——是个约莫三十岁的英俊男子。那是我第二次见到他。可他和我说话，这还是头一回。

===Original===
My aunt talked wi’ him in the housekeeper’s room, and I don’t know what they said. I was a bit feared on the squire, he bein’ a great gentleman down in Lexhoe, and I darn’t go near till I was called. And says he, smilin’:

“What’s a’ this ye a sen, child? it mun be a dream, for ye know there’s na sic a thing as a bo or a freet in a’ the world. But whatever it was, ma little maid, sit ye down and tell all about it from first to last.”

Well, so soon as I made an end, he thought a bit, and says he to my aunt:

“I mind the place well. In old Sir Olivur’s time lame Wyndel told me there was a door in that recess, to the left, where the lassie dreamed she saw my grandmother open it. He was past eighty when he told me that, and I but a boy. It’s twenty year sen. The plate and jewels used to be kept there, long ago, before the iron closet was made in the arras chamber, and he told me the key had a brass handle, and this ye say was found in the bottom o’ the kist where she kept her old fans. Now, would not it be a queer thing if we found some spoons or diamonds forgot there? Ye mun come up wi’ us, lassie, and point to the very spot.”

===Chinese===
姑妈和他在管家屋里谈了话，他们说了些什么，我不知道。我有些怕那位乡绅——他在莱克斯霍一带是位了不起的大人物——我不敢凑上前去，直等到有人叫我。只见他笑着说道：

“你这孩子，你说你瞧见了这许多？那想必是个梦罢了，你知道，这世上压根儿没有什么鬼呀怪呀的东西。可不管那是怎么一回事，小姑娘，你坐下，从头到尾给咱们讲一遍。”

哎，我刚一讲完，他想了一想，便对我姑妈说道：

“那地方我记得清清楚楚。还是在老奥利弗爵士（Sir Olivur）在世的时候，瘸腿的温德尔（Wyndel）就告诉过我，说那处凹进去的墙壁左边有一扇门——也就是这小姑娘做梦瞧见我祖母打开的那一扇。他告诉我这话的时候，已是八十开外的人了，而我还不过是个孩子。算来已是二十年前的事了。从前，银盘和珠宝一向都是存放在那里的，直到后来那间挂着花毯的屋里做了铁橱才挪了地方；他还告诉我，那钥匙配的是黄铜把手；而你这把钥匙，你说是在她存放旧扇子的那只箱底找着的。这么看来，倘若我们在那儿寻着些被遗忘的银勺子、或是钻石，岂不是一桩奇事？小姑娘，你得跟我们一道上去，把那确切的地方指给我们看。”

===Original===
Loth was I, and my heart in my mouth, and fast I held by my aunt’s hand as I stepped into that awsome room, and showed them both how she came and passed me by, and the spot where she stood, and where the door seemed to open.

There was an ald empty press against the wall then, and shoving it aside, sure enough there was the tracing of a door in the wainscot, and a keyhole stopped with wood, and planed across as smooth as the rest, and the joining of the door all stopped wi’ putty the colour o’ yak, and, but for the hinges that showed a bit when the press was shoved aside, ye would not consayt there was a door there at all.

“Ha!” says he, wi’ a queer smile, “this looks like it.”

===Chinese===
我是一百个不愿意，心都提到了嗓子眼，可还是紧紧攥着姑妈的手，踏进了那间叫人胆寒的屋子，把那形影是如何出现、如何从我身旁掠过、她所站的位置、以及那扇门似乎打开的地方，一一指给他们两位看。

那时候，墙边立着一只空空的旧橱；把橱挪开，可不是么——护墙板上清清楚楚地现出一扇门的轮廓，锁眼用木塞堵着，刨得和周围一样平贴；门缝里全都填满了橡木颜色的油灰，若不是把橱挪开之后，铰链稍稍露出了一点点，您根本想不到那里头还有一扇门。

“哈！”他古怪地一笑，“看来就是它了。”

===Original===
It took some minutes wi’ a small chisel and hammer to pick the bit o’ wood out o’ the keyhole. The key fitted, sure enough, and, wi’ a strang twist and a lang skreak, the boult went back and he pulled the door open.

There was another door inside, stranger than the first, but the lacks was gone, and it opened easy. Inside was a narrow floor and walls and vault o’ brick; we could not see what was in it, for ’twas dark as pick.

When my aunt had lighted the candle, the squire held it up and stepped in.

My aunt stood on tiptoe tryin’ to look over his shouther, and I did na see nout.

===Chinese===
他拿一把小凿子和锤子，费了好几分钟才把锁眼里的木塞抠出来。那钥匙插进去，可不是正合适——使劲一拧，发出一声长长的吱嘎响，门闩退了回去，他便把门拉开了。

里头还有一道门，比外头这扇还要古怪，只是锁已经没了，一推便开。门里头是一处窄窄的地方，地面、墙壁、穹顶都是砖砌的；里面有什么，我们瞧不见，因为里头漆黑一片。

姑妈点亮了蜡烛，乡绅把蜡烛举高，跨了进去。

姑妈踮起脚，想从他的肩头上往里瞧，我呢，什么也没瞧见。

===Original===
“Ha! ha!” says the squire, steppin’ backward. “What’s that? Gi’ ma the poker—quick!” says he to my aunt. And as she went to the hearth I peeps beside his arm, and I sid squat down in the far corner a monkey or a flayin’ on the chest, or else the maist shrivelled up, wizzened ald wife that ever was sen on yearth.

“By Jen!” says my aunt, as puttin’ the poker in his hand, she keeked by his shouther, and sid the ill-favoured thing, “hae a care, sir, what ye’re doin’. Back wi’ ye, and shut to the door!”

But in place o’ that he steps in saftly, wi’ the poker pointed like a swoord, and he gies it a poke, and down it a’ tumbles together, head and a’, in a heap o’ bayans and dust, little meyar an’ a hatful.

===Chinese===
“哎呀！哎呀！”乡绅倒退了一步，叫道，“那是什么？——把拨火棍递给我——快！”他对姑妈说。姑妈往壁炉那边走去时，我从他的胳膊边偷偷一瞧，只见远处角落里、那只箱子上蹲着个东西——分不清是一只猴子，还是什么被剥了皮的活物，要不就是世上所见过的、最干瘪、最枯瘦的老妪。

“老天爷！”姑妈把拨火棍塞到他手里，从他肩头上探望了一眼，瞧见那副丑恶的模样，不由得失声叫道，“先生，您可小心着点儿！退出来，快把门关上！”

可他非但没有退，反而蹑手蹑脚地走进去，把拨火棍像一柄剑那样挺着，朝那东西戳了一下——只见那东西整个儿地瘫塌下来，连头带脑，化作一堆白骨和尘土，拢共还装不满一帽子。

===Original===
’Twas the bayans o’ a child; a’ the rest went to dust at a touch. They said nout for a while, but he turns round the skull, as it lay on the floor.

Young as I was, I consayted I knew well enough what they was thinkin’ on.

“A dead cat!” says he, pushin’ back and blowin’ out the can’le, and shuttin’ to the door. “We’ll come back, you and me, Mrs. Shutters, and look on the shelves by-and-by. I’ve other matters first to speak to ye about; and this little girl’s goin’ hame, ye say. She has her wages, and I mun mak’ her a present,” says he, pattin’ my shouther wi’ his hand.

===Chinese===
那是一个孩子的骸骨；其余的一切，一碰便化作了尘土。两人半晌没说话，只是他把躺地上的那颗头骨翻了翻。

我虽年幼，却也自以为十分明白他们俩心里在想什么。

“一只死猫！”他说着，往后退了一步，吹灭了蜡烛，把门关上。“咱们改日再回来，沙特斯太太，你和我，把架子上的东西细细瞧一瞧。我手头还有些别的事要先和你商量；还有，你说这小姑娘要回家了。她的工钱已给了，我还得赏她一件礼物，”他说着，伸手在我肩上拍了拍。

===Original===
And he did gimma a goud pound and I went aff to Lexhoe about an hour after, and sa home by the stagecoach, and fain was I to be at hame again; and I never sid Dame Crowl o’ Applewale, God be thanked, either in appearance or in dream, at-efter. But when I was grown to be a woman, my aunt spent a day and night wi’ me at Littleham, and she telt me there was no doubt it was the poor little boy that was missing sa lang sen, that was shut up to die thar in the dark by that wicked beldame, whar his skirls, or his prayers, or his thumpin’ cud na be heard, and his hat was left by the water’s edge, whoever did it, to mak’ belief he was drowned. The clothes, at the first touch, a’ ran into a snuff o’ dust in the cell whar the bayans was found. But there was a handful o’ jet buttons, and a knife with a green heft, together wi’ a couple o’ pennies the poor little fella had in his pocket, I suppose, when he was decoyed in thar, and sid his last o’ the light. And there was, amang the squire’s papers, a copy o’ the notice that was prented after he was lost, when the ald squire thought he might ’a run away, or bin took by gipsies, and it said he had a green-hefted knife wi’ him, and that his buttons were o’ cut jet. Sa that is a’ I hev to say consarnin’ ald Dame Crowl, o’ Applewale House.

===Chinese===
他果然赏了我一枚金镑；约莫一个钟头之后，我便动身去了莱克斯霍，从那里搭驿车回了家——能重新回到家里，我心里真是有说不出的欢喜；感谢上帝，从那以后，我再没见过阿普尔沃尔的克萝尔老太太，无论是显形还是在梦中。可等我长大成人之后，有一回姑妈到利特尔汉姆（Littleham）我处，与我同住了一天一夜；她告诉我，那具骸骨毫无疑问，正是当年失踪了那么久的那个可怜的小男孩——他是被那个狠毒的老妪关在那黑暗之中、活活等死的，任他怎样尖叫、怎样祷告、怎样捶打，都无人能听见；而不论这事究竟是谁下的手，那孩子的帽子被丢在水边，为的无非是叫人以为他是洗澡时淹死的。在那间寻得骸骨的密室里，那些衣裳头一碰便化成了一撮尘土。可还剩下寥寥一把黑玉扣子，一把绿柄的小刀，还有两枚铜板——想必是那可怜的小家伙受骗被诱进那地方去、最后瞧见一眼天光时，口袋里原有的东西。而在乡绅的文件当中，还存着一张那孩子失踪之后印发的寻人启事的抄本——那时候老乡绅还以为他也许是私逃了，或是叫吉普赛人拐走了；那启事上写着，他身边带着一把绿柄小刀，纽扣是刻花黑玉的。这便是关于阿普尔沃尔宅那位老克萝尔老太太，我所能讲给您听的全部了。

### Prologue / 前言

===Original===
On this case, Doctor Hesselius has inscribed nothing more than the words, "Harman's Report," and a simple reference to his own extraordinary essay on "The Interior Sense, and the Conditions of the Opening Thereof."

The reference is to Vol. I, Section 317, Note Za. The note to which reference is thus made, simply says: "There are two accounts of the remarkable case of the Honourable Mr. Justice Harbottle, one furnished to me by Mrs. Trimmer of Tunbridge Wells (June, 1805); the other at a much later date, by Anthony Harman, Esq. I much prefer the former; in the first place, because it is minute and detailed, and written, it seems to me, with more caution and knowledge; and in the next, because the letters from Doctor Hedstone, which are embodied in it, furnish matter of the highest value to a right apprehension of the nature of the case. It was one of the best declared cases of an opening of the interior sense, which I have met with. It was affected, too, by the phenomenon, which occurs so frequently as to indicate a law of these eccentric conditions; that is to say, it exhibited, what I may term, the contagious character of this sort of intrusion of the spirit-world upon the proper domain of matter. So soon as the spirit-action has established itself in the case of one patient, its developed energy begins to radiate, more or less effectually, upon others. The interior vision of the child was opened; as was, also, that of its mother, Mrs. Pyneweck; and both the interior vision and hearing of the scullery-maid, were opened on the same occasion. After-appearances are the result of the law explained in Vol. II. Section 17 to 49. The common centre of association, simultaneously recalled, unites, or *re*unites, as the case may be, for a period measured, as we see, in Section 37. The *maximum* will extend to days, the *minimum* is little more than a second. We see the operation of this principle perfectly displayed, in certain cases of lunacy, of epilepsy, of catalepsy, and of mania, of a peculiar and painful character, though unattended by incapacity of business."

===Chinese===
关于此案，赫塞利乌斯医生（Doctor Hesselius）只写下了"哈曼报告（Harman's Report）"几个字，并附了一处简单的引见，指向他自己那篇非凡的论文——论"内在感官（the interior sense）及其开启之条件"。

该引见指向第一卷第三百一十七节，注 Z a。被如此援及的那条注释，只这样写道："尊敬的哈博特尔法官大人（the Honourable Mr. Justice Harbottle）这一桩奇案，现存有两份记述，一份由坦布里奇韦尔斯（Tunbridge Wells）的特里默夫人（Mrs. Trimmer）提供（一八〇五年六月）；另一份时日甚晚，出自安东尼·哈曼先生（Anthony Harman, Esq.）。两相比较，我远为偏取前者；其一，因其细致而详尽，据我看来，下笔更为审慎、更见学识；其二，因其中所收录的赫德斯通医生（Doctor Hedstone）的几封书信，为正确领会此案的性质，提供了至为珍贵的材料。这是我所曾寓目的、内在感官开启之症候最为明晰的案例之一。此案且受一种现象所累，而该现象出现之频繁，已足可表明它是此类乖戾病况下的一条规律；换言之，它呈现出——姑且如此称之——灵异世界这般侵入物质本然之领域时所带的那种传染性特征。灵异之作用一旦在某一病人身上确立，其已然展开的势能，便开始向外辐射，或多或少地波及旁人。那孩子的内在视觉得以开启；其母派因内克夫人（Mrs. Pyneweck）的内在视觉亦然；而洗碗女佣的内在视觉与内在听觉，也于同一情形之下双双开启。此后种种再現之象，则是第二卷第十七至四十九节所阐释的那条定律所致。那被同时唤起的共同联想之核心，视情况而合、或复合，其历时之久暂，一如我们在第三十七节中所见。最长者可延及数日，最短者不过一瞬。这一原理的运作，在某些疯症、癫痫、僵症及一种特殊而痛苦的躁狂之症中——虽则并不妨碍患者经办事务——我们可见其展露无遗。"

===Original===
The memorandum of the case of Judge Harbottle, which was written by Mrs. Trimmer of Tunbridge Wells, which Doctor Hesselius thought the better of the two, I have been unable to discover among his papers. I found in his escritoire a note to the effect that he had lent the Report of Judge Harbottle's case, written by Mrs. Trimmer, to Doctor F. Heyne. To that learned and able gentleman accordingly I wrote, and received from him, in his reply, which was full of alarms and regrets on account of the uncertain safety of that "valuable MS.," a line written long since by Doctor Hesselius, which completely exonerated him, inasmuch as it acknowledged the safe return of the papers. The narrative of Mr. Harman, is, therefore, the only one available for this collection. The late Dr. Hesselius, in another passage of the note that I have cited, says, "As to the facts (non-medical) of the case, the narrative of Mr. Harman exactly tallies with that furnished by Mrs. Trimmer." The strictly scientific view of the case would scarcely interest the popular reader; and, possibly, for the purposes of this selection, I should, even had I both papers to choose between, have preferred that of Mr. Harman, which is given, in full, in the following pages.

===Chinese===
关于哈博特尔法官（Judge Harbottle）一案的备忘录，即由坦布里奇韦尔斯的特里默夫人所写、赫塞利乌斯医生视为两份中更为可取的那一份，我在他的遗稿之中遍寻无着。我只在他的书桌里寻见一纸便笺，言明他曾把特里默夫人所写的那份哈博特尔法官一案报告，借予了 F. 海涅医生（Doctor F. Heyne）。于是我便致函那位博学干练的先生，收到他的回函；回函之中，因那部"珍贵手稿"之安危未卜而满纸惊惶与憾惜，并附有一行赫塞利乌斯医生多年前所写的字迹，此行字迹将他开脱得干干净净——其中明言承认，那些文件早已安然归还。因此，哈曼先生的记述，便成了可供本集使用的唯一一份。已故的赫塞利乌斯医生，在我所援引的那张便笺的另一处说道："至于此案（非医学方面）的事实，哈曼先生的记述与特里默夫人所提供的那份，恰相吻合。"此案严格科学一面的看法，怕是难以引起普通读者的兴趣；而且，就算两份记述都摆在我眼前任我取舍，就本选集的用意而言，我多半也仍会偏取哈曼先生这一份。该份记述，全文具载于以下诸页。

## I Aunt Margaret at Home / 一、玛格丽特姑母在家

===Original===
My Aunt Margaret was what is termed a clever woman—that is to say, she was keen and resolute, prompt and active, and difficult to overreach in matters of money or business. Of the former she was, people said, a little too fond. At all events she hated waste, and lived frugally on a dietary which leaned much upon tea and eggs, and sometimes omitted dinner altogether. But though light, her housekeeping was neither beggarly nor altogether uncomfortable.

Aunt Margaret, as I remember her—dear me, how many years ago!—was rather tall, if anything, and decidedly slim and erect, with a countenance which, though shrewd and energetic, had yet something kindly in it. Her features were small and nicely turned, and one could quite suppose that she might have been a pretty girl once on a time.

===Chinese===
我的玛格丽特姑母（Aunt Margaret）是世人所谓的那种"能干女人"——也就是说，她精明果决，敏捷勤勉，凡银钱、生意上的事，很难叫人占了便宜去。至于银钱一桩，人们说她未免爱得过分了些。无论如何，她痛恨靡费，度日极为节俭，饭菜多倚重茶与鸡蛋，有时索性连正餐也一并省去。不过她的治家虽清淡，却既不寒酸，也不至于叫人浑身不得舒坦。

玛格丽特姑母——凭我所记得的模样，天哪，已是多少年前的事了！——身量若说高挑，则稍稍偏高，身段确是清瘦挺拔；面相虽精明强干，却仍含着几分和气。她五官生得小巧端正，叫人尽可揣想，她少时想必也曾是个俏丽的姑娘。

===Original===
She held herself well, and stepped with a good, firm tread, and lightly withal. Hers was a rustic life, somewhat lonely, in a three-storied house, with three rooms on a floor, and a gable at front—steep-roofed and tiled, and with a great growth of jessamine and woodbine about the porch and the windows. Half a dozen tall, dark elms made a comfortable shadow about the house; and a white paling in front enclosed, by the roadside, the little flower garden, with an old mulberry tree in the centre.

In the rear was a lockup yard with coach-house and stable, and a comfortable room in which old Tom Clinton slept with a blunderbuss and backsword in case of robbers. On weekdays Aunt Margaret dressed very plainly—stuff in winter, cotton in summer; but on Sundays she went to church in thick old satins or ancient brocades, so stiff that the squire's lady across the aisle used to talk of them covetously for days after, and wonder why such things were not to be had nowadays.

Aunt Margaret was always particularly neat. She used to carry her keys in an old-fashioned way, from a ribbon by her side, a neat little pincushion, her scissors, and I forget what else. It was the tradition of that chatelaine which I saw revived long after poor Aunt Margaret had gone to her rest. She had long and very pretty hands—her years considered; and, in fact, the only thing I remember decidedly against her was her enamelled box of rappee, and the habit to which it ministered.

===Chinese===
她身姿挺拔，步履沉稳有力，却又举步轻盈。她过的是乡间日子，颇有些清寂，住在一幢三层小楼里，每层三间房，正面一堵山墙——屋顶陡峭，覆着瓦片，门廊与窗前爬满了素馨与忍冬。屋旁立着六七株高大幽暗的榆树，投下一片惬意的浓荫；屋前路边，一道白色木栅栏围着一个小花园，园子正中是一棵老桑树。

屋后是一所可上锁的院落，内设车房与马厩，另有一间舒适的屋子，老汤姆·克林顿（Tom Clinton）就歇在那儿，手边备着一杆大口径短枪和一柄背剑，以防盗贼。平日里，玛格丽特姑母衣着极为朴素——冬日穿毛料，夏日穿棉布；可一到礼拜天，她上教堂时却身着厚实的老缎子或古旧的锦缎，料子硬挺得很，竟引得走道对面的乡绅夫人一连好几天眼红地念叨，纳罕如今怎么再寻不着那样的好东西了。

玛格丽特姑母向来格外整洁。她按老派的法子，把钥匙系在腰间一条缎带上，另有一只精致的小针插、一把剪刀，还有些什么，我已记不真切了。这原是那种女主人腰链（chatelaine）的旧传统，直到可怜的姑母长眠之后许久，我才又见人重新时兴起来。论她的年纪，那双手可算是修长秀美得很了；事实上，我惟一能确然记起叫人不敢恭维之处，便是她那只描金的鼻烟盒，以及它所伺候的那桩癖好。

===Original===
Her prime-minister was Winnifred Dobbs—fattish, rosy, ancient. Time *had* thinned her flowing hair, and bleached it somewhat; but she smiled largely, and was good-humoured; although not very quick, was steady and sure, and chatted volubly, though not always much to the purpose; and Aunt Margaret gave her her tea in the drawing-room, which was an excuse for keeping her there for the rest of the evening; and so Aunt Margaret was not quite so lonely as she might have been.

There was a young and stumpy girl beside, who washed, and did nearly everything, and must have found these young days rather dull. To her the view of the road from the kitchen window was a resource, and the occasional calls of the baker, butcher, and dairyman were precious. She talked and laughed with herself; she sang a great deal in the scullery, and joked with the cat in the kitchen.

Among Aunt Margaret's sources of revenue was her moiety of what she called the Winderbrooke property. Everybody, of course, knows the old town of Winderbrooke. Three houses in the main street belonged to her and her sister. Of these, for convenience, they made a division, the best they could. Aunt Margaret had for her share a tobacconist and half a tailor. The latter was punctual; but the tobacconist owed a whole year's rent, and was already some way in his third half-year. His letters were highly unsatisfactory. The tailor's answers to her inquiries about his defaulting neighbour were reserved and evasive. But that she had a wise terror of law and lawyers my Aunt would have retained an attorney forthwith.

===Chinese===
她的"首相"是威尼弗雷德·多布斯（Winnifred Dobbs）——身形微胖，面色红润，年纪已是不轻。岁月虽使她那一头长发稀疏了些，也褪淡了几分颜色；可她笑容宽厚，性情和顺；虽不太机敏，却稳重可靠，说起话来滔滔不绝，只是未必句句着边际；玛格丽特姑母让她在起居室里与自己同饮茶水，借此名目留她在那儿消磨余下的夜晚——姑母的日子，便也不至于像本可能的那般孤寂了。

另有一个矮胖的小丫头在帮衬着，洗衣并几乎包揽了一切活计，这些年纪轻轻的日子在她想必颇为乏味。于她而言，从厨房窗口望出去的那一段路，便是一种消遣；面包师傅、肉铺老板、送牛奶的人偶尔登门，更是难得的乐事。她自个儿跟自个儿说笑；在洗碗房里放声高唱；在厨房里与那只猫逗趣取乐。

玛格丽特姑母的进项之一，是她所谓"温德布鲁克产业"（Winderbrooke property）里她应得的那一份。那座古城温德布鲁克（Winderbrooke），自然是人尽皆知。大街上有三幢房子，归她与妹妹所有。为图省事，姐妹俩尽了最大努力把它分作两份。玛格丽特姑母名下分到的是一个烟铺、半个裁缝铺。后者交租准时；那烟铺老板却整整欠了一年租金，且已在这第三个半年度里又拖欠了一程。他的来信推三阻四，极不令人满意。姑母向那裁缝打听这位赖账邻居的情形，裁缝的回话却含糊其辞、闪闪烁烁。若不是姑母对打官司和律师一途怀有明智的忌惮，她早就把一位讼师延揽到门下了。

===Original===
"I'm not suprised, Winnie," said my Aunt, snuffing her candle, as she and her confidential handmaid sat by the fire, in her diminutive drawing-room, at their tea; "not the least. Did you ever know one man tell of another when a woman was concerned? John Pendle has been my tenant eleven years and knows all about that roguish snuff-man; but he won't tell me one iota about him. Not that Browning is anything on earth to him. I suppose he doesn't care if Browning was hanged; but simply Browning is a man, and *I a woman.* That's it, Winnie—that's *all*—*I*'m to be robbed, and no one to prevent it. A conspiracy I call it. I tell you, Winnie, I never knew one man prevent another's robbing a woman, except when he hoped to rob her himself."

===Chinese===
"我一点儿也不奇怪，威妮，"姑母说着，剪了剪烛花。此刻她与那贴身心腹的女仆正坐在那间小小的起居室里，依着炉火喝茶。"一点儿也不。你几时见过一个男人肯揭发另一个男人的——只要里头牵涉到一个女人？约翰·彭德尔（John Pendle）做我的房客十一年了，那个卖鼻烟的无赖，他底细尽知；可他半个字也不肯透露给我。倒不是布朗宁（Browning）跟他有什么相干。我看布朗宁就是上了绞架，他也不在乎；只不过是——布朗宁是个男人，而我是个女人。症结就在这里，威妮——就是这么回事——活该我被人劫掠，却没有一个人肯拦一拦。我管这叫串通一气。我告诉你，威妮，我从没见过一个男人肯去拦阻另一个男人劫掠女人——除非他自己也想劫掠那个女人。"

===Original===
Honest Dobbs's fat face and round eyes looked distressed over her teacup at her mistress, while she discoursed; and she made answer only by that expressive but unspellable tick-tick-ticking made by the tip of the tongue at the back of the teeth.

"And rob me they would, Winnie, if I were half such a fool as you, for instance. But I'll show them there are women who do know something of business."

And she nodded mysteriously, but briskly, on her maid with a side-glance of her dark eye.

"I mean to start tomorrow morning, after breakfast, at eight o'clock. You come with me, Winnie, and we'll sleep tomorrow night at Winderbrooke, and *that*, I think, will surprise them."

===Chinese===
诚实的多布斯听她这般高谈阔论，隔着茶杯，那张胖脸和那双圆眼睛望着女主人，神情很是为难；她惟一的回答，不过是舌尖抵着牙背所发出的那种意味深长、却无法形诸文字的"嗒、嗒、嗒"声。

"他们就是要劫掠我呀，威妮，倘若我有你一半的蠢的话。可我要叫他们瞧瞧，世上也有懂点生意经的女人。"

说着，她朝那女仆神秘而利落地一点头，那双乌黑的眼睛顺势斜睨了一下。

"我打算明儿一早吃了早饭，八点钟动身。你跟我一道去，威妮，明儿夜里我们就歇在温德布鲁克——这一着，我想，准叫他们吃一惊。"

## Some Gossip About Chapelizod / 查佩利佐德闲话

===Original===
Ghosts in Chapelizod, my good sir! "Why who knows not so?" A place that is itself a shadow of things past, the living spectre of old times. Chapelizod is all a ghost. If anyone desires to see a suburban village of the once proud city of Dublin reduced to a marrowless skeleton, without a single speculation in its eye by which it can ever hope to rise again, let him go to Chapelizod. Dead walls; dead trees overhanging them; dead lights instead of windows in the houses; the men grave, the women lifeless, the little spirits squeaking and gibbering in the muddy streets! A veritable *caput mortuum* is Chapelizod. No wonder that Bob Martin should fancy he saw a ghost, for he was always looking at one.

===Chinese===
查佩利佐德的鬼魂，我的好先生！"嘿，谁不知道这个？"这地方本身就是往昔事物的影子，是旧日时光的一具活鬼魂。查佩利佐德整个儿就是一个鬼。谁要是想瞧瞧一度骄傲的都柏林（Dublin）城郊那座村庄，如今怎样被抽干了骨髓、剩下一副毫无眼色的空骨架，再没有一丝重振声威的指望——那就让他到查佩利佐德来看看吧。死寂的墙垣；墙头探出的枯死老树；屋子里的窗户，只透出死气沉沉的光；男人们神情凝重，女人们了无生气，小孩子们在那泥泞的街道上叽叽喳喳、叽里咕噜地闹腾！查佩利佐德，真真切切是一具 *caput mortuum*——一具死灰般的残骸。鲍勃·马丁（Bob Martin）会以为他瞧见了鬼，这又有什么好奇怪的？因为他本就成天瞪着一具活鬼瞧呢。

===Original===
It is just fifty years since Chapelizod was marked for the silent tomb, and condemned to perish by a lingering death. The cold hand of Centralisation, long before the insatiable monster was known by that name, clutched its first victim in Chapelizod. I barely remember the event. A heavy storm came down from the west; great rains had previously descended, and the angry spirit of the river screeched. I heard it myself running under the skew arch of the old bridge. There was lightning in the sky, and the clouds flew across the face of the moon like mad things. As yet the air was calm on the surface of the earth, but towards midnight the gale arose and tore up a number of trees in the Park. Before twenty-four hours we all perceived how easy it would have been to foresee what was coming, for in the course of the forenoon the order arrived for disbanding the Royal Irish Artillery. It was now no longer a mystery why it had blown great guns all the night.

===Chinese===
查佩利佐德被盖上了那方寂静墓园的印记、被判了凌迟处死，到如今恰恰五十年了。中央集权（Centralisation）那只冷手——虽说这只饕餮巨怪许久之后才得了这么个名号——抓的头一个祭品，便是查佩利佐德。那桩事我依稀还记得。一场狂风暴雨打西边压将下来；此前连降了几场大雨，河里那愤怒的水神嘶声尖啸。我亲耳听见那水流从老桥那座斜拱底下奔涌而过。半空里有电闪，云团像发了疯一般掠过月面。其时地面上的空气倒还平静，可一到午夜，狂飙骤起，把公园（the Park）里好些大树连根拔起。不到二十四小时，众人这才恍然——原来事先要看出这场祸事何等容易——因为那天上午命令到了：解散皇家爱尔兰炮兵团（Royal Irish Artillery）。头一晚整夜狂风怒号、如炮声轰鸣，到这里再也不是什么谜了。

===Original===
That was the first special act of centralisation—always excepting the fatal centripetal movement from the house in College-green—which was perpetrated against Ireland. The glory of our national service was then extinguished, and Woolwich was made the arsenal sole of the United Kingdom. The royal regiment was broken up, its guns transferred to Sarah Bridge, its veterans drafted—as many of them as thought proper to merge their name in an undistinguished throng—into the general service, and not a few who had grown old in the troop found an asylum in the Royal Hospital at Kilmainham.

===Chinese===
那是头一项针对爱尔兰的特殊的中央集权之举——若不算从学院草坪（College-green）那所宅子发端的那场致命的向心运动的话。我国民族军务的荣光就此熄灭，伍利奇（Woolwich）成了联合王国独一的兵工厂。皇家兵团就此解体，它的大炮被调往萨拉桥（Sarah Bridge），那些老兵——其中凡是愿意把自己所在兵团的名号并入一支素无特色的乌合之众的——都被编入常规军；而不少在部队里熬白了头的人，则到基尔曼纳姆（Kilmainham）皇家医院（Royal Hospital）里寻了一处养老之所。

===Original===
The transition of an old soldier from Chapelizod to Kilmainham was easy, the principal change consisting in putting off a blue coat to put on a red. They were not required to seek unaccustomed seats, or new associations among strangers, in whom the very accents of their tongue would awaken a prejudice against them, and make them objects of vulgar derision; but they dropped gently down the vale of years, amongst their own countrymen, near scenes hallowed to memory, still looking upon those hills which had exhilarated their hearts in the pride and prime of life, and inhaling breezes, wafted down the stream, which had braced and invigorated their lusty sinews, when they were "strong swimmers." They had friends and kindred at the old quarter, whom they continued to visit on festive occasions, "at the season of the year;" and it was pleasant to see the hearty old fellows, in their new "coats of scarlet," on the king's birthday or a Whitsun-Monday, mixing with the crowd of villagers; one leading a little grandson by the hand, another engaged in cheering converse with a married daughter, or linked with some civil *remanet* of the bygone century, with whom, peradventure, he had quaffed many a social cup of ale; and all climbing the green slope that overhangs the Liffey, on their way to the grand review.

===Chinese===
一个老兵从查佩利佐德转入基尔曼纳姆，过渡是容易的，主要的变化不过是脱下蓝外套、换上红外套罢了。他们不必去寻生疏的座次，也不必在陌生人堆里另结新交——在那些人中间，他们一开口的口音便会勾起偏见，叫他们沦为庸俗嘲弄的对象；他们只是在自己同胞之间，在记忆所系的圣景之畔，沿着岁月的山谷悄然下行；他们仍望着那些山峦——那是他们壮盛之年得意之时曾叫他们心怀振奋的；他们仍吸着那顺流而下的微风——那是当年他们尚是"强健的泅者"时，曾叫他们筋骨强健、气力壮盛的。他们在老营盘里有朋友故旧，每逢佳节——"一年当令之时"——仍照旧去拜访；看着那些热心肠的老家伙，穿了新"猩红外套"，在国王诞辰或圣灵降临节的礼拜一，混在村民的人群里，那光景真叫人欢喜：一个牵着小孙子的小手，一个正与已经出嫁的女儿热络叙话，还有一个，胳膊挽着上个世纪遗下来的某位体面的 *remanet*（悬案老友），也许当年还曾与此人共饮过不知多少杯亲热的麦酒；众人一齐爬上那俯瞰利菲河（the Liffey）的青翠斜坡，往那场盛大的阅兵式去了。

===Original===
By degrees, as years rolled on, the bright red spots in that moving picture died out; but it was a consoling reflection to those who turned their thoughts to the evidence thus afforded of the sure and silent work of death, that the ties of life had not been abruptly or prematurely torn asunder by the cold hands of centralizing economy. They who had served their country faithfully and loyally in their youth, were suffered to live out their full time, solaced by those attentions and sympathies, dearer far than the charity of dry rations, which public gratitude, aiding and giving effect to royal bounty, ungrudgingly secured for them.

But our new generation is wiser than to care for the feelings of men. The *heart* of this United Kingdom beats only and exclusively in the centre of its body; and thither all the lifeblood of the land must flow. It may one day be found out, when pulsation refuses to answer at the extremities, that it is possible to overgorge the ventricles of that huge organ. At present, however, it is resolved to "take in all," regardless alike of charters, of rights, of common sense, and of common humanity. The Royal Hospital at Kilmainham is doomed to extinction.

===Chinese===
随着年复一年地流转，那幅活动的画面上那一处处鲜红的亮色，渐渐熄灭了；然而对于那些回心思考死亡那无声无息、却又笃定不息的勾当所留证据的人，却有一桩足以慰藉的念想：生命的种种纽带，并未被那中央集权经济（centralizing economy）的冷手骤然或过早地扯断。那些少年时忠心耿耿为国效力的人，得以享尽天年，有那些体贴与同情相伴宽慰——这可比干巴巴配给的口粮所值的那点慈善，要珍贵得太多——而公共的感恩之心，又助皇家的恩俸得以落实，毫无吝啬地为他们稳稳地保障了下来。

可是我们这一代新人，自作聪明，哪还顾得上体恤别人的心绪。这个联合王国（United Kingdom）的 *心脏*，只在本国的正中央跳动；而全国所有生命的血液，便非得尽数涌到那里去不可。有朝一日，待到四肢末梢再也搏动不起半点脉息之时，说不定人们才会发现：那只庞大脏器的心室，原来也是撑得爆的。然而眼下，他们铁了心要"一概收下"，全不顾特许状、不顾权利、不顾常识、也不顾起码的人道。基尔曼纳姆皇家医院（Royal Hospital at Kilmainham）已判了死刑。

===Original===
It seems nothing that it was founded by royal charter, and by a rate levied upon the pay of soldiers serving in the army of Ireland, "to the end that such of the said army as have faithfully served their sovereign in the strength and vigour of their youth may, in the weakness and disaster that their old age, wounds, or other misfortunes may bring them into, find a comfortable retreat and a competent maintenance therein." It was endowed with lands, by an instrument which provides that "within the precincts of those lands shall be from henceforth, and shall *forever* hereafter continue and be an hospital, in deed and name, for the receipt, abiding, and dwelling of such a number of poor, aged, maimed, and infirm soldiers, to be lodged, harboured, abide, and be relieved therein." The charter by which Trinity College holds its estates is not more sacred, nor the perpetual uses to which they must be applied more distinctly defined. Yet the Queen's government, upon its own mere motion and authority, has taken upon itself to root out this time-honoured foundation. The maimed and aged Irish soldier must henceforth find a "comfortable retreat" in Chelsea, where the voice of kinsman or friend will greet him no more. The sights and sounds, which bring back the days of youth with such a homefelt and soothing power to the memory of the aged, will be excluded from his eyes and ears, and he will die in cheerless exile, an unhappy and unthankful recipient of imperial alms.

===Chinese===
它依据皇家特许状而建，经费出自爱尔兰驻军军饷所课的一笔税，"以使该军中那些于少壮气盛之时忠心侍奉过君主者，在老弱、伤病或其它不幸所招致的衰颓境况中，得在其中寻一处舒适的退居之所与一份相当之赡养"——这些竟全然不算数了！它蒙赐土地，其文书明定："在此土地范围之内，自今而后，将、且将 *永远* 继续为一所医院，名副其实，用以收容、安置、栖居如许数目之贫、老、伤、弱之兵士，使之在其中得受收留、栖身、驻扎并获救济。"三一学院（Trinity College）执掌其产业所依的那道特许状，并未比此更见神圣；其产业须充作之恒久用途，亦未比此规定得更清楚。然而女王陛下政府，竟自行动议、自行做主，悍然铲除了这座历久弥尊的基业。从此，伤残与年迈的爱尔兰兵士，只好到切尔西（Chelsea）去寻他的"舒适退居之所"了——在那里，亲人与友人的声音，再也唤不到他的耳边。那些能把少壮年华如此温情而熨帖地唤回老人记忆的景象与声响，都将从他耳目之前尽数屏除；他将在凄凉的异乡了却残生，做一个郁郁寡欢、受之有愧的帝国施舍的领受者。

===Original===
It was well for the survivors of our National Artillery, that the faith of royal charters, and the kindly feelings of human nature were respected in their days. They had the satisfaction to feel, to their latest moment, that they possessed a country, and that their country had no disposition to disown them; so their end was peace.

===Chinese===
我国国家炮兵的幸存者们总算还算运气——他们当年，皇家特许状的信用、人情天性中的厚道，都还算受着敬重。他们直到咽气那一刻，都能心满意足地感到：自己有一个祖国，而祖国并无半点要将他们抛弃不顾的意思；于是，他们的结局是平静的。

===Original===
Beside those who took service in the British army, or who retired for the remainder of their lives into the shelter provided for them in "the Hospital of King Charles the Second," there were many who, laying aside the military character, merged in the general body of society, and occupied themselves variously in civil employments, according to their natural leanings or abilities. Some few, who had adorned the old brigade in its palmy estate, disdained to quit the scene of its renown, but lingered about the ancient haunts till, one by one, they dropped into the grave. There was General Bettesworth, and his orderly man John Norton. The general inhabited a pretty place, now sadly dismantled, by the river side, and John was his gatekeeper. It was a sight to see them both stepping out for the parish church at Christmas, and the other high festivals, in the full uniform of their respective ranks, powdered, pomatum'd, and bequeued, as if they were sallying forth to be reviewed by Frederick William of Prussia. If Corporal Trim left a representative after him, it was John Norton: stiff in opinion, erect in stature, simple and honest as a child, pious as a parson. His master had all the gentle parts of human nature blended with the same high courage which distinguished my Uncle Toby.

===Chinese===
那些或者投效英军、或者退居"查理二世国王医院"（the Hospital of King Charles the Second）所备养老之所度过余生的人之外，还有不少，他们卸下军伍身份，融入社会一般大众，各按天性禀赋，在民间差事上各有营生。也有少数几位，曾为旧日兵团最辉煌岁月锦上添花，不屑于离开它功名所系之地，仍徘徊流连于旧日出入之所，直到一个一个地相继入土。其中有贝特斯沃思将军（General Bettesworth），以及他的勤务兵约翰·诺顿（John Norton）。将军住在河畔一处如今已破败不堪的漂亮宅子里，约翰便是他的看门人。每到圣诞节及其他重大节令，看他们俩一同步行去教区教堂，那可真是一景：两人都按各自军阶穿戴齐整的全套制服，扑了粉、抹了发膏、拖着小辫子，仿佛是要出门去接受普鲁士腓特烈·威廉（Frederick William of Prussia）的检阅似的。倘若特里姆下士（Corporal Trim）在世上留下了什么代表，那便是约翰·诺顿了：他主意硬、身板挺、心地质朴诚实如孩童、虔诚如牧师。他的主人则兼具人性中所有温厚的品性，又配上那份与我的托比叔叔（Uncle Toby）同样卓尔不群的英勇气概。

===Original===
Is it not strange how many people claim relation to "Uncle Toby?" Nobody thinks of calling him Tristram Shandy's uncle. He is "my uncle," your uncle, everybody's uncle. Sterne has managed to infuse that sweet touch into his nature, which makes the whole world kin to him, and proud to acknowledge it. But this by the by.

===Chinese===
居然有这许多人自称与"托比叔叔"沾亲带故，岂非怪事一桩？谁也不曾想到叫他特里斯特拉姆·项狄（Tristram Shandy）的叔叔。他是"我的叔叔"，是你的叔叔，是大家的叔叔。斯特恩（Sterne）竟设法在他身上注入了那一缕甜美的笔触，叫全世界的人都与他沾亲，并以认这门亲为荣。不过，这且按下不表。

===Original===
An anecdote may here be related which illustrates the character of those primitive soldiers, and of the discipline of the service at the close of the eighteenth century. It happened one morning that John Norton was late at parade, and, as men sometimes do when they are hurried, he had made a mistake in his equipments, having put on his cross-belts wrong.

"Why, John Norton," said the general, "how is this? you have put on your belts the wrong way."

The men began to laugh, and John's ire was kindled; but he was too proud to look at his right hand or his left, to examine into the truth of the case.

"No, general," said he, "I have not."

"Oh but, indeed, John, you have."

"By all that's bad, general," said John, who had a trick of interlarding his discourse with this extraordinary invocation, "I have not."

"Well, then," said the patient commander, "we'll try. Fall in, John Norton. Attention! Carry arms! Prime and load."

All these manoeuvres did John go through, like an automaton, until the last, when, laying his hand upon a bayonet where his cartouch-box ought to be, he exclaimed—

"By all that's bad, general, you're right."

===Chinese===
这里不妨讲一桩轶事，既可见出那些质朴老兵的性格，也可略窥十八世纪末军队的军纪面貌。话说某天早晨，约翰·诺顿迟到了，而人一急便常常忙中出错——他把交叉皮带戴反了。

"哎呀，约翰·诺顿，"将军说，"这是怎么回事？你的皮带戴反了。"

众兵士笑了起来，约翰心头火起；但他太要面子，不肯低头看看自己的左手或右手，去核实一下此事是否果真如此。

"没有啊将军，"他说，"我没戴反。"

"噢，可是，约翰，你当真戴反了。"

"我向天发誓，将军，"约翰说——他有句口头禅，每每要在话里夹上这么一句古怪的发誓——"我没戴反。"

"那么好吧，"这位耐心的统帅说，"我们来试试。立正，约翰·诺顿。听令！持枪！装填弹药！"

约翰像个自动木偶一般，一一照做了这些动作，直到最后那一个——他伸手往本该是弹药盒（cartouch-box）的位置上一摸，却摸着了一把刺刀，便叫道——

"我向天发誓，将军，您说得对。"

===Original===
According to the present strict rules of discipline in the British army a file of men would have been ordered to march so refractory a subject off to the guardhouse; and if he were not tried by a regimental court-martial for insubordination, he might deem himself a fortunate individual. At all events, "good conduct" would never afterwards, should he continue in the service to the age of the Duke of Wellington, emblazon his discharge. But John Norton walked home beside the general's horse listening, with a meek and subdued spirit, to a friendly lecture upon the wisdom of sometimes supposing that others may be in the right as well as one's self.

===Chinese===
按如今英军森严的军纪，这样一名倔强分子，少不得要派一队人把他押去禁闭室；若不被团的军事法庭以抗命罪起诉，他便可算是侥幸的幸运儿了。无论如何，"品行优良"四字，从他往后的履历上是再也别指望见到了——哪怕他在军中一直干到威灵顿公爵（Duke of Wellington）那把年纪。可约翰·诺顿却走在将军的马旁，一路走回家，怀着一颗温顺谦卑的心，听将军友善地训诫他一番——大旨是说：有时候也要设想一下，旁人说不定也是对的，并不只有自己才对。

===Original===
At the other side of the river, nearly opposite to General Bettesworth's, but close to the village, are two adjoining brick houses, somewhat removed from the road. In one of these lived and died General Stratton. The other was occupied by Major Legge. The general was a venerable Ligonier-like man, and his wife a stately matron of the olden time, whom I seem to see this moment, with her stomacher and brocaded dress, and a long narrow scarf trimmed with the richest lace; her grey locks turned up, like flax round a distaff, over her forehead, and a towering bonnet of black silk over all. She was deemed a proud woman, but very good to the poor. As to her pride, I have heard no proof of it, except that she kept the village gossips at bay; but the reputation of her goodness is incontestable.

===Chinese===
河对岸，与贝特斯沃思将军的宅子几乎遥遥相对，却又紧挨村子的地方，有两所毗连的砖屋，离大路略有些距离。其中一所，是斯特拉顿将军（General Stratton）住过并在其中辞世的。另一所，则由莱格少校（Major Legge）住着。将军是个气度庄严的人物，颇有利戈尼尔（Ligonier）之风；他的太太则是旧时代一位仪态端方的贵妇——我此刻仿佛仍能看见她：胸前缀着胸衣饰带，身着锦缎衣裙，肩上披着一条用最上等花边镶边的又长又窄的围巾；两鬓斑白的发丝，像绕在纺锤上的亚麻一般卷在额前，最上头还戴着一顶高耸的黑绸软帽。人皆道她高傲，但她对穷人却极好。至于她的高傲，除却她常把镇上那班爱嚼舌根的人拒之千里之外，我可不曾听过别的实据；然而她心地善良的名声，却是不容置疑的。

===Original===
An Emeritus of a lower grade, but more formidable than the whole *Etat Major* to the juvenile imagination, was William Oulton Prosser, who from the post of a bombardier had retired to Ballyfermot Castle, where he opened an "academy" of liberal instruction. I still quail to remember him. It was only the other day that his name, written in round-hand across the title page of a *Trusler's Chronology*, purchased at Sharpe's auction-room, sent a thrill through me, as if it had been the wind of a round shot. He was a tall, stern-looking pedagogue, who never came down from his bedroom before eleven o'clock in the forenoon; and then he despatched a dirty servant-boy into the schoolroom, which was detached from the castle, to summon the boys on the black list to come in and be whipped. That operation he performed as if he had served in no other rank than that of a drummer all the days of his "sogering" upon earth; and it was administered in the breakfast parlour amid the debris of the repast (bread and butter and eggshells), which the giant had just demolished to give him strength for the task. It had been his wont to inflict condign discipline in the midst of the school; but it happened on a day, that a boy, whose name was included in the usher's report, lay in ambush behind a heap of coats, in the porch; and as the ogre passed through, flourishing the formidable taws, and "chewing vengeance all the way," the poor wretch, in a frenzy of terror and despair, flew upon him, as a cat driven wild by persecution, and bit a large piece out of the calf of his leg. The big tyrant limped away into his den, and swore upon the family Bible that he would never again set foot in the said schoolroom, and that he would whip the said boy. He kept both the oaths, "in a sort of way," being obliged to compromise the matter with the delinquent, who agreed to save his Christian master's conscience, only on condition that the word of promise should be broken to the *hope*. A shadowy castigation, therefore (the ghost of a whipping), was submitted but from that hour the main business of the academy was carried on by deputies, remote from the eye of the master. He still continued, however, to perform the part of an high justiciary, and to take cognizance of copybooks and arithmetical exercises, which the boys were required to exhibit to him in procession.

===Chinese===
另有一位级别略低些的退役者，但他对孩童的想象力而言，却比一整支 *参谋部*（*Etat Major*）还要可怖——这便是威廉·奥尔顿·普罗瑟（William Oulton Prosser），他从一等兵（bombardier）的职位上退下来，到巴利弗莫特城堡（Ballyfermot Castle）开办了一所"博雅教化"的"学馆"。至今回想起来，我仍要打个寒噤。前些日子，我在夏普拍卖行（Sharpe's auction-room）买了一本《特拉斯勒编年史》（*Trusler's Chronology*），扉页上用圆体字写着他的名字，那笔迹竟叫我浑身一激灵，仿佛是实弹擦身的风声。他是个身材高大、神色冷峻的教书匠，每日午前十一时之前从不下楼；届时，他便差遣一个肮脏的小听差进那所与城堡分开的学馆，把榜上有名的学童叫进去挨打。他做这件事的派头，仿佛他这大半辈子在军中——他管当兵叫"sogering"——就只当过一名鼓手似的；行刑的地点是早餐间，四周还散落着那位巨人刚刚狼吞虎咽下去的那顿早饭的残骸（面包屑、黄油与蛋壳）——他正是为了这项任务才填饱了肚子的。他原有一贯的规矩，要在学馆正中当众施此严刑；可偏巧有那么一天，一个上了副手告状名单的孩子，躲在门廊里一堆外套后头埋伏着；那妖怪一手挥舞着可怕的皮鞭（taws），一路"嚼着满嘴的复仇"，从门廊里穿过——那可怜虫在恐惧与绝望的狂乱中，像一只被追逼得发了疯的猫，扑将上去，从他小腿肚上咬下了一大块肉来。这个大暴君一瘸一拐地钻回了自己的窝，对着家传的《圣经》起誓：他再也不踏进那所学馆一步了，却一定要把那个孩子狠狠地揍一顿。这两条誓言他倒都守了——"也算是守了吧"——因为他不得不与那罪魁私下里达成一笔交易：那孩子答应保全他这位基督徒先生的良心，唯一的条件是，那"许下的话"必须打个折扣，留个 *指望*（*hope*）给他。于是一通虚应故事的责罚（一通鞭子的鬼魂）便算交了差；但从那以后，学馆里主要的事务都由副手们代理，离先生那双眼睛远远的了。不过，他仍继续扮演着大法官的角色，对抄写本与算术作业照旧要亲自过问；孩子们须排成一队，鱼贯而入，到他跟前呈验。

===Original===
The remainder of his day was occupied principally in attending to the refrigerating process of some gallon of boiled water, in a huge white jug, which he filled every morning at the breakfast-table, and set upon the stone outside the window to cool. After dinner, this supply was placed on the table by his right hand, and corrected, pro re nata, with whiskey, until, tumbler after tumbler, the whole of its contents disappeared. That was his stint; he never exceeded it; but as soon as it was finished, which was rarely before two or three o'clock next morning, he went to bed; and it depended on the quality of the spirit thus imbibed (the quantity being uniformly the same) in what degree of ill-humour he should apply himself to his professional duties of the following noon.

===Chinese===
他白天余下的光阴，主要用来照看一大白罐开水的"冷却"工序——他每天清早在早饭桌旁灌满这一加仑容量的水，搁在窗外石台上晾凉。晚饭之后，这一供应便由他亲手置于桌上右手处，并视情形（*pro re nata*）兑入威士忌，加以"调剂"；一杯接一杯地，直到整罐东西喝个精光。那是他的定量，从无超额；可一待喝完——这很少在次日凌晨两三点之前——他便上床安寝；而他第二天正午着手办理教书的差事时，心情的恶劣程度，则全看他前一夜所灌酒浆的品质如何（数量是恒定不变的）。

===Original===
Such was the schoolmaster of one of the fashionable boarding-schools in the immediate vicinity of our capital some fifty years since. It was my fortune to be removed from under his ferula to that of another who had been an operative tailor—not an Alton Locke, though—and whose ignorance of everything but handwriting and Gough's *Arithmetic*, was far more astounding than that of the bombardier. He made up, however, in morality, for his shortcomings in erudition; and as they both kept tolerably competent ushers, and had an understanding of mutual profit with the bookseller, care was taken that their pupils should be supplied with a competent stock of tools for learning at all events; so we hobbled through the Latin and Greek course, *utcunque*, and Trinity College made the most of us afterwards.

===Chinese===
这便是约莫五十年前我国首都近郊一所时髦的寄宿学校里的一位教书先生。我后来从他的教鞭之下，转到了另一位先生的门下——此人曾做过裁缝，不过倒不是阿尔顿·洛克（Alton Locke）那一流；他除了书法和古夫的《算术》（*Gough's Arithmetic*）之外，样样都一窍不通，其无知之深，比那位一等兵更叫人瞠目。然而，他在学问上的短处，倒全靠品行端正补了回来；况且这两位先生都还请得起相当称职的副手，又与书商有一笔互利互惠的默契，于是总归能保证门下学生至少有齐全的"学习工具"可用；我们便这般磕磕绊绊地把拉丁文和希腊文的课文学了下去，*好歹*（*utcunque*）学完；至于后来三一学院（Trinity College）拿我们如何处置，那便是另一回事了。

===Original===
If ever your ghost-seer extends his nocturnal saunterings towards Ballyfermot, about "the wee sma' hours ayont the twal," let him have an eye out for a large white jug with a red nightcap and a pair of green goggles; for as surely as drunken spirits are permitted to revisit the glimpses of the moon, in that place and at such an hour will the schoolmaster be abroad.

===Chinese===
倘若你那位爱瞧鬼的人，竟将他的夜游延伸到了巴利弗莫特（Ballyfermot）一带，正赶上"过十二点的深夜时分"（the wee sma' hours ayont the twal），请他千万留意一只戴着红睡帽、架着绿眼镜的大白罐子；因为只要酗酒的鬼魂还被准许重见那月色的一瞥，那么在那地方、在那时辰，这位教书匠的魂魄便必在外头游荡。

===Original===
Upon the dispersion of our own royal regiment, the Macleod Fencibles took up their quarters in the barrack, which thereupon stank horribly of cockaleekie every morning. A raw, wild, breekless tribe they were, fresh caught from the Highlands, at a period when the Trossachs were as inaccessible to the foot of civilised man as the Kyber Pass. The chief of the clan had collected and regimented them, selecting his own officers from the sons of his tacksmen and reivers, and few members of the mess could speak a dozen consecutive words of good English. The colonel, a fiery old Gael, and "vengeance proud," did his best to lick them into form, using his knuckles occasionally, it was said, for that purpose; and, indeed, a vigorous discipline was needful. They wrangled at dinner for the choice morsels of the various joints, three or four knives and forks being sometimes plunged at the same moment into one leg of mutton; and upon a certain occasion, when a large turbot was served, those who sat near the would-be carver saved him the trouble of apportioning it, by forking it away upon their own plates with their long bony fingers. This vexed the colonel exceedingly; for there were strangers at the table who had never dined at a Fencible mess before. For a whole week, therefore, he condemned them to leek-porridge, which was eaten with a spoon, while all the regimental pipers, seated (*more Scotico*) at the end of the apartment, blew "Cauld Kail," and other appetizing "refreins," to bring them to an improving sense of the privations they were enduring. Many of those caterans were afterwards drafted into the general service, and attained the highest honours awarded to good soldiership. These, indeed, came to them by nature; but the acquisition of the manners of gentlemen was not so easy; yet more than one of the individuals, who scrambled on that memorable occasion for the turbot, have been deemed worthy to sit down at royal banquets, and were justly classed amongst the flower of North British chivalry.

===Chinese===
我们自己的皇家兵团散去之后，麦克劳德地方防卫团（the Macleod Fencibles）便进驻了营房，于是乎每天清早，那地方就弥漫着一股子令人作呕的鸡肉韭葱汤（cockaleekie）的气味。他们是一群毛躁粗野、连裤子都穿不齐整的蛮子，刚从高地（Highlands）抓来；其时，特罗萨克斯（Trossachs）之于文明人的脚板，正与开伯尔山口（Kyber Pass）同样不可企及。族长把他们收拢起来、编成队伍，从自家的租户子弟和盗匪（reivers）子弟里挑出军官；军官食堂里能连说一打英文好字儿的，实在没有几人。上校是个脾气火爆的老盖尔人，"怀着一肚子的复仇"，他尽了最大努力要把自己的人马调教出个样子来——据说为达此目的，间或还要动用他的拳头；说实在的，严酷的纪律在这里原是少不得的。吃饭的时候，他们为各个肉块上的上好部位争执不休，有时三四把刀叉会同时插进同一条羊腿；某次席上端上一条硕大的比目鱼（turbot），坐在那位欲操刀分菜之人左右两旁的，竟省了他分肉的麻烦，用自己那长骨嶙峋的手指把它叉走、拨到自家盘里去了。上校对此大为光火——因为席上坐着几位从前不曾在地方防卫团（Fencible）的军官食堂用过饭的客人。于是他罚他们整整吃了一个礼拜的韭葱粥，只能用匙子吃；与此同时，全团所有的风笛手都 *按苏格兰习俗*（*more Scotico*）坐在屋子尽头，吹奏《冷汤》（Cauld Kail）以及其它叫人开胃的"小调"，好叫他们痛切地省悟自己所受的这场苦。这群高地盗匪（caterans）中，有不少后来被编入常规军，并获得了授予优秀军人的最高荣誉。这些品质，原是他们与生俱来的；可要习得绅士的举止做派，便没那么容易了——然而，当年那场抢夺比目鱼的盛举里，倒真不止一人后来被认为够资格在皇家宴席上落座，被公道地归入北不列颠骑士精神（North British chivalry）的精华之列。

===Original===
The Carlow militia came next, a polite corps, but numbering some strange twists among its subalterns. The adjutant, one Clifford, had been raised from the ranks by the favour and discernment of Colonel Latouche. He was a humorous fellow, of a manly, independent mind, and scorned to hang his head at the remembrance of his origin. The General of Division, dining at the mess on the occasion of a quarterly inspection, complimented Clifford upon the excellent state of drill in which he found the regiment, and, alluding to his name, asked "if he had any relations on the staff?"

"No, General," he replied, "but I have a great number on the spade."

It happened, on some occasion, that he displeased his colonel, who, in a hasty moment, declared his regret at having raised him from the state in which he had found him.

"Then, Colonel Latouche," said Clifford, "you are the first of your name that ever was sorry for doing a good action."

It is scarcely necessary to say that so adroit and just a compliment replaced him at once in his good patron's favour.

===Chinese===
接踵而至的是卡洛民兵团（the Carlow militia），这是个礼数周到的团队，但少尉军官里头却也藏着几个怪人。团副官克利福德（Clifford），是蒙拉图什上校（Colonel Latouche）的慧眼与赏识从行伍间提拔起来的。他是个诙谐风趣、心胸磊落独立的人，对自己的出身毫不避讳，绝不肯因记起自己的来历便垂头丧气。有次季检，那位师长（General of Division）在军官食堂用餐，夸赞克利福德把全团的操练训得极为出色，并借着他的姓氏打趣，问他"参谋部（on the staff）里可有亲戚？"

"没有，将军，"他答道，"不过铲子（on the spade）上头倒有一大把。"（注：以 spade 谐音 staff，意指务农为生的亲戚）

某次他冒犯了上校，上校一时火起，说自己后悔不该把他从当初那般境地里提拔起来。

"那么，拉图什上校，"克利福德说，"您是这个姓氏里头第一个为做了一件好事而后悔的人。"

这么机巧又如此恰到好处的一句恭维，立时便让他重新得宠于那位好东家——这点几乎不必赘言。

===Original===
The pride of the old barrack was sorely tried afterwards, by various incursions of featherbeds which came in successively with the Wicklow, South Mayo, North Downshire, and Limerick regiments. Your shell-jacket dandies of this day would stare at the half-moon-shaped cocked hats, black leggings with innumerable small buttons, and draggle-tailed coats of their predecessors. But the hair-powder was worse than all. Can I ever forget Bob Gloster, of the Garryowens, on his return from the grand review one broiling Fourth of June, wiping away, with the sleeve of his new scarlet uniform, the streams of liquefied flour that meandered down his cheeks, and bewailing the day that he had "ever left the sweet English Town,9 where he might have been reared up to an imminent marchant, to be melted out of creation like an althar-candle." Bob volunteered, shortly afterwards, into "the Line," and became well used to the "melting mood" in Spain, where he soon earned for himself a pair of spurs; and when he came home, after the peace of Paris, Major Gloster, quite a polished cavalier, with a fine military accent, I should have liked to see the man who would remind him of his early chances of "imminence" in the mercantile line. It was of such materials that heroes were manufactured; and I could enumerate at least a dozen "ragged colts" who left that old barrack, in the midst of scenes of riot and drunkenness incidental to the volunteering system, and turned out "bra' chargers" at Vittoria, or on the plain of Waterloo.

===Chinese===
那座老营房的体面，此后可被一连串的"羽绒垫子"（featherbeds，意指养尊处优的少爷兵）糟蹋得够呛——随着威克洛（Wicklow）、南梅奥（South Mayo）、北当郡（North Downshire）、利默里克（Limerick）诸团相继开进，这些货色便也陆续涌到。今日那些身着短外套（shell-jacket）的花花公子，要是瞧见自己前辈那新月形的三角帽、缀着数不清小纽扣的黑色绑腿、还有那拖着长后摆的外套，非得目瞪口呆不可。可那头发上扑的粉，比这一切更要命得多。鲍勃·格洛斯特（Bob Gloster），隶属加里奥恩团（the Garryowens），那个酷热的六月四日，盛大阅兵式归来，他用那身崭新猩红军服的袖子，抹着顺着脸颊蜿蜒而下的、化成浆的面粉糊糊，哀叹自己"当初真不该离开那可爱的英格兰小镇9，要不，我本可以从小被栽培成一个颇有出息的买卖人（imminent marchant，方言误读，当作 eminent merchant），如今倒好，给化得像根祭坛蜡烛（althar-candle）似的，化得连个影儿都不剩。"此后不久，鲍勃自愿转到了"正规军"（the Line）里去，到了西班牙，可就把这"融化的心境"（melting mood）尝了个够；他很快在那边为自己挣得了一副马刺；待到巴黎和约（the peace of Paris）签订后归国之时，格洛斯特少校（Major Gloster）已是相当文雅的一位骑士了，操着一口道地的军人腔——我倒很想瞧瞧，有谁敢当面提醒他少年时代曾在商行里"颇有出息"的那段前程。英雄的原材料，原来便是这么一类的货色；我至少能数得出整整一打"瘦骨嶙峋的小马驹"，从那座老营房里走出去——其时正逢自愿兵制度所伴生的那种酗酒作乱场面——后来却在维多利亚（Vittoria）战役或滑铁卢（Waterloo）平原上，一匹匹变成了"神气活现的战马"（bra' chargers）。

===Original===
But Chapelizod was not always a mere depot of Fencibles and militia. It was for a good while the headquarters of the 92nd, or Gordon Highlanders, so truly described in Captain Grant's charming romance. They marched in, all brown and shrivelled by the sands of Egypt, though some years had passed since they had been there. A grave, orderly, religious body of men they were, who seemed always conscious that they were only here for a breathing time, and could not long be spared from the field of death. Their leader was Major Cameron, "the Fassifern," who ended his career of glory at Waterloo. Authors who write "stories founded on facts" take a license to embellish their materials, and to exaggerate the moral as well as the physical attributes of the persons whom they introduce, according to the exigencies of the fable. But there is no exaggeration in Captain Grant's portrait of Cameron. It is a true representation of the man. His outward semblance and his frank and generous spirit, his nobility of mind and person, are painted with equal fidelity. To see that man in front of his regiment was a sight worthy of the olden time. John Kemble did not impart a more exalted notion of the figure of Caius Marcius as he rallied the Roman legions before Corioli, than Cameron's robust but stately form, the dignity of which was in no degree impaired by a slight and scarcely perceptible halt, the effect of a musket-shot in the knee which he had received in Egypt, gave the spectators of the men who had scattered England's chivalry at Bannockburn. If Walter Scott knew him, his picture of Fergus Mac Ivor, all perfect as it is, can scarcely claim the merit of originality.

===Chinese===
但查佩利佐德也并不从来只是地方防卫团和民兵团的屯驻地。有相当一段时日，它是第九十二团——即戈登高地团（the 92nd, or Gordon Highlanders）——的总部；格兰特上尉（Captain Grant）在那本迷人的传奇里，对它有真切的描写。他们开进来时，被埃及的黄沙晒得焦黑、晒得枯皱——虽说他们离开那里已有好些年了。他们是一群庄重、守纪、虔诚的人，仿佛时刻心怀这样一种意识：自己不过是到此处来喘口气的，从那死亡之场上是抽不开太久的。他们的统帅是卡梅伦少校（Major Cameron），人称"法西弗恩"（the Fassifern），他的辉煌军旅生涯终结于滑铁卢。撰写"据实虚构"故事的作家，照例有权添枝加叶，根据情节所需，把他们笔下人物的精神与体魄两方面的品质加以渲染和夸大。然而格兰特上尉所绘的卡梅伦画像，却并无半分夸饰。这是此人真实的写照。他的外貌与他那坦荡慷慨的心胸、他那心灵与体魄上的高贵，都同样忠实地描绘了出来。瞧着这个人立于全团之前，真是一幅无愧于古时的景象。当年约翰·肯布尔（John Kemble）在科里奥利（Corioli）城下重整罗马军团时所塑造的盖乌斯·马基乌斯（Caius Marcius）的身姿，给人的那种崇高之感，未必能胜过卡梅伦那壮健而威严的身影——此身姿丝毫不因其微微的、几乎察觉不出的跛行而有损威仪，那是他在埃及所中的一记火枪伤，正中膝盖——而这身影呈现在观众眼前的，正是当年曾在班诺克本（Bannockburn）一役中把英格兰骑士杀得落花流水的那班人。倘若沃尔特·司各特（Walter Scott）曾识得此人，那么他笔下弗格斯·麦克艾弗（Fergus Mac Ivor）的画像——纵已尽善尽美——却也未必能自称独创了。

===Original===
No regimental biographer has attempted a history of "The Army of Reserve." It is a theme worthy of the pen of Lorrequer (now that poor Maxwell is gone, there is none other capable of doing it justice), and the materials for constructing it are fading rapidly out of the memory of mankind; yet Chapelizod still remembers "the Blackbelts." Who that ever saw can forget them? It is scarcely worth being sixty, indeed, or thereabouts, to have seen them; but since that would be in any case, it is a pride and a joy to have enjoyed the vision; for

> "Eye ne'er shall look upon their like again."

The Blackbelts, so called because those decorations of military equipment in which the song exults as

> "Your belts of white leather,"

were polished off as glossy as the raven's down across the shoulders and breasts of this distinguished corps, were known at the Horse Guards as the Second Garrison Battalion. They were physically, as the Sixtieth Regiment in those days was in a moral sense, the sweepings of the service. Every soldier who was blind of an eye, lame of a leg, maimed in an arm, crooked in form, or diminutive in size, and yet considered able to carry arms in the service of his sovereign, was drafted into the "Blackbelts," and the officers were pretty nearly of a piece with the men. They reminded me of the little hairy men who came in swarms on board Sinbad's vessel and devoured everything, carnal and vegetable, they could stick their claws into. But they were a well-disciplined battalion, and efficient enough for the sort of duty they had to perform. Excellent shots too they were, every man of them. No rifle corps in any service could have surpassed them with the brown bess; a target was knocked to splinters by them in half-an-hour. They were specially employed, on this account, to escort deserters; for escape was not an uncommon thing while the corporal's guard were engaged in social chat along a dusty road. The prisoner would slip his wrist through the handcuff, bolt up a lane, and dodge his pursuers from hedge to hedge till he got clear off. But let a Blackbelt catch but a glimpse of his person emerging from a thicket or doubling round a corner, and he had him down as unerringly as O'Gorman Mahon would bag a woodcock.

===Chinese===
从来没有任何一位团的史官，尝试过为"预备军"（The Army of Reserve）写一部历史。这是个值得洛雷克（Lorrequer）之笔的题材——可怜的麦克斯韦（Maxwell）既已不在，再没第二个人配给它一个公道了——而构建这部历史的材料，正在迅速地自人类的记忆中消退；然而查佩利佐德却还记得"黑皮带团"（the Blackbelts）。凡是见过他们的，谁能忘得了呢？其实，一个人活到六十岁上下，单单为了见识过他们便已算不得什么了；可既已如此，那么见过他们便是一桩足以引以为傲、引以为快的事了；因为

> "再无此眼，能见此等人物。"

这黑皮带团之所以得此名号，是因为那套军中装备的饰件——歌中曾得意地咏唱：

> "你那白皮皮带，"

——在这支名团官兵的肩头和胸前，都被擦得光亮如乌鸦的翎羽，故而得了此名；它在近卫骑兵司令部（the Horse Guards）的正式番号是第二守备营（Second Garrison Battalion）。论体格，他们恰如第六十团（the Sixtieth Regiment）当年在精神意义上那样，是全军扫出来的渣滓。每一名瞎了一只眼、瘸了一条腿、伤了一条胳膊、身形佝偻、抑或个子矮小，却仍被认为尚能持械为君主效力的兵士，都被编入了"黑皮带团"；而军官与兵士，也大致是一路货色。他们叫我想起辛巴达（Sinbad）船上那成群涌来的毛茸茸的小人，凡是爪子够得着的，无论荤素，一概狼吞虎咽。但他们是一支训练有素的营，执行他们那类勤务倒也颇为称职。论枪法，他们个个都是好手，无一例外。任何一支步枪兵团，无论在哪一国军中，都不能在"棕贝丝"（brown bess，滑膛枪的别称）上胜过他们；半个钟头之内，一块靶子便叫他们打得稀烂。正因如此，他们被专派去押解逃兵——因为下士带的那一小队押解兵要是在尘土飞扬的路上闲聊起来，逃兵之事便不算稀罕。犯人把手腕从手铐里一抽，蹿上一条小巷，从一道篱笆躲到另一道篱笆，甩开追兵，便溜之大吉了。可只要叫一个黑皮带团的人瞥见他从灌木丛里探出身子、或是在拐角上一闪，那他便能像奥戈尔曼·马洪（O'Gorman Mahon）打下一只山鹬一般，分毫不差地把他放倒。

===Original===
Two or three incidents of this kind occurred during the stay of the battalion in Chapelizod. One of the occasions was very remarkable. A deserter broke loose in a crowded street and fled amongst men and women, who threw themselves purposely in the way, in order to facilitate his escape. But this manoeuvre did not save him. The corporal levelled his musket, waited coolly till the wretch glanced for a moment into a vacant space, and then shot him dead. The fame of the Blackbelts, as sharpshooters, and the unrelenting sternness with which they acted on such occasions, soon made them the terror of the service, and their prisoners ceased to hope for safety in sudden flight.

===Chinese===
该营驻扎查佩利佐德期间，发生了两三桩此类事件。其中一桩，尤为特别。一名逃兵在一条人潮拥挤的街上挣脱了身，在男女群众中四下奔窜——那些人有意挡在路中，好帮他逃脱。然而这一招并未能救他。那下士端起火枪，冷冷地等着，直等到这可怜虫一时闪入一片空地，便一枪将他击毙。黑皮带团作为神枪手的名声，以及他们在此类场合行事时那种不留情面的峻厉，很快便使他们成了全军谈虎色变的对象；他们押解下的犯人，也再不敢指望凭着突如其来的一跑了之而得保性命了。

===Original===
Before taking leave of the military reminiscences of Chapelizod, let me throw a Parthian glance upon the yeomanry corps commanded by Captain Wilcocks (the late Sir Richard), whose handsome and portly figure I still seem to behold, like a Colossus looking down upon the evolutions of his men. The vicar of the parish, a loyal man, who took a lively interest in the military education of those heroes, offered a gold medal to be shot for, at a distance of a hundred yards, upon the Palmerston fair-green. It was a great occasion, and all the beauty and fashion of three villages adorned it with their presence. There stood the captain to see fair play and encourage the nervous, while his permanent sergeant, Ned Bullard, was ready with a jeer and a joke at the service of everyone that shot wide of the mark. The zealous parson, adumbrated by a *shovel* of such dimensions as we see not in these days of skimping economy, rode up and down the line exhorting the brave to fear nothing, but, remembering that the eyes of their country were upon them, to acquit them like men. Point blank was the practice on that memorable day. Had the target been a thing of life, it would have required to be of the feline species to have survived; for I have no doubt that at least nine out of the hundred bullets struck some part of its circumference. The victor was one Pierce Butler, a round, fat, oily son of Crispin, who had never discharged a bit of lead from a musket barrel before, and who approached his task as we may suppose King Agag to have approached the Prophet Samuel. With averted eye he raised the gun to his shoulder, pulled the trigger, in an agony of desperation, and falling back by the force of the rebound amongst his sympathizing fellow-soldiers, exclaimed, "Hould me up!" It was some time before he could collect his scattered senses sufficiently to comprehend the cheers which announced that he had pierced the bull's eye. But when the great fact was made perfectly plain to his understanding, it was wonderful how promptly his spirit rose with his fortune, and with what a fiercely modest alacrity he strutted forward to the place where the vicar's niece, a charming young lady of eighteen, stood ready to invest him with the trophy. And now let me tell you that the only ghost of that corps that walks this firm set earth is the individual Bob Martin, whom your ghost-seer has so prematurely sent to his account. Bob is still as much as ever he was, which is not saying a great deal for him, extant amongst "articulate men," and, according to his own somewhat indignant account, has "as little call to sperrits, maybe, as gintlemen that takes greater liberties wid them."

===Chinese===
在告别查佩利佐德的军旅旧忆之前，让我再回马一顾，看看由威尔科克斯上尉（Captain Wilcocks，即已故的理查德爵士，Sir Richard）所统率的那支义勇骑兵队（yeomanry corps）——他那英俊魁梧的身形，我此刻仿佛仍能看见，如同一尊巨像俯视着他麾下兵士的操练。教区的牧师本是位忠君爱国之人，对这些英雄的军事教育关怀备至，他捐出一枚金质奖章，要在帕默斯顿集市草地（Palmerston fair-green）上、一百码的距离，以射击来角逐。这是一桩盛事，三个村子的美女与体面人物，都盛装到场，为之增色。上尉站在那里主持公道、给那些怯场的打气；他那常任的中士内德·布拉德（Ned Bullard）则随时备着一句嘲讽、一个笑话，伺候每一位打偏了的射手。那位热心的牧师——他那顶大得异乎寻常的铲形宽边帽（*shovel*），如今这凡事克扣节约的年代里是再见不到的了——骑着马在队列前后来回地鼓动勇士们什么都不必怕，只消记着祖国的眼睛正瞧着他们，要拿出男子汉的气概来。在那值得纪念的一天，枪枪都是直射。倘若那靶子是个活物，除非它是猫族，否则断然活不下来；因为我毫不怀疑，那一百发子弹里至少有九发，打中了靶子周缘的某一点。胜出的是皮尔斯·巴特勒（Pierce Butler），一个圆滚滚、胖墩墩、油光水滑的鞋匠之子（son of Crispin，克里斯平乃鞋匠守护圣徒），他这辈子还从未从滑膛枪管里射出过一粒子弹，走向他这项任务时的样子，我们大可想象亚甲王（King Agag）走向先知撒母耳（Prophet Samuel）时便是这般。他别开眼，把枪托上肩，扳机一扣——怀着拼命般的绝望——借着后坐力往后一仰，跌进了那些与他同情的战友怀里，嚷道："扶住我！"（Hould me up!）过了好一会儿，他散了架的心神才稍稍收拢，能听懂四周那阵宣布他射中了靶心的欢呼声，到底是何意思。可一旦这桩大事实实在在地在他脑子里立住了，那可真奇了——他的心气儿竟随着运道的勃兴而升得如此之快，他带着那么一股子凶悍的谦逊劲儿，大摇大摆地走上前去——牧师那位十八岁的标致外甥女正立在那里，准备把这奖品授给他。如今容我告诉您一句：那个团里至今仍在这方坚实的土地上走动的唯一的鬼魂，便是鲍勃·马丁其人——也就是您那位爱瞧鬼的人，竟如此之早便送去结账的那一位。鲍勃如今仍一如当年之所是——这话替他说不上什么大恭维——仍在"会说话的人"（articulate men）中间活着；而且按他自己那番颇为愤愤不平的说法，他"跟鬼（sperrits）打交道的机会，说不定，倒比那些跟它们更加放肆周旋的先生（gintlemen）们还少些呢（wid）。"

===Original===
But there was a Bob Martin once; the old Bob of all, who served the office of sexton when the population of Ireland scarcely amounted to three millions of interrable bodies. That man could have enwrinkled you all over with grave statistics. It was he that buried Luttrell, and saw the blue light flickering out of the coffin, when the first shovelful of black earth was cast upon it; and formidable were the stories which he related of the same Luttrell. Bob was for a long while "the oldest inhabitant," but, unlike that personage in general, he could remember many things; and he would tell them with a gusto, when engaged knee-deep, or deeper still, in his professional avocation. To him is the world indebted for a few fragments of *Satanic History*, collected from the transactions of "The Hellfire Club," every tittle of which he was prepared to verify before any tribunal.

===Chinese===
然而当年确实有过一个鲍勃·马丁；是最早的那个老鲍勃——他当教堂司事（sexton）的时候，爱尔兰全国可埋葬的人口还不足三百万。那个人能用坟地里的种种统计数字，把你全身都皱出褶子来。埋葬拉特雷尔（Luttrell）的就是他；头一锹黑土撒到棺材上的时候，他还瞧见那道蓝光从棺材里忽闪忽闪地透出来——关于这位拉特雷尔，他所讲的种种故事，更是骇人。鲍勃有很长一段时间是"最老的住户"，可他与一般此类人物不同，他记得起许多事情；而且讲起来津津有味——其时他正两膝没入泥土，甚至更深地埋首于他这桩营生之中。世间有关《撒旦史》（*Satanic History*）的几则残篇，皆是要归功于他的：那是从"地狱火俱乐部"（The Hellfire Club）的种种行事中搜辑而来，其中一星半点，他都准备在任何法庭之上，一一证实。

===Original===
The building of "The Devil's Mills," on the Lower Road to Lucan, was one of those incontestable facts. They were built in one night, at the requisition of the redoubtable Luttrell, who being hard pressed to devise a task beyond the ability of the architect to perform (otherwise he could not get rid of his society, which began to be rather *ennuyant*), he commanded the mill to be erected. But that was no trouble. He looked out of the window, and saw it done.

"Throw a weir and dam across the river." Presto, there it was!

"Make me a rope of sand."

"Ah, there you have me," said the old gentleman, "for the devil himself cannot do that;" and so he was quit for that time. The ruined mill at Woodlands, on the Liffey bank, still attests the reality of this wonder.

===Chinese===
