在通往卢坎（Lucan）的下路上，那座"魔鬼磨坊"（The Devil's Mills）的营造，便是那些无可辩驳的事实之一。它是在一夜之间建成的——那是令人闻风丧胆的拉特雷尔的指令：他急于要出一道难题，叫那位建筑师无能为力（否则他便摆脱不了此人，而此人的陪伴已开始变得颇为 *令人生厌*（*ennuyant*）），便下令造这座磨坊。可这于他倒不算什么难事。他从窗口望出去，那磨坊便成了。

"在河上筑一道堰、一道坝。"——眨眼间，堰坝就成了！

"给我用沙搓一根绳子。"

"啊，这您可把我难住了，"那位老绅士说，"因为便是魔鬼他老人家也搓不出来"；于是那一回，他便这样搪塞了过去。利菲河畔伍德兰兹（Woodlands）那座磨坊的废墟，至今仍是这桩奇事的实证。

===Original===
Again, at an annual meeting of the club, at which whoever happened to be last in a certain saltatory movement of the whole assembly, became the lawful prey of the "grand master," it was Luttrell's luck to be left behind. But his good genius did not forsake him.

"What are your eyes for?" he cried, nothing daunted. "Take the fellow that is coming after me."

The devil let go his prey and seized—*a shadow*; whence the remarkable fact, that, to the hour of his death, Luttrell never had a shadow. Bob Martin had seen him a dozen times, without a shadow. He could not swear, indeed, that the sun shone on such occasions; but of the material fact, that Luttrell belonged to the *ascii* of the earth, there could not be a possible doubt.

===Chinese===
另有一回，俱乐部年年例会之时，有一项仪式：全体成员一同参与某种跳跃运动，谁要是落在最后，便沦为"大首领"（grand master）合法的猎物。偏巧那一回，拉特雷尔倒霉落在了最后。但他的福星并未抛弃他。

"您那双眼睛是干什么用的？"他毫无惧色地嚷道，"把跟在我后头来的那个人抓去就是了。"

魔鬼放开了他的猎物，扑过去——*一个影子*；由此便有了一桩奇事：拉特雷尔自此以至咽气那一天，再也没有了影子。鲍勃·马丁曾见过他不下十几次，身上没有影子。当然，他不能起誓说那些场合太阳一定当头照着；然而关于这桩实体的事实——拉特雷尔属于世上那班 *无影族*（*ascii*）——却是无可置疑的了。

===Original===
On a third occasion, when immersed in study—it would be curious to know the name of the volume—the old one peeping over his shoulder, gave him a familiar tap, and said:—

"Come down, and finish it at my fireside."

"Stay," said Luttrell, whose ready wit was never at a "nonplush," "I have a codicil to add to my will. Give me a delay till this inch of candle is burned out."

The request seemed so moderate, that it was granted without hesitation.

"Upon your honour?"

"As I'm a gentleman."

"Then, perhaps, you'll have no objection to sit a short time in the dark?" So said, so done. He blew out the candle, locked it up in his desk, marked the sign of the cross over the keyhole, and requested his friend to ring the bell for fresh lights.

Now, though Bob was a staunch Protestant, and held mutterings in as much contempt as Lord John Russell, he believed most firmly that nothing could have hindered the old gentleman from following that inch of candle into the desk, and annihilating it with one puff of his breath, if the sign of the cross had not been so timely interposed to bar him out.

===Chinese===
又有一次，他正埋头读书——很想知道那是一本什么书——那老东西从他肩头探过头来，亲昵地拍了拍他，说道：——

"下来吧，到我炉边把它读完。"

"且慢，"拉特雷尔说——他的急智从不曾"卡壳"（nonplush）——"我的遗嘱还有一份附录要添。请容我宽限片刻，等这一寸蜡烛烧完。"

这请求听来如此合情合理，便毫不犹豫地获允了。

"以您的荣誉担保？"

"我以绅士身份担保。"

"那么，您大约不介意在黑暗里坐上一会儿吧？"——说到做到。他把蜡烛吹灭，锁进自己的书桌里，在钥匙孔上画了个十字，然后请他的朋友拉铃叫人来取新的灯火。

虽说鲍勃是个坚定的新教徒，对那等嘟嘟囔囔的做派，其鄙视之情与约翰·罗素勋爵（Lord John Russell）不相上下，他却坚信不疑：倘若不是那十字的记号及时挡在了门口，那老绅士原本是毫无阻碍的——尽可跟着那一寸蜡烛钻进书桌里，一口气将它吹个精光。

===Original===
But Bob's conversation was rich in remembrances of better men. His father had been married by "the Dane," whereby he meant Dean Swift, and a considerable proportion of his store of traditionary anecdote was connected, more or less, with that great name; nor was he singular in that. All the old men of his time preserved a lively sense of the wit and patriotism of the eccentric Drapier. They could tell all that is written, and a great deal that is not written, illustrative of his peculiar humour. As for Bob, he was able to point out the particular spot on the Castleknock road, where he stopped his horse to bargain with a cowboy for a secret whereby he was enabled to prognosticate the weather. The dean had passed by, lightly clad, in full confidence that the weather would continue fair.

"Go back for your cloak, sir," said the urchin; "it will rain."

Without heeding the warning, he passed on; and in an hour's time was wet to the skin. He returned to the spot, and demanded how the boy could foresee the shower? The youngster required half-a-crown for the information, which having obtained after some chaffering, he said:—

"You see that big stone, your reverence, in the middle of the field. Well, whenever you want to know if it is going to rain, come to that place, and if you find the bull scratching himself against that big stone, you may be sure of it."

To that big stone many a chuckling sexagenarian could point, as a memento of "the Dane," whose memory the whole community loved and revered, having been outwitted for once by a poor country boy. It may stand there yet, for aught I can tell.

===Chinese===
然而鲍勃肚里的旧话，更多的还是些更体面的人物的回忆。他父亲便是"那丹麦人"主持婚礼成亲的——他所谓"丹麦人"（the Dane），即指斯威夫特教长（Dean Swift）；他那肚子里一大宗祖传的轶闻旧事，或多或少都跟这个名字有些关系；而此事他也并非独此一家。他那一代所有的老人，对那位古怪的德拉皮尔（Drapier，斯威夫特的笔名）的机锋与爱国之心，都保留着一种鲜活的感觉。他们讲得出现有记载中有关他那独特幽默的一切，更能讲出许多没有记载的。至于鲍勃本人，他能指点给你看，在卡斯尔诺克路（the Castleknock road）上具体哪一处地方，教长曾勒住马，与一个放牛娃谈生意，要花钱买下他一个秘密，凭这秘密便能预卜天气。原来，教长轻装经过，深信天气会一直晴好。

"先生，回去取您的斗篷吧，"那小淘气说，"要下雨了。"

教长不听警告，径自前行；不到一个钟头，便浑身湿透。他回到原地，追问那孩子怎会预知这场雨？那小鬼索要半克朗（half-crown）方肯透露天机；几番讨价还价之后，钱到手了，他便说道：——

"教长先生，您瞧见田当中央那块大石头没有？好啦，您往后想知道会不会下雨，便到那地方去，要是瞧见那头公牛在那块大石头上蹭痒，您就可以断定——准下。"

许多一位心满意足的六旬老人，都能指点给你看那块大石头，当作"丹麦人"的一件纪念——这位"丹麦人"，全镇的人都敬爱他的名声，因为他居然有一次被一个乡下穷孩子给算计了。据我所知，那块石头说不定至今还在那里。

===Original===
It was surely something, when the peasantry of a whole district were accustomed to amuse one another with the sayings and doings of the greatest of the wits of Queen Anne. The schoolmaster may have done much for the world in the last half-century, but he certainly has not raised the minds or improved the taste of that class. There are very few Bob Martins, in whose mouths the names of Swift, and Sheridan, and Delany, and Archbishop Boulter are now as "familiar as household words."

===Chinese===
一整个地区的乡下人，居然习惯于拿安妮女王（Queen Anne）朝最伟大的一位才子的言行来彼此逗乐取乐——这想来也着实是件了不起的事。这半个世纪以来，教书先生也许为这世界做了不少事，可他确实没能拔高那一阶层的心智，也没能改善他们的趣味。鲍勃·马丁这种人，如今是凤毛麟角了——在他们嘴里，斯威夫特（Swift）、谢里丹（Sheridan）、德拉尼（Delany）以及大主教博尔特（Archbishop Boulter）这些名字，曾一如"家喻户晓的熟语"一般挂在嘴边。

### The Magician Earl / 魔法师伯爵

===Original===
It is well known that the great Earl of Desmond, though history pretends to dispose of him differently, lives to this hour enchanted in his castle, with all his household, at the bottom of the lake.

There was not, in his day, in all the world, so accomplished a magician as he. His fairest castle stood upon an island in the lake, and to this he brought his young and beautiful bride, whom he loved but too well; for she prevailed upon his folly to risk all to gratify her imperious caprice.

They had not been long in this beautiful castle, when she one day presented herself in the chamber in which her husband studied his forbidden art, and there implored him to exhibit before her some of the wonders of his evil science. He resisted long; but her entreaties, tears, and wheedlings were at length too much for him and he consented.

But before beginning those astonishing transformations with which he was about to amaze her, he explained to her the awful conditions and dangers of the experiment.

===Chinese===
世人皆知，那位伟大的德斯蒙德伯爵（Earl of Desmond）——尽管史书装作对他另有了一番了局——实则至今仍受咒缚，连同满门家眷，幽居于盖尔湖底的城堡之中。

在他所处的时代，举世之内，再没有一位魔法师能如他这般造诣精深。他最美的一座城堡，矗立在湖中的一座小岛上，他便将年轻貌美的新娘接到这里。他爱她未免爱得太深；正是她怂恿了他这痴愚之人，教他甘冒一切风险，只为满足她那骄横的任性。

他俩住进这座美丽的城堡没多久，有一天，她便闯进了丈夫研习禁术的那间密室，在那里恳求他，要在她眼前展现几分他那邪术的奇景。他推拒了很久；但她的央求、眼泪与甜言蜜语，到头来还是叫他招架不住，他终于应允了。

然而，在动手施行那套即将令她瞠目结舌的惊世变形之前，他向她说明了这场试验的可怖条件与凶险。

===Original===
Alone in this vast apartment, the walls of which were lapped, far below, by the lake whose dark waters lay waiting to swallow them, she must witness a certain series of frightful phenomena, which once commenced, he could neither abridge nor mitigate; and if throughout their ghastly succession she spoke one word, or uttered one exclamation, the castle and all that it contained would in one instant subside to the bottom of the lake, there to remain, under the servitude of a strong spell, for ages.

The dauntless curiosity of the lady having prevailed, and the oaken door of the study being locked and barred, the fatal experiments commenced.

===Chinese===
在这间空旷的大厅里，她须独自一人目睹一连串可怖的景象——这大厅的墙基，在极深处，被湖水舔拍着，那幽暗的湖水正潜伏着，等着将他们一口吞噬；这些景象一旦开端，他便既不能将其缩短，也无法使其减轻半分；而在这一道道阴森景象接连显现的全程之中，她若是说出一个字，或是发出一声惊呼，这座城堡连同其中所有的一切，便会顷刻间沉入湖底，在强大咒缚的奴役之下，困守在那里，历经千秋万代。

夫人那无所畏惧的好奇心终究占了上风，书房的橡木门一经落锁上闩，那致命的试验便开始了。

===Original===
Muttering a spell, as he stood before her, feathers sprouted thickly over him, his face became contracted and hooked, a cadaverous smell filled the air, and, with heavy winnowing wings, a gigantic vulture rose in his stead, and swept round and round the room, as if on the point of pouncing upon her.

The lady commanded herself through this trial, and instantly another began.

===Chinese===
他立在她面前，口中喃喃念诵咒语，霎时间，他周身密密地生出羽毛，脸庞皱缩，勾作利喙之状，空气中弥漫起一股尸臭；紧接着，伴随着沉重的鼓翼之声，一只硕大无朋的秃鹫取代了他的所在腾空而起，绕着屋子一圈又一圈地盘旋，看那架势，仿佛就要朝她猛扑下来。

夫人强自镇定，挨过了这一场考验，下一场便立时接踵而至。

===Original===
The bird alighted near the door, and in less than a minute changed, she saw not how, into a horribly deformed and dwarfish hag: who, with yellow skin hanging about her face and enormous eyes, swung herself on crutches toward the lady, her mouth foaming with fury, and her grimaces and contortions becoming more and more hideous every moment, till she rolled with a yell on the floor, in a horrible convulsion, at the lady’s feet, and then changed into a huge serpent, with crest erect, and quivering tongue. Suddenly, as it seemed on the point of darting at her, she saw her husband in its stead, standing pale before her, and, with his finger on his lip, enforcing the continued necessity of silence. He then placed himself at his length on the floor, and began to stretch himself out and out, longer and longer, until his head nearly reached to one end of the vast room, and his feet to the other.

===Chinese===
那只巨禽在门边落了地，不出一分钟，便——她也说不清是怎样变的——化作了一个骇人地畸形、矮小的老妪：这老妪脸上挂着蜡黄的皮囊，瞪着一双硕大无朋的眼睛，拄着拐杖，一摇一晃地朝夫人挪来，口中因狂怒而泛起白沫，脸上的种种怪相与扭动也一刻比一刻更加狰狞，直到她惨叫一声，在一阵可怖的痉挛中滚倒在夫人脚下的地板上，随即又化作一条巨蛇，蛇冠高竖，长舌颤动不止。猛然间，正当它看似就要朝她疾射而出的刹那，她看见的却已不再是蛇，而是她的丈夫，面无人色地立在她面前，一根手指按在唇上，叮嘱她务必继续噤声。随后，他直挺挺地躺倒在地板上，开始一点一点地伸展身躯，越伸越长，越伸越长，直到他的头几乎触到这间大厅的一端，而他的脚几乎触到了另一端。

===Original===
This horror overcame her. The ill-starred lady uttered a wild scream, whereupon the castle and all that was within it, sank in a moment to the bottom of the lake.

But, once in every seven years, by night, the Earl of Desmond and his retinue emerge, and cross the lake, in shadowy cavalcade. His white horse is shod with silver. On that one night, the earl may ride till daybreak, and it behoves him to make good use of his time; for, until the silver shoes of his steed be worn through, the spell that holds him and his beneath the lake, will retain its power.

===Chinese===
这般恐怖终于击溃了她。这位命途多舛的夫人发出一声凄厉的尖叫，城堡连同其中所有的一切，霎时间便沉入了湖底。

然而，每隔七年，便有那么一夜，德斯蒙德伯爵会率扈从们现身，化作一队影影绰绰的行列，横渡湖面。他骑的那匹白马，蹄上钉着白银的马掌。仅此一夜，伯爵可以纵马直骑到天明，他务必好生利用这点光阴；因为，唯有等到他那坐骑的银掌磨穿之日，那将他与他满门眷属困于湖底的咒缚，才会失却法力。

===Original===
When I (Miss Anne Baily) was a child, there was still living a man named Teigue O’Neill, who had a strange story to tell.

He was a smith, and his forge stood on the brow of the hill, overlooking the lake, on a lonely part of the road to Cahir Conlish. One bright moonlight night, he was working very late, and quite alone. The clink of his hammer, and the wavering glow reflected through the open door on the bushes at the other side of the narrow road, were the only tokens that told of life and vigil for miles around.

In one of the pauses of his work, he heard the ring of many hoofs ascending the steep road that passed his forge, and, standing in this doorway, he was just in time to see a gentleman, on a white horse, who was dressed in a fashion the like of which the smith had never seen before. This man was accompanied and followed by a mounted retinue, as strangely dressed as he.

===Chinese===
我（安妮·贝利小姐，Miss Anne Baily）幼年之时，尚有一位名叫泰格·奥尼尔（Teigue O'Neill）的人健在，他肚里藏着一桩离奇的故事。

他是个铁匠，他的铁匠铺子就坐落在山岗的高处，俯瞰着那片湖水，所在之地，是通往卡希尔康利什（Cahir Conlish）的大路上一段荒僻的去处。一个皎洁的月夜，他独自一人，一直劳作到了深夜。他那铁锤的叮当声，还有那透过敞开的铺门、摇曳着映在窄路对面灌木丛上的火光，是方圆数里之内，唯一能表明这里尚有生息、尚有人醒着的迹象。

在他劳作的一个间隙里，他听见一阵密集的马蹄声沿着经过他铺子的那条陡峭山路上行而来；他站到门口，恰好来得及看见一位骑着白马的绅士，那人的装束之古怪，是这位铁匠平生从未见过的。此人前后皆有骑马的扈从相伴相随，装束与他一般奇异。

===Original===
They seemed, by the clang and clatter that announced their approach, to be riding up the hill at a hard hurry-scurry gallop; but the pace abated as they drew near, and the rider of the white horse who, from his grave and lordly air, he assumed to be a man of rank, and accustomed to command, drew bridle and came to a halt before the smith’s door.

He did not speak, and all his train were silent, but he beckoned to the smith, and pointed down to one of his horse’s hoofs.

Teigue stooped and raised it, and held it just long enough to see that it was shod with a silver shoe; which, in one place, he said, was worn as thin as a shilling. Instantaneously, his situation was made apparent to him by this sign, and he recoiled with a terrified prayer. The lordly rider, with a look of pain and fury, struck at him suddenly, with something that whistled in the air like a whip; and an icy streak seemed to traverse his body as if he had been cut through with a leaf of steel. But he was without scathe or scar, as he afterwards found. At the same moment he saw the whole cavalcade break into a gallop and disappear down the hill, with a momentary hurtling in the air, like the flight of a volley of cannon shot.

===Chinese===
从那宣告他们逼近的铿锵嘈杂之声听来，他们一上山坡时骑得飞快，仿佛一阵慌急的疾驰；可待到走近，势头便放缓下来，那骑白马的人——凭着他那端庄威严的气度，铁匠断定他必是位惯于发号施令的显贵——勒住缰绳，停在了铁匠铺门前。

他一言不发，他全部的随从也都默不作声，他只朝铁匠招了招手，又指了指自己坐骑的一只蹄子。

泰格俯下身去，托起那只蹄子，端详了刚够看清：那蹄上钉着的，是一只银掌；据他说，那银掌有一处已磨得薄如一枚先令的银币了。这一迹象登时叫他明白了自己的处境，他惊骇地念着祷文向后退缩。那位威严的骑者，面露痛苦与暴怒之色，猝然朝他抽来——抽的是一件在空中呼啸作响、状如长鞭的东西；一道冰冷仿佛贯穿了他的身躯，像是被一片薄薄的钢叶切开了似的。可事后他发觉，自己身上既无伤痕，也无痛楚。就在同一瞬间，他只见那一整队人马骤然放蹄疾驰，冲下山去，半空中掠过一阵短暂的呼啸，犹如一排炮弹掠空而过。

===Original===
Here had been the earl himself. He had tried one of his accustomed stratagems to lead the smith to speak to him. For it is well known that either for the purpose of abridging or of mitigating his period of enchantment, he seeks to lead people to accost him. But what, in the event of his succeeding, would befall the person whom he had thus ensnared, no one knows.

===Chinese===
来者正是伯爵本人。他这是又使出了他惯用的一桩计策，好诱使铁匠开口与他搭话。因为众所周知，无论旨在缩短、还是减轻他所受咒缚的期限，他都要设法引诱路人主动上前与他攀谈。然而，倘若他当真得逞，那个被他这般套住的人，又会落得怎样的下场，便无人知晓了。

## The Child That Went with the Fairies / 跟仙灵走的孩子

===Original===
Eastward of the old city of Limerick, about ten Irish miles under the range of mountains known as the Slieveelim hills, famous as having afforded Sarsfield a shelter among their rocks and hollows, when he crossed them in his gallant descent upon the cannon and ammunition of King William, on its way to the beleaguering army, there runs a very old and narrow road. It connects the Limerick road to Tipperary with the old road from Limerick to Dublin, and runs by bog and pasture, hill and hollow, straw-thatched village, and roofless castle, not far from twenty miles.

===Chinese===
在古城利默里克（Limerick）以东约十里爱尔兰旧驿之处，有一脉山峦名唤斯利夫埃利姆（Slieveelim）。当年萨瑟兰·萨斯菲尔德（Sarsfield）英姿勃发，突袭威廉王（King William）正运往围城大军的辎重炮弹，翻越此山时，曾借这山间岩穴沟壑藏身——此事遂令此山声名远扬。就在这脉山岭之下，蜿蜒着一条极古老、极狭窄的道路。它把利默里克通往蒂珀雷里（Tipperary）的大道，与利默里克通往都柏林的旧路连为一体，一路经过泥沼与牧场、山岭与沟壑、麦秸覆顶的村落和无顶的废堡，绵延近二十英里。

===Original===
Skirting the healthy mountains of which I have spoken, at one part it becomes singularly lonely. For more than three Irish miles it traverses a deserted country. A wide, black bog, level as a lake, skirted with copse, spreads at the left, as you journey northward, and the long and irregular line of mountain rises at the right, clothed in heath, broken with lines of grey rock that resemble the bold and irregular outlines of fortifications, and riven with many a gully, expanding here and there into rocky and wooded glens, which open as they approach the road.

===Chinese===
我所说的那脉草木青葱的山岭，沿其脚下一带，这条道路有一段格外荒僻孤寂。足有三英里爱尔兰旧驿的路程，它穿过一片了无人烟的乡野。一路北行，左侧铺展着一片辽阔的黑沼，平如湖面，四围矮树丛生；右侧则隆起一道绵长而不规整的山脊，满覆石楠，灰岩的纹路断续其间，状似堡垒那样险峻粗犷的轮廓；山腹之中又裂开许多沟壑，有的地方豁然张开，化作岩石嶙峋、林木掩映的幽谷，待到逼近路旁，便向行人敞开了口。

===Original===
A scanty pasturage, on which browsed a few scattered sheep or kine, skirts this solitary road for some miles, and under shelter of a hillock, and of two or three great ash-trees, stood, not many years ago, the little thatched cabin of a widow named Mary Ryan.

===Chinese===
这条孤寂的路两旁，几英里内只生着稀疏的牧草，零星几只羊、几头牛低头啃食。在一座小丘的背风处，两三棵大梣树荫蔽之下，就在不多年前，还立着一栋麦秸覆顶的小屋，屋主是个寡妇，名唤玛丽·瑞安（Mary Ryan）。

===Original===
Poor was this widow in a land of poverty. The thatch had acquired the grey tint and sunken outlines, that show how the alternations of rain and sun have told upon that perishable shelter.

===Chinese===
这寡妇贫苦极了，纵然生在一个本就贫苦的国度。屋顶的麦秸早已泛成灰白，一道道凹陷的轮廓，分明诉着雨水与日头交替啃噬这层单薄遮蔽的痕迹。

===Original===
But whatever other dangers threatened, there was one well provided against by the care of other times. Round the cabin stood half a dozen mountain ashes, as the rowans, inimical to witches, are there called. On the worn planks of the door were nailed two horseshoes, and over the lintel and spreading along the thatch, grew, luxuriant, patches of that ancient cure for many maladies, and prophylactic against the machinations of the evil one, the house-leek. Descending into the doorway, in the chiaroscuro of the interior, when your eye grew sufficiently accustomed to that dim light, you might discover, hanging at the head of the widow’s wooden-roofed bed, her beads and a phial of holy water.

===Chinese===
然而别样祸患纵有千百，独有一桩，却因前人的用心筹谋，防得甚是周全。小屋四周栽着半打山梣——那一带的人唤作花楸，据说与巫人天生相克。门板已磨得陈旧，上面钉着两只马蹄铁；门楣之上，沿着麦秸屋顶，则蓬蓬勃勃地生着一丛丛"屋韭"（house-leek）——这古老的药草能治百般病痛，又能辟除那恶者一切的诡计暗算。再走进门里去，在屋内半明半暗的光影里，待你的眼睛渐渐习惯那昏暝，便可发觉：寡妇那张木顶大床的床头，挂着她的念珠，还有一小瓶圣水。

===Original===
Here certainly were defences and bulwarks against the intrusion of that unearthly and evil power, of whose vicinity this solitary family were constantly reminded by the outline of Lisnavoura, that lonely hill-haunt of the “Good people,” as the fairies are called euphemistically, whose strangely dome-like summit rose not half a mile away, looking like an outwork of the long line of mountain that sweeps by it.

===Chinese===
这一道道防备与壁垒，自是专为抵御那超凡入邪之力的侵扰而设；至于这股力量就近在咫尺，这孤零零的一家人是无时无刻不被提醒着的——提醒他们的，是利斯纳武拉（Lisnavoura）那座山的轮廓。那座孤零零的山头，素来是"好人们"（the Good People）盘踞出没之所——人们对仙灵（fairies）向来这般讳饰地称呼。它那形貌奇特的穹顶状山巅，就在不到半里之外拔地而起，望去仿佛那条逶迤而过的山脉前伸出来的一座前哨堡垒。

===Original===
It was at the fall of the leaf, and an autumnal sunset threw the lengthening shadow of haunted Lisnavoura, close in front of the solitary little cabin, over the undulating slopes and sides of Slieveelim. The birds were singing among the branches in the thinning leaves of the melancholy ash-trees that grew at the roadside in front of the door. The widow’s three younger children were playing on the road, and their voices mingled with the evening song of the birds. Their elder sister, Nell, was “within in the house,” as their phrase is, seeing after the boiling of the potatoes for supper.

===Chinese===
其时正当落叶时节，秋日薄暮的夕照，把闹鬼的利斯纳武拉拖长的影子，正正投在那孤零零的小屋门前，漫过斯利夫埃利姆高低起伏的山坡与山腹。门前的路旁长着几株萧瑟的梣树，枝叶渐稀，鸟儿犹在丛中啼啭。寡妇的三个年幼的儿女正在路上玩耍，他们的声音与鸟雀傍晚的歌吟交织一处。他们的大姐内尔（Nell），用他们的话说，正"在屋里头"张罗着，照看晚饭煮着的土豆。

===Original===
Their mother had gone down to the bog, to carry up a hamper of turf on her back. It is, or was at least, a charitable custom—and if not disused, long may it continue—for the wealthier people when cutting their turf and stacking it in the bog, to make a smaller stack for the behoof of the poor, who were welcome to take from it so long as it lasted, and thus the potato pot was kept boiling, and hearth warm that would have been cold enough but for that good-natured bounty, through wintry months.

===Chinese===
他们的母亲已下到沼地去，要背一篓泥炭回来。这原是，至少从前原是，一桩体恤行善的风俗——若尚未废弛，愿它长存不替——较富庶的人家在沼地里割泥炭、垛泥炭时，会另垛一小堆留给穷苦人，听凭他们随意取用，取尽为止。于是，那些本会在寒冬里冷透的炉灶，因着这份好心肠的施舍，得以叫那口煮土豆的锅子始终沸腾着、炉火始终燃着。

===Original===
Moll Ryan trudged up the steep “bohereen” whose banks were overgrown with thorn and brambles, and stooping under her burden, reentered her door, where her dark-haired daughter Nell met her with a welcome, and relieved her of her hamper.

===Chinese===
莫尔·瑞安（Moll Ryan）喘着粗气，爬上那条陡峭的"小径"（bohereen）——两岸长满了荆棘与野莓——她佝偻着腰背负担，跨进自家门里，黑发的女儿内尔迎上来招呼了一声，替她把篓子卸下。

===Original===
Moll Ryan looked round with a sigh of relief, and drying her forehead, uttered the Munster ejaculation:

“Eiah, wisha! It’s tired I am with it, God bless it. And where’s the craythurs, Nell?”

“Playin’ out on the road, mother; didn’t ye see them and you comin’ up?”

“No; there was no one before me on the road,” she said, uneasily; “not a soul, Nell; and why didn’t ye keep an eye on them?”

“Well, they’re in the haggard, playin’ there, or round by the back o’ the house. Will I call them in?”

“Do so, good girl, in the name o’ God. The hens is comin’ home, see, and the sun was just down over Knockdoulah, an’ I comin’ up.”

===Chinese===
莫尔·瑞安四下环顾，长舒一口气，抹了抹额上的汗，吐出一句芒斯特（Munster）乡间的叹语：

"哎呀，唏沙！可把我累坏了，老天保佑。那些小东西呢，内尔？"

"在路上玩着呢，妈；您上来的时候没瞧见他们？"

"没瞧见；我这一路上没见着一个人影，"她不安地说，"一个活物都没有，内尔；你怎么没看着他们点儿？"

"嗨，他们在谷场里玩呢，要么就在屋后头那一带。我把他们叫进来？"

"去叫吧，好姑娘，看在老天爷分上。瞧，鸡都归窝了，我上来的时候，太阳正落到诺克杜拉（Knockdoulah）山后头去了。"

===Original===
So out ran tall, dark-haired Nell, and standing on the road, looked up and down it; but not a sign of her two little brothers, Con and Bill, or her little sister, Peg, could she see. She called them; but no answer came from the little haggard, fenced with straggling bushes. She listened, but the sound of their voices was missing. Over the stile, and behind the house she ran—but there all was silent and deserted.

===Chinese===
于是高个子、黑头发的内尔跑了出来，站在路上朝两头张望；可她看不见两个小弟弟——康（Con）和比尔（Bill）——还有小妹妹佩格（Peg）的半点影踪。她高声叫唤；可那围着一圈乱蓬蓬灌木的小谷场里，毫无应答。她侧耳细听，却听不见他们的声息。她翻过台阶，绕到屋后去——那里却是一片死寂，空无一人。

===Original===
She looked down toward the bog, as far as she could see; but they did not appear. Again she listened—but in vain. At first she had felt angry, but now a different feeling overcame her, and she grew pale. With an undefined boding she looked toward the heathy boss of Lisnavoura, now darkening into the deepest purple against the flaming sky of sunset.

Again she listened with a sinking heart, and heard nothing but the farewell twitter and whistle of the birds in the bushes around. How many stories had she listened to by the winter hearth, of children stolen by the fairies, at nightfall, in lonely places! With this fear she knew her mother was haunted.

No one in the country round gathered her little flock about her so early as this frightened widow, and no door “in the seven parishes” was barred so early.

===Chinese===
她朝着沼地的方向尽力望去；可他们终不露面。她又听了一回——仍旧徒劳。起初她原是恼怒，可此刻另一种情绪压倒了她，她脸上一阵发白。怀着一种说不清道不明的凶兆，她望向利斯纳武拉那石楠丛生的圆顶——此时正衬在一片燃烧的夕照里，渐渐深成最浓重的紫。

她心一寸寸沉下去，再侧耳听去，听见的不过是四下灌木丛中鸟儿道晚安的啁啾与啼啭。她在冬夜的炉火旁听过多少故事啊——讲孩子们如何在薄暮时分、在荒僻之地被仙灵拐走！这一桩恐惧，她知道母亲也被它缠了一辈子。

方圆一带，再没有哪个做母亲的，像这个惊惶的寡妇这样早地把自家的一窝小儿女拢到身边；也再没有哪一扇门——"七个堂区之内"——关得这样早。

===Original===
Sufficiently fearful, as all young people in that part of the world are of such dreaded and subtle agents, Nell was even more than usually afraid of them, for her terrors were infected and redoubled by her mother’s. She was looking towards Lisnavoura in a trance of fear, and crossed herself again and again, and whispered prayer after prayer. She was interrupted by her mother’s voice on the road calling her loudly. She answered, and ran round to the front of the cabin, where she found her standing.

“And where in the world’s the craythurs—did ye see sight o’ them anywhere?” cried Mrs. Ryan, as the girl came over the stile.

“Arrah! mother, ’tis only what they’re run down the road a bit. We’ll see them this minute coming back. It’s like goats they are, climbin’ here and runnin’ there; an’ if I had them here, in my hand, maybe I wouldn’t give them a hiding all round.”

“May the Lord forgive you, Nell! the childhers gone. They’re took, and not a soul near us, and Father Tom three miles away! And what’ll I do, or who’s to help us this night? Oh, wirristhru, wirristhru! The craythurs is gone!”

“Whisht, mother, be aisy: don’t ye see them comin’ up?”

And then she shouted in menacing accents, waving her arm, and beckoning the children, who were seen approaching on the road, which some little way off made a slight dip, which had concealed them. They were approaching from the westward, and from the direction of the dreaded hill of Lisnavoura.

But there were only two of the children, and one of them, the little girl, was crying. Their mother and sister hurried forward to meet them, more alarmed than ever.

“Where is Billy—where is he?” cried the mother, nearly breathless, so soon as she was within hearing.

“He’s gone—they took him away; but they said he’ll come back again,” answered little Con, with the dark brown hair.

“He’s gone away with the grand ladies,” blubbered the little girl.

“What ladies—where? Oh, Leum, asthora! My darlin’, are you gone away at last? Where is he? Who took him? What ladies are you talkin’ about? What way did he go?” she cried in distraction.

“I couldn’t see where he went, mother; ’twas like as if he was going to Lisnavoura.”

With a wild exclamation the distracted woman ran on towards the hill alone, clapping her hands, and crying aloud the name of her lost child.

Scared and horrified, Nell, not daring to follow, gazed after her, and burst into tears; and the other children raised high their lamentations in shrill rivalry.

===Chinese===
那一方水土的年轻人，对这般可怖又莫测的精怪，本就怀有相当深的畏惧，内尔也自不例外；而她的惧意，又因染了母亲的缘故，加倍地深重。她如痴如醉地陷在恐惧里，望着利斯纳武拉，一遍又一遍地在胸前画十字，一句接一句地低声祷告。母亲的喊声从路上传来，把她惊醒。她应了一声，绕到小屋前头，见母亲已站在那里。

"那些小东西到底哪儿去啦——你哪儿都没瞧见他们一眼？"瑞安夫人在女孩翻过台阶时喊道。

"哎呀，妈！他们不过是顺着路跑下去一截罢了。这会儿就该瞧见他们回来了。这帮小东西跟山羊似的，一会儿爬这儿、一会儿跑那儿；要叫我逮着了，捏在手心里，嘿，少不得要挨个儿揍他们一顿。"

"愿主饶恕你，内尔！孩子们没了。他们被拐走啦，我们四下里一个人都没有，汤姆神父（Father Tom）又在三里开外！我该怎么办呢，今夜谁来帮我们？哎呀，苦哇，苦哇！那些小东西没了呀！"

"嘘，妈，别急：您没瞧见他们正上来了？"

她一边压低声音喝止，一边扬起手臂，虚张声势地吆喝着，朝那几个孩子招手——只见他们正从路上走来；那路在前面不远处略略下凹了一截，方才把他们的身影遮住了。他们是从西边来的，正是从那叫人胆寒的利斯纳武拉山那一带来。

可是孩子只有两个，其中一个，那个小妹妹，正哭着。母亲和姐姐急忙迎上前去，比刚才更慌了。

"比利呢——比利在哪儿？"母亲刚到听得见的距离，便气喘吁吁地喊。

"他走了——他们把他带走了；可他们说他还回来的，"深棕色头发的小康答道。

"他跟着那几位阔太太走啦，"小妹妹抽抽搭搭地说。

"什么太太——在哪儿？哎呀，我的利姆（Leum）呀，我的心肝！我的心肝宝贝，你到底也走了吗？他在哪儿？谁把他带走了？你说的什么太太呀？他往哪条路走的？"她神色狂乱地叫嚷。

"我瞧不见他往哪儿去了，妈；瞧着像是往利斯纳武拉那边去的。"

这神志昏乱的妇人一声惨叫，独自朝那座山奔去，一边拍着手，一边高声呼喊着她丢失的孩子的名字。

内尔骇得魂飞魄散，又不敢跟上去，只能怔怔地望着她的背影，泪如雨下；另外两个孩子也尖锐地此起彼伏地号啕起来。

===Original===
Twilight was deepening. It was long past the time when they were usually barred securely within their habitation. Nell led the younger children into the cabin, and made them sit down by the turf fire, while she stood in the open door, watching in great fear for the return of her mother.

After a long while they did see their mother return. She came in and sat down by the fire, and cried as if her heart would break.

“Will I bar the doore, mother?” asked Nell.

“Ay, do—didn’t I lose enough, this night, without lavin’ the doore open, for more o’ yez to go; but first take an’ sprinkle a dust o’ the holy waters over ye, acuishla, and bring it here till I throw a taste iv it over myself and the craythurs; an’ I wondher, Nell, you’d forget to do the like yourself, lettin’ the craythurs out so near nightfall. Come here and sit on my knees, asthora, come to me, mavourneen, and hould me fast, in the name o’ God, and I’ll hould you fast that none can take yez from me, and tell me all about it, and what it was—the Lord between us and harm—an’ how it happened, and who was in it.”

And the door being barred, the two children, sometimes speaking together, often interrupting one another, often interrupted by their mother, managed to tell this strange story, which I had better relate connectedly and in my own language.

===Chinese===
暮色愈来愈浓。他们平日关紧门户的时辰，早已过了许久。内尔把两个小的领进屋里，让他们在泥炭炉火旁坐下，自己却立在敞开的门口，怀着极大的恐惧，盼着母亲归来。

过了好一阵，她们果然看见母亲回来了。她进屋，在炉边坐下，哭得肝肠寸断。

"门我闩上了吧，妈？"内尔问。

"嗯，闩上吧——今夜我已经丢得够多的了，还留着门敞着，干啥？好叫你们再多走几个？可你先舀一掬圣水，弹一点儿在身上，心肝儿，再把水端过来，让我也洒一点儿在自己和这些小东西身上；我倒要怪你呢，内尔——天都快黑了，你放小东西们出去，自己竟忘了也这么做。过来，坐到我膝上来，心肝，过来，我的心肝宝贝，看在老天爷分上紧紧抱住我，我也紧紧抱住你，叫谁也休想再把你们从我手里夺走——你们都给我讲讲，到底出了什么事，是什么东西——愿主挡去一切灾祸——是怎么发生的，都有些什么人。"

门闩上了。两个孩子，有时一齐开口，时常抢着打断对方，又时常被母亲打断，七嘴八舌地，总算讲出了这桩离奇的事。这件事，我看还是由我用自己的话，把它从头到尾连缀着讲一遍，更清楚些。

===Original===
The Widow Ryan’s three children were playing, as I have said, upon the narrow old road in front of her door. Little Bill or Leum, about five years old, with golden hair and large blue eyes, was a very pretty boy, with all the clear tints of healthy childhood, and that gaze of earnest simplicity which belongs not to town children of the same age. His little sister Peg, about a year older, and his brother Con, a little more than a year elder than she, made up the little group.

Under the great old ash-trees, whose last leaves were falling at their feet, in the light of an October sunset, they were playing with the hilarity and eagerness of rustic children, clamouring together, and their faces were turned toward the west and storied hill of Lisnavoura.

===Chinese===
我已说过，瑞安寡妇的三个孩子，正在她门前那条又窄又旧的路上玩耍。小比利，又叫利姆（Leum），年约五岁，一头金发，一双蓝色的大眼睛，是个极俊俏的男孩，带着健康孩童那种明净的气色，又带着乡下孩子那种专注而天真的神情——城里的同龄孩子是断断没有那种神情的。他的小妹妹佩格约莫比他大一岁，哥哥康又比佩格大一岁多一点，这几个小人儿便凑成了这一小群。

几株老梣树荫下，最后的几片落叶正纷纷坠在他们脚边，十月夕照之中，他们嬉闹着，带着乡下孩子那种乐不可支、兴致勃勃的劲头，叽叽喳喳地叫嚷着；他们的脸都朝着西边，朝着那座载满传说的利斯纳武拉山。

===Original===
Suddenly a startling voice with a screech called to them from behind, ordering them to get out of the way, and turning, they saw a sight, such as they never beheld before. It was a carriage drawn by four horses that were pawing and snorting, in impatience, as it just pulled up. The children were almost under their feet, and scrambled to the side of the road next their own door.

This carriage and all its appointments were old-fashioned and gorgeous, and presented to the children, who had never seen anything finer than a turf car, and once, an old chaise that passed that way from Killaloe, a spectacle perfectly dazzling.

Here was antique splendour. The harness and trappings were scarlet, and blazing with gold. The horses were huge, and snow white, with great manes, that as they tossed and shook them in the air, seemed to stream and float sometimes longer and sometimes shorter, like so much smoke—their tails were long, and tied up in bows of broad scarlet and gold ribbon. The coach itself was glowing with colours, gilded and emblazoned. There were footmen in gay liveries, and three-cocked hats, like the coachman’s; but he had a great wig, like a judge’s, and their hair was frizzed out and powdered, and a long thick “pigtail,” with a bow to it, hung down the back of each.

===Chinese===
忽然，身后传来一声尖利的喝叫，吆喝着他们赶紧让路，孩子们一回头，便看见了一桩他们从未见过的景象。原来是一辆马车，由四匹马拉着，刚刚停稳，马匹正不耐烦地刨着蹄子、喷着响鼻。孩子们几乎就在马蹄底下，赶紧手忙脚乱地躲到靠自家门那一侧的路旁去。

这辆马车连同它全部的排场，俱是古色古香、富丽堂皇，对这几个孩子而言——他们平生见过最气派的，不过是运泥炭的板车，再有就是基拉卢（Killaloe）那边有一次路过的一辆旧式轻便马车——眼前这一幕，简直把他们晃得睁不开眼。

这是古时的奢华排场。鞍辔与饰带俱是大红，金光灼灼。那几匹马身形高大，通体雪白，鬃毛又长又盛，待它们在空中一甩一抖，便似浓烟一般，时而拖得长、时而飘得短——尾巴也长，用宽宽的大红金缎带系成蝴蝶结扎起。马车本身则色彩斑斓，描金涂彩，绘着纹章。车旁随行的仆役穿着鲜艳的号衣，戴着与车夫相似的三尖帽；车夫头上却戴着一顶大大的假发，形如法官所戴；仆役们的头发则都烫得蓬松，扑着粉，脑后各拖着一根又粗又长的"辫子"，末端还系着个蝴蝶结。

===Original===
All these servants were diminutive, and ludicrously out of proportion with the enormous horses of the equipage, and had sharp, sallow features, and small, restless fiery eyes, and faces of cunning and malice that chilled the children. The little coachman was scowling and showing his white fangs under his cocked hat, and his little blazing beads of eyes were quivering with fury in their sockets as he whirled his whip round and round over their heads, till the lash of it looked like a streak of fire in the evening sun, and sounded like the cry of a legion of “fillapoueeks” in the air.

“Stop the princess on the highway!” cried the coachman, in a piercing treble.

“Stop the princess on the highway!” piped each footman in turn, scowling over his shoulder down on the children, and grinding his keen teeth.

The children were so frightened they could only gape and turn white in their panic. But a very sweet voice from the open window of the carriage reassured them, and arrested the attack of the lackeys.

===Chinese===
这一众仆役，身量都极矮小，与那几匹高头大马相较，比例滑稽得可笑；他们面相尖削蜡黄，一双小眼睛不安分地闪着火光，一脸刁钻狠毒之色，看得孩子们心里发凉。那小个子车夫在三尖帽下虎着脸，龇出一口白牙；他那双火珠般的小眼睛在眼眶里气得直打颤，一边把马鞭在他们头顶上一圈又一圈地抡着，那鞭梢在夕照里看起来活像一道火光，破空之声则像一群"鞭子精"在半空中齐声尖叫。

"在大路上截住公主！"车夫用尖锐的假声叫道。

"在大路上截住公主！"仆役们挨个儿尖声附和，回过头来居高临下地瞪着孩子们，磨着那口尖牙。

孩子们吓坏了，只能张口结舌，吓得脸色煞白。可这时从马车敞开的车窗里，传来一个极温柔动听的声音，安抚了他们，也止住了仆役们的进逼。

===Original===
A beautiful and “very grand-looking” lady was smiling from it on them, and they all felt pleased in the strange light of that smile.

“The boy with the golden hair, I think,” said the lady, bending her large and wonderfully clear eyes on little Leum.

The upper sides of the carriage were chiefly of glass, so that the children could see another woman inside, whom they did not like so well.

This was a black woman, with a wonderfully long neck, hung round with many strings of large variously-coloured beads, and on her head was a sort of turban of silk striped with all the colours of the rainbow, and fixed in it was a golden star.

This black woman had a face as thin almost as a death’s-head, with high cheekbones, and great goggle eyes, the whites of which, as well as her wide range of teeth, showed in brilliant contrast with her skin, as she looked over the beautiful lady’s shoulder, and whispered something in her ear.

“Yes; the boy with the golden hair, I think,” repeated the lady.

===Chinese===
一位美貌而"极华贵"的夫人，正从车窗里朝他们微笑，他们在这陌生的笑意里，都觉得一阵说不出的欢喜。

"那个金头发的男孩子，我想，"夫人说道，把她那双大而格外澄澈的眼睛，望向小利姆。

马车的上半截两侧大多是玻璃，孩子们由此看得见车里还有另一个女人——这一个，他们就不怎么喜欢了。

这是个黑皮肤的女人，脖子长得离奇，上面挂着一串又一串五颜六色的大珠子；头上裹着一种头巾，是彩虹般各色相间的条纹丝绸所制，头巾上别着一颗金星。

这黑女人一张脸瘦得几乎像个骷髅，颧骨高耸，两只大眼暴突；当她从那位美丽夫人的肩头探过去，附在她耳畔低语时，那眼白和一排阔牙，衬着她那身黑皮肤，亮得刺眼。

"是；那个金头发的男孩子，我想，"夫人又重复了一遍。

===Original===
And her voice sounded sweet as a silver bell in the children’s ears, and her smile beguiled them like the light of an enchanted lamp, as she leaned from the window with a look of ineffable fondness on the golden-haired boy, with the large blue eyes; insomuch that little Billy, looking up, smiled in return with a wondering fondness, and when she stooped down, and stretched her jewelled arms towards him, he stretched his little hands up, and how they touched the other children did not know; but, saying, “Come and give me a kiss, my darling,” she raised him, and he seemed to ascend in her small fingers as lightly as a feather, and she held him in her lap and covered him with kisses.

Nothing daunted, the other children would have been only too happy to change places with their favoured little brother. There was only one thing that was unpleasant, and a little frightened them, and that was the black woman, who stood and stretched forward, in the carriage as before. She gathered a rich silk and gold handkerchief that was in her fingers up to her lips, and seemed to thrust ever so much of it, fold after fold, into her capacious mouth, as they thought to smother her laughter, with which she seemed convulsed, for she was shaking and quivering, as it seemed, with suppressed merriment; but her eyes, which remained uncovered, looked angrier than they had ever seen eyes look before.

===Chinese===
她那声音在孩子们听来，清甜如一只银铃；她的微笑蛊惑着他们，恍如一盏魔灯的光。她从车窗里探出半身，带着一种说不出的疼爱之色，望着那金发碧眼的小男孩；小比利仰起头来，竟也带着一种又惊又喜的依恋，回报她一笑。待她俯下身，伸出她那戴满珠宝的双臂向他探去，他便把一双小手高高举起——他们是怎么碰到一起的，旁的孩子全没看清；只听她说着："来，给我亲一个，我的心肝，"便把他抱了起来，他似乎在她的指尖上轻若无物地飘起，宛如一根羽毛；她把他抱在膝上，亲吻不绝。

旁的孩子毫无惧色，恨不得能和得宠的小弟弟换个位置才好。唯独有一桩叫人不痛快、又有点儿叫人害怕的，便是那个黑女人，她还和方才一样，在车里站着、探着身子。她把手里一方华贵的丝金手帕，一寸寸地抿到唇边，似乎一折又一折地，把好长一截都塞进了她那张阔嘴里——孩子们只当她是要捂住自己的笑，因为她分明像笑得抽搐了一般，浑身抖个不停，像是强自按捺着的一阵狂喜；只是她那双没遮住的眼睛，却露出孩子们从未在谁眼中见过的、那样凶狠的光。

===Original===
But the lady was so beautiful they looked on her instead, and she continued to caress and kiss the little boy on her knee; and smiling at the other children she held up a large russet apple in her fingers, and the carriage began to move slowly on, and with a nod inviting them to take the fruit, she dropped it on the road from the window; it rolled some way beside the wheels, they following, and then she dropped another, and then another, and so on. And the same thing happened to all; for just as either of the children who ran beside had caught the rolling apple, somehow it slipt into a hole or ran into a ditch, and looking up they saw the lady drop another from the window, and so the chase was taken up and continued till they got, hardly knowing how far they had gone, to the old crossroad that leads to Owney. It seemed that there the horses’ hoofs and carriage wheels rolled up a wonderful dust, which being caught in one of those eddies that whirl the dust up into a column, on the calmest day, enveloped the children for a moment, and passed whirling on towards Lisnavoura, the carriage, as they fancied, driving in the centre of it; but suddenly it subsided, the straws and leaves floated to the ground, the dust dissipated itself, but the white horses and the lackeys, the gilded carriage, the lady and their little golden-haired brother were gone.

At the same moment suddenly the upper rim of the clear setting sun disappeared behind the hill of Knockdoula, and it was twilight. Each child felt the transition like a shock—and the sight of the rounded summit of Lisnavoura, now closely overhanging them, struck them with a new fear.

They screamed their brother’s name after him, but their cries were lost in the vacant air. At the same time they thought they heard a hollow voice say, close to them, “Go home.”

Looking round and seeing no one, they were scared, and hand in hand—the little girl crying wildly, and the boy white as ashes, from fear, they trotted homeward, at their best speed, to tell, as we have seen, their strange story.

===Chinese===
可那位夫人美貌如此，孩子们便只顾看她；她继续抚弄、亲吻着膝上的小男孩；又朝旁的孩子微微一笑，用手指擎起一只硕大的黄褐色的苹果。马车缓缓地动了起来，她点了点头，像是邀他们去拿那只果子，便从窗口把它丢在了路上；那苹果顺着车轮旁滚出去一截，孩子们追了上去；接着她又丢下一只，又一只，如此接二连三。可每一只的遭遇都一样：旁的孩子刚要追上那滚动的苹果，它不知怎的就滑进了一个窟窿，或滚进了路旁的沟里；他们一抬头，又见夫人从窗口丢下了另一只；这场追逐便这般此起彼伏地持续着，直到他们几乎不知自己走了多远，来到了通往奥尼（Owney）的那条古岔路口。似乎就在那儿，马蹄与车轮扬起了一阵奇异的尘土，恰好被那种即便在最无风的日子里也能把尘土旋成一根柱子的小旋风卷住，一时把孩子们裹在里头，又一路旋转着朝利斯纳武拉卷去——他们恍惚觉得，那马车正行在这旋风的正中；可忽然之间，风息了，草茎与落叶飘然坠地，尘土消散殆尽——而那几匹白马、那些仆役、那辆描金的马车、那位夫人，还有他们那个金发的小弟弟，统统都不见了。

也就在这一刹那，那一轮清清楚楚的落日的上沿，突然沉到了诺克杜拉山的山后，暮色降了下来。每一个孩子都觉着这变化像挨了一下闷棍——而抬眼看见利斯纳武拉那浑圆的山巅，此刻正紧贴在他们头顶上方悬着，又给了他们一阵新的惊恐。

他们朝着弟弟远去的方向，尖叫着他的名字，可他们的呼喊都消失在空荡荡的天际里。与此同时，他们恍惚听见一个空洞的声音，就在他们身旁说起话来："回家去吧。"

他们四下张望，看不见一个人影，吓得要死；于是手牵着手——小妹妹撕心裂肺地哭着，小男孩吓得面如死灰——撒开腿，拼了命地往家跑，好去把他们那桩离奇的故事讲出来，一如我们方才所见。

===Original===
Molly Ryan never more saw her darling. But something of the lost little boy was seen by his former playmates.

Sometimes when their mother was away earning a trifle at haymaking, and Nelly washing the potatoes for their dinner, or “beatling” clothes in the little stream that flows in the hollow close by, they saw the pretty face of little Billy peeping in archly at the door, and smiling silently at them, and as they ran to embrace him, with cries of delight, he drew back, still smiling archly, and when they got out into the open day, he was gone, and they could see no trace of him anywhere.

This happened often, with slight variations in the circumstances of the visit. Sometimes he would peep for a longer time, sometimes for a shorter time, sometimes his little hand would come in, and, with bended finger, beckon them to follow; but always he was smiling with the same arch look and wary silence—and always he was gone when they reached the door. Gradually these visits grew less and less frequent, and in about eight months they ceased altogether, and little Billy, irretrievably lost, took rank in their memories with the dead.

===Chinese===
莫莉·瑞安从此再没见过她的心肝宝贝。可是这丢失的小男孩的一点踪影，倒还被他从前的玩伴们瞧见过几回。

有时，母亲出门打短工割干草挣几个小钱去了，内莉在洗午饭的土豆，或者在那条流过近旁沟壑的小溪里"捶打"着衣物，他们便会瞧见小比利那张俊俏的小脸，淘气地从门口探进来，冲他们无声地笑着；待他们欢叫着一拥而上要去抱他，他便往后退去，依旧是那副淘气的笑脸；等他们追到屋外明处，他已经不见了，哪里也寻不着他的半点踪影。

这样的事时常发生，每次情形大同小异。有时他探进头来张望得久些，有时短些；有时只是他那只小手伸进来，弯着根指头，招他们跟他走；可他永远带着同样一副淘气的神情、同样警觉的沉默微笑着——也永远是等他们追到门口，他便消失了。渐渐地，这类造访越来越稀，约莫八个月之后，便彻底断绝了；小比利既已无可挽回地失去，便在他们记忆之中，与死者归作了一类。

===Original===
One wintry morning, nearly a year and a half after his disappearance, their mother having set out for Limerick soon after cockcrow, to sell some fowls at the market, the little girl, lying by the side of her elder sister, who was fast asleep, just at the grey of the morning heard the latch lifted softly, and saw little Billy enter and close the door gently after him. There was light enough to see that he was barefoot and ragged, and looked pale and famished. He went straight to the fire, and cowered over the turf embers, and rubbed his hands slowly, and seemed to shiver as he gathered the smouldering turf together.

The little girl clutched her sister in terror and whispered, “Waken, Nelly, waken; here’s Billy come back!”

Nelly slept soundly on, but the little boy, whose hands were extended close over the coals, turned and looked toward the bed, it seemed to her, in fear, and she saw the glare of the embers reflected on his thin cheek as he turned toward her. He rose and went, on tiptoe, quickly to the door, in silence, and let himself out as softly as he had come in.

After that, the little boy was never seen any more by anyone of his kindred.

===Chinese===
一年半将尽的一个冬日清晨，他失踪已近一年半了——母亲天刚擦亮、公鸡才叫过不久，便动身去利默里克集市卖几只家禽。小妹妹挨着熟睡的姐姐躺着，就在天蒙蒙亮的时分，听见门闩被人轻轻抬起，看见小比利走了进来，又随手轻轻把门带上。屋里光线尚足以辨出：他赤着脚，衣衫褴褛，脸色苍白，一副饥寒交迫的模样。他径直走到炉火前，蜷在泥炭余烬上头，慢慢地搓着双手，一边把那将要熄灭的泥炭拢到一处，一边似乎冷得发抖。

小妹妹惊恐地一把抓住姐姐，悄声说："醒醒，内莉，醒醒；比利回来啦！"

内莉依旧睡得死沉。可那小男孩——他正把双手伸在炭火上方——却回过头来朝床这边望了一眼，她看着像是带着惧色；他朝她转过来时，她看见余烬的红光映在他消瘦的脸颊上。随即他站起身，踮着脚，一言不发地快步走到门口，像进来时那样轻轻地，又让自己出去了。

从那以后，这个男孩就再没被任何一位亲人见到过。

===Original===
“Fairy doctors,” as the dealers in the preternatural, who in such cases were called in, are termed, did all that in them lay—but in vain. Father Tom came down, and tried what holier rites could do, but equally without result. So little Billy was dead to mother, brother, and sisters; but no grave received him. Others whom affection cherished, lay in holy ground, in the old churchyard of Abington, with headstone to mark the spot over which the survivor might kneel and say a kind prayer for the peace of the departed soul. But there was no landmark to show where little Billy was hidden from their loving eyes, unless it was in the old hill of Lisnavoura, that cast its long shadow at sunset before the cabin-door; or that, white and filmy in the moonlight, in later years, would occupy his brother’s gaze as he returned from fair or market, and draw from him a sigh and a prayer for the little brother he had lost so long ago, and was never to see again.

===Chinese===
那些在这种事上被人请去、专与超自然之事打交道的"仙灵郎中"（fairy doctors），穷尽了他们所会的种种——却全是徒劳。汤姆神父也亲来了一趟，试着以更神圣的仪式做他能做的一切，结果同样毫无效验。于是，小比利对母亲、对哥哥、对姐姐们而言，便已经死了；然而并没有一座坟收留他。别的那些为亲情所珍爱的人，都葬在阿宾顿（Abington）那座古老墓园的圣土之中，各有墓碑标出所在，好让生者能在碑前跪下，为亡魂的安息念上一句善祷。可小比利藏身何处，再没有任何标志能指给这些慈爱的眼睛看——除非是在利斯纳武拉那座古山之中；那座山日落时把长长的影子投在小屋的门前；到后来的年月里，哥哥从集市或庙会上归来，月光下的山影白茫茫、朦胧胧的，总会引得他凝望许久，从他胸中引出一声叹息、一句祷告，为那个他失去已久、永不能再见的弟弟。

## The Dead Sexton / 死去的司事

===Original===
The sunsets were red, the nights were long, and the weather pleasantly frosty; and Christmas, the glorious herald of the New Year, was at hand, when an event—still recounted by winter firesides, with a horror made delightful by the mellowing influence of years—occurred in the beautiful little town of Golden Friars, and signalized, as the scene of its catastrophe, the old inn known throughout a wide region of the Northumbrian counties as the George and Dragon.

Toby Crooke, the sexton, was lying dead in the old coach-house in the inn yard. The body had been discovered, only half an hour before this story begins, under strange circumstances, and in a place where it might have lain the better part of a week undisturbed; and a dreadful suspicion astounded the village of Golden Friars.

===Chinese===
落日殷红，长夜漫漫，寒霜之气宜人；恰在圣诞——新年荣耀的先驱——将近之际，一桩往事发生了。此事至今仍为冬夜炉畔所传述，岁月的冲淡令其中惊惧变得令人回味。事情出在金修士镇（Golden Friars）这座秀美的小镇，而灾祸降临的所在，便是那间在诺森伯兰诸郡（Northumbrian counties）方圆数百里内无人不知的老客栈——"乔治与龙"（George and Dragon）。

教堂司事托比·克鲁克（Toby Crooke）死了，陈尸于客栈院里那间旧马车房中。这具尸首是在本篇故事开始之前仅半小时方才被人发现的，发现时的情形颇为古怪，而那地方偏僻幽深，纵使尸首搁上大半个礼拜也未必有人搅扰。一时间，一桩骇人的疑团震骇了整个金修士镇。

===Original===
A wintry sunset was glaring through a gorge of the western mountains, turning into fire the twigs of the leafless elms, and all the tiny blades of grass on the green by which the quaint little town is surrounded. It is built of light, grey stone, with steep gables and slender chimneys rising with airy lightness from the level sward by the margin of the beautiful lake, and backed by the grand amphitheatre of the fells at the other side, whose snowy peaks show faintly against the sky, tinged with the vaporous red of the western light. As you descend towards the margin of the lake, and see Golden Friars, its taper chimneys and slender gables, its curious old inn and gorgeous sign, and over all the graceful tower and spire of the ancient church, at this hour or by moonlight, in the solemn grandeur and stillness of the natural scenery that surrounds it, it stands before you like a fairy town.

===Chinese===
冬日的夕阳正从西山一道峡谷间斜照过来，将那些光秃秃的榆树枝丫、镇子四周草地上每一片细小的草叶，都映得通红似火。小镇以浅灰色石头筑成，陡峭的山墙和纤细的烟囱从湖畔平整的草地间拔地而起，轻盈飘渺；背靠另一侧群山围合而成的壮阔天然剧场，那重重山峦的雪峰在天幕上隐约可见，染着西天雾蒙蒙的霞光。你若沿着山坡下到湖边，遥望金修士镇——它那尖塔般的烟囱和修长的山墙，它那古趣盎然的老客栈和气派的招牌，还有那古朴教堂秀美的钟楼与尖顶，统领全局——无论在此时分的霞光下，还是在月色之中，置身于周遭那庄严肃穆、万籁俱寂的山光水色之间，整座小镇便如仙境之城一般，出现在你眼前。

===Original===
Toby Crooke, the lank sexton, now fifty or upwards, had passed an hour or two with some village cronies, over a solemn pot of purl, in the kitchen of that cosy hostelry, the night before. He generally turned in there at about seven o’clock, and heard the news. This contented him: for he talked little, and looked always surly.

Many things are now raked up and talked over about him.

===Chinese===
托比·克鲁克这瘦长条子的司事，年过半百，头天夜里还在那间舒适客栈的厨房里，同几个村中老友一起正正经经地灌了一壶热气腾腾的苦艾麦酒，消磨了一两个时辰。他照例在七点左右踅进店里来，听一听各路消息。这便够他受用了：他本就话少，面色也总是阴沉沉的。

如今关于他的种种旧事，又被翻出来，你一言我一语地议论开了。

===Original===
In early youth, he had been a bit of a scamp. He broke his indentures, and ran away from his master, the tanner of Bryemere; he had got into fifty bad scrapes and out again; and, just as the little world of Golden Friars had come to the conclusion that it would be well for all parties—except, perhaps, himself—and a happy riddance for his afflicted mother, if he were sunk, with a gross of quart pots about his neck, in the bottom of the lake in which the grey gables, the elms, and the towering fells of Golden Friars are mirrored, he suddenly returned, a reformed man at the ripe age of forty.

For twelve years he had disappeared, and no one knew what had become of him. Then, suddenly, as I say, he reappeared at Golden Friars—a very black and silent man, sedate and orderly. His mother was dead and buried; but the “prodigal son” was received good-naturedly. The good vicar, Doctor Jenner, reported to his wife:

===Chinese===
他年少时节本是个不学好的浪荡子。他撕毁了学徒契约，从师父——布莱米尔（Bryemere）那个鞣皮匠——那里跑了；前前后后闯了不知多少祸，又不知多少次脱身出来。正当金修士镇这方小天地里的人一致断定：若在他脖子上吊上一罗格特酒壶，将他沉到湖底去——金修士镇的灰色山墙、榆树和巍巍群峰都倒映其中的那面湖水——那于各方（也许除了他本人）都是件大好事，对他那苦命的母亲来说也是甩掉了一个大包袱——恰在这般议论纷纷之际，他却忽然回来了，四十岁的人，说是已改邪归正。

整整十二年，他杳无音信，没人知道他的下落。后来，正如我所说，他又突然出现在金修士镇——一个黑黝黝的、沉默寡言的人，举止端方，行事规矩。他的母亲早已下葬；但这"浪子回头"，镇上人倒也好脾气地接纳了。好心的牧师詹纳博士（Doctor Jenner）对他妻子说：

===Original===
“His hard heart has been softened, dear Dolly. I saw him dry his eyes, poor fellow, at the sermon yesterday.”

“I don’t wonder, Hugh darling. I know the part—‘There is joy in Heaven.’ I am sure it was—wasn’t it? It was quite beautiful. I almost cried myself.”

The Vicar laughed gently, and stooped over her chair and kissed her, and patted her cheek fondly.

“You think too well of your old man’s sermons,” he said. “I preach, you see, Dolly, very much to the *poor*. If *they* understand me, I am pretty sure everyone else must; and I think that my simple style goes more home to both feelings and conscience—”

“You ought to have told me of his crying before. You *are* so eloquent,” exclaimed Dolly Jenner. “No one preaches like my man. I have never heard such sermons.”

Not many, we may be sure; for the good lady had not heard more than six from any other divine for the last twenty years.

===Chinese===
"他那颗硬心肠到底软下来了，亲爱的多莉。昨天讲道的时候，我亲眼看见他擦眼泪呢，可怜的人。"

"那有什么奇怪的，休，亲爱的。那一段我晓得——'天上欢喜'嘛。我敢说那一篇讲得真是——是不是？真是美极了。我自己都差点掉泪了。"

牧师温和地笑了笑，俯身凑到她椅子边，吻了吻她，又爱怜地拍了拍她的脸颊。

"你太抬举你老头子的讲道了，"他说。"你看，多莉，我讲道大半是对着*穷人*的。*他们*若听得懂，旁人就一定也听得懂。我这种朴朴素素的路数，反而更直抵人心——无论情感还是良心——"

"你早该告诉我他哭了的事。你*就是*能说会道，"多莉·詹纳（Dolly Jenner）叫道。"没人讲道比得上我家的。我从没听过那样的讲道。"

这话自然不假——要知道这位好太太二十年来，从任何别位牧师那里听过的讲道，统共也不过六回而已。

===Original===
The personages of Golden Friars talked Toby Crooke over on his return. Doctor Lincote said:

“He must have led a hard life; he had ‘dried in’ so, and got a good deal of hard muscle; and he rather fancied he had been soldiering—he stood like a soldier; and the mark over his right eye looked like a gunshot.”

People might wonder how he could have survived a gunshot over the eye; but was not Lincote a doctor—and an army doctor to boot—when he was young; and who, in Golden Friars, could dispute with him on points of surgery? And I believe the truth is, that this mark had been really made by a pistol bullet.

Mr. Jarlcot, the attorney, would “go bail” he had picked up some sense in his travels; and honest Turnbull, the host of the George and Dragon, said heartily:

“We must look out something for him to put his hand to. *Now’s* the time to make a man of him.”

The end of it was that he became, among other things, the sexton of Golden Friars.

===Chinese===
托比·克鲁克回来之后，金修士镇的头面人物们把他议来论去。林科特医生（Doctor Lincote）说：

"他这些年过的必是苦日子；人都'干缩'成那样了，倒练出一身结实的筋肉。我倒觉得他当过兵——他站立的架势像个军人；右眼上方那道疤，看着像是枪伤。"

人们或许要纳闷，眼上方中了枪怎还能活命？可林科特难道不是医生么——年轻时还是军医呢；金修士镇上，在外科方面有谁敢跟他争？而我所知的真相是：那道疤痕，确系手枪子弹所留。

律师贾尔科特先生（Mr. Jarlcot）"敢打包票"说，他这一趟在外头跑，定是长了见识的；"乔治与龙"那位实在的掌柜特恩布尔（Turnbull）也由衷地说：

"咱们得给他找点事做。*趁现在*，把他造就成一个正经人。"

事情的结果便是——他当上了金修士镇的教堂司事，此外还兼着些别的差事。

===Original===
He was a punctual sexton. He meddled with no other person’s business; but he was a silent man, and by no means popular. He was reserved in company; and he used to walk alone by the shore of the lake, while other fellows played at fives or skittles; and when he visited the kitchen of the George, he had his liquor to himself, and in the midst of the general talk was a saturnine listener. There was something sinister in this man’s face; and when things went wrong with him, he could look dangerous enough.

There were whispered stories in Golden Friars about Toby Crooke. Nobody could say how they got there. Nothing is more mysterious than the spread of rumour. It is like a vial poured on the air. It travels, like an epidemic, on the sightless currents of the atmosphere, or by the laws of a telluric influence equally intangible. These stories treated, though darkly, of the long period of his absence from his native village; but they took no well-defined shape, and no one could refer them to any authentic source.

The Vicar’s charity was of the kind that thinketh no evil; and in such cases he always insisted on proof. Crooke was, of course, undisturbed in his office.

===Chinese===
他做司事倒是一丝不苟，从不误事。他不管别人的闲事；但他是个沉默寡言的人，人缘并不好。他在人群中总是独来独往；旁人打墙手球、玩九柱戏的时候，他只管独自沿着湖边走来走去；他到"乔治与龙"的厨房里来，也只顾自斟自饮，在一屋子的喧天说笑中间，他是个阴沉的听客。此人面相上有一种说不出的凶险之气；但凡事情不顺他的意，那副神情便可怖得很。

金修士镇上，关于托比·克鲁克的闲话，在暗地里窃窃私语地流传着。没人说得清这些话是从哪里来的。世间的流言之传播，再没有比这更神秘的了。它好比一只瓶子倒在了空气里。它像瘟疫一般，借那看不见的气流播散，又或循着同样无从捉摸的地气之理，四处蔓延。那些故事影影绰绰地牵涉到他离开故乡的那段漫长岁月；但始终没有个确切的轮廓，谁也指不出它们出自哪个可靠的源头。

牧师的仁慈之心，是那种"不计算人的恶"的仁慈；遇到这种事，他总要讲究真凭实据。克鲁克自然安安稳稳地做着他的司事。

===Original===
On the evening before the tragedy came to light—trifles are always remembered after the catastrophe—a boy, returning along the margin of the mere, passed him by seated on a prostrate trunk of a tree, under the “bield” of a rock, counting silver money. His lean body and limbs were bent together, his knees were up to his chin, and his long fingers were telling the coins over hurriedly in the hollow of his other hand. He glanced at the boy, as the old English saying is, like “the devil looking over Lincoln.” But a black and sour look from Mr. Crooke, who never had a smile for a child nor a greeting for a wayfarer, was nothing strange.

===Chinese===
惨案败露的前一天傍晚——灾祸过后，枝微末节的小事总会被人一一记起——一个男孩沿着湖边走回来，路过他身边时，只见他坐在一块岩石的背风处，一截倒伏的树干上，正数着银钱。他那瘦骨嶙峋的身子四肢蜷作一团，膝盖几乎顶着下巴，修长的手指在另一只手的掌心里急急忙忙地拨弄着钱币。他瞟了那男孩一眼——正如英国老话所说——活像"魔鬼俯瞰林肯城"。不过，克鲁克先生这张黑沉酸苦的脸，向来如此：他对孩子从来挤不出一个笑脸，对过路客也从没有一声招呼，所以这倒也算不得什么新鲜事。

===Original===
Toby Crooke lived in the grey stone house, cold and narrow, that stands near the church porch, with the window of its staircase looking out into the churchyard, where so much of his labour, for many a day, had been expended. The greater part of this house was untenanted.

The old woman who was in charge of it slept in a settle-bed, among broken stools, old sacks, rotten chests and other rattle-traps, in the small room at the rear of the house, floored with tiles.

===Chinese===
托比·克鲁克住在教堂门廊近旁那座灰色石屋里，屋子阴冷逼仄，楼梯间的窗户正对着教堂墓地——那片坟地，便是他许多时日以来大半劳作之所。这房子大部分都空着。

看房子的老妪，睡在屋后一间铺了地砖的小房间里，一张折叠榻床上，四围堆满了破凳子、旧麻袋、朽烂的箱柜以及各色破烂家什。

===Original===
At what time of the night she could not tell, she awoke, and saw a man, with his hat on, in her room. He had a candle in his hand, which he shaded with his coat from her eye; his back was towards her, and he was rummaging in the drawer in which she usually kept her money.

Having got her quarter’s pension of two pounds that day, however, she had placed it, folded in a rag, in the corner of her tea caddy, and locked it up in the “eat-malison” or cupboard.

She was frightened when she saw the figure in her room, and she could not tell whether her visitor might not have made his entrance from the contiguous churchyard. So, sitting bolt upright in her bed, her grey hair almost lifting her kerchief off her head, and all over in “a fit o’ t’ creepins,” as she expressed it, she demanded:

“In God’s name, what want ye thar?”

“Whar’s the peppermint ye used to hev by ye, woman? I’m bad wi’ an inward pain.”

“It’s all gane a month sin’,” she answered; and offered to make him a “het” drink if he’d get to his room.

But he said:

“Never mind, I’ll try a mouthful o’ gin.”

And, turning on his heel, he left her.

===Chinese===
半夜里——她说不清是什么时辰——她猛然醒来，只见屋里站着一个男人，戴着帽子。他手里擎着一支蜡烛，用衣襟挡着光不叫她瞧见；他背朝着她，正在翻弄她平素放钱的那个抽屉。

好在那一天她刚领了一季两英镑的养老金，便把钞票叠好裹在一块破布里，塞在茶叶罐的角落，锁进了那口食橱里。

她一见屋里有个人影，吓得不行，也说不准这位不速之客是不是从紧挨着的教堂墓地那边溜进来的。于是她直挺挺地坐在床上，一头花白头发几乎要把头巾顶起来，浑身上下，用她自己的话说，"起了一身鸡皮疙瘩"，她喝问道：

"奉上帝的名，你搁那儿要做啥？"

"你原先搁在手边的薄荷酒呢，婆子？我肚里痛得厉害。"

"一个月前就没了，"她答道；又说，他若肯回自己屋去，她可以给他弄一杯热的喝。

他却说：

"不打紧，我来抿一口杜松子酒。"

说罢一转身，撇下她走了。

===Original===
In the morning the sexton was gone. Not only in his lodging was there no account of him, but, when inquiry began to be extended, nowhere in the village of Golden Friars could he be found.

Still he might have gone off, on business of his own, to some distant village, before the town was stirring; and the sexton had no near kindred to trouble their heads about him. People, therefore, were willing to wait, and take his return ultimately for granted.

At three o’clock the good Vicar, standing at his hall door, looking across the lake towards the noble fells that rise, steep and furrowed, from that beautiful mere, saw two men approaching across the green, in a straight line, from a boat that was moored at the water’s edge. They were carrying between them something which, though not very large, seemed ponderous.

===Chinese===
到了早晨，司事不见了。不仅他的住处没人知道他的去向，及至四下打听开来，整个金修士镇上也找不到他半点影子。

不过，他也许是在镇上人还没起床之前，因着自己的什么事，动身去了远处的什么村子；司事又没有近亲会替他操心。因此人们倒也乐于等等，暂且当作他总会回来的。

下午三点钟光景，好心的牧师站在自家门前，隔着湖面，眺望对岸那从美丽的湖畔拔地而起、又陡又褶的巍巍群山，这时他看见两个人从水边一只泊着的船上下来，穿过草地，径直朝这边走来。两人抬着一件东西，东西不大，看着却沉甸甸的。

===Original===
“Ye’ll ken this, sir,” said one of the boatmen as they set down, almost at his feet, a small church bell, such as in old-fashioned chimes yields the treble notes.

“This won’t be less nor five stean. I ween it’s fra’ the church steeple yon.”

“What! one of our church bells?” ejaculated the Vicar— for a moment lost in horrible amazement. “Oh, no!—*no*, that can’t possibly be! Where did you find it?”

He had found the boat, in the morning, moored about fifty yards from her moorings where he had left it the night before, and could not think how that came to pass; and now, as he and his partner were about to take their oars, they discovered this bell in the bottom of the boat, under a bit of canvas, also the sexton’s pick and spade—“tom-spey’ad,” they termed that peculiar, broad-bladed implement.

===Chinese===
"老爷，您来看看这个，"其中一个船夫说道，同时将一座小教堂铜钟放在了几乎是他脚边的地方——那种老式编钟里发出最高音的小钟。

"这少说也有五英石重。我寻思它就是从那边教堂钟楼上来的。"

"什么！我们教堂的钟？"牧师失声叫道——一时间陷入了骇然的惊愕之中。"噢，不！——*不*，这怎么可能！你们在哪里找到的？"

原来那天早晨，船夫发现小船偏离了头天夜里拴系的位置，往外挪了约莫五十码，他怎么也想不通这是怎么回事；如今他和同伴正要拿桨，却发现船舱底下一块帆布下面藏着这口铜钟，还有司事的镐和锹——他们管那种特制的宽口铲锹叫"阔面锹"（tom-spey'ad）。

===Original===
“Very extraordinary! We must try whether there is a bell missing from the tower,” said the Vicar, getting into a fuss. “Has Crooke come back yet? Does anyone know where he is?”

The sexton had not yet turned up.

“That’s odd—that’s provoking,” said the Vicar. “However, my key will let us in. Place the bell in the hall while I get it; and then we can see what all this means.”

To the church, accordingly, they went, the Vicar leading the way, with his own key in his hand. He turned it in the lock, and stood in the shadow of the ground porch, and shut the door.

A sack, half full, lay on the ground, with open mouth, a piece of cord lying beside it. Something clanked within it as one of the men shoved it aside with his clumsy shoe.

===Chinese===
"太蹊跷了！我们得去看看钟楼上是不是少了一口钟，"牧师说着，慌张起来。"克鲁克回来了没有？有谁知道他在哪儿吗？"

司事仍未露面。

"怪了——真叫人生气，"牧师说。"不过我有钥匙，开得进去。先把钟搁在门厅里，我去拿钥匙；然后咱们看看这到底是怎么回事。"

于是他们一行人往教堂走去，牧师领头，手里攥着他自己的钥匙。他把钥匙插进锁孔一转，站在门廊的阴影里，随手关上了门。

地上搁着一只半满的麻袋，袋口敞着，旁边散着一截绳头。一个男人用他那笨重的鞋头把袋子往旁边一拨，里面叮当响了一声。

===Original===
The Vicar opened the church door and peeped in. The dusky glow from the western sky, entering through a narrow window, illuminated the shafts and arches, the old oak carvings, and the discoloured monuments, with the melancholy glare of a dying fire.

The Vicar withdrew his head and closed the door. The gloom of the porch was deeper than ever as, stooping, he entered the narrow door that opened at the foot of the winding stair that leads to the first loft; from which a rude ladder-stair of wood, some five and twenty feet in height, mounts through a trap to the ringers’ loft.

Up the narrow stairs the Vicar climbed, followed by his attendants, to the first loft. It was very dark: a narrow bow-slit in the thick wall admitted the only light they had to guide them. The ivy leaves, seen from the deep shadow, flashed and flickered redly, and the sparrows twittered among them.

===Chinese===
牧师推开教堂大门，探头朝里张望。西天暗淡的霞光从一扇窄窗照进来，将那些廊柱与拱券、古老的橡木雕饰以及斑驳的纪念碑石，都映照出一种行将熄灭的炉火般凄凉的光。

牧师缩回头，关上了门。门廊里比先前更幽暗了。他弯下腰，钻进一扇窄门，门开在通向第一层阁楼的旋梯脚下；从那阁楼再往上，一道粗陋的木梯约有二十五英尺高，穿过一道活板门，通往敲钟人的阁楼。

牧师沿着窄梯攀上第一层阁楼，随行的人跟着他。阁楼里极暗：厚厚的石壁上只有一道窄窄的箭缝形小窗，透进来的光是他们在黑暗中唯一的指引。从幽深的暗处望去，墙外的常春藤叶闪着红光，忽明忽灭，麻雀在叶子间叽叽喳喳地叫着。

===Original===
“Will one of you be so good as to go up and count the bells, and see if they are all right?” said the Vicar. “There should be—”

“Agoy! what’s that?” exclaimed one of the men, recoiling from the foot of the ladder.

“By Jen!” ejaculated the other, in equal surprise.

“Good gracious!” gasped the Vicar, who, seeing indistinctly a dark mass lying on the floor, had stooped to examine it, and placed his hand upon a cold, dead face.

The men drew the body into the streak of light that traversed the floor.

It was the corpse of Toby Crooke! There was a frightful scar across his forehead.

===Chinese===
"你们哪位上去数一数钟，看看齐不齐？"牧师说。"应该有——"

"哎哟！那是什么？"一个男人在梯子脚下倒退一步，惊叫起来。

"我的天！"另一个人同样吃了一惊，叫出声来。

"老天爷！"牧师倒吸一口冷气——他隐约看见地板上躺着一团黑乎乎的东西，弯腰去查看，一只手却摸到了一张冰冷、死寂的脸。

众人把那尸体拖到横贯地板的那一线光里。

正是托比·克鲁克的尸首！他额头上横着一道骇人的伤疤。

===Original===
The alarm was given. Doctor Lincote, and Mr. Jarlcot, and Turnbull, of the George and Dragon, were on the spot immediately; and many curious and horrified spectators of minor importance.

The first thing ascertained was that the man must have been many hours dead. The next was that his skull was fractured, across the forehead, by an awful blow. The next was that his neck was broken.

His hat was found on the floor, where he had probably laid it, with his handkerchief in it.

The mystery now began to clear a little; for a bell—one of the chime hung in the tower—was found where it had rolled to, against the wall, with blood and hair on the rim of it, which corresponded with the grizzly fracture across the front of his head.

===Chinese===
消息一传出去。林科特医生、贾尔科特先生，还有"乔治与龙"的特恩布尔，立刻赶到了现场；此外还有许多好奇而惊骇的看客，身份不等，挤了一屋子。

最先查明的事实是：此人已死去多时。其次：他的额骨被一记猛击击碎，横贯前额。再者：他的颈骨折断了。

他的帽子搁在地板上，大约是他自己先前放下的，手帕还塞在帽子里。

事情的原委渐渐有了一点眉目：一口钟——钟楼上编钟里的一口——滚落在墙根，钟沿上沾着血迹和头发，正与他前额那道惨烈的骨折伤吻合。

===Original===
The sack that lay in the vestibule was examined, and found to contain all the church plate; a silver salver that had disappeared, about a month before, from Dr. Lincote’s store of valuables; the Vicar’s gold pencil-case, which he thought he had forgot in the vestry book; silver spoons, and various other contributions, levied from time to time off a dozen different households, the mysterious disappearance of which spoils had, of late years, begun to make the honest little community uncomfortable. Two bells had been taken down from the chime; and now the shrewd part of the assemblage, putting things together, began to comprehend the nefarious plans of the sexton, who lay mangled and dead on the floor of the tower, where only two days ago he had tolled the holy bell to call the good Christians of Golden Friars to worship.

The body was carried into the yard of the George and Dragon and laid in the old coach-house; and the townsfolk came grouping in to have a peep at the corpse, and stood round, looking darkly, and talking as low as if they were in a church.

===Chinese===
门廊里那只麻袋也经了查验，里头装的全是教堂的金银器皿：一只银托盘——约莫一个月前从林科特医生的珍品贮藏中不翼而飞的；牧师的金铅笔——他一直以为是忘在议事录里的；银勺若干，还有从十来户人家陆续"征用"来的各色物件。这些物件近年来相继神秘失踪，已叫这诚实的小小社区人心惶惶。编钟里被摘下了两口；此刻人群中那些精明的人，把种种线索串联起来，渐渐看明白了这位司事的奸谋——他此刻血肉模糊地横死在钟楼地板上，而仅仅两天之前，他还在这里敲响神圣的钟声，召唤金修士镇的好基督徒们前来礼拜。

尸首被抬进了"乔治与龙"的院子，搁在那间旧马车房里；镇上的人三三两两地涌进来看死人，围着站了一圈，面色阴沉，说话的声音低得像在教堂里一样。

===Original===
The Vicar, in gaiters and slightly shovel hat, stood erect, as one in a little circle of notables—the doctor, the attorney, Sir Geoffrey Mardykes, who happened to be in the town, and Turnbull, the host—in the centre of the paved yard, they having made an inspection of the body, at which troops of the village stragglers, to-ing and fro-ing, were gaping and frowning as they whispered their horrible conjectures.

“What d’ye think o’ that?” said Tom Scales, the old hostler of the George, looking pale, with a stern, faint smile on his lips, as he and Dick Linklin sauntered out of the coach-house together.

“The deaul will hev his ain noo,” answered Dick, in his friend’s ear. “T’ sexton’s got a craigthraw like he gav’ the lass over the clints of Scarsdale; ye mind what the ald soger telt us when he hid his face in the kitchen of the George here? By Jen! I’ll ne’er forget that story.”

===Chinese===
牧师裹着绑腿，微微戴一顶铲形帽，笔直地站着——他和医生、律师，还有恰好在镇上的杰弗里·马迪克斯爵士（Sir Geoffrey Mardykes），以及掌柜特恩布尔，构成一个小小的头面人物圈子——站在铺了石板的院子正中央。他们方才查看过尸体，院子四周一拨拨进进出出的闲人，伸着脖子、皱着眉头，一边交头接耳地说着种种骇人的揣测。

"你怎么看？"汤姆·斯凯尔斯（Tom Scales）说道——他是"乔治与龙"的老马夫，脸色发白，嘴唇上挂着一丝冷峻而隐约的笑意。他同迪克·林克林（Dick Linklin）一道从马车房里踱了出来。

"这下魔鬼可收了他的本钱了，"迪克凑在他朋友耳边答道。"司事这脖颈子断的，跟他当初把那姑娘从斯卡斯代尔（Scarsdale）悬崖上推下去时一模一样；你还记得那个老兵躲在'乔治与龙'厨房里遮着脸讲的那段事不？老天！我一辈子也忘不了那个故事。"

===Original===
“I ween ’twas all true enough,” replied the hostler; “and the sizzup he gav’ the sleepin’ man wi’ t’ poker across the forehead. See whar the edge o’ t’ bell took him, and smashed his ain, the selfsame lids. By ma sang, I wonder the deaul did na carry awa’ his corpse i’ the night, as he did wi’ Tam Lunder’s at Mooltern Mill.”

“Hout, man, who ever sid t’ deaul inside o’ a church?”

“The corpse is ill-faur’d enew to scare Satan himsel’, for that matter; though it’s true what you say. Ay, ye’re reet tul a trippet, thar; for Beelzebub dar’n’t show his snout inside the church, not the length o’ the black o’ my nail.”

While this discussion was going on, the gentlefolk who were talking the matter over in the centre of the yard had dispatched a message for the coroner all the way to the town of Hextan.

===Chinese===
"我琢磨那全是真的，"马夫答道，"还有他趁人睡着时用拨火棍敲在人家额头上的那一下。你瞧钟沿劈在他额头上，把他自己的眼皮砸了个稀烂，一模一样。老天在上，我真纳闷那魔鬼怎的没在夜里把他的尸首摄了去——就像他对穆尔特恩磨坊（Mooltern Mill）汤姆·伦德（Tam Lunder）的那具干的一样。"

"得了吧，老兄，谁见过魔鬼钻进教堂里头来？"

"就说嘛，那死相难看得连撒旦自己也得吓一跳，这话不假；不过你说的也没错。嗳，你这一条说到点子上了；因为别西卜（Beelzebub）断不敢在教堂里头露他的鼻子——连我指甲盖那么一丁点黑影都不敢露。"

他们这边议论着的时候，院子正中那几位绅士也在商议此事，已经差人一路赶到赫克斯坦（Hextan）镇上，去请验尸官了。

===Original===
The last tint of sunset was fading from the sky by this time; so, of course, there was no thought of an inquest earlier than next day.

In the meantime it was horribly clear that the sexton had intended to rob the church of its plate, and had lost his life in the attempt to carry the second bell, as we have seen, down the worn ladder of the tower. He had tumbled backwards and broken his neck upon the floor of the loft; and the heavy bell, in its fall, descended with its edge across his forehead.

Never was a man more completely killed by a double catastrophe, in a moment.

The bells and the contents of the sack, it was surmised, he meant to have conveyed across the lake that night, and with the help of his spade and pick to have buried them in Clousted Forest, and returned, after an absence of but a few hours—as he easily might—before morning, unmissed and unobserved. He would no doubt, having secured his booty, have made such arrangements as would have made it appear that the church had been broken into. He would, of course, have taken all measures to divert suspicion from himself, and have watched a suitable opportunity to repossess himself of the buried treasure and dispose of it in safety.

===Chinese===
此时天边最后一抹残霞已经褪尽；验尸官的讯问自是明天才谈得上，当晚断然来不及了。

事情的原委至此已骇然清晰：这司事原打算盗窃教堂的金银器皿，却在试图把第二口铜钟搬下那道年深月久、磨损不堪的钟楼木梯时，送了性命。他仰面摔下，在阁楼地板上跌断了颈骨；沉重的铜钟跟着坠落，钟沿正好横劈在他的前额上。

一个人在同一刹那被双重横祸断送得如此干净利落，可谓前所未有。

据众人推测，那几口钟和麻袋里的赃物，他原打算当夜用船载过湖去，再借着锹和镐，将它们埋进克劳斯泰德森林（Clousted Forest），然后不过离开几个时辰——这点时间他尽有——在天亮之前赶回来，不叫人察觉，不叫人起疑。他既已把赃物弄到手，想必还会布置一番，叫人以为教堂是遭了贼；他自会想方设法把嫌疑从自己身上撇清，再瞅一个合适的时机，把那批埋藏的财宝取出来，安全脱手。

===Original===
And now came out, into sharp relief, all the stories that had, one way or other, stolen after him into the town. Old Mrs. Pullen fainted when she saw him, and told Doctor Lincote, after, that she thought he was the highwayman who fired the shot that killed the coachman the night they were robbed on Hounslow Heath. There were the stories also told by the wayfaring old soldier with the wooden leg, and fifty others, up to this more than half disregarded, but which now seized on the popular belief with a startling grasp.

The fleeting light soon expired, and twilight was succeeded by the early night.

The inn yard gradually became quiet; and the dead sexton lay alone, in the dark, on his back, locked up in the old coach-house, the key of which was safe in the pocket of Tom Scales, the trusty old hostler of the George.

===Chinese===
这一来，从前种种或明或暗地跟着他潜入镇中的旧事，一下子全都浮上了台面，格外分明。普伦老太太（Old Mrs. Pullen）看见他时竟昏了过去，事后告诉林科特医生，她说她认定他就是那个在汉斯洛荒原（Hounslow Heath）上抢劫他们、开枪打死车夫的强盗。此外还有那个装着一条木腿、云游四方的老兵讲的种种故事，以及另外几十桩——此前大半被人当作耳旁风，如今却以骇人之势攫住了镇上人的心思。

转瞬即逝的余晖很快熄了，暮色之后便是早早降临的夜。

客栈的院子渐渐安静下来；死去的司事独自仰躺在黑暗中，锁在那间旧马车房里，钥匙稳稳地揣在汤姆·斯凯尔斯——"乔治与龙"那位可靠的老马夫——的口袋里。

===Original===
It was about eight o’clock, and the hostler, standing alone on the road in the front of the open door of the George and Dragon, had just smoked his pipe out. A bright moon hung in the frosty sky. The fells rose from the opposite edge of the lake like phantom mountains. The air was stirless. Through the boughs and sprays of the leafless elms no sigh or motion, however hushed, was audible. Not a ripple glimmered on the lake, which at one point only reflected the brilliant moon from its dark blue expanse like burnished steel. The road that runs by the inn door, along the margin of the lake, shone dazzlingly white.

White as ghosts, among the dark holly and juniper, stood the tall piers of the Vicar’s gate, and their great stone balls, like heads, overlooking the same road, a few hundred yards up the lake, to the left. The early little town of Golden Friars was quiet by this time. Except for the townsfolk who were now collected in the kitchen of the inn itself, no inhabitant was now outside his own threshold.

===Chinese===
约莫八点钟光景，马夫独自站在"乔治与龙"敞开的大门前的路上，刚把一袋烟抽完。一轮明月挂在寒霜满天的夜空中。湖对岸的群山拔地而起，像虚影一般的山。空气纹丝不动。那些光秃秃的榆树，枝枝丫丫之间，连一丝最轻最细的叹息声、一丝最微的颤动也听不见。湖面上一道波纹也不见，只在某一点上，那深蓝的湖面映出一轮皎月，亮闪闪的，像擦亮的钢面。沿着湖边、经过客栈门前的那条路，白得晃眼。

牧师家大门两侧的高大石柱，在深色的冬青和杜松之间白得像鬼影一般；柱顶那两颗大石球，像两颗脑袋，居高临下地守着同一条路，在湖的上游几百码处，靠左手的位置。金修士镇这座小小的山镇入夜早，此时已经安静下来了。除了此刻聚在客栈厨房里的那些人之外，没有一个居民还站在自家门槛外头。

===Original===
Tom Scales was thinking of turning in. He was beginning to fell a little queer. He was thinking of the sexton, and could not get the fixed features of the dead man out of his head, when he heard the sharp though distant ring of a horse’s hoof upon the frozen road. Tom’s instinct apprised him of the approach of a guest to the George and Dragon. His experienced ear told him that the horseman was approaching by the Dardale road, which, after crossing that wide and dismal moss, passes the southern fells by Dunner Cleugh and finally enters the town of Golden Friars by joining the Mardykes road, at the edge of the lake, close to the gate of the Vicar’s house.

A clump of tall trees stood at this point; but the moon shone full upon the road and cast their shadow backward.

The hoofs were plainly coming at a gallop, with a hollow rattle. The horseman was a long time in appearing. Tom wondered how he had heard the sound—so sharply frosty as the air was—so very far away.

===Chinese===
汤姆·斯凯尔斯正打算回屋去了。他觉得有点不对劲。他脑子里尽是那司事的事，怎么也甩不掉死人那副僵凝的面容。忽然，他听见冰冻的路面上远远传来一声清脆的马蹄声。汤姆凭着本能就知道，"乔治与龙"有客要来了。他那只老练的耳朵告诉他，来人是沿着达代尔路（Dardale road）过来的——那条路穿过那片又大又荒凉的达代尔沼泽（Dardale Moss），绕过南边的群山，经过邓纳峡谷（Dunner Cleugh），最后在湖边与马迪克斯路交汇，正对着牧师家的大门，由此进入金修士镇。

那个交汇处矗立着一丛高树；但月光径直照在路上，把树影向后投去。

蹄声分明是疾驰而来的，带着空洞的嗒嗒声。可骑马的人却迟迟不现身。汤姆纳闷，自己怎会在这霜气逼人的寒夜里，隔着那么老远就听见了声音。

===Original===
He was right in his guess. The visitor was coming over the mountainous road from Dardale Moss; and he now saw a horseman, who must have turned the corner of the Vicar’s house at the moment when his eye was wearied; for when he saw him for the first time he was advancing, in the hazy moonlight, like the shadow of a cavalier, at a gallop, upon the level strip of road that skirts the margin of the mere, between the George and the Vicar’s piers.

The hostler had not long to wonder why the rider pushed his beast at so furious a pace, and how he came to have heard him, as he now calculated, at least three miles away. A very few moments sufficed to bring horse and rider to the inn door.

It was a powerful black horse, something like the great Irish hunter that figured a hundred years ago, and would carry sixteen stone with ease across country. It would have made a grand charger. Not a hair turned. It snorted, it pawed, it arched its neck; then threw back its ears and down its head, and looked ready to lash, and then to rear; and seemed impatient to be off again, and incapable of standing quiet for a moment.

===Chinese===
他没猜错。来人确是从达代尔沼泽那边的山路过来的；紧接着他便看见了一个骑马的人——那人必定是在他目光疲倦的那一刹那，拐过了牧师家屋角；因为当他头一眼看见来人时，那人已经在朦胧的月色里，像一个骑士的影子一般，策马疾驰在那段沿着湖边、连接"乔治与龙"和牧师家石柱的平坦路上了。

马夫没等多久，便明白了来人何以如此疯赶，也明白了自己何以能在——他此刻估量——至少三英里之外就听见了蹄声。不多片刻，人马便已到了客栈门前。

那是一匹神骏的黑马，有些像百年前闻名一时的那种爱尔兰猎马，驮上十六英石也能在原野上健步如飞。拿来做战马，再威风不过。它通体不见一根杂毛。它打着响鼻，刨着蹄子，拱起脖颈；随即又向后抿耳朵、低下头，一副蓄势要踢、继而要尥蹶子的模样；仿佛急不可耐地要再跑起来，一秒钟也站不安稳。

===Original===
The rider got down—

> As light as shadow falls.

But he was a tall, sinewy figure. He wore a cape or short mantle, a cocked hat, and a pair of jackboots, such as held their ground in some primitive corners of England almost to the close of the last century.

“Take him, lad,” said he to old Scales. “You need not walk or wisp him—he never sweats or tires. Give him his oats, and let him take his own time to eat them. House!” cried the stranger—in the old-fashioned form of summons which still lingered, at that time, in out-of-the-way places—in a deep and piercing voice.

As Tom Scales led the horse away to the stables it turned its head towards its master with a short, shill neigh.

“About *your* business, old gentleman—we must not go too fast,” the stranger cried back again to his horse, with a laugh as harsh and piercing; and he strode into the house.

===Chinese===
骑手翻身下马——

> 宛如落影一般轻盈。

却见他身量高大，筋骨强健。他披着一件斗篷，或者说是短披风，戴一顶三角帽，足登一双长筒马靴——这般装束直到上世纪末，在英格兰某些偏僻角落里还不曾绝迹。

"牵着他吧，老伙计，"他对老斯凯尔斯说。"用不着遛他、也不用给他擦身——他从不出汗，也不知疲倦。给他上燕麦就是了，由着他慢慢吃。喂——掌柜的！"那陌生人喊道——用的是旧式叫门的招呼法，彼时在偏僻地方尚有遗风——声音低沉而尖锐。

汤姆·斯凯尔斯牵着马往马厩去时，那马回过头来朝着主人，发出一声短促而尖厉的嘶鸣。

"干*你的*活去吧，老先生——咱们可不能走得太急，"陌生人回头冲他的马喊道，笑声同样刺耳而尖利；说罢大步流星地跨进了门。

===Original===
The hostler led this horse into the inn yard. In passing, it sidled up to the coach-house gate, within which lay the dead sexton—snorted, pawed and lowered its head suddenly, with ear close to the plank, as if listening for a sound from within; then uttered again the same short, piercing neigh.

The hostler was chilled at this mysterious coquetry with the dead. He liked the brute less and less every minute.

In the meantime, its master had proceeded.

“I’ll go to the inn kitchen,” he said, in his startling bass, to the drawer who met him in the passage.

And on he went, as if he had known the place all his days: not seeming to hurry himself—stepping leisurely, the servant thought—but gliding on at such a rate, nevertheless, that he had passed his guide and was in the kitchen of the George before the drawer had got much more than halfway to it.

===Chinese===
马夫牵着这匹马穿过客栈的院子。经过马车房大门时——死去的司事就躺在里面——那马侧着身子凑近门板，打着响鼻，刨着蹄子，猛地低下头去，耳朵紧贴着木板，仿佛在倾听里面的动静；接着又发出同样一声短促而尖锐的嘶鸣。

马夫被这番与死人之间诡异的亲昵，骇得通体发凉。他越看这畜生越觉得不喜欢。

与此同时，马的主人已经往里走了。

"我去厨房，"他对在过道里迎上来的跑堂的说道，声音低沉得吓人。

说罢便径直往里走，好似在这里住了一辈子似的：看不出半点着急的模样——那仆人心想，他步子闲闲散散的——可不知怎的，他滑行一般走得飞快，还没等跑堂的走到一半路，他已越过了引路的人，抢先一步踏进了"乔治与龙"的厨房。

===Original===
A roaring fire of dry wood, peat and coal lighted up this snug but spacious apartment—flashing on pots and pans, and dressers high-piled with pewter plates and dishes; and making the uncertain shadows of the long “hanks” of onions and many a flitch and ham, depending from the ceiling, dance on its glowing surface.

The doctor and the attorney, even Sir Geoffrey Mardykes, did not disdain on this occasion to take chairs and smoke their pipes by the kitchen fire, where they were in the thick of the gossip and discussion excited by the terrible event.

The tall stranger entered uninvited.

He looked like a gaunt, athletic Spaniard of forty, burned half black in the sun, with a bony, flattened nose. A pair of fierce black eyes were just visible under the edge of his hat; and his mouth seemed divided, beneath the moustache, by the deep scar of a harelip.

Sir Geoffrey Mardykes and the host of the George, aided by the doctor and the attorney, were discussing and arranging, for the third or fourth time, their theories about the death and the probable plans of Toby Crooke, when the stranger entered.

===Chinese===
一炉旺火烧着干柴、泥炭和煤，把这间舒适而宽敞的屋子照得通亮——炉火映在锅碗瓢盆上，映在碗柜上层层叠叠的白镴盘碟上；天花板上挂着一长串一长串的洋葱、一条条熏肉和一只只火腿，它们的影子在炉火的红光里摇摇晃晃地跳动。

医生和律师，甚至杰弗里·马迪克斯爵士，此番也不嫌弃在厨房炉边坐下来抽烟斗——因为这里正是议论那桩惨事、七嘴八舌说得最热闹的地方。

那高大的陌生人也不等人请，径直走了进来。

他看着像一个四十来岁、精瘦健壮的西班牙人，面孔在烈日下晒得半黑，鼻梁又扁又多骨。帽檐底下隐约可见一双凶悍的黑眼睛；唇髭之下，他的嘴似乎被一道兔唇的深疤从中间劈成了两半。

杰弗里·马迪克斯爵士和"乔治与龙"的掌柜，再加上医生和律师，正第三次、第四次地反复推敲着关于托比·克鲁克之死及其种种图谋的种种揣测，陌生人就在这时走了进来。

===Original===
The newcomer lifted his hat, with a sort of smile, for a moment from his black head.

“What do you call this place, gentlemen?” asked the stranger.

“The town of Golden Friars, sir,” answered the doctor politely.

“The George and Dragon, sir: Anthony Turnbull, at your service,” answered mine host, with a solemn bow, at the same moment—so that the two voices went together, as if the doctor and the innkeeper were singing a catch.

===Chinese===
来人把帽子从他那一头黑发上微微抬起一抬，脸上似笑非笑的，不过片刻。

"先生们，这地方叫什么？"陌生人问道。

"金修士镇，先生，"医生客气地答道。

"'乔治与龙'客栈，先生：安东尼·特恩布尔（Anthony Turnbull），听您差遣，"掌柜同时在旁边一板正经地一躬身答道——两个人的声音叠在了一起，倒像医生和掌柜在对唱一首轮唱曲。

===Original===
“The George and the Dragon,” repeated the horseman, expanding his long hands over the fire which he had approached. “Saint George, King George, the Dragon, the Devil: it is a very grand idol, that outside your door, sir. You catch all sorts of worshippers—courtiers, fanatics, scamps: all’s fish, eh? Everybody welcome, provided he drinks like one. Suppose you brew a bowl or two of punch. I’ll stand it. How many are we? *Here*—count, and let us have enough. Gentlemen, I mean to spend the night here, and my horse is in the stable. What holiday, fun, or fair has got so many pleasant faces together? When I last called here—for, now I bethink me, I have seen the place before—you all looked sad. It was on a Sunday, that dismalest of holidays; and it would have been positively melancholy only that your sexton—that saint upon earth—Mr. Crooke, was here.” He was looking round, over his shoulder, and added: “Ha! don’t I see him there?”

Frightened a good deal were some of the company. All gaped in the direction in which, with a nod, he turned his eyes.

“He’s *not* thar—he *can’t* be thar—we *see* he’s not thar,” said Turnbull, as dogmatically as old Joe Willet might have delivered himself—for he did not care that the George should earn the reputation of a haunted house. “He’s met an accident, sir: he’s dead—he’s elsewhere—and therefore can’t be here.”

===Chinese===
"乔治与龙，"骑马的人重复了一遍，一面把他那双长手伸向已经凑近的炉火。"圣乔治、国王乔治、龙、魔鬼——先生，你门外头挂的那位可真是一尊了不得的神像啊。什么香客都能招徕——朝臣的、狂信的、混混的：来者不拒，是吧？只要他肯像样地喝酒，谁都欢迎。不如这样，你来调它一两盆潘趣酒。算我的。咱们一共多少人？*来*——数一数，管够。先生们，我今夜就在此歇脚了，我的马也在马厩里了。是什么节庆、什么热闹、什么集市，把这么多张快活面孔凑到了一处？上回我打这儿过——容我想想，这地方我来过的——你们一个个愁眉苦脸的。那天是个礼拜天，节庆里最没意思的那种；要不是贵地的司事——那位人间圣徒——克鲁克先生也在，那晚上简直要叫人闷死了。"他说着，回过头去四下张望，又道："嗬！我好像看见他在那边了？"

满座的人好些都吓了一大跳。众人都朝着他点过头、转过目光的方向望去，一个个张口结舌。

"他*不*在那儿——他*不可能*在那儿——我们*亲眼看见*他不在那儿，"特恩布尔斩钉截铁地说——那口气活像老乔·威利特（Joe Willet）讲话一般——他可不愿意"乔治与龙"落下个凶宅的名声。"他出了意外，先生：他死了——他不在这儿——所以不可能在那儿。"

===Original===
Upon this the company entertained the stranger with the narrative—which they made easy by a division of labour, two or three generally speaking at a time, and no one being permitted to finish a second sentence without finding himself corrected and supplanted.

“The man’s in Heaven, so sure as you’re not,” said the traveller so soon as the story was ended. “What! he was fiddling with the church bell, was he, and d——d for that—eh? Landlord, get us some drink. A sexton d——d for pulling down a church bell he has been pulling at for ten years!”

“You came, sir, by the Dardale-road, I believe?” said the doctor (village folk are curious). “A dismal moss is Dardale Moss, sir; and a bleak clim’ up the fells on t’ other side.”

===Chinese===
于是众人便七嘴八舌地把事情原委讲给陌生人听——他们分工合作，讲得倒也顺当：通常两三个人同时开口，谁也别想把第二句话说完整，便被人纠正、被人抢了话头。

"此人已在天堂，千真万确，正如诸位不在天堂一样，"故事一讲完，那旅人便说道。"什么！他摆弄教堂的钟来着，是吗，结果就为这个下了地狱——嗯？掌柜的，来点喝的。一个教堂司事，摘一口他敲了十年的钟，竟就因此下了地狱！"

"先生，您是从达代尔路过来的吧？"医生问道（乡里人好奇心重）。"达代尔沼泽可真是阴森哪，先生；翻过那边的山也是一段寒风刺骨的苦路。"

===Original===
“I say ‘Yes’ to all—from Dardale Moss, as black as pitch and as rotten as the grave, up that zigzag wall you call a road, that looks like chalk in the moonlight, through Dunner Cleugh, as dark as a coal-pit, and down here to the George and the Dragon, where you have a roaring fire, wise men, good punch—here it is—and a corpse in your coach-house. Where the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together. Come, landlord, ladle out the nectar. Drink, gentlemen—drink, all. Brew another bowl at the bar. How divinely it stinks of alcohol! I hope you like it, gentlemen: it smells all over of spices, like a mummy. Drink, friends. Ladle, landlord. Drink, all. Serve it out.”

The guest fumbled in his pocket, and produced three guineas, which he slipped into Turnbull’s fat palm.

“Let punch flow till that’s out. I’m an old friend of the house. I call here, back and forward. I know you well, Turnbull, though you don’t recognize me.”

“You have the advantage of me, sir,” said Mr. Turnbull, looking hard on that dark and sinister countenance—which, or the like of which, he could have sworn he had never seen before in his life. But he liked the weight and colour of his guineas, as he dropped them into his pocket. “I hope you will find yourself comfortable while you stay.”

“You have given me a bedroom?”
